A full-scale drill was also conducted based on a simulated scenario involving the Mysuru–Hyderabad flight. Initially, the incoming aircraft from Hyderabad was declared “delayed” owing to fog, and passengers were given water and snacks to ensure comfort.
Subsequently, the airline announced the cancellation of the flight, leading to a simulated situation of passenger agitation. It was effectively managed by the airline staff and Karnataka State Industrial Security Force personnel.
Passengers were offered refunds or ticket rescheduling as per their preference, after which they collected their baggage and exited the terminal. Friends and relatives waiting at the city-side were also informed of the updated status, said Ms. Kumari, who oversaw the drill. Air Traffic Control officials, terminal managers, representatives from Indigo, Karnataka State Industrial Security Force, and others stakeholder representatives were present.

title: CPI flays Constitutional amendments on religious lines
summary: CPI warns against religious amendments to the Constitution, urging public opposition to protect India's democratic and secular foundations.
content:
Communist Party of India (CPI) State Executive Committee member A. Ramanaidu on Saturday called on the public and political groups to strongly oppose any attempts to amend the Constitution in the name of religion, warning that such moves posed a threat to India’s democratic and secular foundations.
Addressing a theoretical and political training programme for district-level cadres at the CPI party office here, Mr. Ramanaidu said the cadres of Left parties must be ideologically equipped to fight for people’s issues. He alleged that the present political climate was marked by efforts to fuel divisions along religious, caste and regional lines for the sake of power, while sidelining Constitutional values.
Expressing concern over what he termed ‘covert attempts’ to change the Constitution, Mr. Ramanaidu urged the public to hold the BJP-led NDA government at the Centre accountable.
CPI district secretary S. Nagaraju and senior cadres from all the Assembly constituencies of Chittoor district participated in the meeting.

title: Maharashtra govt. unhappy with Jitendra Singh’s statement on IIT-Bombay, Minister tells House
summary: Maharashtra government expresses displeasure over Union Minister Jitendra Singh's IIT-Bombay remarks, emphasizing Mumbai's pride and identity.
content:
The Maharashtra government is unhappy with Union Minister Jitendra Singh’s recent statement about Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay, Maharashtra Minister Ashish Shelar told the Legislative Council on Saturday (December 13, 2025). He was responding to a notice issued by Shiv Sena (UBT) MLC Anil Parab on the issue. He also said that an upset Chief Minister had written to the Union government about it.
Mr. Singh had recently said that he was happy that the name of the IIT was IIT-Bombay, and not IIT-Mumbai. The statement had caused a stir in the State, with both the Opposition as well as the ruling dispensation hitting back at Mr. Singh. Maharashtra Navnirman Sena leader Raj Thackeray had also expressed strong displeasure about it.
“It needs to be clearly stated that the Maharashtra government is unhappy with this statement. The Chief Minister has already written a letter to the Union Minister concerned about it. So, the government’s position is not just that it is unhappy, but that the displeasure has been conveyed as well,” Mr. Shelar told the House during its Winter Session.
“We have not yet received the notification about it [the notice raised in the House]. And though this does not fall in the purview of my department, this issue is close to the heart for all of us. It is of significance for Maharashtra, for Mumbai, and it is a matter of pride and identity for the Marathimanoos. So, I wish to express my opinion on the notice issued on the topic,” Mr. Shelar said while speaking in the Council.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MLC Anil Parab had raised the issue, seeking to know Maharashtra government’s official position in the matter. “Mumbai is a matter of identity and pride for the Marathimanoos. Balasaheb Thackeray had done a lot for the issue of renaming Bombay as Mumbai, so had [former Union Minister and BJP leader] Ram Naik. So I had asked the government for its position on the Union Minister’s statement,” Mr. Parab toldThe Hindufrom Nagpur.

title: Punjab rural polls: Punjab CM Mann slams Congress, SAD for 'high-handedness' charge; says they accepted defeat
summary: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann criticizes Congress and SAD for defeat acceptance, countering fake ballot allegations in rural polls.
content:
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Saturday (December 13, 2025) slammed the Congress and Akali Dal over their "high-handedness" allegation against the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in the Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti polls, saying they have accepted their defeat in the elections.
Congress leader and former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi alleged that the AAP Government in the State had printed fake ballot papers for the December 14 Zila Parishad and Block Samiti elections.
Referring to Mr. Channi's statement, Mr. Mann took on the Congress and reminded it that the AAP supported the grand old party over the issue of "vote theft" whereas it was questioning the polling through ballot papers in Punjab.
Mr. Mann also highlighted the Congress' defeat in Bihar, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and bypolls in Punjab and asserted that where they register victory in polls, then voting process is right and where they lose, they start "crying".
Addressing the media here, Mr. Mann lambasted Mr. Channi, saying he made an "irresponsible" statement and also spoke four colloquial Punjabi phrases including 'Hath na pahunche, thoo kori' (which means out of reach) to lash out at the Congress.
These four idioms are suitable for Congress which lose because of their "misdeeds" and blame others, he said.
"Charanjit Singh Channi, who was the Chief Minister for 111 days, made an irresponsible statement that AAP printed 100 ballot papers each with AAP symbol printed on them at each polling booth. If you analyze it, it shows that they have accepted their defeat," said Mr. Mann.
"Both the Congress and Akali Dal have accepted their defeat in the rural polls but are accusing the AAP government of high-handedness against Opposition candidates," the Chief Minister claimed.
Giving details of the Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti polls, Mr. Mann said out of 2,833 zones of Block Samitis, 340 AAP candidates, three Congress nominees and eight Independents have been elected unopposed.
"If the Congress and independent candidates were elected unopposed, then wasn't there any high-handedness in these seats?" Mr. Mann asked.
He said AAP's 2,771 candidates, Congress’s 2,433, SAD's 1,814, BJP's 1,127, BSP's 195, SAD (Amritsar)'s three and 686 others are fighting the panchayat samiti polls. "How were the nomination papers of opposition candidates found to be correct?" he asked rhetorically.
Opposition parties had earlier targeted the ruling AAP, accusing it of misusing official machinery in preventing their candidates from filing their nomination papers and rejecting their candidature.
He said there are a total of 347 Zila Parishad zones. For these zones, Congress is fighting 331 zones, Akali Dal 298, BJP 215, BSP 50, SAD (Amritsar) 4 and 143 others. A total of 1,396 candidates are contesting the Zila Parishad polls.
Nomination papers of these candidates were also accepted, he said.
Targeting the Congress, Mr. Mann said that after losing recent elections in Bihar, they blamed the BJP for their defeat. "Ask Tejashwi Yadav. He says the Congress defeated him. Last time, Congress took 60 seats, but won 16-17 seats. This time they took 63 seats and won only 6 seats,“ he said.
“The Congress does not introspect,” he said, adding that in Delhi, they do not blame anyone because they do not win any seat there.
"In Punjab, they accuse us of printing ballot papers. Tell Channi saab, where we printed the ballot papers. In reality, they have accepted their defeat," said Mr. Mann.
The CM, targetting Mr. Channi, said that the Congress should boycott the polls if he thinks that the AAP printed the ballot papers.
Mr. Mann alleged that rival political parties are supporting common candidates against the AAP by forming an alliance for the rural polls.
Lashing out at the Sukhbir Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal, Mr. Mann said the 'B' in SAD is 'Beadbi' and 'badmash', alleging that it gave tickets to the relatives of a gangster. "Akali Dal has decided to seek votes from people at gunpoint," he alleged.
Lambasting Mr. Channi while referring to recent Navjot Kaur Sidhu's 'Rs 500 crore for Chief Minister's chair remark' that sparked a political row, Mr. Mann alleged the Congress has opened a 'Neelaam Ghar' (auction house). “You put your chits there. If somebody else offered a high rate then what will you do? If you do not get the CM chair, then think about Deputy CM post. Navjot Kaur Sidhu is revealing the rates of posts in the Congress", he said.
“They [the Opposition] consider Punjab a ‘saleable material’", he said. “One has clearly said that make me Punjab CM otherwise he was happy working on TV,” said Mr. Mann while referring to Navjot Singh Sidhu.
Taking on former Chief Minister Amarinder Singh, Mr. Mann said he has now started abusing the BJP. "If nobody listens to you, then resign," he said, adding that he likes the Congress’s culture.
He also spoke about the Congress' defeat in Haryana, MP and Bihar polls. He said that in the Gujarat bypoll, Congress fielded its candidate despite knowing that AAP has its nominee there to make BJP candidate win. However, the AAP candidate won, said Mr. Mann.
He further highlighted the Congress' defeat in Tarn Taran, Ludhiana West, Jalandhar West, Dera Baba Nanak, Chabbewal and Gidderbaha bypolls.
Targeting the rival parties, Mr. Mann said they have accepted their defeat in the polls.
"They have come to know that people are not with them. That is why they start alleging that AAP looted votes. Why can't they introspect?" he asked.
Mr. Mann spoke about 600 units of free electricity, water for irrigation reaching the last mile and good condition of roads, opening of mohalla clinics, and 17 toll plazas shut in villages.
"We are seeking votes based on our works. But, they [the Opposition] are crying that their papers were snatched," the Chief Minister said.

title: IFFK 2025: ‘Kaathirippu’ is a riveting psychological drama on introspection and repentance
summary: Discover 'Kaathirippu,' a gripping psychological drama exploring introspection and morality through the dialogue of two strangers.
content:
For almost the entirety ofKaathirippu, the protagonist David, played by Jitheesh Raichel Samuel, is repairing what appears to be a radio — tightening its screws, setting its parts into grooves, cautiously mending a once-functional machine. David’s workshop is filled with trinkets like these, which may have once been deemed working. He devotes his days to restoration. But the real question is, can everything be fixed, or are some things beyond repair?
Soon, he encounters Anoop, played by Renju Thadikkaran, who mistakenly enters David’s house, hoping to stay the night there while he waits for his friend. David kicks him out at first, only to bring Renju back to his home. Gradually, the duo gets to know each other, revealing more details about David’s past and identity.
Kaathirippu, written and directed by Nipin Narayanan, premiered at the 30th International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK) in the Malayalam Cinema Today category.
The 83-minute film is set in a single location and features only two characters, with the plot advancing through their engaging conversation. Each dialogue and action reveals something new about the protagonist, who maintains an air of mystery.
The dilapidated state of the setting, shots of slimy slugs, leaky taps, and squeaky chairs, express a visual of alluring disarray — gradually building the suspense.
The film raises questions about what’s right and wrong, and how humans tend to decide for themselves what is morally correct, while simultaneously creating narratives that suit their moral position.Kaathirippuexplores an unending wait for consequences to one’s actions, as the anticipation itself becoming retribution.
The film begins with a text, “We dreamed of making a film, and we made one.”,  underlining a collective vision which came to fruition. “It is a dream all of us crew members saw individually, and it became a collective dream when we came together,” says Nipin, who completed a postgraduate diploma in direction and screenplay writing from K R Narayanan National Institute of Visual Science and Arts (KRNNIVSA), Kottayam, in 2016.
Jitheesh Raichel Samuel, Renju Thadikkaran and Nipin Narayanan (below)
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
The film’s crew mostly consists of KRNNIVSA alumni: Jitheesh and Renju completed a postgraduate diploma in acting from the college in 2016. Cinematographer Adharsh G Krishnan was part of the 2019 batch, and Febin K Thomas, who handled music, is a 2016 alumnus.
The crew, who has created multiple short film assignments at college, was confident of making a feature-length film without committing to a big budget. “We had the technicians to pull off the project. But the only problem was money. This forced us to think along the lines of limited characters and limited spacing,” says Nipin. “I was used to doing movies which had a thriller character, creating curiosity among the audience,” he adds.
“Initially, it was just one character in one space who faced troubles like anxiety. There was a lot to be fixed within him, but he didn’t know how to solve it. So, we introduced another character to help him. We have incorporated incidents we have heard from our circles, and events we have experienced, to the plot,” says Nipin, a cartoonist, author, and scriptwriter.
The maker says it was his goal to premiere his debut at IFFK, which he considers a platform for creators like him to find an audience. “We had started working on this film four months ago,” says Nipin, who has penned the script forKarakkam, which is set to release in January 2026.

title: Drill on radiation leakage held at Kaiga NPCIL unit
summary: A successful mock drill was conducted at Kaiga NPCIL unit to test emergency preparedness for potential radiation leaks in Uttara Kannada.
content:
A drill on testing preparedness in the event of a radiation leak at the Kaiga atomic power generation station of Nuclear Power Corporation of India (NPCIL) was successfully conducted in the ‘likely to be radiation affected villages’ of Uttara Kannada district recently.
According to a press release issued by Deputy Commissioner of Uttara Kannada district K. Lakshmipriya, the drill on possible radiation leak was conducted on December 11.
“After the emergency alert message received by the district administration from site emergency director of Kaiga Site at 6.30 a.m. on December 11, two radiation leak impact zones were created with L zone comprising of Hartuga, Goole, and Nagekove and M zone comprising of Kuchegar, Shirve, Keravadi and Devalamukki and the drill was carried out,” the release said.
Following the alert, an emergency meeting was chaired by the chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority and the Deputy Commissioner at 6.45 a.m. directing the officials to immediately take remedial measures.
Subsequently, villages impacted by the radiation leak were barricaded, an alert sounded, and an appeal was made to the public not to pay heed to rumours on social media after declaring a holiday for schools and colleges.
As part of the drill, transport officials arranged buses for ferrying the public to rehabilitation centres set up for the purpose. At the same time, health check-ups were conducted for residents of affected villages. Citizens, animals and vehicles coming out of the affected villages were de-contaminated and water and other materials and equipments used for decontamination were safely disposed of. By 2.10 p.m. an announcement to containing the radiation leak at Kaiga station was issued by the district administration and subsequent press release was issued for the information of the general public about the thwarting the danger.

title: Kerala local body polls: Powerful showing helps UDF shrug off the despondency of being out of power since 2016
summary: UDF's local body election success revitalizes hopes for 2026 Assembly victory, showcasing unity against Hindutva and local governance issues.
content:
A compelling showing in the local body elections appears to have helped the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) Opposition shrug off the despondency of having been shut out of government since 2016. The UDF also views the victory as a stepping stone to winning the Assembly elections in 2026. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s post on X reflected the party’s newfound optimism.
He thanked the Kerala electorate for the “decisive verdict” and expressed confidence that the UDF would “receive a similar mandate” in the Assembly elections. Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan, Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president Sunny Joseph, and All India Congress Committee general secretary K. C. Venugopal shared the sentiment with the journalists. Mr. Satheesan said the UDF’s emergence as a big tent accommodating varied social groups catalysed the coalition’s “best performance since the first elections for local bodies in 1995”.
He credited “Team UDF” for reasserting its political identity as the sole bulwark against Hindutva ascendancy by thwarting the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance’s (NDA) bid for electoral dominion, allegedly with Left Democratic Front (LDF) help, in several constituencies. Senior Congress leader Ramesh Chennithala termed the results a “victory of the people”. He said the UDF had regained its 2010 winning streak. However, he said the victory should not blind leaders to the challenges that lie ahead.
Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president Sunny Joseph, MLA, said the UDF fought a twin-pronged battle against the LDF and the NDA with a relatively depleted election war chest. The UDF defeated the LDF’s bid to diminish the Opposition through voter suppression, brazen electoral boundary manipulation, and covert tactical alliances with the NDA. Mr. Joseph said the UDF’s campaign, which spotlighted the Sabarimala Ayyappa temple gold theft as emblematic of the government’s disdain for personal faith, corruption, and nepotism, resonated strongly with the electorate. He accused the NDA of “slinking away” from the Sabarimala issue to maintain its tacit alliance with the LDF.
Mr. Venugopal accused the LDF of “gifting the mayoralty of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation” to the NDA. He stated that the LDF’s covert acceptance of the NDA’s anti-worker labour code and revanchist National Education Policy (NEP) had exposed its “true face” to Kerala’s secular-democratic electorate.
A Congress insider said the UDF’s leadership conclave in Sulthan Bathery in Wayanad early in the year laid the road map to the Opposition’s robust performance in the local body polls. It streamlined the candidate selection process, factoring in caste, religion, and age demographics alongside public appeal and leadership. Moreover, the UDF executed a boots-on-ground operation that prioritised doorstep conversations with voters.
Furthermore, the UDF prepared a region-specific ‘chargesheet’ against the government, emphasising local issues such as human-wildlife conflict, a cratering agrarian economy, and a decline in public service delivery, especially in health. At the same time, he said, the UDF presented a credible alternative to local body governance for people fed up with decades of LDF rule.
He said the UDF’s decision to suspend leaders accused of serial sexual predation put the onus on the LDF to do the same. “The LDF’s shortcomings in enforcing probity of leaders in public life resonated strongly with voters,” he added.

title: Rajahmundry airport conducts mock dry run of flight operations
summary: Rajahmundry Airport conducts a mock dry run to enhance flight operations efficiency during winter fog disruptions.
content:
The Airports Authority of India (AAI) on Saturday (December 13, 2025) conducted a mock dry run of flight operations at Rajahmundry Airport in view of the potential for flight delays and disruptions caused by fog during the ongoing winter season.
In an official release, Rajahmundry Airport Director N.K. Sreekanth said that the personnel from Air Traffic Control, India Meteorological Department, IndiGo Airlines, Alliance Air, Ground Handling Agencies (GHA) and Heligo Charters participated in the dry run.
Mr. Sreekanth stated that the dry run would be highly beneficial in ensuring safe, efficient and smooth handling of flight operations, even under adverse weather conditions in the future.

title: Parents association seeks action on student suicides in A.P.
summary: A.P. Parents Association demands urgent action on student suicides, urging the government to prioritize mental health and educational reforms.
content:
Schools and colleges should not become ranking factories but temples teaching life lessons, said the members of Parents Association of Andhra Pradesh (PAAP). Expressing concern over nine student suicides within six months of the new academic year in SPSR Nellore district, the PAAP members conducted a round-table meeting here on Friday.
The PAAP members demanded the Chief Minister to immediately respond to the matter, implement the Supreme Court orders and release a white paper on these tragic incidents. On the occasion, PAAP president S. Narahari said, “We must save our children’s lives from ranking factories. Of the nine suicides, seven took place in hostels or colleges affiliated to educational institutions.”
“PAAP strongly argues that there is a systemic crisis in the State that is costing the lives of our children. The government has failed to release any white paper on this. On July 25, 2025, in the Sukdeb Saha case, the Supreme Court bench declared the mental health of students as a right to life under Article 21 and issued 15 mandatory guidelines. However, the A.P. government has not followed it,” he added.
The PAAP members warned that if the Supreme Court’s orders were not implemented immediately, it would be forced to file a contempt of court petition against the State government to protect the rights of the students.

title: Man held for selling adulterated ghee in Secunderabad
summary: Man arrested in Secunderabad for selling adulterated ghee, risking public health and facing legal action.
content:
Acting on credible information, the Commissioner’s Task Force (North Zone), along with Market police, apprehended a man for allegedly manufacturing and selling adulterated ghee in the Second Bazar area of Secunderabad on Saturday (December 13).
The accused, Annamali Sainathan, 68, was taken into custody during a raid at his residence. Police said he was formerly running a tiffin centre near Monda Market and had turned to the illegal activity after discontinuing the business due to financial difficulties.
Investigators said that the accused was preparing spurious ghee at his residence by mixing plant based oils including coconut oil, palm oil and vegetable oil, along with food colours, and sold it as cow ghee. The product was packed in one litre poly packs and was supplied to local markets and pooja stores at ₹600 per kilogram, falsely claiming to be genuine.
Police seized around 200 kg adulterated ghee, a weighing machine, a packing machine, packing covers and a mobile phone, all valued at about ₹1.5 lakh. Officials said that the activity posed a risk to public health and amounted to cheating consumers for unlawful gain. Legal action is being initiated under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Act.

title: Class X girl dies of cardiac arrest in Konaseema
summary: A 15-year-old girl in Konaseema died of cardiac arrest during class, prompting an ongoing police investigation.
content: A 15-year-old girl reportedly died due to cardiac arrest during a class in a private school in Ramachandrapuram town in Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on Saturday (December 13, 2025). The incident occurred during the second class of the day at around 9.30 a.m. In video footage released by the police, the girl was seen falling from the bench. “The girl was declared brought dead at a local government hospital. Cardiac arrest is said to be the cause of death. A case has been registered and the investigation is on,” said Ramachandrapuram Circle Inspector M. Venkata Narayana.

title: 2025 local body polls: Congress-led United Democratic Front makes a comeback, LDF suffers setback
summary: In the 2025 local body polls, the Congress-led UDF returns to power while the LDF faces a significant defeat in Kerala.
content:
The ruling CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF) suffered a huge setback in the 2025 local body elections in Kerala with the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) making a strong comeback across Corporations, municipalities and panchayats in the State.
But the big story of the day was the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led NDA emerging as the single-largest front in the high-profile Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, winning 50 of the 101 wards in the LDF-ruled civic body.
Votes polled in the two-phased elections in Kerala on December 9 and December 11 were counted across multiple centres on Saturday.
Of the six Corporations, the UDF won four — Kollam, Kochi, Thrissur and Kannur, 505 of the 941 grama panchayats, 79 of the 152 grama panchayats, seven out of the 14 district panchayats and 54 of the 86 municipalities, according to the updates released by the State Election Commission (SEC) at 7.30 p.m.
The LDF, which held five Corporations in 2020, could win only Kozhikode this time. It also won 340 grama panchayats, 63 block panchayats, seven district panchayats and 28 municipalities.
The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation where it was the major Opposition during 2020-25, in addition to 26 grama panchayats and two municipalities.
The results in 75 local bodies were tied. This list included 64 grama panchayats, 10 block panchayats and one municipality. Other parties and Independents won in six grama panchayats and one municipality.
At the time of filing this report, the UDF held 9,015 of the 17,337 grama panchayat wards, while the LDF’s numbers dipped to 6,559. The BJP-led NDA won 1,444 grama panchayat wards, while 1,273 were won by others/Independents.
In the 2,267 block panchayat wards, 1,241 were won by the UDF, 923 by the LDF, 54 by the NDA-BJP and 49 by others/Independents. Of the 346 district panchayat wards, UDF claimed 171 and the LDF 109, NDA-BJP won one district panchayat ward and others/Independents, one.
In the 3,240 municipal wards, UDF won 1,458, LDF 1,100, the NDA-BJP 324 and others/independents 323. In the 421 Corporation wards, 187 were won by the UDF, 125 by the LDF and 93 by the BJP. 15 went to other parties/Independents.
While the UDF wave was felt across local bodies, the BJP visibly improved its positions in the urban local bodies, emerging as the top player in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation and as the main opposition party in several municipalities.
In the 101-ward Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, where 51 seats are needed for a majority, elections have been held only in 100 wards. The election to the Vizhinjam ward is awaited where it had been put off following the death of a candidate.
The LDF, which had had a clear upper hand in the previous elections held in 2020, has lost significant ground across local bodies this time.
Well-known names who scripted victories in 2025 included former Congress MLA Anil Akkara who won from Adat panchayat in Thrissur, Congress’s former MLA K. Sabarinadhan who won from the Kowdiar ward of Thiruvananthapuram Corporation and BJP candidate and former DGP R. Sreelekha who won from the Sasthamangalam ward of Thiruvananthapuram Corporation.
Prominent candidates who lost included the LDF Mayor of Kollam Corporation Honey Benjamin and former Mayor V. Rajendrababu, also of the LDF.
Newly-elected members/councillors will take the oath on December 21.
The outcome of the 2025 local body elections was keenly awaited given the fact that Kerala is readying for the State Assembly elections in 2026. The local body elections were held in two phases on December 9 and 11.
The combined voter turnout in the two phases had stood at 73.69% with 2,10,79,609 crore of the total 2,86,07,658 voters in Kerala’s 14 districts exercising their franchise.
The counting of the votes polled in the two-phased December 9 and December 11 elections were held across 244 centres on Saturday. Counting began with the postal ballots issued to the election officials at 8 a.m. The results were out in full by Saturday evening.

title: Police issue New Year eve guidelines for hotels, pubs and clubs
summary: Police issue New Year eve guidelines for hotels, pubs and clubs
content:
The Hyderabad Police on Saturday issued a set of guidelines for hotels, pubs, clubs, bars and restaurants planning New Year celebrations on the intervening night of December 31, 2025 and January 1, 2026, cautioning that violations would invite strict legal action.
Hyderabad City Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar said establishments rated three-star and above proposing ticketed programmes beyond midnight must obtain prior permission at least 15 days in advance.
He said organisers would be responsible for maintaining law and order, safety and public decency within their premises.
As per the directions, CCTV cameras with recording facilities must be installed at all entry and exit points as well as parking areas. Organisers have been instructed to deploy adequate security personnel for crowd control, parking management and traffic regulation, and to ensure that tickets or passes are not issued beyond the approved capacity of the venue.
Outdoor sound systems, including DJs and public address systems, must be shut by 10 p.m. in accordance with Supreme Court guidelines. Music is permitted beyond that time only within closed indoor premises and strictly up to 1.00 a.m., with noise levels not exceeding the prescribed limits.
The police have prohibited the use or display of fireworks and firearms at event venues. Organisers have also been warned to prevent obscenity in performances, ensure minors are not allowed into pubs and bars, and stop the consumption or sale of drugs or narcotic substances on their premises.
Managements have been directed not to serve liquor beyond the hours permitted by the Excise Department and to make arrangements for drivers or cabs for customers found to be intoxicated. Hotels, pubs and clubs have also been instructed to prominently display advisories on drunk driving, penalties under the Motor Vehicles Act, and the concept of a designated driver for the safety of patrons.

title: Aland vote theft case: Subhash Guttedar, son deny charges, call it ‘politically motivated’
summary: Subhash Guttedar and son deny vote theft charges, claiming political motivation behind allegations linked to Congress protests.
content:
BJP leader and former Aland MLA Subhash Guttedar and his son Harshanand Guttedar have rejected the charges levelled against them in the chargesheet filed by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing alleged voter fraud during the 2023 Assembly elections in Aland constituency.
Responding to the SIT naming them as prime accused, the father-son duo claimed that the move was politically motivated and timed to suit the Congress party’s “vote theft” narrative ahead of the planned agitation in New Delhi on Sunday.
Addressing the media in Kalaburagi on Saturday, the Guttedars said the chargesheet had been filed in haste.
“The elections were held in 2023, and B.R. Patil did not raise the issue of vote theft for two-and-a-half years. Only after Rahul Gandhi started speaking about ‘vote theft’ at the national level did Mr. Patil claim that it had happened in Aland as well,” Mr. Subhash Guttedar said.
He said he had already been cleared by courts in earlier cases where serious allegations had been made against him and expressed confidence of getting relief in the present case as well. He added that both he and his son had cooperated with the SIT and given statements, clearly stating that they had no role in any alleged voter deletion.
“Deletion of voters is a process governed by rules. Form 7 has to be submitted, Anganwadi workers forward it, and the tahsildar scrutinises it. It is not something that we can do on our own,” he said, denying any contact with those who had allegedly applied for voter deletion.
Asked about his next course of action, he said he would challenge the chargesheet legally and alleged that the move was aimed at preventing him from contesting future elections.
Echoing his father’s views, Harshanand Guttedar said an earlier inquiry by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had made no headway for nearly two years.
The SIT chargesheet followed an investigation into allegations of large-scale deletion and manipulation of voters’ names in Aland constituency during the 2023 Karnataka Assembly elections.

title: JSP leaders told to focus on membership drive in Srikakulam
summary: JSP leaders urged to enhance membership drive in Srikakulam to strengthen grassroots support and attract diverse community members.
content:
Jana Sena Party general secretary and MLC Konidela Nagababu on Saturday (December 13, 2025) asked Etcherla party in-charge Syed Vishwaksen and other leaders to focus on membership drive and enrol maximum number of members with an aim to strengthen the party at grass root level. He attended the party review meeting as the chief guest held at Laveru in Etcherla mandal of Srikakulam district.
Speaking on the occasion, he said that the people from all sections of society were being attracted towards policies of JSP and clean image of JSP president and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan. Mr. Vishwaksen thanked Mr. Nagababu for selecting Etcherla as the nodal constituency where the party would take up several activities in the next few months.

title: UDF sweeps 10 municipalities in  Ernakulam
summary: UDF wins 10 municipalities in Ernakulam, while NDA surprises LDF with Thripunithura victory in a tight race.
content:
The United Democratic Front (UDF) retained its supremacy in the majority of the municipalities in Ernakulam, while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) gave a shocker to the Left Democratic Front (LDF) as it won Thripunithura for the first time in a photo finish.
The UDF earned an impressive win in 10 of the 13 municipalities as it improved upon its performance in the 2020 local body polls, when it had won eight municipalities. Eloor municipality was the only relief for the LDF amidst the setback it faced in the district. It won the 32-member civic body by securing victory in 15 wards, while the UDF increased its tally from seven seats in 2020 to 12 seats this time. Four Independents will decide who will rule the Angamaly municipality as the LDF won 13 seats while the UDF bagged 12 seats.
The UDF won Aluva, Thrikkakara, Piravom, Perumbavoor, North Paravur, Muvattupuzha, Maradu, Kothamangalam, Koothattukulam, and Kalamassery municipalities.
Of the 13 municipalities, the UDF had won eight in the 2020 elections. It included Thrikkakara, Kalamassery, Muvattupuzha, Perumbavoor, North Paravur, Maradu, Aluva and Angamaly. The LDF had secured victory in Eloor, Koothattukulam, Kothamangalam, Piravom and Thripunithura municipalities. At the end of the term of the present council in 2025, the UDF increased its overall tally to nine municipalities after rebel Communist Party of India (Marxist) councillor Kala Raju helped the front wrest power in Koothattukulam municipality. The front retained Koothattukulam and wrested Kothamangalam and Piravom from the LDF this time.
A neck-and-neck race was visible between the NDA and the LDF in the Thripunithura municipality as the counting progressed. Though the Left front managed to secure a slight lead in the initial hours, the NDA surged ahead in the final phase to emerge as the single largest party with 21 seats. The LDF came a close second, with 20 seats, while the UDF improved its performance to 12 seats from the eight wards it had won in 2020.
Thripunithura was considered as the BJP’s biggest stronghold among the 13 municipalities in Ernakulam district. The party had served as the principal opposition in the temple town, dislodging the United Democratic Front (UDF) over the last two terms since 2015. The LDF’s tally came down to 21 from the 25 seats it had won in the previous election. The outcome came as a jolt to the front as the municipality was an LDF stronghold since its formation in 1978.

title: National Lok Adalat reunites estranged couples in Koppal
summary: National Lok Adalat in Koppal successfully reunites estranged couples, settling numerous matrimonial and civil cases on a single day.
content:
13-12-2025
Several estranged couples reconciled and decided to resume their married life during the National Lok Adalat in Koppal district on Saturday.
According to officials, 10 matrimonial cases were settled through mediation, with husbands and wives agreeing to resolve their differences. The settlements were achieved following counselling and guidance by mediators, advocates and judges. One of the notable cases involved a couple who had been living separately for the past 10 years but reunited on the advice of their respective lawyers, mediators and the presiding judge.
Apart from family disputes, many cases relating to insurance claims, water bills, bank loans, house tax, domestic violence, maintenance, cheque bounce, birth and death registrations, civil and criminal matters, motor vehicle accident claims and MMDR cases were also taken up
In courts across Koppal, Gangavati, Kushtagi, and Yelburga taluks, 6,764 cases were disposed of, out of a total of 8,613 listed on the day.
In pre-litigation matters relating to insurance, water charges, and motor accident claims, 72,591 cases were settled out of 79,305 taken up, involving a total settlement amount of ₹13.52 crore. Overall, 79,355 cases were disposed of, out of 87,918 taken up in a single day, with settlements amounting to ₹93.98 crore.
The Koppal District Legal Services Authority expressed its gratitude to the judges, advocates, litigants and mediator-advocates for their cooperation in achieving record settlements through amicable resolution during the Lok Adalat.

title: Law student arrested for injuring businessman with airgun during practice
summary: Law student arrested for injuring businessman with airgun during shooting practice in Bengaluru; investigation ongoing.
content:
Police arrested a law student for allegedly injuring a businessman during a practice session at his house in Basavanagudi in southern part of the city.
The accused has been identified as Mohammad Afzal, a resident of Basavanagudi. The police have seized three airguns from him, which he had allegedly purchased for shooting practice for sporting events.
The incident occurred on December 10 around 8 p.m., when the victim, Rajagopal D., who runs a restobar in south Bengaluru, was walking with a relative near K.R. Park.
According to the FIR, the victim heard a loud noise and then got hit on his neck. He later filed a complaint stating that he had been shot with an airgun.
A senior police officer overseeing the investigation toldThe Hinduthat the probe was challenging due to the size of the pellet, prompting investigators to pursue a two-pronged approach.
“We formed a team to identify stores that sell airguns in the city and examined data on people who had purchased such weapons in the locality. At the same time, we conducted ballistic tests to determine the distance and direction from which the pellet originated,” the officer said.
The ballistic test results indicated possible points of origin of the pellet, following which the accused was traced after questioning multiple individuals.
Preliminary investigation revealed that Afzal has been practising shooting for the past year, as he wanted to take part in shooting sports.
“He claims that he was practising at home and that he missed the target once, which led to the mishap. However, we are verifying his statement,” the officer added. Police are yet to identify the specific air gun allegedly used in the incident.
The Basavanagudi police have filed an FIR against Afzal under BNS Section 125 (act endangering life or personal safety of others) and relevant provisions of the Arms Act.

title: Gujarat couple, child trying to immigrate to Portugal kidnapped in Libya: Officials
summary: Gujarat couple and child kidnapped in Libya while attempting to immigrate to Portugal; ₹2 crore ransom demanded.
content:
A couple from Gujarat’s Mehsana district and their three-year-old daughter were allegedly taken hostage in Libya for a ransom of ₹2 crore while trying to immigrate to Portugal, officials said on Saturday (December 13, 2025).
Kismatsinh Chavda, his wife Heenaben and daughter Devanshi were kidnapped in the North African nation, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, en route to Portugal, where the man’s brother is settled, Mehsana Superintendent of Police Himanshu Solanki said.
He said that the family from Badalpura village in the district was travelling with the help of a Portugal-based agent with the plan to settle in the European country. The official said Mehsana Collector S.K. Prajapati has been informed about the incident.
The family took a flight to Dubai from Ahmedabad on November 29. From there, they were taken to Benghazi City in Libya, where they were kidnapped, Mr. Solanki said.
“[Mr.] Chavda’s brother is settled in Portugal, and he was travelling with the help of an agent based in Portugal. The family was travelling with the intention to settle there, and the agents involved in the case are not Indians,” Mr. Solanki said.
The official said that the kidnappers have contacted the relatives of the family in Mehsana, demanding ₹2 crore as ransom.
Collector Prajapati said that Mr. Chavda’s kin approached him on Friday (December 13, 2025), and that he has informed the State Government and the Ministry of External Affairs about their case.

title: TTD to grow trees for ‘Dwajasthambham’ in 100 acres
summary: TTD plans a 100-acre 'Divine Plantation' project to cultivate sacred trees for eco-friendly, Agama-compliant temple flag masts.
content:
The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) is considering a pioneering ‘Divine Plantation’ project over 100 acres of land to cultivate auspicious trees required for the ‘Dwajasthambham’, the holy flag mast, central to Agama-compliant Hindu temples.
TTD Trust Board Chairman B.R. Naidu said the initiative would ensure availability of ritually sanctified, home-grown timber for temples managed and established by the Hindu institutions.
The project, aligned with the vision of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, aims to blend ecological responsibility with preservation of ancient traditions.
As per Agama Shastra, ‘Dwajasthambhams’ must be crafted from a single, mature sacred tree such as teak, Indian kino, or select Shorea species, nurtured over decades and consecrated through prescribed rites.
By raising these ‘temple trees’ in its lands, TTD seeks to ensure Agamic purity, sustainability and self-reliance for future generations.

title: From red dawn to blue wave: UDF turns despair to dominance in a matter of hours in Kochi Corporation
summary: UDF transforms despair into victory, overtaking LDF in Kochi Corporation's election with a dramatic turnaround during counting day.
content:
The counting day put United Democratic Front (UDF) supporters in the Kochi Corporation through an emotional rollercoaster for the initial couple of hours.
From a sense of being doomed to turning the tables on the Left Democratic Front (LDF) in what promised to be a cliffhanger of a contest, and finally the sheer ecstasy of coasting easily past the simple majority mark, they experienced it all.
There was nothing to indicate what was in store as the postal ballots were taken up for counting. P.R. Ranish, the LDF candidate from the Konthuruthy division, was the first to take a lead, though it was immediately matched by the lead of the UDF’s Shiny Mathew from the Fort Kochi division, a lead she never surrendered throughout the counting. Then came a series of leads for LDF candidates in five more divisions in quick succession, followed by leads for two BJP candidates, even as the UDF’s lead remained restricted to just one division.
As it appeared that the LDF was off the blocks in a flash, the State Election Commission’s portal slowly but steadily turned red. With several prominent UDF leaders shown trailing, many news channels rushed to call an “LDF wave” in the Corporation.
At 8.45 a.m., the LDF led in 12 divisions, the UDF in four, and the BJP in two. Around that time, the first result was declared — UDF’s Antony Kureethara, who was the Opposition leader in the last council, lost to the BJP’s T. Padmakumari in the Island North division, and the writing seemed to be on the wall.
The UDF’s bright spots were the leads of its potential mayoral candidates, Deepthy Mary Varghese and V.K. Minimol, in the Stadium and Palarivattom divisions, respectively. However, the LDF continued to mount pressure, and at 9:12 a.m., it surged ahead in 24 divisions compared to the UDF’s nine, with the BJP holding leads in three, though the margins were negligible.
The UDF’s fightback coincided with the completion of postal ballot counting and the start of counting votes stored in electronic voting machines. The gap began narrowing, slowly at first, suggesting a neck-and-neck battle, and then rapidly, as almost all LDF candidates who were leading began to trail.
At 10 a.m., the numbers were tied at 32 each, and thereafter the LDF’s tally dropped at an alarming pace as the UDF surged ahead. Shortly thereafter, it became clear that it was indeed a UDF wave in Kochi.

title: Kerala local body polls: UDF makes inroads into Kottayam
summary: UDF gains control in Kottayam local body polls, winning 16 district panchayat seats and regaining power in two municipalities.
content:
Riding a strong anti-incumbency wave, the United Democratic Front (UDF) has made significant gains across Kottayam district, wresting control of a majority of local bodies.
The Congress-led coalition has won the district panchayat, secured a clear edge in most block and grama panchayats and raced on to power straightaway in two municipalities. In the 23 member district panchayat, the UDF surged to 16 seats, up sharply from seven in the outgoing council. In contrast, the Left Democratic Front’s (LDF) strength fell to seven from 14. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA), meanwhile, failed to retain its lone seat.
Of the six municipalities in the district, the UDF has returned to power in two and is well placed to form administrations in three more with the support of Independents. The verdict in the Pala municipality, however, remains inconclusive, with the UDF and LDF locked in a neck and neck contest with 10 and 11 seats respectively. Here, five Independents, including three belonging to a family driven political front, have emerged as key players who will decide the fate of the civic body.
In Kottayam municipality, the LDF suffered an unexpected setback, with several of its prominent candidates going down to defeat. Among them was Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) [NCP (SP)] leader Lathika Subash, who lost decisively to UDF candidate Susheela Gopakumar.
The BJP led NDA managed to seize power in three grama panchayats, including Aymanam and Poonjar Thekkekara, and improved its representation in Changanassery municipality. The coalition has also won four seats across the 11 block panchayats.
Out of the 71 grama panchayats in the district, the UDF increased its tally to 44 from 17, while the LDF now holds a clear majority in only 19, down from 51 in the previous term. Results in four panchayats remain hung. The BJP, which had focussed much of its campaign on grama panchayats, secured 122 representatives across these local bodies.
Among the municipalities, the UDF has registered clear victories in Kottayam and Ettumanur, while Independents will play a decisive role in Pala, Changanassery, Erattupetta and Vaikom. Though the Kerala Congress (M) failed to make significant gains elsewhere, it posted a strong showing in Pala, where 10 of the 19 candidates it fielded emerged victorious.

title: Kerala local body polls: UDF, NDA make dents in LDF’s strongholds in Alappuzha district
summary: UDF and NDA make significant gains in Alappuzha local body polls, reducing LDF's dominance in key municipalities.
content:
The United Democratic Front (UDF) made considerable gains in the traditional strongholds of the Left Democratic Front (LDF) in the local body polls in Alappuzha district.  The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) too improved its performance.
The UDF emerged as the single largest front in the Alappuzha, Kayamkulam, Haripad, Chengannur and Mavelikara municipalities. The NDA emerged as the dark horse as it surged ahead of the LDF to attain the second position in the Chengannur and Mavelikara municipalities.  The LDF’s victory was reduced to the Cherthala municipality alone this time. Besides Cherthala, it had won the Alappuzha and Kayamkulam municipalities in the 2020 polls. The Left front won 16 of the 24 divisions in the Alappuzha district panchayat. The UDF won eight divisions. In 2020, the LDF had won 21 divisions in the district panchayat.
Though it could manage a lead in the grama panchayats, the Left front’s performance slipped when compared to the 2020 polls as it could manage to secure only 36 seats this time. In 2020, the corresponding figure was 55. The UDF improved its performance to 23 seats from 12 in the previous election. The LDF won seven block panchayats as its performance dipped when compared to 2020 polls (11). The UDF improved its tally from one in the last election to four this time.
The UDF made significant strides in the five municipalities that it won this time. In Mavelikara, the front won 15 seats. The NDA pushed the Left front to the third position after it bagged victory in eight seats. The LDF could manage to win only four seats. The UDF retained power in the Chengannur municipality by winning 13 seats while the NDA came second here with six seats. The Left front bagged five seats.
Senior Congress leader Ramesh Chennithala congratulating UDF candidate Ajith Kumar for historic win in the Alappuzha municipality in the local body polls on Saturday. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Suresh Alleppey
In the Alappuzha municipality, the UDF emerged as the single largest front by winning 23 of the 53 wards. The LDF secured 21 seats while the NDA won in five. Four Independents, which included representatives of the Social Democratic Party of India and People’s Democratic Party, will play a key role in the formation of the new council. In the 2020 elections, the LDF had ruled the council with 35 seats while the UDF had won only 11 seats.
The UDF recorded an impressive win in the Haripad municipality after it won 16 seats. The LDF’s performance recorded a dip as it could manage to win only seven seats from 10 it had won in 2020. The Left front managed to retain control of the Cherthala municipality after it won 20 seats. The UDF won 10 seats while the NDA bagged victory in four seats.
The UDF wrested power from the LDF in the Kayamkulam municipality after it won 21 seats. The Left front, which had won 23 seats in 2020, was reduced to 13 seats this time. The NDA won five seats.

title: Semi-Christmas celebrated in Ongole
summary: Semi-Christmas celebrations in Ongole featured speeches on love and peace by local leaders at J.D. Seelam Bhavan.
content:
Semi-Christmas celebrations were organised under the auspices of the Democratic Journalist Forum at J.D. Seelam Bhavan premises in Ongole, on Saturday. City Mayor Gangada Sujatha participated as the chief guest, while TDP leader Raj Vimal and prominent lawyer Nukathoti Ravikumar participated as the special guests at the function.
Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Sujatha said, “The birth of Jesus was to save humanity from sin. He is considered as the personification of love, peace and service.” Meanwhile, Mr. Raj Vimal said that people believe in Jesus with utmost devotion and on the occasion of Christmas, prayers will be offered at every church along with devotional worship.

title: Will defeat BJP with the help of AI: Akhilesh Yadav
summary: Will defeat BJP with the help of AI: Akhilesh Yadav
content:
Hyderabad
Samajwadi Party (SP) president and former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav asserted that his party would make effective use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to defeat the BJP in the forthcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
Addressing the media on the sidelines of Vision India: AI Summit in Hyderabad, he said that the party was organising such summits across major cities to create awareness among youth on the use of technology in governance and the future transformation driven by technology.
Responding to questions on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls being undertaken by the Election Commission, he alleged that the BJP government was attempting to delete nearly three crore votes in Uttar Pradesh through the SIR process. Improper use of technology was resulting in the deletion of genuine voters’ names.
Accusing the BJP of misusing the SIR for electoral gains, he said the exercise was aimed solely at helping the BJP win elections in States like Uttar Pradesh. “This is not SIR, this is NRC in disguise,” he alleged, claiming that since the government could not implement the National Register of Citizens (NRC) directly, it was using SIR as an alternative.
Mr. Akhilesh Yadav underlined the need to effectively utilise AI technology in key sectors such as agriculture, infrastructure development, urbanisation, improved civic amenities in cities, traffic management and healthcare.
Expressing concern over the rise in cybercrime, he said that Uttar Pradesh records the highest number of cybercrimes in the country. He warned about the circulation of AI-generated fake videos on social media, stressing the urgent need to deploy AI itself to curb such threats. “Technology should benefit everyone,” he said.

title: Local body polls: BJP makes it three in a row in Palakkad municipality
summary: BJP retains control of Palakkad municipality, securing 25 seats despite internal conflicts and falling short of a majority.
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has retained control of the Palakkad municipality for a third consecutive term by securing 25 of the 53 seats in the municipal council.
The BJP secured 25 seats despite facing its biggest-ever internal feud. In the outgoing council, the party held 28 seats, while in 2015, when it came to power for the first time, it had secured 24 seats.
Though it fell short of a majority by two seats, the BJP being the party with the maximum number of councillors will continue to rule the municipality, as the UDF secured only 17 seats and the LDF eight. There Independents,  including a UDF rebel, also emerged victorious.
Any possibility of the LDF supporting the UDF or the UDF accepting LDF backing to dislodge the BJP in Palakkad appears highly unlikely as the two fronts are arch-rivals and such an arrangement would contradict their stated political positions.
The BJP won the Ayyapuram West, Kalpathy East, Thonippalayam, Kumarapuram, Mattumantha, Murukani, Puthur South, Puthur North, Sekharipuram, Ayyapuram East, Manappullikkavu, Koppam, Sulthanpetta, Mankavu, Kaikuthuparamba, Pattikkara, Vadakkanthara East, Selvapalayam, Kunnathurmedu South, Sreeramapalayam, Melamuri, Meparamba, Karnaginagar West, Vadakkanthara, and Jainamedu wards.
The UDF won the Olavakode Central, Kalpathy, Kunnumpuram, Kallepulli North, Kallepulli South, Narikuthi, Kunnathurmedu North, Chierakkadu, Kenathuparamba, Poolakkad, Vennakkara South, Vennakkara Central, Thirunellayi East, Thirunellayi West, Kallikkadu, Kottamaidanam, and Nurani wards.
The LDF won the Valiyapadam, Parakunnam, Vadakumuri, Civil Station, Murikavu, West Yakara, Yakara Central and the Othungode wards, while Independents claimed the Vithunni, Pallipuram and Olavakode South wards.
BJP State treasurer E. Krishnadas defeated UDF’s Vinod Pattikkara by 415 votes in the Pattikkara ward. Mr. Krishnadas, a former BJP Palakkad district president and the vice-chairperson of the outgoing municipal council, is being portrayed as a strong contender for the municipal chairperson’s post.
BJP district secretary P. Smithesh defeated Congress leader K. Bhavadas in the Murukani ward by 87 votes. In 2020, Mr. Bhavadas had won as a UDF rebel.
The Congress is lamenting the loss of several potential seats as well as key leaders, including Mr. Bhavadas and P.V. Rajesh. In the Koppam ward, Mr. Rajesh was defeated by BJP’s M. Sasikumar by 54 votes. A former municipal chairman, Mr. Rajesh’s seniority and experience were considered by the the Congress while fielding him.
The UDF cadres feel that allegations of sexual abuse against Palakkad MLA Rahul Mamkootathil negatively impacted the party’s prospects in the municipality. Many neutral voters were reportedly swayed away from the UDF due to the controversy surrounding the MLA. Moreover, several Congress workers believe that if he had worked with them while maintaining a clean image, the UDF could have achieved better results in the municipality.

title: The Hindu in School Science Fest and Ramanujan Spark Quest successfully concludes
summary: Over 400 students showcased their scientific and mathematical talents at The Hindu's School Science Fest in Madikeri.
content:
The Hindu in School Science Fest (Avishkar) and Ramanujan Spark quest, organised by The Hindu in School at Madikeri on December 13, evoked a good response as over 400 students from schools across Kodagu district showcased scientific curiosity and mathematical talent. They demonstrated their projects and innovations in science.
Speaking after inaugurating Avishkar-2025, Major Raghava B., principal, Field Marshal K.M. Cariappa College, advised children to stay away from gadgets as these are distractions, and urged them to focus on education, which, he said, was a tool to change society and the world.
He urged students to build their future by improving and developing their knowledge base and pointed out that taking part in such contests will help them think positively and develop a keen interest in science.
Underlining the need to promote creativity in science, he complimentedThe Hindufor giving a platform to the young minds to showcase their knowledge and talent.
Pushparaj, academic director of Excellent Moodubidire, the title sponsor for the event, called upon students to further improvise their projects. An orientation programme was also conducted for students on the occasion.
In the Science Fest, Tharun N.M. and Kajal of Kauvery School, Virajpet, won the first prize,  Likhith G.V. and Vijnan of General Thimmayya Public School won the second prize, and  Muthanna K.G. and Shrivathsa of Kauvery School, Virajpet, won the third prize.
In the Ramanujan Spark Quest, around 200 students from Classes 6 to 10 participated and five students from each class won prizes.
Class 6: First prize was won by Avin Ponannaof General Thimayya Public School, second prize by Hardhik Gowda H.P. of General Thimayya Public School, and third prize by Gaurav Krishnan P.S. of Kauvery School, Virajpet.
Class 7:First prizewas won byDakshith Gowda N. of Shanthinikethan School, second prize by Roshan Aarya C. of Udgam School, and third prize by Chalsie M.G. of Kauvery School, Virajpet.
Class 8: First prize was won by Deviea O.V. of Udgam School, second prize by Supreet Dev Tiwari of Kendriya Vidyalaya, and third prize by Rishith K.S of General Thimayya Public School.
Class 9: First prize was won by Nishanth S. Shetty, Udgam School, second prize by Bhoomika Bhojamma K.S., Kauvery School, and third prize by Aditri Ravikiran Kisan, General Thimayya Public School.
Class 10: First prize was won by Ayush Gowda, KALS, Gonikoppal, second prize by Shanthanu Aravind,  KALS, Gonikoppal, and third prize by Moulya Muthamma M.B., KALS, Gonikoppal.

title: CM, Dy. CM to participate in ‘vote theft’ protest in Delhi on Sunday
summary: CM Siddaramaiah and Dy. CM Shivakumar to join 'vote theft' protest in Delhi, highlighting concerns over 2024 Parliamentary polls.
content:
In the midst of ongoing talk on leadership change in Karnataka, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and his deputy D.K. Shivakumar will participate in the “vote chori” (voter theft) protest in New Delhi on Sunday.
According to official schedules, Mr. Shivakumar travelled to Delhi on Saturday, and Mr. Siddarmaiah would leave for Delhi on Sunday morning. Both leaders are expected to participate in the protest in the national capital against alleged vote theft during the 2024 Parliamentary polls.
The Congress began the protest against the “vote theft” campaign against the Election Commission of India at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on August 8.
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, who led a protest rally in Bengaluru, would take the lead in Sunday’s rally in Delhi. Agriculture Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy is expected to take a group of loyal legislators to Mr. Shivakumar to Delhi.
Close to 3,000 party workers and 30 legislators from Karnataka are expected to participate in the protest.
Mr. Shivakumar, who is also the KPCC chief, said Mr. Gandhi started the fight against vote theft in Karnataka. “We had exposed voter data theft back in the 2023 Legislative Assembly elections and lodged complaints with the Election Commission,” he said.
Speaking on the vote theft case in the Aland constituency ahead of the 2023 Assembly elections, which has now been chargesheeted by the SIT, he said MLAs will raise this in the Assembly session on Monday. “This is not just the voice of Karnataka but of the entire country”.

title: ‘I am an eight-time MLA, won’t be threatened,’ says DKS
summary: D.K. Shivakumar asserts his political strength amid threats, emphasizing his experience as an eight-time MLA in Bengaluru.
content:
Amid ongoing political speculation on leadership changes in the State, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said he was “not intimidated” by threats, asserting his political experience.
During his interaction with representatives of the Bangalore Apartments’ Federation (BAF) at Vidhana Soudha, he said, “I am an eight-time MLA and have gone to jail without fearing the Prime Minister or the Home Minister.”
This came in response to a letter Mr. Shivakumar read out, written to him by a citizen, cautioning him against neglecting apartment residents. The letter stated that apartment owners could influence the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) elections and alleged that successive governments had neglected their concerns.
Describing the tone of the letter as ‘threatening’, the Deputy Chief Minister said in an argumentative tone, “We are not intimidated. One must have basic common sense about who they are talking to. If I did not want to help, why would I have called people here and sought their feedback?”.
He referred to his electoral record, noting that his repeated victories reflected the trust and support of the people. “I have won eight times. That is the kind of love people have shown, and it reflects the faith and trust they have placed in me. I have been part of Bengaluru’s growth and development,” he said.
Following the Deputy Chief Minister’s comments, the Janata Dal (Secular) accused Mr. Shivakumar of ‘intimidating citizens and displaying arrogance unbecoming of a constitutional office-holder’.
The JD(S), on its official X handle, said questioning elected representatives was a democratic right and alleged that Mr. Shivakumar, as Deputy Chief Minister and Minister in charge of Bengaluru City Development, had threatened citizens from the stage.
“Such conduct did not bring credit to public representatives in a democracy,” the party said, adding that voters would respond appropriately at the polls.

title: DKS pitches Apartment Bill, seeks apartment residents’ support in GBA polls
summary: DKS proposes the Karnataka Apartment Bill to support residents, urging their involvement ahead of GBA elections amid Bengaluru's growth.
content:
The State government is planning to introduce the Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Management) Bill, 2025, to protect the interests of apartment owners and residents, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said on Saturday.
During the interaction with apartment owners and members of Bangalore Apartments Federation (BAF) at Vidhana Soudha, organised by the Urban Development Department, Mr. Shivakumar said the government was engaging with stakeholders to gather feedback ahead of finalising the proposed legislation.
He asked those who could not participate in the interaction to email their suggestions within 10 days.
Mr. Shivakumar said that the Bill was being brought at a time when Bengaluru had grown significantly, with nearly 19% of its residents living in apartments, and noted that no government had attempted to amend or overhaul the Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act, 1972, since its introduction.

The apartment representatives, during the meeting, raised concerns over the lack of clear transfer of ownership rights and undivided share of land from builders or promoters to apartment owners, delays in handover of completion certificates and documents, non-transfer of corpus funds, and ambiguity over the status of common areas and commercial spaces.
The participants also flagged the absence of a dedicated and time-bound dispute resolution mechanism for conflicts within associations, calling for clearer provisions on redevelopment and amalgamation of ageing apartment complexes, consolidation of governance under a single comprehensive law instead of multiple overlapping statutes, and greater use of technology to ease compliance.
Mr. Shivakumar also used the stage to seek the cooperation of apartment residents in the upcoming GBA elections.
“I am not expecting any praise or compliments for the work being done by the government.  I want to be remembered for being good to people. The government belongs to the people. I don’t want anything else but votes,” he said.

title: Accident victim gives fresh lease of life to five others
summary: K. Satheesh (55), a resident of Kowdiar and Principal, Government Higher Secondary School, Chembuchira, Thrissur, passed away on Friday in the capital, giving a new lease of life to five others.
content:
K. Satheesh (55), a resident of Kowdiar and Principal, Government Higher Secondary School, Chembuchira, Thrissur, passed away on Friday in the capital, giving a new lease of life to five others.
Satheesh had been seriously injured when the two wheeler he was riding was hit by a car near AG’s office on December 8. While undergoing treatment in a private hospital here, his brain death was confirmed on Friday, following which his family expressed the wish to donate his organs.
According to his wife, Mamatha, an official at the Government Secretariat, Satheesh had often expressed his wish to be an organ donor.
With the family taking the lead in donating his organs, the process was enabled and  coordinated by K-SOTTO. One of the kidneys went to an end-stage renal patient at Thiruvananthapuram Government  Medical College, while the second kidney and liver was transplanted in two patients suffering from end-stage organ failure at the private hospital where the brain death had been confirmed.
The cornea was retrieved by the Regional Institute of Ophthalmology for transplantation on two patients there
Health Minister Veena George while expressing her condolences, also thanked the family of Satheesh, including his wife and two children, for their noble gesture

title: Samiti urges government to establish red gram procurement centres
summary: Samiti urges government to establish red gram procurement centres and resolve crop compensation and insurance claims in Kalaburagi.
content:
The Zilla Raitha Horata Samiti has urged the State government to immediately establish red gram procurement centres in Kalaburagi district and address pending issues related to crop compensation and insurance claims.
Addressing a press conference here on Saturday, samiti members Avvanna Myakeri and Basavaraj Ingin welcomed the Centre’s decision to allow procurement of 9.67 lakh tonnes of red gram at minimum support price (MSP) through National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation (NAFED) and National Cooperative Consumers Federation (NCCF), to help farmers facing low market prices.
Mr. Myakeri said compensation of ₹8,500 to ₹17,000 per hectare under NDRF norms had been announced for crop damage across 3.24 lakh hectares, but the amount has not yet been credited. He urged the Centre to immediately release the compensation.
The samiti also demanded settlement of ₹307 crore in pending crop insurance claims for about 1.2 lakh farmers for 2024–25, and early release of insurance claims for the current season, for which farmers have already paid premiums.
Responding to the issue of sugarcane price, the samiti members accused the State government of going back on its assurance. They said that although a price of ₹3,300 per tonne was announced by the State government following farmers’ protests, sugar factories in Kalaburagi district had earlier agreed to pay ₹3,160 per tonne. However, farmers are now being paid only around ₹3,000 per tonne, which would result in heavy losses. The samiti demanded that the government immediately fix the sugarcane price at ₹3,160 per tonne for the district.

title: LDF activist in Kerala loses bet, shaves off moustache
summary: LDF activist Babu Varghese shaves his moustache after losing a bet following UDF's victory in Pathanamthitta municipality elections.
content:
The UDF victory in the Pathanamthitta municipality on Saturday cost an LDF worker his moustache.
Babu Varghese, an LDF activist, had struck a bet with his friends during the campaign that he would shave off his moustache if the LDF failed to retain power in the civic body. With the UDF emerging victorious, Mr. Varghese stayed true to his word and adopted a clean-shaven appearance.
Taking the outcome in good spirit, Mr. Varghese said the elections often throw up surprises. “What mattered to me was keeping my promise,” he remarked, adding that losing the moustache was simply part of honouring a wager made in the heat of political banter.

title: Sittilingi: a tribal valley’s inspiring success story
summary: Discover how Sittilingi transformed from high infant mortality to health equity through community-driven initiatives and dedicated healthcare professionals.
content:
The tribal hospital in Sittilingi valley in Dharmapuri district
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                N. Bashkaran
On a misty Monday morning in the Sittilingi valley, nestled snugly between the Kalvarayan and Sitheri hills in western Tamil Nadu, people trickled into a stone compound of single-level structures made of sundried bricks, Mangalore-tiled roofs, and arched windows.
The earthen structure, resembling a village retreat, is a tribal hospital providing secondary healthcare facilities in one of the remotest parts of Tamil Nadu, about 45 km from the block headquarters of Harur in Dharmapuri.
Among the visitors that day was Revathi. She had brought her mother from Navakollai, 20 km away, as she has been doing for the last 10 years, bypassing the primary health centre just 5 km from her village.
“I’ve never seen anything like this place anywhere. They take women’s problems seriously. The doctors take time to listen and explain, spending at least 15 to 20 minutes with a patient. Even in private hospitals, doctors don’t listen to our complaints,” she says.
Sometime in 1993, a young couple in their early 30s, both clinicians from Gandhigram, arrived in the tribal valley of Sittilingi with a dream: to be doctors in a place where they were needed, where no other doctors had gone until then.
This dream would take shape as a 35-bed tribal hospital and give birth to the Tribal Health Initiative (THI), a community health programme (CHP) that would overturn Sittilingi’s abysmal infant mortality numbers within a decade, and go on to radically redefine the scope of health beyond the clinical, extending it to the social and economic determinants of well-being over the three decades since.
Gynaecologist Lalitha Regi and anaesthetist Regi George chose Sittilingi because of its geographical isolation, which has limited access to care as in all tribal areas, and its appalling infant mortality rate (IMR) – 147 babies per 1,000 live births – at the time.
If the couple conceptualised a CHP, the level of morbidity and mortality called for a different kind of action.“There was so much morbidity that we needed to address that first,” says Dr. Lalitha. They took over aporambokeland, where locals helped put up a one-room mud-and-thatch structure. “For three years, deliveries and some surgeries took place under a 100-watt bulb, on a bench.”
Dr. Regi George and Dr. Lalitha Regi, founders of the Tribal Health Initiative
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                 N. Bashkaran
Then came, through ActionAid, a 10-bed hospital and a centre to train locals to look after themselves. “The belief then, as it is now, was that any planning and resources had to come from here, not from outside,” adds Dr. Lalitha.
Early November this year, the McGill School of Population and Global Health named the Regis co-recipients of the prestigious Paul Farmer Award for Global Health Equity. The citation described their achievements as “countering the failures of imagination” and “having lived a life of accompaniment”.
Building from the ground up
The couple’s first health worker was a Class 8 passout Rajamma, who joined the hospital as a trainee in 1994. “We went to the villages asking for educated girls to help us at the hospital,” says Dr. Lalitha.
But the State’s all-pass-up-to-Class 8 curriculum, meant that young girls like Rajamma could read alphabets but not words or full Tamil sentences. Therefore, their training began with basic language and arithmetic before progressing to anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, diagnosis, and treatment.
“Diagnosis focused on the diseases prevalent in this area, nothing extra. What they would see, how they would diagnose and treat…” added Dr. Regi. “That’s why we called them health workers, because they were much more than nurses.” Similarly, they trained lab technicians and an accounts team. Much was improvised as there was no money. The hospital’s first autoclave was a pressure cooker. “We had to make do with what we had for all sorts of emergencies, because people couldn’t go anywhere,” adds Dr. Regi.
Health auxiliaries
“We were seeing people only when they came to the hospital. There was no one to see what was happening in the village. So, we asked each village to select one person free of child-rearing responsibilities.” Twenty-one villages had sent 25 women, who would become trained health auxiliaries, and go on to form the backbone of the community health programme.
The first goal was to tackle infant mortality. Since malnutrition, respiratory diseases, and diarrhoeal diseases accounted for a high proportion of under-five deaths in most places, health auxiliaries were trained to focus only on these, through nutrition management, malnutrition prevention, early detection and treatment of respiratory diseases, recognising symptoms of pneumonia, and safe delivery practices.
“In the villages, skilled mothers did home deliveries. The health auxiliaries would monitor home deliveries and bring them to the hospital in case of an emergency,” says Dr. Lalitha.
Women crafting garments in Sittilingi valley under the Tribal Health Initiative
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                N. Bashkaran
By 2003, the IMR dropped to 60, and further declined to 20 by 2008, when even the Tamil Nadu average was 35 and the national average, 53. Today, Sittilingi’s IMR stands at 8.
Maadeshwari’s life changed after one such village meeting in 1998. She had completed only up to Class 8. When the hospital came up, she knew she wanted to do something there. “Seeing my teachers and Dr. Lalitha, I too wanted to be like them and achieve something in life.”
She wrote her SSLC examinations and joined the hospital as a health worker trainee. She was trained in deliveries, surgeries, out-patient and operation theatre. “Initially, one of us (trainee) would faint at the sight of blood. But, Dr. Lalitha and Dr. Regi trained us patiently, showing us each step – from the mother’s arrival to the delivery and beyond.”
Then came another big step.
Focus on farming
At the Sittilingi Organic Farmers Association (SOFA), one of the 700 organic farmers registered with the offshoot of the THI peers into a laptop camera. “This seeding of biometric data is for the certification of the organic produce from the particular farmer’s land,” says Manjunath, coordinator of SOFA and one of the earliest community members of the THI.
“In 2003, we carried out an external evaluation of the THI,” says Dr. Lalitha. “Among the observations was that if we want to achieve what we did with the IMR, there are other social, economic, and political determinants of health, like food, employment, and income [we should consider]. Unless you address the economy of the people, you cannot tell them what they should eat.”
“There were many complaints — schools not functioning, poor roads, transport, and water. But one consistent issue was that farming was at a loss, yet it was the only thing they knew,” explains Dr.Regi.
Farmers were initially resistant to organic farming, fearing losses. But after two years of talks, four farmers took it up, and soon, the initiative spread. SOFA was formed, which today represents 700 organic farmers in the Sittilingi Valley. Sittilingi’s organic produce, including millets, turmeric, pulses, and a variety of millet-based products such as biscuits and savouries, is now a regular feature in organic stores.
Reviving a lost art
In subsequent years, the THI’s focus on the local economy deepened. The Sittilingi panchayat also includes two Lambadi villages and one Dalit village. “I noticed that the rich craft of Lambadi embroidery had died because nobody wore that attire anymore,” Dr. Lalitha said.
A little probing led her to Neela and Gammi, two women in their seventies who had learnt the craft from their grandmothers. “They wore sarees, and their mothers wore sarees, but their grandmothers were the last to wear the Lambadi attire,” she said.
