This was followed by 7.9°C in Sirpur (Kumaram Bheem Asifabad), 8.6°C in Moinabad (Rangareddy), 8.7°C in Bheempoor (Adilabad), 9.1°C in Akbarpet (Siddipet), 9.8°C in Nizampet (Medak) and Bantwaram (Vikarabad) and 10°C in Pembi (Niraml).
The remaining 25 districts recorded temperatures ranging between 10°C and 14°C. In Urban pockets, Uppal in Medchal Malkajgiri recorded a minimum temperature of 10.8°C followed by Maredpally in Hyderabad recording 12°C.

title: Singareni Collieries, Altmin to collaborate for battery-grade lithium refinery in Telangana’s Hyderabad
summary: Singareni Collieries and Altmin partner to establish India's first large-scale lithium refinery in Telangana, targeting 2027 operations.
content:
Singareni Collieries Company (SCCL) and Hyderabad-based Altmin have signed an Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to set up India’s first large-scale battery-grade lithium refinery inTelangana, Hyderabad.
The proposed project envisages an investment of ₹2,250 crore and the establishment of a 30,000 tonnes per annum lithium carbonate refinery in Telangana. The refinery is targeted to commence operations by 2027 and poised to play a strategic role in supporting India’s rapidly growing electric vehicle and energy storage ecosystem. It will position the State at the forefront of India’s critical minerals and clean energy transition, Telangana Government said in a release on Monday (December 15, 2025) on the MoU that was signed in the presence of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy at the recently concluded Telangana Rising Summit in Hyderabad.
The Telangana Rising Global Summit 2025 concluded today with Hon'ble Chief Minister Shri@revanth_anumulaunveiling the#TelanganaRising2047, a people - led roadmap aimed at transforming Telangana into a $1 trillion economy by 2034 and a $3 trillion economy by 2047.The Chief…pic.twitter.com/vVVxgEzK3g
Under the partnership, SCCL, which is jointly owned by the government of Telangana and the Government of India, and Altmin will form a joint venture to localise lithium refining in India and bring globally benchmarked technology into the country. The project also includes plans to secure long-term raw material supply through overseas mineral assets, strengthening India’s energy security and significantly reducing dependence on imported refined lithium.
It will be the first of its kind project in India establishing large-scale, domestic refining capacity for battery-grade lithium, a critical mineral that is central to electric vehicles, energy storage systems and the clean energy transition. “By localising lithium refining within the country, the initiative will significantly reduce India’s dependence on imported refined lithium, strengthen national energy security and support the rapid expansion of India’s electric vehicle (EV) and advanced battery manufacturing ecosystem,” the government said.
“Telangana is committed to building the backbone of India’s clean energy economy. This lithium refinery marks a decisive step towards making India self-reliant in critical minerals and advanced battery technologies,” Mr. Reddy said. The proposed initiative is expected to act as a catalyst for the development of an integrated battery manufacturing ecosystem in Telangana, attracting downstream investments in cell manufacturing, advanced materials and clean mobility technologies, while creating substantial employment opportunities and high-end technical capabilities in the State.
The State Government said it will support the project with facilitation of approvals, infrastructure support and ecosystem coordination, measures that will reaffirm Telangana’s vision to emerge as India’s leading hub for new energy, advanced manufacturing and strategic industries.

title: Kerala local body polls 2025: Special elections on January 13 in three postponed wards
summary: Kerala's special elections for three local body wards are set for January 13, 2025, following candidate deaths.
content:
The special elections to three local body wards in Kerala where the 2025 local body elections had been put off on account of the death of candidates will be held on January 13, State Election Commissioner A. Shajahan said on Tuesday. The polled votes will be counted on January 14.
The election notification will be issued on Wednesday.
Elections to the Payimbadam ward, Moothedam grama panchayat in Malappuram district, Onakkoor ward in Pambakkuda grama panchayat in Ernakulam, and the Vizhinjam ward of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation had been postponed following the death of candidates.
Nomination papers can be filed till December 24. Their scrutiny will be held on December 26. December 29 is the last date for the withdrawal of the nominations.
Existing candidates in these wards need not file nomination papers again, the commission said.
Although the SEC had withdrawn the model code of conduct in the State with effect from December 15, it remains in effect in the whole of the Moothedam and Pambakuda grama panchayats and in the case of Vizhinjam, which is a Corporation ward, within the ward boundaries.

title: ‘Noise pollution’ by azaan triggers debate in Karnataka Council
summary: Karnataka BJP members debate noise pollution from azaan, urging government action during the Legislative Council session in Belagavi.
content:
Alleging thatazaan, the call to prayer in mosques, causes ‘noise pollution’, members of the BJP urged the government of Karnataka to take action as per the Supreme Court’s direction, during Question Hour in the Legislative Council in Belagavi on December 16.
BJP member D.S. Arun, who raised the question, stated that he and his family members had been disturbed by the regularazaanfrom a mosque close to his place in Shivamogga. “The volume of loudspeakers in mosques has gone up in recent days. The Congress government has no guts to take action against people using loudspeakers at mosques,” he remarked, triggering a heated debate.
C.T. Ravi, Bharathi Shetty, N. Ravi Kumar, and Keshava Prasad of the BJP demanded that the government implement the rule strictly to avoid noise pollution. They alleged that the government, which banned the use of DJ music during the Ganesha festival, had allowed loudspeakers in mosques, which operate throughout the year.
The members in the treasury benches accused the BJP members of politicising the issue.
Minister for Environment and Forests Eshwar Khandre stated that the rules are the same for all. The government of Karnataka had constituted district-level committees to test noise levels at religious places where loudspeakers were being used. The committee would include ACP or the DySP, the Executive Engineer of the urban local body, and a representative from the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board. The committee would take action whenever there was a complaint, he said.
The Minister said that his department had issued an order insisting that loudspeakers should be used only between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. The Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rule, 2000, specified the maximum decibel levels with respect to sensitive areas, residential areas, commercial areas, and industrial areas. Violation of the rule would attract punishment. “We need to spread awareness among the public about noise pollution,” he added.

title: Kerala seeks withdrawal of ‘VB G RAM G’ Bill replacing MGNREGS
summary: Kerala urges the Union government to withdraw a Bill replacing MGNREGS, citing threats to livelihoods and state finances.
content:
Kerala has demanded that the Union government withdraw the new Bill introduced in Parliament to replace the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MNREGS), as the proposed legislation is “nothing short of a declaration of war against the ordinary people of the country, jeopardising their livelihoods”.
Kerala would be one of the most adversely affected States if the proposed legislation is allowed to become a law because it puts an annual additional liability of ₹1,600 crore on the State, Minister for Local Self-Governments department M.B. Rajesh told reporters here on Tuesday (December 16, 2025).
The proposed legislation completely negates the core principles of the employment guarantee programme and represents a total abdication of the Centre’s responsibility of providing employment and shifts 40% of the expenditure burden onto the States, he said
The MGNREGS is a flagship programme launched by the UPA government to provide up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households willing to undertake unskilled manual work. Implemented in Kerala since 2006, the scheme has been vital for poverty alleviation, providing livelihoods to thousands of families.
Mr. Rajesh claimed that in the last ten years, the BJP-led Union government has been systematically attempting to weaken the scheme by withholding wages, allowing large arrears to accumulate, and by reducing the number of workdays. The arrears due to Kerala now stands at ₹826.9 crore, he said.
Mr. Rajesh said that several provisions in the new Bill undermines States’ interests and the concept of employment as a right. He said the new Bill is dictated by targets and budgets fixed by the Centre instead of being driven by demand, while at the same time it absolves the Centre of all responsibility.
According to the new Bill, the Centre will fix State-wise normative allocations for each financial year and any expenditure beyond that will have to be borne by the States. The Centre will no longer be obligated to reimburse additional person-days generated, effectively abolishing the right to work.
The change in the funding pattern – from a fully Centrally-sponsored scheme to a 60:40 Centre-State shared Budget – will place a huge burden on States like Kerala, Mr. Rajesh said. With an average annual expenditure of ₹4,000 crore, Kerala will now have to bear 40% — around ₹1,600 crore — under the new provisions, amounting to economic strangulation by the Centre.
Central assistance to Kerala has also been declining steadily. So far this year, Kerala has received only ₹2,928.34 crore under MGNREGS, he said.
He said that the promise to increase work days from 100 to 125 is hollow because the Bill clearly states that this increase in work days is applicable only to rural areas that the Centre notifies. Given the urban nature of many of the grama panchayats in the State, Kerala is likely to lose out on that count too.
The new name of the proposed Bill – Viksit Bharat Guarantee For Rozgar And Ajeevika Mission (Grameen), shortened as VB G RAM G – does away with the name of Mahatma Gandhi. While this change in name is objectionable, the government is more worried about the provisions in the Bill that could end the livelihood of lakhs of families, especially women, in Kerala, Mr. Rajesh said.
The original scheme provided for compensation and allowance if work could not be guaranteed and the new Bill while retaining these clauses, pushes the entire responsibility of compensation to the States.
Mr. Rajesh said that the National Democratic Alliance (NDA)’s alliance partners have already expressed their apprehensions about the scheme. Kerala appealed to the State’s Members of Parliament to jointly take up the fight against the new Bill.

title: Heads and deputy heads of local bodies in Kerala to be elected on December 26 and 27
summary: Local body elections for heads and deputy heads will take place on December 26 and 27, as announced by the SEC.
content:
The heads and deputy heads of the local bodies will be elected on December 26 and December 27, the State Election Commission said on Tuesday (December 16).
The chairpersons and Mayors of municipalities and corporations, respectively, will be elected at 10.30 a.m. on December 26. Deputy chairpersons of municipalities and Deputy Mayors of Corporations will be elected at 2.30 p.m. on the same day.
The presidents of grama, block and district panchayats will be elected at 10.30 a.m. on December 27. Vice-presidents will be elected on the same day at 2.30 p.m. In the case of Corporations and district panchayats, the District Collectors are the Returning Officers. In the grama and block panchayats, the Returning Officers concerned are the nominated officials.  Returning Officers have been specially assigned for municipalities.
One member/councillor has to propose a candidate and another member has to second it. If the nominated member is not present, his written consent has to be produced. A member cannot propose or second multiple nominees. The name of a member who is contesting to a reserved post need not be proposed or seconded.
If there are multiple contestants for a post, the election will be held via open ballot. Members who cast their votes are required to enter their names and affix their signatures at the back of the ballot. If there is only one candidate, he or she will be declared elected without voting.
The quorum of the election meeting is at least half of the elected members of the local body concerned. If the quorum is not met, the election will be put off to another working day. In this case, it will not be insisted that the quorum is met.
If there are only two candidates, then the person who has secured more votes would be declared elected. In the event of both candidates securing an equal number of valid votes, the winner will be declared through a draw of lots. The person whose name is drawn first will be declared elected.
If there are more than two candidates, the process is a little more complex. If one of the contestants secure more votes than the other two combined, he/she will be declared elected. If no contestant secures that many votes, the contestant who secures the least votes will be removed and the election continued. This process will continue until a candidate secures more votes than the all others combined.
If there are three or more candidates and the lowest votes are secured equally by two or more candidates, a draw of lots will be held and the person whose name is drawn will be eliminated.
Elected members/councillors who have not taken the oath or affirmation are not eligible to vote.
Members/councilors are required to cast their vote by marking an ‘x’ against the candidate of their choice. After writing their own name and affixing the signature, the members should put the ballot in the box/tray kept near the Returning Officer.
If the elections are held in multiple phases, ballots of different colours will be used in each phase.
Once the elections are over, Mayors, chairpersons, presidents will take the oath before the Returning Officer. Deputy Mayors, vice-chairpersons and vice-presidents will take the oath respectively before the mayors, chairpersons and presidents.
The SEC had announced that newly-elected members and councillors of local bodies will take the oath or affirmation on December 21.
The members of the Wandoor block panchayat will take the oath  on December 22. The five-year-term of this block panchayat does not get completed on December 20. The members of the Chokkad grama panchayat will take the oath on December 26. The presidents and vice-presidents in these local bodies will be elected on December 31.

title: KSRTC nets record ticket collection of ₹10.77 crore
summary: KSRTC achieves a record ticket collection of ₹10.77 crore, driven by increased passenger patronage during the Sabarimala pilgrimage.
content:
Riding high on increased passenger patronage during the Sabarimala pilgrimage season, the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) netted a record daily ticket revenue (operating revenue) of ₹10.77 crore on December 15, 2025. Considering the non-ticket revenue of ₹76 lakh during the day, the total revenue for the day is estimated at ₹11.53 crore.
The coordinated efforts of the KSRTC management, employees, supervisors and officers have helped the KSRTC post a new benchmark in the daily collection of the public utility, said a statement here on Tuesday (December 16, 2025). The public utility also achieved this by improving its operations efficiency without increasing the ticket fare.
Transport Minister K.B. Ganesh Kumar highlighted that recent reforms by KSRTC have significantly advanced its goal of self-sufficiency. The introduction of new buses and improved services have been well-received by passengers.

title: Tiger dies after getting caught in snare in Kodagu
summary: Tiger dies in Kodagu snare, prompting urgent action from officials to remove traps and raise awareness among local residents.
content:
A tiger died after getting caught in a snare at a plantation in Kodagu district, triggering concern among forest authorities.
The incident occurred at Srimangala, near the Nagarahole forest. Following the incident, Minister for Forest, Ecology and Environment Eshwar Khandre chaired an emergency meeting in Belagavi on Tuesday to review the situation. He spoke to forest officials in Mysuru district and issued instructions.
In the wake of the tiger death, Mr. Khandre directed forest officials to create awareness among the people living along forest fringes and educate them on the legal consequences of wildlife deaths caused by such snares.
The Minister instructed officials to form teams across all forest ranges and conduct regular searches for illegal traps along forest boundaries. He further directed that strict legal action be initiated against those responsible for the tiger’s death.
Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Head of Forest Force Meenakshi Negi, Chief Wildlife Warden P.C. Ray, Principal Secretary Manoj Kumar, and other senior officials were present at the meeting.

title: Bengaluru police arrest woman in Chittoor for theft on Tiruvannamalai-bound bus, jewellery worth ₹7.5 lakh seized
summary: Bengaluru police arrest a woman in Chittoor for stealing ₹7.5 lakh in jewellery from a bus passenger.
content:
The Parappana Agrahara police in Bengaluru have arrested a woman and seized gold and silver jewellery worth ₹7.5 lakh in connection with the theft of ornaments from a bus passenger travelling from Bengaluru to Tiruvannamalai in Tamil Nadu.
According to the police, the accused was traced and arrested in Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh on December 12, following an investigation based on a complaint by a Koramangala resident. During the arrest, officers recovered around 70 grams of gold and 22 grams of silver jewellery from her.
The complaint, lodged on November 24, stated that the incident occurred a day earlier when the complainant boarded a bus from the Madiwala bus stand with gold and silver ornaments in her handbag. “While the bus was en route to Tiruvannamalai, a woman passenger allegedly dropped some coins on the floor. When the complainant bent down to pick them up, the woman was suspected to have taken advantage of the distraction to steal jewellery from the victim’s bag,” an official said.
The complainant later realised that about 80 grams of gold and 22 grams of silver were missing and approached the police.
Based on the complaint, the police launched an investigation, tracked the suspect, and arrested her. The accused has since been released on bail, the police said, adding that further investigation is under way.

title: Prakash Veer interview: On working with Darshan and making ‘The Devil’
summary: Kannada filmmaker Prakash Veer talks to The Hindu about making ‘The Devil’, starring Darshan, fondly called ‘D Boss’ by his fans.
content:
Kannada filmmaker Prakash Veer talks to The Hindu about making ‘The Devil’, starring Darshan, fondly called ‘D Boss’ by his fans. The actor is currently in prison for the alleged murder of Chitradurga resident Renukaswamy. The movie has got a grand response in the opening week and the director opens on the controversy, the challenges of pulling off a film with multiple hurdles, the reason behind Darshan’s immense stardom and the issue of online trolling of movies and actors.

title: West Bengal Sports Minister Aroop Biswas resigns over chaos at Lionel Messi’s event at Salt Lake stadium
summary: West Bengal Sports Minister Aroop Biswas resigns amid chaos at Messi's event, prompting government inquiries into police conduct.
content:
West Bengal Sports Minister Aroop Biswas on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) resigned over the chaos at Lionel Messi’s event at Salt Lake stadium on December 13.
Mr. Biswas tendered his resignation to Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee who accepted the Minister’s request.
“As per the enclosed letter, I appreciate the sentiment and intention of the Sports Minister to offer a relief from the Sports Department for the sake of impartial inquiry into the Vivekananda Yuva Bharati Krirangan (VYBK) incident on 13th December, 2025,” a letter signed by the Chief Minister said.
Ms. Banerjee added that Mr. Biswas “is correct (to resign) and until and unless the impartial inquiry is over, the Sports Department will be looked after by me for the time being”.
Violence had erupted at Salt Lake Stadium on December 13 as football fans vandalised the stadium after Lionel Messi’s brief appearance. Organisers of the event including the Minister surrounded Lionel Messi and the spectators who bought tickets at a hefty price were enraged after being unable to find a glimpse of the football icon.
The State government also issued show cause notices to top officials like Director General of Police Rajeev Kumar, Bidhannagar Police Commissioner Mukesh Kumar and Principal Secretary of Youth Affairs and Sports department Rajesh Kumar Sinha.
A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been constituted with Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) Jawed Shamim, ADG South Bengal Supratim Sarkar, Director (Security) Peeyush Pandey and Barrackpore Police Commissioner Muralidhar.
Additionally, the government suspended Bidhannagar DCP Aneesh Sarkar and initiated departmental proceedings against the officer.
On December 13, the State government set up an enquiry commission led by Justice (retd) Ashim Kumar Ray.

title: Watch: ‘VB-G RAM G’ Bill will weaken MGNREGA: Priyanka Gandhi

She accused the government of undermining Gram Sabhas, shifting away from demand-based funding, and reducing the Centre’s financial responsibility. The Congress also staged a protest holding Mahatma Gandhi’s photographs, demanding the Bill be withdrawn and sent for wider consultation.

title: Bombay High Court reserves order on PIL seeking CBI probe into Lavasa project
summary: Bombay High Court reserves judgment on PIL demanding CBI probe into alleged irregularities in the Lavasa project involving the Pawar family.
content:
A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Justice Gautam Ankhad on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) reserved its order on a criminal public interest litigation (PIL) seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities in the Lavasa hill station project in Pune district.
The PIL, filed by advocate Nanasaheb Vasantrao Jadhav, names former Union Minister Sharad Pawar, Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar, and Baramati MP Supriya Sule, among others, alleging the grant of illegal permissions, misuse of public resources, and large revenue losses through stamp duty exemptions and land allotments.
Appearing in person, Mr. Jadhav argued that the petition was maintainable despite earlier proceedings. He told the Bench, “The PIL had not been dismissed earlier, but was only held to be mis-constituted, and therefore remained maintainable,” citing the Supreme Court’s ruling inState of Uttarakhand vs. Balwant Singh Chaupalto stress that “genuine PILs raising issues of public importance should not be rejected on technical grounds.”
The petitioner also relied on judgments inState of West Bengal vs. Committee for Protection of Democratic RightsandSubrata Chattoraj vs. Union of Indiato argue that High Courts have wide powers under Article 226 to direct a CBI probe in cases involving serious allegations and failure of local agencies.
The petition alleges that permissions under Section 63(1A) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act were illegally granted to Lavasa Corporation for purchasing agricultural land, despite there being no provision for hill station development at the time. It claimed the scam was “preplanned” and involved Yashomala Leasing and Finance Pvt. Ltd. merging with Lavasa Corporation without mandatory permissions, allegedly under Sharad Pawar’s influence.
The PIL states that Supriya Sule and her husband Sadanand Sule received shares in Lavasa following the merger, while Ajit Pawar, as Irrigation Minister and Maharashtra Krishna valley Development Corporation (MKVDC) chairman, approved leases and permissions that violated statutory norms.
The PIL claimed that the Lavasa project, spread across 18 villages in Mulshi and Velhe talukas, has remained unresolved for over a decade, during which farmers lost their livelihoods as agricultural land became unfit for cultivation. It stated that compensation paid to farmers was inadequate and that, with the right to property no longer being a fundamental right, vulnerable landowners had little legal recourse.
The petitioner also highlighted that complaints filed since December 2018 with Pune Police and Pune Rural Police were not acted upon. “Replies under RTI stated the matter did not fall within their jurisdiction,” Mr. Jadhav said, adding that local agencies failed to act for nearly five years, leaving him with no option but to seek court directions for a CBI probe.
Citing a Comptroller and Auditor General report and a People’s Commission of Inquiry report, the petitioner alleged losses running into hundreds of crores. The PIL claims that notifications issued in 2001 and 2002 allowed Lavasa to avoid paying crores in stamp duty, despite the project being commercial in nature.
It further alleged that about 141.15 hectares of MKVDC land were leased to Lavasa for 30 years without tenders, and permissions were granted to construct eightbandharasin the Mose valley. The Urban Development Department allegedly appointed Lavasa as a Special Planning Authority under the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, which the PIL described as “first of its kind” and contrary to law. The petitioner stated that this SPA status was later withdrawn by the BJP–Shiv Sena government in 2017, acknowledging that the appointment was irregular.
To justify maintainability despite delay, the petitioner argued that “crime never dies” and citedJapani Sahoo vs. Chandra Sekhar Mohanty, stating that mere delay cannot defeat criminal proceedings. The PIL also seeks directions for the case to be tried in a fast-track CBI court and for periodic status reports to be filed before the High Court.
The court also considered two intervention applications but indicated that it was not inclined to allow them at this stage. One application, filed by Sharad Pawar, sought impleadment, arguing that the petitioner suppressed facts and that the PIL was barred by constructive res judicata. Mr. Pawar’s plea stated, “The entire premise on which the complaint is filed has been adjudicated upon in 2018 and is also in issue before the Supreme Court by way of an SLP. Therefore, the present petition styled as ‘Criminal PIL’ is not maintainable.” The application added that he is “neither a proposed accused nor an accused and has every right to be heard before any order is passed.”
Another application by Mursalin Shaikh invoked Section 340 of the Criminal Procedure Code, seeking initiation of prosecution against Mr. Pawar for perjury and deliberate contempt, alleging that he filed a false and misleading affidavit to mislead the judiciary. The application cited multiple IPC provisions and the Contempt of Courts Act and sought exemplary costs along with prosecution.
The matter has been reserved for judgment.

title: Opposition’s forest, mining claims trigger Assembly uproar in Chhattisgarh
summary: Opposition protests in the Chhattisgarh Assembly over alleged deforestation and mining claims
content:
Congress MLAs created a ruckus in the Chhattisgarh Assembly on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) after their demand for a discussion on alleged rampant mining and deforestation was disallowed by the Speaker.
The Opposition legislators alleged that the State’s Vishnu Deo Sai-led Bharatiya Janata Party Government was working for the benefit of industrialists and capitalists.
Moving an adjournment motion notice, Congress members claimed that areas such as Surguja, Hasdeo Aranya coalfields, Tamnar and Bastar were witnessing mass protests and road blockades, alleging that fake public hearings were being conducted for the approval of coal mines.
The Congress alleged that unprecedented deforestation was being witnessed in the Tamnar area in Raigarh, and large-scale felling of trees was allegedly taking place on forest and revenue land.
Citing Hasdeo Arand—often referred to as the ‘lungs of Chhattisgarh’— the Opposition MLAs said that deforestation in the region has already led to loss of lakhs of trees, and poses serious threats to biodiversity, water resources and elephant corridors. They warned that continued deforestation could intensify human-elephant conflict and worsen water scarcity.
The adjournment motion statement also said “there are widespread instances of fraudulent public hearings, public protests, lathi-charges, sit-ins, and road blockades”.
Responding to the allegations, Forest and Climate Change Minister Kedar Kashyap said the Vishnu Deo Sai Government was sensitive towards forests, wildlife, tribals and the environment, and was committed to their protection and conservation, even as he rejected claims of fake public hearings, protests and lathi-charges.
He cited the Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun, to claim that Chhattisgarh’s forest cover had increased by 94.75 sq km, while the area under ‘trees outside forests’ had risen by 702 sq km, the highest in the country, he said.
Mr. Kashyap said that over the past two years, only five mining cases involving 1,300.869 hectares of forest land had been diverted under the Forest (Conservation) Act, strictly in accordance with rules and after obtaining approval from the Central Government. He also refuted claims of large-scale deforestation and quoted tree-felling figures way lower than those claimed by the Opposition. He added that compensatory afforestation was being carried out in all forest land diversion cases.
After the Minister’s reply, Speaker Raman Singh disallowed the adjournment motion notice, and Congress members started sloganeering against the government. They then trooped in the Well of the House, following which the Speaker announced the suspension of 30 Congress members. The suspension was revoked by the Speaker a few minutes later.

title: Declared ‘dead’ in draft rolls, Trinamool councillor walks into crematorium, demands own last rites
summary: Trinamool councillor Surya Dey, listed as 'dead' in voter rolls, demands last rites at a Kolkata crematorium, highlighting electoral absurdity.
content:
A Trinamool Congress councillor on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) walked into a crematorium near Kolkata and demanded that his last rites be performed, claiming that the Election Commission of India (ECI) listed him among the “dead” in the draft electoral rolls.
A booth-wise list of the deceased and migrated voters was released ahead of West Bengal's draft electoral rolls earlier in the day.
Surya Dey, the Trinamool councillor of Dankuni Municipality's Ward 18, said that while checking the lists linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, he claimed his name figured among the "dead", though he had filled and submitted his enumeration form to the booth-level officer.
"Since the Commission has declared me dead, it should complete the process," Dey told reporters as he walked into Kalipur crematorium, flanked by supporters. "Let the officials come and cremate me." 	He called this administrative absurdity with serious consequences.
"I am an elected public representative. If I can be shown dead on paper while I am very much alive, imagine what can happen to ordinary voters," he said.
He held Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar responsible for what he termed a "conspiracy" behind the deletion.
Mr. Dey asserted he had complied with every procedural requirement under the SIR, submitting forms and documents during the enumeration drive.
"Despite that, I have been struck off. This is not a clerical error; this is dangerous," he alleged.
Also Read |ECI publishes draft electoral rolls in Bengal; over 58 lakh names deleted under SIR
The episode quickly travelled from the crematorium to social media.
TMC spokesperson Arup Chakraborty, in a Facebook post, said, "Dankuni Municipality Ward 18 councillor Surya Dey, resident of Chanditala Assembly constituency. Serial number 40, Booth number 226. According to the voter list on Tuesday, he is dead. Is this SIR or a farce?”
The ECI has not responded to the specific allegation.
The incident comes on a politically charged day, with the ECI on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) publishing West Bengal's draft electoral rolls following the Special Intensive Revision exercise, deleting over 58 lakh names on grounds ranging from death and migration to duplication and non-submission of enumeration forms.
According to official data, 58,20,898 names were excluded, reducing the electorate from 7.66 crore to 7.08 crore after the SIR process conducted between November 4 and December 11.
The deletions have affected several high-profile Assembly segments and sharpened political fault lines, setting the stage for the contentious verification and hearing phase ahead of state elections due early next year.
Standing at the crematorium, the TMC councillor underlined the point he wanted to remember, even if the rolls had erased him.
"I walked here myself," he said. "I am breathing, talking, protesting. If this is how voters are being treated, democracy itself is being taken to the pyre."

title: M.B. Patil for revision of UDAN scheme to help flight operations
summary: M.B. Patil calls for a revision of the UDAN scheme to extend concessional airfares and sustain regional flight operations.
content:
Minister for Infrastructure Development M.B. Patil has stressed the need for extending the benefit of the concessional airfares under the UDAN scheme for at least seven to 10 years, from the existing three years, to sustain the flight operations in regional areas.
Answering a question by member Thippannappa Kamakanur, on stopping the flight service between Kalaburagi and Bengaluru, the Minister said that the service had been stopped due to the decline in demand from passengers.
Under the UDAN scheme, the flight operators enjoy the benefit of concessional airfares for three years. The benefit extended to the airline expired in March 2023. However, the operator continued the services up to October 15, 2025, when the last flight took off. “We have been demanding that the Centre extend the UDAN benefits for more years; otherwise, many airports will stop functioning in the coming years,” he stated.

title: ACB nabs Deputy Executive Engineer in Osmania University
summary: ACB nabs Deputy Executive Engineer in Osmania University
content:
A deputy executive engineer working in Osmania University was arrested by the Anti Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Tuesday after he was trapped while accepting a bribe of ₹6,000.
The accused was identified as Rakonda Srinivasulu, Deputy Executive Engineer in the Osmania University Building Division, on the university campus, in Tarnaka.
According to the ACB, the accused allegedly demanded a bribe of ₹11,000 from the complainant for releasing pending bills amounting to ₹7.37 lakh related to renovation works carried out in Maneru Boys’ Hostel on the university campus. The bribe was also sought to ensure that no obstacles were created in future contract works of Osmania University. Officials said the accused had earlier accepted an initial bribe amount of ₹5,000 through a digital payment application.
During the trap, the accused allegedly accepted part payment of ₹6,000, which was recovered at his instance.
The accused was arrested and produced before the special court for SPE and ACB cases in Nampally. The case is under investigation, and the identity of the complainant has been withheld for security reasons.
The ACB reiterated that people can report bribe demands by public servants through the toll-free number 1064 or via its official social media platforms, assuring confidentiality to complainants.

title: Kerala Legislature International Book Festival from January 7
summary: Join the Kerala Legislature International Book Festival from January 7-13, featuring 200 publishers, renowned authors, and vibrant cultural events.
content:
The Kerala Legislative Assembly is all set to host the fourth edition of the Kerala Legislature International Book Festival (KLIBF 4) from January 7 to January 13, 2026, on the Assembly premises here.
Making the book festival, which has garnered international attention, a landmark cultural and intellectual event this year, a bevy of literary and cultural programmes has also been arranged.
Entry to the seven-day festival is free. During the festival days, visitors will also have the opportunity to tour the Assembly hall and the Legislative museum. More than 200 publishers will participate in the book festival, with over 250 stalls being set up. Renowned writers, journalists and socio-cultural activists of national and international repute, including Taslima Nasrin, Rana Ayyub, Chulaananda Samaranayake, Prafull Shiledar, Zaira Shah Haleem, and Banu Mushtaq, will take part in the festival, alongside a large number of popular and celebrated Malayalam writers.
The festival will feature book launches, book discussions, panel dialogues, interactions with authors, interviews, and lectures, spread across six different venues, making the event intellectually vibrant and culturally rich. A specially designed Students’ Corner will host interactions between eminent personalities and students. Puppet shows, magic shows, and children’s programmes will add charm and excitement to the Students’ Corner. Book launches and discussions organised by publishers will take place across three venues on the Assembly premises.
A model legislative Assembly, aimed at familiarising students with the functioning of the Legislature, will be conducted at the Old Assembly Hall in the Secretariat building.
A special highlight of this year’s festival will be the performance of Theyyam, a traditional ritual art form of north Kerala, scheduled from January 8 to January 12, offering visitors a unique cultural experience. Colourful mega shows in the evenings, a food festival showcasing Kerala’s culinary diversity, and opportunities for readers to obtain autographs from their favourite authors will further transform the book festival into a grand celebration in the capital city, according to organisers here on Tuesday.

title: Telangana moves Supreme Court with plea to restrain Andhra Pradesh on PBLP
summary: Telangana petitions the Supreme Court to halt Andhra Pradesh's illegal Polavaram project activities, citing violations of inter-state agreements.
content:
HYDERABAD
The Telangana government on Tuesday filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court seeking directions to restrain Andhra Pradesh and its agencies from proceeding with the preparation of a detailed project report (DPR), taking up the process of tenders and execution of the Polavaram-Banakacherla/Nallamalasagar Link Project (PBLP/PNLP).
In the petition, it has also prayed to prevent A.P. from going ahead with the plans of associated capacity expansions of Polavaram project and also stop regulating agencies such as the Central Water Commission, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Ministry of Environment, Forests & Climate Change, Polavaram Project Authority, Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards from appraising the pre-feasibility report and DPR of the PNLP.
Further, it has requested the Apex Court to direct the agencies concerned from granting clearances and approvals and releasing funds for the impugned project PNLP and unapproved expansions of Polavaram project, pending a lawful and inter-State complaint process. A.P.’s plans of taking up PNLP and Polavaram project expansion is in violation of binding Tribunal Awards and AP State Reorganisation Act, the Telangana government stated in the petition.
Against the approval for diversion of 80 tmc ft water from Polavaram project to Krishna river through the former’s canal system for use in the Krishna Delta, the A.P. government was expanding the project infrastructure to carry an additional 200 tmc ft water further intended to increase it to 300 tmc ft a year to Krishna river and beyond through PBLP/PNLP without any approvals, the petition explained.
The petition brought to the Supreme Court’s notice that A.P. has already undertaken the Polavaram expansion for PNLP and thereafter submitted its pre-feasibility report to CWC. Without even waiting for the CWC’s consent, a prerequisite to prepare DPR as per existing guidelines and despite instructions of CWC not to take up DPR, A.P. has floated tenders, completed technical bids and taken up financial bids on December 17.
Telangana has further brought to the Apex Court’s notice through the petition that the appraisal of PFR of the impugned project based on flood waters by the CWC is itself contrary to the guidelines of CWC and MoJS. “The petition is about enforcement of the binding Award of GWDT as the executive actions of A.P. are in violation of the same and it’s not a water dispute and it’s purely legal to be taken up by the court”, Telangana prayed.
The MoJS and CWC have already sensitised A.P. against its illegal actions but the latter is vehement in its illegalities and it warrants judicial intervention as neither the PPA nor GRMB, having authority to injuct/prohibit A.P. from proceeding with the illegal action, are acting and forced Telangana to move the Apex Court, Telangana said in the petition.

title: Jagan demands CBI probe into Joji Nagar demolition
summary: Jagan Mohan Reddy demands a CBI probe into Joji Nagar demolition, alleging high-level involvement and legal violations affecting 42 families.
content:
Former Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) demanded a CBI inquiry into “the role of people in high positions involved in the demolition of houses at Joji Nagar in Vijayawada” and assured the ‘victims’ of legal help.
Speaking to the media here, Mr. Reddy expressed solidarity with the victims of Joji Nagar stating that their houses were demolished despite court order giving them relief up to December 31. He said all those involved in the demolition would be brought to book.
The YSRCP chief alleged that Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, HRD Minister Nara Lokesh, local MP Kesineni Sivanadh and local Jana Sena corporator were behind the demolition and said that 42 families residing in the colony spread across 2.17 acres of land valued at ₹150 crore were deprived of their homes despite the fact that they had all the permissions and were paying EMIs.
He said that overlooking the fact that the case was pending in the Supreme Court and the residents had relief up to December 31, the demolition was executed in the presence of heavy police presence. Mr. Reddy alleged that fake documents were created during Mr. Naidu’s previous tenure and a bogus society was registered with a back date in 2016 and the litigation was created only to hand over the prime land to private players.
YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy interacting with the families whose houses were demolished at Joji Nagar.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K.V.S. GIRI
Mr. Reddy said only a CBI inquiry would bring out the facts and the behind-the-scenes operations. He further said that his party would extend all possible legal help to the locals, who were residing there for the past 25 years. He said that the YSRCP would sort out these issues and initiate stringent action against those responsible for the demolition when the party comes to power in the State.
Alleging gross misuse of power in the State, the YSR Congress Party chief questioned how permissions were given if the ‘victims’ did not own the land. He accused the TDP of encroaching lands
He said encroachment of land through prolonged litigation had become a deliberate pattern under TDP rule in the State with the party leaders and cadre systematically occupying lands by misusing legal processes, creating disputes to delay justice and ultimately grabbing public and private property. “Such actions reflect a complete disregard for the rule of law and people’s rights,” he said.

title: I will continue as CM until high command decides, declares Siddaramaiah in Legislature
summary: Siddaramaiah asserts his commitment as Chief Minister until a decision from the high command, confident in Congress future success.
content:
The leadership issue in the ruling Congress figured in the Assembly session on Tuesday, with Chief Minister Siddaramaiah stating on the floor of the Assembly that he would continue as the Chief Minister until the high command made a decision. He emphasised that Congress regime will continue for the full five-year term “as the people of the State have blessed it”.
“I am the Chief Minister. I want to clearly say that we have a high command and we will abide by whatever it decides. Secondly, people of the State have blessed us to rule for five years, and we will continue to rule for five years,” the Chief Minister asserted, while replying to Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok who raised the issue during the Question Hour.
Taunting the Chief Minister for his diplomatic stand, BJP member S. Suresh Kumar said, “So far the Chief Minister would say that he would continue in his post for five years. But now he has switched to the plural by replacing ‘I’ with ‘We’,” he said, adding that it reminds him of St. Kanaka Dasa’s famous lines on shedding egoism and selfishness.
Responding to this, the Chief Minister asked the BJP not to compare him with the great saint-poet. Continuing to emphasise the choice of plural, he said, “We are running the government and hence I am using the plural”.
He asserted that the Congress government would not only complete the full term, but also return to form the government by winning the 2028 Assembly polls.
The Chief Minister launched a counterattack on the BJP by remarking that it had formed the government twice despite not getting the people’s mandate. “People of the State have never blessed the BJP, and they are not going to do it in the future either. In fact, your numbers in the Assembly is going to further dwindle in the next polls,” he told the BJP members.
When BJP members continued the taunt and asked whether the Congress high command had “blessed” him just as the people of the State, the Chief Minister reiterated, “We will abide by whatever the high command decides”.
Irritated by the continued questioning, he said, “All the 140 Congress MLAs are with us, and they would not get provoked however much ever your try”.
The issue unfolded after Congress member H. D. Ranganath, identified with Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s camp, alleged during Question Hour that there was a disparity in allocation of funds by the Co-operation Department (earlier headed by K.N. Rajanna, who has been at loggerheads with the Deputy Chief Minister) to his constituency when compared with Madhugiri (represented by Mr. Rajanna). Soon after, the Chief Minister assured him of setting right anomalies, if any, by next year. Mr. Ashok remarked in a lighter vein that, “Dr. Ranganath is anguished, and he is performing pooja to ensure that Mr. Shivakumar becomes Chief Minister”.
Responding to this, Mr. Siddaramaiah told him to desist from stoking the fire. Hinting that Mr. Siddaramaiah was evolving strategies to protect his chair, Mr. Ashok said he was planning to write a book titled “Siddaramaiah’s strategies” on the lines of “Chanakya’s strategies.”

title: Around 16 Maoists detained in a remote tribal village, once hotbed of naxal activity, in Kumram Bheem Asifabad district
summary: Police detain 16 Maoists in Pedaldoba village, once a naxal stronghold, in Telangana's Kumram Bheem Asifabad district.
content:
Around 16 Maoists from Chhattisgarh were reportedly detained by police in Pedaldoba village of Sirpur (U) mandal, once hotbed of naxal activity, in Telangana’s Kumram Bheem Asifabad district in the early hours of Tuesday.
The exact identity of the underground cadres of the banned outfit was not immediately known.
Acting on specific inputs, a special party police team led by Asifabad ASP S. Chitharanjan raided a thatched house at Pedaldoba, a remote village in the tribal mandal near the inter-State border with Maharashtra in the wee hours of the day.
The police detained around 16 Maoists and shifted them to the district headquarters, sources said.
The police are trying to establish the identity of the detained Maoists and the reason for their arrival in the interior tribal village along Telangana’s border with Maharashtra.
The movement of underground Maoist cadres in the remote tribal hamlet comes at a time when there is a spurt in surrender of Maoists operating in the Dandakaranya forest region spanning parts of Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.

title: Development of IFFCO Kisan SEZ will provide 30,000 direct, 40,000 indirect jobs: Nellore Collector
summary: The IFFCO Kisan SEZ in Nellore aims to create 30,000 direct jobs and boost industrial growth with ₹870 crore investment.
content:
All eyes are fixed on the IFFCO Kisan SEZ (IKSEZ), spread across 2,776 acres in Nellore district, following the State Cabinet’s recent approval to develop infrastructure in the zone with an investment of ₹870 crore.
The decision has rekindled hopes of industrial revival in the region, which has a huge potential to tap the agrarian market by attracting industries and as well provide local employment.
Part of the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC), the multi-product Special Economic Zone (SEZ) is spread across 1,900 acres and the Domestic Tariff Zone (DTZ) spans 877 acres, which is well connected with railway network, highway network (NH 16), seaport and airport.
According to District Collector Himanshu Shukla, the development of the SEZ will provide 30,000 direct and 40,000 indirect jobs, besides creating 29,400 new jobs, if more industries set up base. Three major firms have already shown interest to establish units and signed MoUs, while many more are in the pipeline, according to sources.
It may be recalled that Nellore MP Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy had met the Indian Farmers Fertilisers Cooperative Limited (IFFCO) Chairman Dileep Sanghani and the then Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Udai Shanker Awasthi a couple of times this year to moot industrial development in the region.
Currently, Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy and Hindustan Coco Cola Beverages (HCCB) Limited have their plants here.
However, for reasons unknown, the number of industrial units remain grossly incommensurate to the availability of facilities like compound wall, uninterrupted power supply, sewage treatment plant, storm water drains, internal roads and security.
The latest proposal to create amenities with an outlay of ₹870 crore is expected to fill the gap and pave the way for rapid industrialisation in the Nellore-Kavali belt.

title: Two arrested, over ₹23 lakh recovered in investment fraud
summary: Two arrested, over ₹23 lakh recovered in investment fraud
content:
Two men from Mumbai were arrested by the cybercrime wing of the Hyderabad police in connection with an investment fraud that duped a Hyderabad citizen of over ₹23 lakh. The accused, identified as Dharmesh Jaswantbhai Barot, 35, and Mohd Shahid Hanif Ansari, 38, orchestrated the scam through fake stock trading platforms and fraudulent WhatsApp groups.
The case came to light following a complainant on August 9, 2025, in which the victim stated that she was lured into joining a WhatsApp group claiming to provide expert trading tips. The accused used FaerPE trading app to induce her to trade in “Block Deals,” initially allowing small withdrawals to gain trust before freezing her total investment under the pretext of a “T+2 settlement period.”
Investigation revealed that the accused manipulated fake dashboards and profit charts to appear professional. “Dharmesh targeted Rapido bike taxi drivers, including Shahid, promising commissions of up to ₹10 lakh in exchange for their current bank accounts. These accounts, including Shahid’s Naira enterprises RBL account, were used as conduits to layer and siphon off the cheated money, making the trail difficult to track,” said Hyderabad Cyber Crimes DCP V. Aravind Babu.  Police seized two mobile phones connected to the operation.
Meanwhile, the Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police have urged citizens to remain cautious of fake investment schemes, invest only through SEBI-registered brokers and verified platforms, and report any cybercrime immediately via the helpline 1930.

title: Fake ACB officers arrested
summary: Police arrest four fake ACB officers for extorting ₹2 lakh from the Registrations and Stamps Department in Vijayawada.
content:
The police on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) arrested a four-member fake Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) gang that allegedly extorted ₹2 lakh from the Registrations and Stamps Department registrar.
The gang, including a woman, called Mogalturu Sub-Registrar S. Srinivas on November 12 this year and introduced themselves as ACB police from Vijayawada. They threatened to conduct a raid, file criminal cases, and demanded that ₹2 lakh be transferred through UPI.
Acting on a complaint, the team led by West Godavari district Superintendent of Police Adnan Nayeem Asmi and Narsapuram DSP G. Sriveda arrested the fake ACB officials at the parcel office at Vijayawada railway station in the wee hours on Tuesday.
The accused were identified as N. Jaya Krishna, V. Ramanjaneyulu, Vanitha and P. Tharun, natives of Anantapuram district, the police said.

title: MBA, BBA students get hands-on marketing experience at Vizianagaram trade fair
summary: MBA and BBA students gain practical marketing skills through direct consumer interactions at Vizianagaram's mega trade fair.
content:
Students from MBA and BBA programmes gained practical hands-on experience in sales and communication through direct interaction with consumers at the mega trade fair held in Vizianagaram from December 14 to 16.
Centurion University of Technology and Management (CUTM), and Satya Institute of Technology and Management (SITAM) deputed their students to interact with consumers as part of practical exercise to improve their marketing skills
CUTM students N. Kavya Sri and Keerthi Priya said that it provided a great opportunity to convince customers to buy products from local shops instead of online e-commerce portals.
CUTM vice president D .N. Rao said that live interactions would help students gain confidence and prepares them  to perform well during campus interviews. Sivva Jagganna Chetty Hardware Company Managing Director Sivva Jagan said that trained marketing staff was the need of the hour for business houses.
The three-day mega trade fair is organised by the Vizianagaram Business Entrepreneurs Association.

title: Centre nod to 100-bed ESIC hospital at Shamshabad
summary: The Centre has approved a 100-bed ESIC hospital at Raikunta in Shamshabad mandal, clearing ₹16.125 crore land acquisition, Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy said.
content:
The Centre has approved the construction of a 100-bed ESIC hospital at Raikunta village in Pedda Golkonda, Shamshabad mandal, with the Ministry of Labour & Employment clearing land acquisition worth ₹16.125 crore during the 197th ESIC meeting held last week, informed Union Minister of Coal & Mines G. Kishan Reddy on Tuesday.
At present, there are over 1.32 lakh ESI-insured workers within the Ranga Reddy district. In accordance with the large-scale industrialisation taking place in and around the Hyderabad airport at Shamshabad and across the district, the number of workers is expected to increase in the coming days. Hence, it was decided to have a new hospital.
Mr. Reddy expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for "accelerating the access to quality medical infrastructure" and also to Union Minister of Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The ESIC super specialty hospital located at Sanathnagar is already providing corporate-level medical services to workers having ESI insurance.  Apart from this, ESI hospitals are functioning at Nacharam, Ramachandrapuram, Sirpur Kagaznagar, and Warangal areas, said a press release.

title: Set up foundation in the name of Chennanna Walikar, writers and academics urge State
summary: Writers and activists in Kalaburagi urge the State to establish a foundation honoring revolutionary poet Chennanna Walikar.
content:
Writers, academicians and social activists who gathered in Kalaburagi on Tuesday to observe the sixth death anniversary of noted revolutionary poet Chennanna Walikar urged the State government to establish a foundation in his name, headquartered in Kalaburagi.
Speaking at the commemorative programme organised at the Government First Grade Degree College and Postgraduate Centre (Autonomous), senior writer and Karnataka Sahitya Academy member Siddarama Honkal said that Chennanna Walikar was among the most powerful rebel voices in the Kannada literary tradition who consistently articulated the pain and struggles of the most marginalised sections of society.
“The State government has established the Siddayya Puranik Pratishtan in Koppal and the Basavaraj Kattimani Pratishtan in Belagavi to promote the study of works by those writers. Chennanna Walikar’s literary contributions, which are equally significant, have been ignored. The State must establish a foundation in his name in Kalaburagi, his home district,” Mr. Honkal said in his inaugural address.
Senior writer Swamirao Kulkarni, presiding over the event, said that sustained efforts are being made to press the State government to recognise Walikar’s contribution through a dedicated foundation. He pointed out that although the State has set up 27 foundations in the names of prominent literary and social figures, only one, the Siddayya Puranik Pratishtan, is located in the Kalyana Karnataka region.
“This does not mean the region lacks literary giants. It has many. Yet, successive governments have neglected them. This reflects a continued indifference towards Kalyana Karnataka,” he said and added that Walikar’s writings played a crucial role in raising consciousness among oppressed communities and inspiring resistance against exploitation and injustice.
Principal of a Pre-University College and a member of the Kannada Pustaka Pradhikara, B.H. Niragudi, who was the chief guest, drew attention to what he described as persistent factual errors in school textbooks regarding Walikar’s life. He said that despite repeated representations, incorrect information about the poet’s birthplace continues to appear in textbooks.
Chennanna Walikar was born and raised in Shankarawadi village near Shahabad in Kalaburagi district. However, textbooks initially mentioned Raichur district. After repeated objections, this was changed to another incorrect reference stating that he was from Chittapur taluk of Yadgir district. Students across the State are still being taught this wrong information, he said.
Mr. Niragudi said that efforts are under way at the Kannada Pustaka Pradhikara to bring out the collected works of neglected writers from the Kalyana Karnataka region.
“As part of this initiative, we are publishing the collected works of Chennanna Walikar, Shantarasa and Geetha Nagabhushan,” he said.
Delivering a special lecture, principal of the Government First Grade Degree College, Kamalapur, Amrita Kataka described Walikar as a rare writer who redefined literary engagement. Born into economic hardship and social marginalisation, she said, Walikar’s poems powerfully captured themes of discrimination, injustice, oppression and exploitation.
“His writings did not merely describe suffering. They urge the oppressed to resist injustice and work towards a more humane and egalitarian society,” she said and recalled that Walikar was also an active participant in social movements.
“If there were any agitation, protest and struggle against any social discrimination, economic exploitation or environmental injustice, he was present with his traditional drum, singing revolutionary songs and mobilising people to raise their voices,” she added.
Principal of the Government First Grade (Autonomous) Degree College, Savitha Tiwari, and the poet’s wife Siddamma, among others, were present.

title: TTD action plan to ensure pilgrims a hassle-free ‘Vaikunta Ekadasi Dwara Darshan’ for 10 days from December 30
summary: TTD outlines plans for a smooth Vaikunta Ekadasi Dwara Darshan from December 30, ensuring token-only access on the first three days.
content:
The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) conducted an extensive review of arrangements for the Vaikunta Ekadasi Dwara Darshan, scheduled from December 30 to January 8, with special emphasis on crowd management during the first three days.
The meeting was chaired by TTD Additional Executive Officer Ch. Venkaiah Chowdary. Joint Executive Officer Veerabrahmam, Chief Vigilance and Security Officer (CVSO) Muralikrishna, and Tirupati Superintendent of Police Subbarayudu were present.
Terming the annual festival a mega spiritual event, Mr. Chowdary underscored the need for seamless coordination between the TTD departments and the police to ensure an incident-free pilgrimage, comparable to the scale and precision of the annual Brahmotsavams.
Detailed discussions were held on the preparedness of key wings, including temple administration, Annaprasadam, sanitation, reception, publicity, radio and broadcasting, Srivari Seva, vigilance and police for effective crowd regulation.
He further directed officials to intensify publicity, clearly informing devotees that darshan during the first three days — December 30 and 31, 2025, and January 1, 2026 — would be permitted only to those holding tokens issued through the e-DIP system. Devotees without tokens, he said, must be courteously guided and facilitated Sarva Darshan from January 2 to 8.
Mr. Chowdary instructed the SVBC, the PR wing, and the radio and broadcasting units to issue continuous multilingual announcements at all key transit points.
Mr. Subbarayudu later briefed the meeting on the security planning, risk management, multi-agency coordination, and event capacity mapping in close coordination with the TTD security wing.

title: SCR bags four NEC awards
summary: South Central Railway wins four NEC awards, including 'Best Performing Unit' for Diesel Traction Training Centre, in 2025.
content:
South Central Railway (SCR) was bestowed with four National Energy Conservation (NEC) Awards for the year 2025 with General Manager Sanjay Kumar Srivastava receiving the award for ‘Best Performing Unit’ for Diesel Traction Training Centre (DTTC), Guntakal in ‘Buildings category/Government buildings sector’ from President Droupadi Murmu in New Delhi on Tuesday.
The other awards are — Certificate of Merit each for Raichur railway station, Kacheguda railway station and Lingampalli railway station. Principal chief electrical engineer Brij Mohan Meena, Chief electrical general engineer K. Nagendra Prasad, DRM – Guntakal Chandra Shekar Gupta, DRM – Hyd Santosh Kumar Verma, DRM – Secunderabad R. Gopalakrishnan and other senior officers also attended the function and received awards for stations in their jurisdiction, said a press release.

summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor strongly opposed the proposed G RAM G Bill  in the Lok Sabha, calling it a retrograde move that undermines India’s commitment to its most vulnerable citizens. He criticised the removal of Mahatma Gandhi’s name from the rural employment law, saying it attacks the moral and philosophical foundation of the programme.
