In its order, the court had also recorded that a dispute regarding the story, screenplay, and dialogues was pending.
Mr. Mathew later approached the court again, alleging that the film was released and screened in violation of the court’s order by including the names of Shaji and Sumesh as screenplay writers.

title: District-level camp on Deposit Education and Awareness Fund on Friday
summary: A district-level camp on the Deposit Education and Awareness Fund will be held in Thiruvananthapuram on Friday.
content: A district-level camp on the Deposit Education and Awareness Fund will be held in Thiruvananthapuram on Friday. The event is being organised as part of the ‘Your Money, Your Right’ public awareness campaign launched by the Union Finance Ministry, a statement on Wednesday said. District Collector Anu Kumari will inaugurate the camp at the YWCA Hall at 10.30 a.m. As part of the camp, digital help desks and assistance counters will be set up to recover unclaimed bank deposits, insurance claims, dividends, pension and mutual funds. Assistance is also available for KYC updates, filling up claim forms and verifying documents. The camp will be a continuation of the earlier campaign conducted through various bank branches in Thiruvananthapuram district, the statement said. Bank of Baroda, Bank of India, Canara Bank, Central Bank of India, Indian Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, Punjab National Bank, State Bank of India, Union Bank of India, Kerala Gramin Bank and Kerala Bank are among the participants.

title: Despite State-Centre understanding, Sabari rail remains a non-starter
summary: Despite agreements, the Sabari rail project faces delays as Kerala and Railways struggle over funding and land acquisition issues.
content:
Though the Kerala government has communicated its readiness to implement the Sabari rail project, which will link Sabarimala with the existing railway line, by sharing 50% of the cost, it is unlikely to get on track soon due to several reasons.
First, despite the formal understanding between the Chief Minister and the Centre regarding its implementation, the project has not made any headway, with the Railways requesting Kerala to give ‘clear acceptance’ to share 50% of the cost instead of ‘conditional acceptance.’
The State has been demanding that the debt incurred by the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) by financing the project be fully exempted from the State’s borrowing limit, even as the State has assured the Railways that it would acquire the land for the project by using the 50% share of the project cost agreed to be shouldered by the State.
Meanwhile, the office of the Deputy Chief Engineer, Southern Railway, has communicated to the State government that instead of providing a conditional acceptance, it should convey a ‘clear acceptance’ to bear the cost of land acquisition as part of the committed 50% share of the project cost so that the same can be communicated to the Railway Board for defreezing the project.
Speaking toThe Hindu, a senior bureaucrat said as per the understanding between the State and the Centre, the State government has directed the District Collectors of Ernakulam, Idukki, and Kottayam to initiate land acquisition proceedings after restoring the land acquisition units. However, to make the project a reality, the Centre should agree to the State’s request, he said.
Further, the different stances adopted by the Centre and the State on defreezing the project, conceived close to three decades ago, have again brought things back to square one.
On the one hand, the State has been demanding that the Railways defreeze the project so that the State government can expedite the land acquisition and allied matters, and on the other, the Railways continue to request the Kerala government to start land acquisition proceedings so that the project can be defrozen by the Ministry of Railways.
To start land acquisition in full swing, the State requires funds for which it pins its hopes on getting a waiver from the Centre.
In short, the project is still a non-starter despite the claims by the Central and State governments that they have reached a formal understanding to implement the project.
In the latest remarks in Parliament during question hour, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw made it clear that the construction of the Angamaly–Sabarimala railway line could be started once land acquisition is completed. However, there is no clarity on how and when the land acquisition can be completed, as the State is still awaiting a political decision from the Centre on the KIIFB loan waiver.
Meanwhile, the Railways are planning to hold a feasibility study for the proposed Dindigul–Sabarimala railway line. According to the revised estimate for the project, the cost will be Rs 3,801 crore, with the State being responsible for 50% of the project cost.

title: Telangana prepares to operationalise nine Critical Care Blocks to cut emergency referrals to Hyderabad
summary: Telangana is set to launch nine Critical Care Blocks to enhance emergency services and reduce patient referrals to Hyderabad.
content:
The Telangana government has stepped up preparations to operationalise nine additional Critical Care Blocks following a recent review of the project’s progress by Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha, sources in the Health department said.
The Critical Care Blocks are part of a broader initiative under which 31 such facilities have been sanctioned across the State, with each block built at an estimated cost of ₹28 crore. Of these, four Critical Care Blocks located at Sangareddy, Nalgonda, Karimnagar and Nizamabad have already been inaugurated and are currently providing services, while the remaining units are at different stages of completion.
Officials familiar with the Minister’s review said that civil works and equipment installation have been completed at nine more locations, making them ready for inauguration. These facilities are located in Wanaparthy, Kamareddy, Jagtial, Jangaon, Vikarabad, Godavarikhani, Asifabad, Kothagudem and Adilabad. “The Health department is planning to commence services from the first week of January, subject to the completion of final scheduling and operational arrangements,” said a senior health official.
Each Critical Care Block has been developed as a 50-bed advanced emergency care facility, equipped to manage trauma cases, cardiac emergencies, neurological conditions and other life threatening situations. According to officials, the units are intended to deliver timely treatment during the crucial golden hour, particularly in districts that earlier lacked immediate access to tertiary level critical care.
During the review meeting, the Health Minister is learnt to have underlined that inaugurations should be carried out only when the facilities are fully ready to function. Officials have been instructed to ensure that all medical equipment is operational and that trained doctors, nurses and paramedical staff are deployed so that patient services can begin immediately after inauguration.
“With the phased rollout of the remaining Critical Care Blocks, the Health department expects a substantial reduction in referrals to Hyderabad and a strengthening of emergency response capabilities across Telangana,” the official added.

title: Minor boy in police custody after ‘rape’ of five-year-old
summary: Police on Wednesday detained a  minor boy on charges of allegedly sexually assaulting a five-year-old girl at a village in Kothacheruvu mandal in Sri Sathya Sai district.
content:
The police on Wednesday detained a  17-year-old boy on charges of allegedly sexually assaulting a five-year-old girl at a village in Kothacheruvu mandal in Sri Sathya Sai district.
According to sources, the boy had reportedly invited the child from the neighbourhood to his house on the pretext of offering her some eatables. Later, after sexually assaulting her, the boy left the girl at her house and went into hiding. The incident was said to have occurred a couple of days ago.
On Wednesday morning, the girl’s parents noticed their daughter in an unconscious state and rushed her to a local hospital, where the doctors informed them about the sexual assault. Based on a complaint, the area police took the boy into custody and made arrangements to shift him to the local juvenile home. Further investigation is under way.

title: ICG ship Sarthak makes first port call at Iran’s Chabahar
summary: ICG ship Sarthak's inaugural visit to Iran's Chabahar port enhances India's maritime cooperation and regional security initiatives.
content:
The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) ship Sarthak, an offshore patrol vessel, entered Chabahar port in the Islamic Republic of Iran on  Tuesday (December 16, 2025) for a four-day visit till December 19.
Strategically located, Chabahar is a deep-water port that provides India with a direct maritime gateway to Iran, Afghanistan and Central Asia.
According to the Ministry of Defence, marking the first-ever visit of an Indian Coast Guard ship to Chabahar, the port call underscores India’s growing maritime engagement in the region and its ability to support secure supply lines to Afghanistan and Central Asia. The visit is aligned with India’s SAGAR and MAHASAGAR vision of fostering secure, cooperative and inclusive maritime engagements.
During the visit, ICG ship Sarthak will engage in a range of professional and community-oriented activities with the Iranian Navy and other Iranian maritime agencies. These include courtesy calls and professional interactions aimed at strengthening institutional linkages and enhancing mutual understanding in maritime safety and security.
Key highlights of the port call include joint training activities in maritime search and rescue, maritime law enforcement and marine pollution response. A marine pollution response demonstration in Chabahar harbour, focusing on oil spills and hazardous and noxious substances spills, will showcase coordinated response mechanisms. MRCC-to-MRCC coordination drills, a table-top exercise and joint visit, board, search and seizure drills will further enhance interoperability and operational preparedness between the two sides, it added.
In addition to professional engagements, the visit will feature sports fixtures and a beach walkathon with the participation of embarked National Cadet Corps cadets. These activities align with the national Puneet Sagar Abhiyan, aimed at promoting marine environmental awareness and coastal cleanliness.
The port call at Chabahar follows the ship’s earlier visit to Kuwait, where ICG ship Sarthak interacted with the Kuwait Coast Guard, highlighting the Indian Coast Guard’s expanding footprint and constructive engagement with regional maritime partners.
The four-day visit of ICG ship Sarthak to Chabahar reflects India’s commitment to strengthening maritime cooperation, promoting a rules-based maritime order, and contributing to peace, stability and sustainable development across the wider Indian Ocean Region and the Gulf.

title: RTC unions to begin awareness drive on ‘surprise strike’ after talks with Karnataka government fail
summary: RTC unions are launching an awareness campaign for a potential surprise strike after unsuccessful talks with the Karnataka government.
content:
After a series of inconclusive meetings with the State government, the Joint Action Committee (JAC) of transport corporation employees is likely to start an awareness campaign across road transport corporation (RTC) depots, signalling the possibility of a strike that could be launched without prior notice.
“We will not announce when or how the strike will take place. All unions will unite and the strike will be declared suddenly,” Jagadish, a member of the JAC, said.
Union leaders said the JAC was preparing the ground for a “surprise strike” as a pressure tactic, following what they described as repeated failures by the government to address long-pending demands. Pamphlets detailing employee grievances will be distributed across depots, and workers will be briefed about the course of action proposed by the unions.
The move comes days after a meeting on Saturday between Transport Minister Ramalinga Reddy and JAC representatives, convened on the directions of Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, ended without a resolution. The talks were aimed at addressing key demands, including the release of arrears and a comprehensive pay revision for employees of State-run transport corporations.
The Saturday meeting followed an earlier round of discussions on November 26 involving the Chief Minister, the Transport Minister, and union representatives, during which the unions had reiterated their demands. As directed by the Chief Minister, Mr. Reddy had convened the latest meeting to review the issues raised by RTC employees.
However, union leaders said the repeated rounds of talks had yielded no concrete outcome. Mr. Jagadish said that meetings with the Chief Minister and the Transport Minister had been held more than four times without any meaningful progress. “These meetings have become a waste of time. Nothing useful is happening,” he said.
The JAC’s primary demands include the immediate release of pending arrears and the implementation of a long-overdue pay revision. According to the unions, unpaid dues across the four RTCs have mounted to ₹8,010 crore.
Other demands include higher staff allowances, better medical facilities for employees and the regularisation of drivers and technical staff currently working on a contract basis. The unions have also insisted that electric buses should be operated only by permanent drivers, arguing that deploying contract staff could compromise safety and operational efficiency.
Earlier, Mr. Reddy had said that, with the Assembly session under way, he would brief the Chief Minister on the discussions with union leaders during the session, after which a decision could be taken.

title: V-C postings: K.C. Venugopal sees tacit understanding between Governor, govt.
summary: Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal, MP, has said that the compromise reached between the Kerala Governor and the State government on the appointment of Ciza Thomas as Vice-Chancellor of APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University and that of Saji Gopinath as the Vice-Chancellor of Digital University Kerala,  is part of a tacit understanding between the two
content:
Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal, MP, has said that the compromise reached between the Kerala Governor and the State government on the appointment of Ciza Thomas as Vice-Chancellor of APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University and that of Saji Gopinath as the Vice-Chancellor of Digital University Kerala,  is part of a tacit understanding between the two
He suggested that the Governor and the Chief Minister came to an understanding about the very same individuals about whom they had reservations, indicating that they had been directed “from above” to settle their differences before the Supreme Court gave its decision.
He said that the  Governor and the Chief Minister have been misleading and making a fool of the public. When Ciza Thomas was first appointed the VC, the SFI and the CPI(M) had no qualms about organising violent protests for days together, disrupting the functioning of the University and thus jeopardising the future of students.
At the same time, the Governor had taken an open stance that Saji Gopinath was not acceptable as VC.
Mr. Venugopal wondered how the vehemence and antagonism displayed by the Governor and the Chief Minister had suddenly vanished
The allegations raised about the two VC candidates by both the Chief Minister and the Governor too seem to have been buried overnight, Mr. Venugopal said.

title: ₹2.73 crore restored in accounts of cyber fraud victims in Kalaburagi
summary: Police recover ₹2.73 crore for cyber fraud victims in Kalaburagi, urging prompt reporting to prevent further losses.
content:
The police, along with the Cyber, Economic and Narcotics (CEN) team, have successfully tracked down cyber fraudsters and recovered a total of ₹2,73,24,849 which has been refunded to the victims who fell prey to cybercrimes in 2025.
Police Commissioner Sharanappa S. Dhage, addressing a press conference in Kalaburagi on Wednesday, highlighted that the Cyber Crime Police Station under the jurisdiction of the city police has diligently investigated cases of cybercrime.
Investigation was carried out under the guidance of Deputy Commissioners of Police Kanika Sikriwal, Praveen H. Nayak, and Assistant Commissioner of Police James Menezes from the City Crime Branch (CCB) as well as staff from the Cyber Helpdesk Portal 1930.
The police team uncovered a large-scale network of cybercriminals and recovered a total of ₹96.82 lakh from 2,211 cases reported through the Cyber Helpdesk Portal 1930, involving a total fraud amount of ₹8.93 crore.
Additionally, ₹1.76 crore was recovered from 40 cases registered in police stations involving a total fraud amount of ₹12.72 crore. In total, ₹2.73 crore has been refunded to the accounts of the victims.
Dr. Dhage also highlighted that cybercrimes tend to spike on weekends, especially on Saturdays and Sundays, when banks are closed and victims are unable to file complaints.
However, he urged the public to report the crime within 24 hours through the Cyber Helpdesk Portal 1930, as there is a high chance (70% to 85%) of recovering the defrauded amount. He advised the public to file complaints within 24 hours to maximize the chances of recovery.
The Police Commissioner also advised the public to remain vigilant against cyber fraud, stating that banks, police officers or government officials will never ask for sensitive details such as OTPs, PINs, CVV numbers or passwords.
He cautioned people against responding to unsolicited calls, messages, suspicious links or unknown codes. In case of any financial fraud, he urged victims to immediately contact the Cyber Helpdesk by dialing 1930 or lodge an online complaint on the cybercrime portal.
He also said that hacked or fake social media accounts should be reported without delay to the respective platforms. Emphasizing the importance of digital safety, Dr. Dhage advised the public to regularly update passwords for bank accounts, UPI services, email IDs and social media accounts.

title: Funds meant for welfare of mining areas spent violating guidelines: CAG report
summary: CAG report reveals misuse of mining welfare funds for unauthorised purchases and projects, violating established guidelines.
content:
Belagavi
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India has taken note of irregular expenditure of funds under the Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana (PMKKKY), violating the guidelines.
The CAG has audited the money spent towards the welfare of areas affected by the mining, utilising funds collected by the District Mineral Foundation Trusts (DMFTs), between 2015 and 2023. The trusts collected ₹4,003.51 crore during the period and incurred an expenditure of ₹1,826.46 crore. The CAG report was tabled in the Legislative Assembly in Belagavi on Wednesday.
The CAG, in its findings, noted that the Deputy Commissioner of Ballari utilised ₹68 lakh to purchase 12 vehicles, utilising the DMFT fund in 2021, violating the guidelines. Similarly, the report noted that ₹1.26 crore was spent towards the salary of Home Guards and the improvement of roads in the Deputy Commissioner’s office premises in Ballari between 2020 and 2023.
When the CAG sought reply for the expenditure, in violation of the guidelines, the State government maintained that it was spent as per the approval of the Finance Department. However, the CAG reported that the government’s response was not acceptable.
“The reply was not acceptable as the Finance Department has no powers to sanction expenditure as per the DMFT rules,” the report stated.

title: Jagga Reddy accuses BJP of attempting to erase Gandhi’s legacy
summary: Jagga Reddy accuses BJP of attempting to erase Gandhi’s legacy
content:
HYDERABAD
Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) working president T. Jagga Reddy, on Wednesday, alleged that the BJP-led Central government was attempting to erase the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru by “diluting the spirit of welfare schemes introduced by the Congress”.
A massive public meeting would be held in Sangareddy soon to highlight the contribution of the Gandhi family to the nation, he said.
Addressing the media at Gandhi Bhavan on Wednesday, he said that the Mahatma Gandhi National Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), which he stated provides employment to nearly eight crore people, was introduced during the UPA regime under the leadership of Sonia Gandhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has removed Mahatma Gandhi’s name from the scheme, he said, and accused the BJP of systematically undermining the contributions of leaders associated with the Freedom Movement.
Mr. Jagga Reddy claimed that the BJP leadership was conspiring to eliminate Mahatma Gandhi from the nation’s historical narrative. He asserted that Rahul Gandhi would be elected Prime Minister with a majority of 300 MPs in the next general elections, claiming that people across the country were disillusioned with the present regime.

title: YSRCP flags allocation of TTD land at Alipiri for private resort
summary: YSRCP criticizes government for allocating TTD land to Oberoi Group for resort, questioning ecological impact and legality.
content:
The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) is in for a fresh bout of controversy, with the YSRCP pointing an accusing finger at the government’s decision to give away TTD land measuring 20 acres to the Oberoi Group for constructing five-star category villas and resort at Alipiri, the foot of Tirumala hills.
Addressing the media here on Wednesday, senior YSRCP leader and former TTD Chairman Bhumana Karunakar Reddy questioned the government’s propriety in giving away on a platter the land worth ₹520 crore as per the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) value for a “purpose other than intended in the TTD Act.”
“The TTD’s land parcels at Alipiri are invaluable. Giving them away to a private entity for building a resort is not only condemnable but also a sin,” he said.
“When government lands are available in its vicinity, why should the State give away the TTD’s land, with absolutely nothing coming in return to the TTD?” he sought to know.
When the Oberoi Group’s initial proposal to establish hotels under the ‘Mumtaz’ brand was caught in a controversy, the same was changed to ‘Svara Hotels’.
“Even after the controversy subsided with the name change and there was no objection, the government withdrew the land originally allotted at Peruru village (in Tirupati rural) and, instead, swapped it with a more prominent land parcel belonging to the TTD (in Tirupati urban). I suspect a conspiracy in this,” Mr. Karunakar Reddy said.
During a visit to the site, he said that work had begun even without the issue of work order, besides alleging that several precious redsanders trees had been felled indiscriminately. “How can the government provide land in this ecologically sensitive zone to a private entity?” he wondered.
Citing it the case of alienation of forest land for a tourism project, the YSRCP leader said neither Minister for Environment and Forest K. Pawan Kalyan nor Tourism Minister Kandula Durgesh could feign ignorance of the issue.s

title: Trial begins in Renukaswamy murder case: victim’s parents depose
summary: Trial in the Renukaswamy murder case begins as victim's parents testify against accused, including actor Darshan Thoogudeepa.
content:
Bengaluru’s 57th CCH Court on Wednesday commenced the trial in the Renukaswamy murder case, in which Kannada film actor Darshan Thoogudeepa and his friend Pavitra Gowda are among the 17 accused.
The proceedings began with the chief examination of Renukaswamy’s father, Kashinathaiah, and mother, Rathna Prabha. Prasanna Kumar, Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) appearing for the prosecution, conducted the examination from 11 a.m.
Darshan, Pavitra, and the other accused, who are currently lodged at the Parappana Agrahara Central Prison, attended the trial proceedings via video conference. Advocate Balan appeared for Pavitra and cross-examined the parents of the deceased.
During the examination, Renukaswamy’s parents identified the clothes he was wearing when he left home prior to the murder, as well as the clothes on his body when it was found. They also described the nature of the injuries on Renukaswamy’s body. In addition, they identified Renukaswamy’s engagement ring bearing the inscription “RS”. The parents told the court that “R” stood for their son’s name, Renukaswamy, and “S” for Sahana, their daughter-in-law.
Following the chief examination, the defence advocate cross-examined Kashinathaiah. Midway through the cross-examination of Rathna Prabha, the court adjourned the matter to Thursday. The proceedings lasted for three hours.
Renukaswamy, aged 33, was allegedly abducted from Chitradurga and murdered at a shed in Pattanagere in west Bengaluru in June 2024. His maimed body was found near a storm water drain in Sumanahalli by security guards of an apartment complex on June 9, 2024.
Initially, four persons falsely surrendered before the Kamakshipalya police. However, the police investigation unravelled a different and orchestrated murder. Subsequent investigations led the police to arrest Darshan, Pavitra, and the other accused.

title: ‘Aspiring Mysuru’ mega expo from December 18
summary: Join the 'Aspiring Mysuru' expo from December 18, showcasing government schemes and innovations at Bharat Scouts and Guides Ground.
content:
A three-day mega exhibition titled ‘Aspiring Mysuru’ begins at the Bharat Scouts and Guides Ground in Mysuru on December 18.
The exhibition is being organised by Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, and it aims to create public awareness about various Union government schemes, public sector enterprises, the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, and innovations across sectors.
Organiser Vanish Gupta said the exhibition will serve as an interactive platform for the people of Mysuru, giving them comprehensive information on developments and schemes in the fields of science and technology, electronics and information technology, environment, forests and climate change, health, ports, mining, handicrafts and textiles.
The exhibition will be open on all three days from 10 a.m. to 5.30 p.m., and entry is free, according to a press release.

title: CPI(M) unleashing violence across State: Satheesan
summary: The Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan has accused the CPI (M) of unleashing violence across the State following the party’s post-poll debacle.
content:
The Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan has accused the CPI (M) of unleashing violence across the State following the party’s post-poll debacle.
Talking to media persons here on Wednesday, he said that the police were remaining as mute spectators when the goons of CPI (M) went on a rampage in Payyannur and Panoor in the Chief Minister’s own district Kannur, armed with machetes and crude country-made bombs
In Pinarayi Vijayan’s own village, Pinarayi, a CPI (M) worker’s palm was in smithereens after the explosives he was handling exploded suddenly. Yet, the police has been at pains to stress that it was not a country-made bomb but a fire cracker that exploded.
Pinarayi Vijayan is not fit to occupy the position of Chief Minister because his own party workers were manufacturing bombs to tackle their rival party members and the police was silently aiding it, Mr. Satheesan said. The Chief Minister, who heads the Home department is making a mockery of his own police force, when the latter is forced to declare that it was not a country bomb but a fire cracker that went off, he added.
He demanded that the criminals going on a rampage be arrested and brought under police control. The CPI(M) is stooping to abominable levels to attack its opponents  just because they fared poorly in the local body polls. Partymen are going around, openly issuing threats of violence. The government should take action against the criminals and lay down the rule of law. But the people of Kerala will give them the right response, Mr.. Satheesan said.
Mr. Satheesan  was also dismissive of the “challenge” thrown at him by Kadakampally Surendran and said that he will present all the evidence (relating to the gold theft at Sabarimala) before the court at the appropriate time.
“ It was the court which made the observation that the gold-covered sculptures at Sabarimala were sold to a millionaire. I just made the observation that  the then Dewaswom Minister Kadakampally Surendran should come clean on this. It was the court which commented that everyone knew about the “transactions” that had taken place at Sabarimala. I will present all evidence in the court when the time comes,” Mr. Satheesan said.
On the comments made by the CPI(M) district secretary, Raju Abraham, that the sentiments of believers had been hurt by the parody song on Sabarimala gold theft that was widely popularised by the UDF, Mr. Satheesan said that it was the theft of Lord Ayyappa’s gold that hurt the sentiments of believers, not the parody song.
He pointed out that parody songs in Kerala were nothing new and that singing a parody song was not a crime.. He reminded the CPI(M) that the same devotional song was parodied by the party earlier to lampoon Congress leaders like the late K. Karunakaran. He said that it was ridiculous if the CPI(M) thinks that using a devotional song to ridicule those who committed the gold theft at Sabarimala is a larger crime than the gold theft itself.
The Leader of the Opposition clarified that the UDF was not in discussions at present with any party for it to join the alliance, nor had it assigned anyone to negotiate with any parties. However, the UDF will widen and strengthen its support base in the run up to the Assembly elections. The UDF is indeed the State’s largest political alliance and it had polled 15 lakh additional votes in the just-concluded polls, Mr. Satheesan said.
He said that Pinarayi Vijayan and M.V. Govindan were free to keep themselves deluded that there was no anti-incumbency or that the CPI(M)’s base was as strong as ever. The BJP secured 50 seats in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation and it was the CPI(M)’s seats that they wrested, he pointed out.

title: Taking note of huge debt of State public transport corporations, Karnataka HC awards lower interest for delayed payment of leave encashment to retired staff
summary: Karnataka HC reduces interest on delayed leave encashment payments for retired transport staff, acknowledging financial struggles of public corporations.
content:
Taking note that State public transport corporations were compelled to borrow around ₹2,000 crore only to meet its salary obligations, the High Court of Karnataka has ordered payment of lower interest to retired employees of the North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NWKRTC) for delayed payment of leave encashment amount to them.
The court noted that the public transport corporations suffered financial losses owing to the pandemic, and this burden was compounded owing to strike by employees and the State government’s policy decision of giving tree bus travel for women.
Stating that a balance must be stuck between the right of employees to be compensated for delay and the financial realities confronting public transport corporations sustained by the public funds, Justice M. Nagaprasanna directed the NWKRTC to pay interest at 6% on leave encashment for the delayed period instead of 9-10% as demanded by retired employees.
The NWKRTC had not only delayed by 10 to 25 months after retirement in paying the leave encashment amount to the petitioners, Yallappa and others, who retired post the pandemic, but had also failed to pay interest to them on the amount for the delayed period as per norms. During the hearing, the NWKRTC said that it is willing to pay interest at 6% while pointing out that 5.58% was the rate of interest prevailing in the banks at the relevant period in which the petitioners had retired from the service.
While directing the NWKRTC to pay the interest to the petitioners within 12 weeks, the court said that it has to pay interest at 9% if the interest amount is not paid within 12 weeks.s

title: Land acquisition under way for 11 major industries, says Nellore Collector
summary: Nellore Collector announces land acquisition for 11 major industries, aiming to develop Kavali as an industrial township.
content:
Collector Himanshu Shukla said that the land acquisition has been under way for 11 major industries in SPSR Nellore district. According to Collector, the authorities have been acquiring land in the district for six companies, while they are identifying lands for the remaining five.
In an interaction with the media, he said, “Along with solving the problems in the district, we are also working in a planned manner for its development. I have been focusing mainly on the land acquisition process for setting up new industries. My main intention is to industrialise the western region on par with the eastern region of the district.”
“Discussions are under way with several industrialists to establish units in Atmakur and Udayagiri areas as well. The steps have been taken to set up some industries in Jaladanki and Duttalur mandals also. Of 6,000 acres of land required for BPCL oil refinery project, nearly 3,200 acres have been acquired, while the rest will be acquired soon,” the Collector said.
“If everything goes well, the foundation stone for BPCL project will be laid in February 2027,” he said, adding that the land acquisition process for Indosol Solar Private Limited was on full swing. The district administration is also focussing on the creation of direct and indirect job opportunities through industrial development in the respective areas.
Meanwhile, the State Cabinet had recently approved the allotment of land to IFFCO Kisan SEZ, which had been pending for the past 30 years. Of the total 2,772 acres, IFFCO will develop 1,600 acres, while the government will develop 120 acres, the Collector informed. He further said that efforts will be made to establish industries by handing over Kovur Sugar Factory to the APIIC.
“The State government aims to provide satisfactory compensation to farmers and employees and establish environmentally friendly industries in the area. Kavali is likely to be developed as an industrial township with the establishment of Ramayapatnam Port, Indosol Solar and BPCL industries. The companies are expected to start operations in the next two years,” Mr. Shukla said.

title: Tropical forestry conclave marks end of KFRI’s golden jubilee celebrations
summary: KFRI's tropical forestry conclave concludes its golden jubilee, emphasizing global forest research, conservation, and community empowerment.
content:
Marking the culmination of its year-long golden jubilee celebrations, the Kerala Forest Research Institute (KFRI) launched a five-day tropical forestry conclave, inaugurated by Minister for Forests and Wildlife Protection A.K. Saseendran, ushering in a series of research paper presentations and discussions from Monday to Friday.
A conference, featuring international researchers on the subject of tropical forest management, including paper presentations and discussions, is being organised on the institute’s main campus in Peechi as part of the conclave. Over a hundred researchers will present their findings during the conclave.
As a symbol of the KFRI’s commitment to forest research and conservation, the conclave, which bring the golden jubilee (1975-2025) to a close, will also include an exhibition of forest research-related equipment and technologies, a gathering of medicinal plant cultivators from South India, a meeting of representatives from forest conservation research institutions, and the inauguration of new facilities and release of publications, according to KFRI sources.
In his inaugural address, Mr. Saseendran said the research at the KFRI has played a crucial role in expanding the knowledge of tropical afforestation. He also observed that the KFRI’s activities have been critical in developing innovative strategies for forest conservation, ecological restoration, and the empowerment of local communities. “It is a great and commendable achievement that the KFRI’s major studies are published in international journals, which allows the global community to learn about our forests,” he said.
Kannan C.S. Warrier, Director of Kerala State Council for Science, Technology, and Environment (KSCSTE)-KFRI, summarised the five decades of research at the institute in his presidential address. A special address was delivered by B. Mohan Kumar, Chairperson of the KSCSTE-KFRI Research Council.
The conclave is the culmination of a year-long series of events that brought together various stakeholders to discuss the challenges and opportunities related to tropical forests. It included lectures, panel discussions, and interactive workshops to foster collaboration among researchers, policymakers, and environmental enthusiasts.

title: KIIFB funds use: CM approaches Kerala HC, seeks quashing of ED notice
summary: Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan seeks Kerala HC's intervention to quash ED notice on KIIFB's masala bond funds usage.
content:
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, in his capacity as Chairperson of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB), has approached the Kerala High Court seeking to quash a notice issued by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on the utilisation of funds raised through masala bonds by KIIFB for infrastructure projects.
The notice had been issued under the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA). In his plea, Mr. Vijayan contended that the ED complaint does not warrant any adjudication proceedings, and that it has been vitiated by ‘malafides.’ The resultant adjudication proceedings will be a clear abuse of the process, and if permitted, will degenerate into a weapon of harassment or persecution of the petitioner, directors and officials (of KIIFB). The interests of justice warrant quashing of the notice.
Rebutting the allegation against KIIFB that the proceeds from External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) through masala bonds were used contrary to the mandate, he contended that the acquisition of property is an exercise by the government of its right of eminent domain and by virtue of the same compensation is paid to the deprived landowner. No transfer of land is made in favour of KIIFB. Moreover, it is not a speculative activity for commercial profiteering. Notifications in this regard will reveal that acquisition of land for the infrastructure sector is not a prohibited end use of ECB proceeds, he said, adding that there was no contravention of FEMA provisions and RBI norms.
He further contended that KIIFB is authorised to borrow any sum required for the purposes of the KIIF Act, with the previous sanction of the government. Towards this purpose, KIIFB is empowered to issue any financial instrument, including General Obligation Bonds, Revenue Obligation Bonds or any other appropriate financial instruments, or raise funds through any financial structures, including Revenue Bonds, with structured repayment mechanism, Land Bonds and any other appropriate financial instruments or by making arrangements with banks, multilateral funding agencies or Institutions approved by the government. Masala bonds are a special category of bonds denominated in Indian Rupees, and issued for funding permissible uses under extant guidelines, including for infrastructure projects.
The Kerala High Court had on Tuesday issued a three-month interim stay on a notice issued by the ED to KIIFB on the utilisation of funds raised through masala bonds for the board.

title: SVIMS gets new medical infrastructure
summary: SVIMS inaugurates new medical godown and accommodation facilities for patient attendants, enhancing healthcare infrastructure in Tirupati.
content:
New buildings to house the central medical godown and additional accommodation facilities for the attendants of patients were formally inaugurated on the TTD’s Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences (SVIMS) campus here on Wednesday.
TTD Board Chairman B.R. Naidu, who declared the facilities open, explained that the three-storeyed godown, measuring 37,000 sq. ft., was built with ₹10.65 crore to house medical/general stores, cold storage units, offices and a conference hall, meant to efficiently manage the medical supplies.
Similarly, the patient attendants’ rest house got a second and third floor with ₹4.40 crore to accommodate 300 attendants. People accompanying patients coming for treatment from far-off places were provided food and accommodation here.
The central laboratory system is under construction. Once completed, all lab facilities will come under one roof.
SVIMS Director and Vice-Chancellor R.V. Kumar said plans were afoot to complete the staff quarters, a central kitchen, 350 additional beds, five operation theatres, five ICUs and an advanced cancer care building, with the support of the TTD.
TTD Board members Sadasiva Rao, Santha Ram and Naresh Kumar, Joint Executive Officer V. Veerabrahmam, BIRRD Director G. Jagadish, and TTD’s Chief Engineer T.V. Satyanarayana accompanied the Chairman.

title: With no clear majority, hectic parleys on to form Alappuzha municipal council
summary: Intense negotiations unfold in Alappuzha as UDF and LDF vie for control of the municipal council amid no clear majority.
content:
With no party securing a clear majority in the Alappuzha municipality, both the United Democratic Front (UDF) and the Left Democratic Front (LDF) are engaged in intense negotiations to form the administrative council.
In the 53-member council, the UDF has emerged as the single largest bloc with 23 seats, followed closely by the LDF with 22. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) has won five seats, while the People’s Democratic Party (PDP), the Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI), and an Independent have secured one seat each.
Both the UDF and the LDF are vying for the support of Independent councillor Jose Chellappan, who was elected from Mangalam ward, and S. Faizal of the PDP, who won from Lajaneth ward. Sources said both fronts have offered Mr. Chellappan the post of vice-chairperson, though he is yet to take a final decision.
“I will take a final decision on whether to support the UDF or the LDF in the coming days,” Mr. Chellappan said. Echoing similar views, Mr. Faizal said discussions were continuing and the PDP would announce its “stand shortly”.
Meanwhile, both the UDF and the LDF are unlikely to seek the support of the lone SDPI councillor. Within the UDF, the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) has also staked a claim for the post of vice-chairperson. The Congress is understood to be considering offering the IUML the chairpersonship of the Health Standing Committee as part of internal negotiations.
The post of the municipal chairperson in the Alappuzha municipality is reserved for women.

title: Kurnool Cluster University semester exam results declared
summary: Kurnool Cluster University announces semester exam results, with 71.25% pass rate for III semester and 88.18% for V semester.
content: Cluster University, Kurnool, in-charge Vice-Chancellor V. Venkata Basava Rao and Registrar G. Srinivas on Wednesday released the results of the degree semester III and V examinations held in November. Of the 866 students who appeared for the III semester examinations, 617 passed with a percentage of 71.25. In the V semester examinations, 804 students appeared, of which 709 passed with a percentage of 88.18.

title: People’s organisations condemn Centre’s new rural employment Bill
summary: People’s and farm rights groups under the NREGA Sangharsh Morcha condemned the proposed VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025, to replace MNREGA and demanded its immediate withdrawal.
content:
Several people’s and agricultural rights organisations, under the nationwide umbrella of NREGA Sangharsh Morcha, condemned the introduction of Viksit Bharat - Guarantee For Rozgar And Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Bill, 2025 (VB-G RAM G), to replace the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 (MNREGA). They demanded immediate withdrawal of the Bill.
“The VB-G RAM G Bill is not a reform but a rollback of democratic and constitutional guarantees won by workers through decades of sustained struggles. The Union government is seeking to dismantle a historic rights-based legislation and reduce the right to work to a discretionary dole,” a statement issued by the Morcha said.
Addressing a press conference on Wednesday, representatives of the Dalit Bahujan Front (DBF), Rythu Swarajya Vedika (RSV), Telangana People’s Joint Action Committee (TPJAC), People’s Monitoring Committee and National Alliance for Justice, Accountability & Rights spoke against the Bill.
Ravi Kanneganti from TPJAC said the MNREGA had been a safety net for crores of people, and its repeal without public consultations will lead to mass unemployment. He urged the Telangana government to pass a resolution in the Legislative Assembly opposing the Bill.
P. Shankar from DBF demanded that the Bill be sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee, and remarked that the poor of the country will not benefit from the “name change from Gandhiji to Ramji”. He pointed out that the funding for the scheme is being wilfully scuttled for the past 10 years, and called the latest move as anti-constitutional. Puli Kalpana from DBF said the Bill would rob the female MNREGA workers of their independence.
Sree Harsha from RSV said the laws being repealed by the Centre were hard earned victories of people’s organisations over two decades.
Further, the Bill’s heavy reliance on mandatory biometric authentication and geo-spatial technology represent a fundamental shift in power form community led social audit to centrally managed surveillance and control, he said.
Akhil Surya from National Alliance for Justice, Accountability & Rights said the right to work is a constitutional directive and imperative under the Article 41 of the Constitution. The new law will roll this constitutional imperative backwards.
P.Prasad from Telangana Agricultural Workers Union said the union is giving a call to burn copies of the Bill at all district headquarters. He said it will enhance the financial burden on the State governments from 10% to 40% besides seriously undermining federal spirit. Pointing out that the Centre, through its digital restrictions, has deleted seven crore job cards over the past few years, he said Adivasis were the most affected due to this policy.

title: BJP slams plea for debate on Central agencies ‘targeting’ Congress leaders
summary: BJP criticizes Congress plea for debate on alleged targeting by Central agencies, leading to a heated House adjournment.
content:
Congress MLA A.S. Ponnanna’s plea for a debate in the House on Central agencies allegedly targeting Congress leaders triggered a heated debate between members of the treasury benches and the Opposition, forcing Speaker U.T. Khader to adjourn the proceedings here on Wednesday.
During Zero Hour, Mr. Ponnanna, referring to a Delhi High Court order rejecting an ED’s plea against Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and others in the National Herald case, alleged that the Central government has been misusing its agencies to target leaders of the Opposition.
A notice has been issued to Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. “We need to discuss the issue and arrive at an unanimous resolution,” he said.
Even as he raised the issue, the members in the Opposition, including Leader of Opposition R. Ashok, objected to him mentioning the issue. They argued that the rules of the procedures of the House do not allow such an issue to be taken up during the Zero Hour.
“If the issue is debated, who will reply to the debate in the House?” asked Mr. Ashok.
However, on the other side, members of the Congress argued that they have a right to raise the issue. Social Welfare Minister H.C. Mahadevappa said that the House, set up as per the Constitution, has the right to discuss the functioning of the agencies which also should abide by the principles of the Constitution.
At one point, BJP member Sunil Kumar found fault with the Speaker for allowing the Congress MLA to raise the issue during Zero Hour. As the commotion continued, the Speaker adjourned the House. Then, the Speaker held meetings with representatives of both the ruling and Opposition, in his chamber.
When the House reassembled, Minister for Law H.K. Patil made a statement defending Mr. Ponnanna’s right to raise the issue during Zero Hour. Citing the rules of House proceedings, he maintained that the member had the right to seek a debate concerning the privileges of the members of the House, as the Deputy Chief Minister has also been served notice by the Central agency.
The matter ended as the Speaker gave a ruling rejecting the Congress MLA’s plea to debate the issue in the House.

title: Newborn with missing fingers found abandoned in Sathya Sai district
summary: Newborn girl with missing fingers found abandoned in Sathya Sai district; police investigate the case for her parents.
content:
A three-day-old baby girl was found abandoned by unidentified persons near Kalasamudram village at Kadiri Rural mandal in Sri Sathya Sai district, on Wednesday.
According to the police, some locals heard the cries of a child from the bushes at the roadside in the village, and after finding the baby, they informed the Kadiri police. A police team, along with officials of the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), rushed to the spot and rescued the child, who was immediately shifted to the Kadiri Government Hospital for medical care.
Doctors said that the newborn was currently stable and healthy. However, during a medical examination, it was found that the baby had a congenital disorder with four of her fingers on the left hand missing.
The Kadiri police registered a case and launched an investigation to trace those responsible for the act.

title: Telangana ranks fifth in patent filings, says report
summary: Telangana ranks fifth in India for patent filings in 2024-25, showing significant growth in intellectual property activities.
content:
Telangana featured prominently across several parameters of India’s intellectual property ecosystem during 2024-25, according to the annual report 2024-25 released by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs, Trade Marks and Geographical Indications (CGPDTM). The State’s presence extended beyond patent filings to include design applications, national IP awareness programmes, examiner training and capacity-building initiatives.
In patent filings by Indian applicants, Telangana recorded 4,293 applications during 2024-25, placing it fifth nationally. The State showed a clear year-on-year increase compared to 2023-24, when 2,795 applications were filed. Telangana was among the States specifically identified by the CGPDTM as having contributed significantly to the rise in domestic patent filings, alongside Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
A closer break-up shows that Telangana accounted for 4,288 ordinary patent applications, one convention application, and four national phase applications in 2024-25 said Subhajit Saha, a GI practitioner.
Telangana also registered a visible footprint in design filings. During 2024-25, the State accounted for 979 design applications filed. In terms of design registrations, Telangana recorded 637 registered designs, placing it among the contributing States in the national total of 27,299 registered designs during the year.
The participant profile from Telangana included three school attendees, 3,207 college students, 1,023 participants from institutes, and 308 university-level participants. Gender-wise data showed 2,883 female and 1,658 male participants from the State, indicating a higher participation of women in IP awareness initiatives.
As part of a major recruitment drive, 407 newly appointed Examiners of Patents and Designs joined induction training programmes conducted at RGNIIPM-Nagpur, and Dr MCR HRD Institute in Hyderabad, in January 2025, the report said.
In terms of IP awareness and outreach, Telangana saw extensive activity under the National Intellectual Property Awareness Mission (NIPAM). During 2024-25, as many as 22 NIPAM programmes were conducted in the State. Through these programmes, a total of 4,541 participants from Telangana were sensitised to intellectual property rights.

title: First phase of Organ Transplantation Institute to be launched soon
summary: The first phase of the Institute of Organ Transplantation being newly established at Kozhikode will be launched soon now that the State Cabinet has sanctioned the creation of 60 new posts for the Institute.
content:
The Hindu Bureau
The first phase of the Institute of Organ Transplantation being newly established at Kozhikode will be launched soon now that the State Cabinet has sanctioned the creation of 60 new posts for the Institute.
The Cabinet which met on Wednesday approved 14 posts of Professors, seven posts of Associate Professors and that of 39 Assistant Professors for the Institute.
In the first phase, the Institute of Organ Transplantation will function from Kozhikode Government Medical College. The work on the first phase is expected to begin soon
The government had sanctioned ₹643.88 crore for making the organ transplantation institute a reality. The Institute will be launched with full-fledged facilities, including sophisticated equipment.
The government envisages the Organ Transplantation Institute as an umbrella organisation, which brings together scientists, researchers and expert clinicians and which will coordinate all activities related to organ donation and transplant in the State, including treatment and rehabilitation. The institute will come up on 20 acres at Chevayur in Kozhikode.
The institute will manage not just organ transplants and treatment, but research, teaching, training as well as activities to promote organ donation. It has been envisaged to provide comprehensive care and management of patients, right from the treatment of end-stage organ failure to organ transplant as well as post-transplant rehabilitation.
The institute will be in four blocks of six floors each. The plan is to build a 510-bed modern hospital with 219 general beds, 42 special ward beds, 58 ICU beds, 83 high dependency unit beds, 16 operating rooms, dialysis centre and transplant research centre.
In the first phase, 330 beds and 10 operating rooms will be readied and in the second phase, the remaining 180 beds and six operating rooms will be completed. In the first phase, 14 speciality divisions will come up and seven more in the second phase.
The government also aims to develop the Institute as a major teaching centre and is aiming at launching 31 academic courses.
Once the institute is fully operational, it would have the capacity to handle transplants of various organs, including cornea, kidney, liver, intestines, pancreas, heart, lungs, bone marrow, soft tissue, hands as well as bones, the statement said.
At present, all organ transplant surgeries in the public sector are managed by the Government Medical College Hospitals in Thiruvananthapuram, Kottayam and Kozhikode, as well as the General Hospital at Ernakulam.

title: Indian Army contingent leaves for India-U.A.E. joint exercise Desert Cyclone II
summary: Indian Army contingent departs for UAE to enhance defence cooperation in joint exercise Desert Cyclone II, focusing on urban operations.
content:
An Indian Army contingent has departed on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) for the United Arab Emirates to participate in the second edition of the India-United Arab Emirates (U.A.E.) Joint Military Exercise Desert Cyclone II, scheduled to be held at Abu Dhabi from December 18 to 30, 2025.
According to the Ministry of Defence, the Indian contingent comprises 45 personnel, primarily drawn from a battalion of the Mechanised Infantry Regiment. The U.A.E. Land Forces will be represented by a contingent of similar strength from the 53 Mechanised Infantry Battalion.
The aim of the exercise is to enhance interoperability and further strengthen defence cooperation between the Indian Army and the U.A.E. Land Forces. The joint training will focus on sub-conventional operations in an urban environment under a United Nations mandate, enabling both forces to operate together in peacekeeping, counter-terrorism and stability operations, it added.
During the nearly two-week-long exercise, troops from both sides will train together on a wide range of tactical drills, including fighting in built-up areas, heliborne operations and detailed mission planning. The exercise will also see the integration of unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and counter-UAS techniques for the conduct of operations in urban settings.
Building on the momentum generated by the successful visit of the Commander, U.A.E. Land Forces, on October 27 and 28, 2025, and the Commander, U.A.E. Presidential Guard, from December 15 to 19, 2025, Exercise Desert Cyclone II is expected to further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between India and the U.A.E.
The conduct of Desert Cyclone II underscores the deepening strategic partnership and military diplomacy between the two countries. It reaffirms their shared commitment to regional peace, security and stability, while promoting mutual understanding of tactics, techniques and procedures and contributing to the development of interoperable military capabilities.

title: Street vendors’ union alleges continued harassment, seeks implementation of Street Vendors Act in Karnataka
summary: Street vendors' union in Bengaluru demands enforcement of Street Vendors Act amidst ongoing harassment and lack of support from civic bodies.
content:
The Karnataka Pragathipara Beedhi Vyaparigala Sangha, a labour union of street vendors, on Wednesday alleged that harassment of vendors has continued across Bengaluru despite the reorganisation of the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) into five municipal corporations.
The union said provisions of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014, have not been implemented by any of the newly formed civic bodies.
Addressing a press conference, representatives of the sangha said that although a comprehensive survey of street vendors was conducted last year under the Act, identity cards and vending certificates are yet to be distributed. As per the scheme framed under the Act, these documents should have been issued within three months of the completion of the survey. While the cards have reportedly been printed, no steps have been taken to distribute them, forcing vendors to face continued harassment by police and municipal officials, the union claimed.
The union also alleged repeated eviction attempts in areas such as Vijayanagar, Jayanagar, Church Street, and Munireddypalya.
Another major concern raised was the absence of Town Vending Committees. The term of the committees constituted in 2020 has ended, but new panels are yet to be formed, leaving vendors without any grievance redressal mechanism, a release stated.
The sangha in its release demanded immediate distribution of identity cards through municipal offices, reconstitution of Town Vending Committees, training for officials on the Act, budgetary support for vendor shelters, free access to public toilets for women vendors, and an end to harassment. It warned of protests if the demands are not met in the coming days.

title: CAG highlights inadequate preparedness in disaster management in Karnataka
summary: CAG report reveals Karnataka's inadequate disaster management, highlighting non-functional sensors and misappropriated funds.
content:
The report of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India has highlighted the vulnerabilities, inadequate preparedness in disaster management system of Karnataka, amid increasing natural disasters.
Analysing the efforts from 2017-18 to 2022-23 in managing calamities and risk reduction, the report pointed out that although Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) was established in 2008, the State Disaster Management Policy was published after 12 years, only in 2020.
It said that the State Emergency Operation Centre was under-equipped in terms of human resources and infrastructure, which affected its functioning. The Disaster Response Force Units had huge vacancies —  ranging from 67% to 96% — of the sanctioned strength resulting in the units facing difficulties in carrying out duties and rescue operations.
KSNMDC had installed Telemetric Rain Guages (TRGs) and Telemetric Weather Stations (TWSs) in a phased manner between 2009 and 2015, but as of December 2023, it was found that 43% of TRGs and 52% of TWSs were defective, the report said.
It has also pointed out that the funds released by the State were not calamity-specific, complicating monitoring of NDRF/SDRF grants. The CAG has found misappropriation of ₹18.59 lakh at Chintamani in Chikkaballapura district, unutilised funds of ₹7.69 crore in Fire Emergency Department, and taluks of Haveri district spending ₹1.81 crore out of SDRF for reasons not related to natural calamities/disasters.
On the drought management front, CAG has found that the State had not framed region-specific guidelines for drought management and Karnataka Groundwater Authority failed to control illegal groundwater extraction for commercial purposes through private water tanks.
The CAG has pointed out that although the State Action Plan for Flood Risk was established in 2021, it lacked preparation for flood management in critical sectors. It found that 49 out of the 100 Water Level Sensors installed in Bengaluru remained non-functional as on December 2023. The State has not established a legal framework for flood infrastructure.
On the compensation front also, CAG has found discrepancies. It has said that compensation for damages was inconsistent and the verification processes were inadequate. It also found that there were 22,496 cases of house damage reconstruction pending despite ₹213.94 crore disbursed.
The CAG has recommended revamping Emergency Operation Centre and enhancing training for officials, among other things.

title: SRM University-AP organises meet on centre-margin power dynamics
summary: SRM University-AP hosts an international conference on centre-margin power dynamics, exploring interdisciplinary perspectives on governance and identity.
content:
An international conference titled ‘Breaking Barriers: Reimagining Centre–Margin Dynamics from Interdisciplinary Perspectives’ organised by the Department of Literature and Language at Easwari School of Liberal Arts, SRM University-AP, focussed on a critical reflection of the enduring binaries of centre and margin in the contemporary world.
Rajkumar, a professor from the University of Delhi, spoke about how entrenched hierarchies of power influence governance, identity, knowledge and belonging, while simultaneously exploring how the Centre-margin binary is not fixed and how power is a flexible entity.
Angshuman Kar from the University of Burdwan spoke on the ‘Marginality and Politics of Literary Repatriation of Australian Aborigines’ with multiple parallel sessions on a spectrum of topics on the first day of the three-day conference.
Vice-chancellor of SRM University-AP Ch. Satish Kumar observed that marginalisation exists in every sector, and it is the social fabric that determines marginalisation, overshadowed by the game of power dynamics.

title: UCIL donates drones to enhance policing in Kadapa
summary: UCIL donates drones to Kadapa police, enhancing crime control and traffic regulation through technology-driven surveillance.
content:
Superintendent of Police Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath has said that policing will become more efficient and vigilant with the deployment of drone cameras.
Speaking after receiving two state-of-the-art drone cameras donated by the Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL) on Wednesday, he said that the drones would be deployed to control crime, curb anti-social activities and regulate traffic. The cameras worth ₹3 lakh were donated under UCIL’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activity.
Mr. Nachiket emphasised the crucial role of technology-driven policing to curb offences such as chain snatching, eve-teasing, to prevent road accidents, thefts and anti-social activities.
“VIP security arrangements, traffic regulation at key junctions and surveillance in sensitive areas will also become more fool-proof with drone cameras”, he added.
The two advanced drones were handed by UCIL’s general manager Suman Sarkar to Deputy Superintendent (Pulivendula) B. Murali for use within his jurisdiction.

title: Nod for leasing 5 acres to Central Forensic Science Laboratory
summary: The Cabinet meeting held here on Wednesday has decided to lease 5 acres in Melthonnakkal village, Technocity, Technopark Phase IV campus, to the Union Home Ministry for setting up a Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) in Kerala as part of the National Forensic Infrastructure Enhancement Scheme.
content: The Cabinet meeting held here on Wednesday has decided to lease 5 acres in Melthonnakkal village, Technocity, Technopark Phase IV campus, to the Union Home Ministry for setting up a Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) in Kerala as part of the National Forensic Infrastructure Enhancement Scheme. The Chief Executive Officer of Technopark has given permission to lease the land for 90 years at a rate of ₹100 per acre per annum.

title: IFFK proceeds with more censor exempted films being screened
summary: After unprecedented scheduling issues caused by the  Union Information and Broadcasting (I&B) Ministry’s denial of censor exemption to 19 films, International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK) appeared to return normalcy on Wednesday with films including A Poet, Eagles of the Republic and Flames which were cancelled on the previous days getting screened.
content:
After unprecedented scheduling issues caused by the  Union Information and Broadcasting (I&B) Ministry’s denial of censor exemption to 19 films, International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK) appeared to return normalcy on Wednesday with films includingA Poet,Eagles of the RepublicandFlameswhich were cancelled on the previous days getting screened.
The Kerala government had on Tuesday directed the State Chalachitra Academy to screen the films, in defiance of the ministry’s denial of censor exemption. According to Academy sources, the Union ministry on Wednesday accorded exemption to a few more films on Wednesday, with only six more films remaining to be cleared. However, some confusion prevailed in the evening, with the academy not going ahead with the screening one of the films in the six remaining films to be cleared.
Amid the public outrage over the Union government’s denial of censorship exemption, a former artistic director of the film festival on Wednesday claimed that procedural lapses on the part of the organisers had led to the fiasco and warned against blaming political targeting.
Deepika Suseelan, who was the artistic director of the 27th edition of the festival attributed the ministry’s decision to delays on the part of the Chalachitra Academy in sending films for clearance.
For a festival happening in December, the list of films that need censor exemption along with synopses and other documents need to be submitted at least by the first week of November, she said. However, Academy officials said that the denial of exemption was evidently political and not procedural as only a few films were held up.
Meanwhile, the absence of KSCA chairman Resul Pookutty during the event due to prior commitments abroad had raised eyebrows, with noted film directors stating that it was disappointing. Film director and former KSCA chairman Kamal said a situation without the head of the festival’s attendance could have been avoided. Filmmaker Bijukumar Damodaran said it was for the first time that an IFFK is being held without the chairman or an artistic director.(With inputs from PTI)

title: Coalition government encouraging sportspersons: SAAP
summary: Andhra Pradesh's coalition government prioritising sports, says SAAP chairperson
content:
Andhra Pradesh will be transformed into a sporting hub, said Ravi Naidu, chairperson of the Sports Authority of AP (SAAP) during his visit to P. Anand Indoor Stadium in Ongole on Wednesday (December 17).
Addressing the media on the occasion, he said: “Telugu Desam Party-led government had brought a sports policy and gave great importance to sports in the State during its previous term 2014-18. However, the subsequent government neglected the sports sector.”
Mr. Naidu said 3% reservation has been provided to sportspersons in government jobs, and employment is being given without any tests. He said nearly 421 sportspersons in the State were given jobs in the recently conducted Mega DSC.

title: Parliament clears Bill to allow 100% FDI in insurance sector
summary: Parliament passes a Bill allowing 100% FDI in insurance, sparking debate over its impact and data privacy concerns.
content:
A day after the Lok Sabha passed it, the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) passed the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Bill, which allows 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in the insurance sector. The Upper House also cleared the Repealing and Amending Bill that repeals 71 obsolete laws. The Lok Sabha had passed both the Bills on Tuesday (December 16, 2025).
Parliament Winter Session:Follow LIVE updates on December 17, 2025
The structure of insurance regulation is very clearly laid out in the Bill, and the premium collected from Indians by foreign insurance companies will be kept in the country, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said, replying to a debate on the Bill.
Private sector insurance companies were participating in all welfare schemes of the Union government, and the Bill would ensure that foreign companies will also participate in social sector-related activities and government schemes, Ms. Sitharaman said. “We are not giving them any room to get away from that responsibility,” she said.
The increase in the FDI limit to 100% would ensure more foreign companies invest in India as, in many cases, they do not find joint venture partners due to various reasons, the Minister said. With more companies, the competition will increase, and premiums should drop, she said.
Also Read |SHANTI Bill spurs private sector to make, run nuclear plants
Earlier, during the debate, the Opposition demanded that the Bill should be sent to a select committee of Parliament given the far-reaching impact it has on the insurance sector.
Initiating the debate, senior Congress MP Shaktisinh Gohil said the new Bill posed a threat to data privacy as foreign companies would demand the PAN and Aadhaar cards of their customers, which may lead to digital frauds. The Centre should learn from the experience of privatising the civil aviation sector, Mr. Gohil said, and urged that the Bill should be sent to a select committee.
Questioning the use of two languages, both Hindi and English, in the name of the Bill, Saket Gokhale of the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) also said the Bill opened the door to profit extraction by foreign companies.
A market share of $600 billion would go to foreign investors once the Bill was implemented, Kanimozhi N.V.N. Somu of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) said. “This is daylight robbery. The government should not squander opportunities to promote and strengthen its own PSUs (public sector undertakings), but this government through this Bill is favouring foreign investors and burdening our own insurance companies,” Ms. Kanimozhi said.
EDITORIAL | ​Stepping stone: On nuclear policy, the SHANTI Bill
The Rajya Sabha also passed the Repealing and Amending Bill. The Bill would remove 71 outdated laws, correcting errors that had crept in during the law-making process, and removing discriminatory aspects of certain laws, Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said. “We give priority to ease of living along with ease of doing business,” the Minister said. “These reforms are a step towards liberation from a colonial mindset,” he added.
The Bill seeks to repeal 71 Acts, including the Indian Tramways Act, 1886; the Levy Sugar Price Equalisation Fund Act, 1976; the Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (Determination of Conditions of Service of Employees) Act, 1988; the General Clauses Act, 1897; the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908; and the Indian Succession Act, 1925.

title: Cong. backed candidates continue winning streak in GP polls
summary: Cong. backed candidates continue winning streak in GP polls
content:
Hyderabad
Congress-backed candidates continued their winning streak in the third and final phase of Gram Panchayat elections for the posts of Sarpanch and ward members.
Polling was by and large peaceful on Wednesday barring stray incidents of clashes between ruling Congress and BRS cadre in some districts.
Congress-backed candidates won as many as 6,476 Sarpanch posts followed by BRS supported nominees winning 3,347 posts. BJP-backed candidates clinched 651 Sarpanch posts with Independents and others winning 1,555. The counting of votes will continue late in the night.
The State Election Commission (TGSEC) notified a total of 12,728 Sarpanch posts and 1,12,242 Ward Member posts. The elections were held in three phases on December 11, 14 and 17. The elections witnessed as many as 1204 sarpanch and 25,551 ward members getting elected unanimously.
The SEC said that 85.77% polling was recorded in the third and final phase, with as many as 43.37 lakh voters exercising their franchise in 31 districts out of the total electorate of 50.56 lakh voters. Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district recorded a high of 92.56% polling followed by Medak 90.68 and Suryapet district recording 89.25% turnout.

title: Palaniswami welcomes move to increase workdays under new rural jobs scheme
summary: Palaniswami supports extending rural workdays to 125 but urges the Centre to keep Mahatma Gandhi's name in the scheme.
content:
The AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Wednesday welcomed the decision of the Union government to increase the duration of work from 100 days to 125 days under the Viksit Bharat — Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB—G RAM G) Bill.
In a post on his social media handle, Mr Palaniswami, however, urged the Centre to retain the words - Mahatma Gandhi - in the title of the proposed scheme, which was, till now, called the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.
At the same time, he criticised Chief Minister M.K. Stalin for not increasing the duration of work to 150 despite having assured people of the State in the run-up to the 2021 Assembly poll.
In a statement, the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Workers’ Rights Retrieval Kazhagam coordinator O. Panneerselvam said the VB — G RAM G Bill would reduce the number of worker-beneficiaries and lower the wages for agricultural workers during the peak seasons of sowing and harvesting, besides increasing the financial burden for States. He demanded that either the Bill be withdrawn or referred to the parliamentary joint committee.

title: Over 62.40 lakh children to be covered under Pulse Polio campaign in Karnataka on December 21
summary: Karnataka's Pulse Polio campaign on December 21 aims to vaccinate over 62.4 lakh children aged 0-5 against polio.
content:
Over 62.4 lakh children in the 0–5 age group will be covered under the Pulse Polio immunisation campaign to be held across Karnataka on December 21, Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao said on Wednesday.
Addressing a press conference at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi, the Minister said the National Immunisation Day (Pulse Polio) is being observed as a precautionary measure to sustain India’s polio-free status, even as cases continue to be reported from neighbouring countries. In 2025, Pakistan reported 51 and Afghanistan 10 cases of wild polio virus, highlighting the risk of importation.
The campaign will be conducted in one round using the bivalent oral polio vaccine (bOPV). Vaccination will be carried out at booths on December 21, followed by door-to-door visits over the next two to three days to ensure that no child in the 0–5 age group is missed.
Mr. Rao emphasised that all children below five must be given two drops, even if they have received polio drops earlier. Under the routine immunisation programme, every child is entitled to five doses of oral polio vaccine and three doses of inactivated polio vaccine (IPV), he said.
Special focus will be placed on high-risk and hard-to-reach areas, including villages, hilly and forest regions, brick kilns, migrant settlements, urban slums, farmhouses, and transit points such as railway stations, metro stations, airports, and seaports.
For the campaign, the Health Department has set up 33,258 booths, with the support of 1,030 mobile teams and 2,096 transit teams. As many as 1,13,115 vaccinators and 7,322 supervisors have been deployed. The programme is being implemented in coordination with various government departments and supported by organisations such as the WHO, UNICEF, Rotary International, the Indian Academy of Paediatrics and the Indian Medical Association.
The Minister said the polio vaccine is completely safe and appealed to parents not to be swayed by rumours. The nearest vaccination booth can be located through the Nearby Vaccination Centre Karnataka mobile application.
He said public cooperation was crucial to ensure that every one of the 62.40 lakh targeted children is protected.

title: Tourism a top priority sector, says Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu
summary: Andhra Pradesh prioritizes tourism development, highlighting untapped potential and infrastructure projects to boost local economies and connectivity.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has declared tourism and the creation of hospitality infrastructure as the State’s top priority sector.
Speaking at the inaugural of the two-day Collectors’ conference at the Secretariat on Wednesday, Mr. Naidu noted that projects like Wonderla Amusement Park coming up in Visakhapatnam and Imagicaa World in Tirupati would be game-changers in the tourism sector, while observing that its potential was largely untapped.
Principal Secretary (Tourism) Ajay Jain informed the Chief Minister that during the recent CII Partnership Summit-2025, the Tourism Department had signed 209 MoUs worth about ₹30,000 crore across 26 districts, and it demonstrated widespread interest in the development of tourism infrastructure throughout the State.
Mr. Naidu told the officials of the Industries Department to take steps for excluding 82,000 acres of land belonging to the AP Industrial Infrastructure Corporation from Section 22 A of the Registration Act so that they could be made available to the industries. He called for an action plan to hone the skills of youth to help the government achieve the employment generation goals.
Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan told the Collectors to focus on improving road connectivity to the tribal hamlets as it was a must for development, and on the implementation of Palle Pandugaprogramme.
