YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has said that the party would challenge the privatisation of medical colleges in courts as Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu showed no signs of backing off and instead maintained that the decision augurs well for medical education.
He vowed to cancel the much-hyped PPP model of construction of medical colleges when the YSRCP returns to power, calling it a big scam.
Addressing a meeting of YSRCP leaders after flagging off vehicles carrying papers containing  1 crore signatures against the privatisation of medical colleges to Lok Bhavan in Vijayawada on Thursday, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said he lost hope that Mr. Chandrababu Naidu would pay heed to wise counsel and recalled that former CM N. Janardhan Reddy had to step down due to permission given to private medical colleges.
Mr. Naidu was justifying the PPP model of construction of medical colleges as a welcome move by covering up the intention behind it, which was to privatise medical education, he alleged.
Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy stated that the YSRCP leaders collected a record 1,04,11,136 signatures opposing the privatisation of medical colleges and that the party would ensure that the government did not proceed with it.
He noted that schools and hospitals were being run by governments since independence as otherwise those services would become inaccessible to the common people. However, Mr. Chandrababu Naidu was bent on privatising the medical colleges on grounds that were not at all convincing, he said.
Speaking about the Collectors’ Conference, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said Mr. Naidu was blaming the Collectors for his ‘falling graph’ instead of mending ways wherever required in public interest.
The NDA government would be presenting its third budget in March but it has so far failed in improving the people’s living standards and developing the State. All the welfare schemes introduced by the YSRCP were scrapped, he said.

title: Mandya ramps up SSLC preparation with 56 nodal officers
summary: Mandya appoints 56 nodal officers to enhance SSLC exam results by monitoring schools and addressing academic issues.
content:
With the aim of improving SSLC examination results, 56 nodal officers have been appointed in Mandya district and tasked with monitoring academic performance in schools under their jurisdiction.
Presiding over a review meeting on measures to enhance SSLC results in Mandya on Wednesday, ZP Chief Executive Officer Nandini K.R. directed the nodal officers to visit the schools assigned to them by December 20. They have been instructed to identify prevailing issues in the schools and submit a detailed report to the DDPI through the respective BEOs.
The CEO said complaints have been received from students and the public alleging that in some schools, the syllabus is not being taught properly, teachers are avoiding classes citing various reasons, special classes are not being conducted, and model examinations. Nodal officers have been asked to personally verify these issues and ensure corrective measures are taken.
She directed that model examinations must be conducted for SSLC students in all 253 high schools. Answer scripts have to be evaluated by teachers from other taluks to ensure transparency. Students failing in these tests must be given special attention, she said.
For effective monitoring, a WhatsApp group comprising nodal officers, BEOs, DDPI, and other officials will be created by the ZP office. From the first day, nodal officers have been instructed to share photographs of school visits, suggestions for improving results, and details of strategies being implemented.
From Thursday onwards, for three consecutive days - Thursday, Friday, and Saturday - tests should be conducted for two subjects per day, as less than three months remain for the final examination. Question papers will be supplied at the district level, examinations must be conducted transparently, and answer scripts evaluated by teachers from other taluks. Students scoring less than 50% should receive focused academic support.
Officials were told that a follow-up meeting will be held after 15 days, during which nodal officers and the DDPI have to present a concrete action plan to improve the results of aided and private schools as well.

title: Two held for ganja peddling in Nandyal
summary: Two arrested for ganja peddling in Nandyal; police seized 2.5 kg of drugs, a car, and mobile phones.
content: Police have arrested two persons for allegedly selling ganja in Nandyal town and seized 2.5 kg of the contraband, a car and two mobile phones from them. Speaking to the media here on Thursday (December 18), Assistant Superintendent of Police (Nandyal sub-division) M. Javali Alphonso said the accused, identified as Shaik Muneer Basha and Shaik Mahboob Basha of Basapuram village in Gajulapalli mandal, were arrested from Pradhama Nandi temple arch. She said Muneer Basha brought the contraband from Araku and was planning to sell it with the help of the other accused. A case has been registered against the duo under the NDPS Act.

title: CM Naidu lauds Parvatipuram’s 'Mustabu' initiative
summary: CM Naidu praises Parvatipuram's 'Mustabu' initiative, promoting hygiene and cleanliness among 79 lakh schoolchildren in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu lauded the  ‘Mustabu’ programme launched by Parvatipuram Collector N. Prabhakar Reddy to promote cleanliness and personal hygiene among schoolchildren, during the Collector’s conference held in Amaravati on Wednesday and Thursday. Mr. Naidu also announced that the initiatve would be implemented across all educational institutions in Andhra Pradesh covering 79 lakh students.
Mr. Naidu also asked Mr. Prabhakar Reddy to give presentation on the 'Mustabu' programme during the Collectors conference.
According to a release from the Parvatipuram Collector’s office,  under the 'Mustabu' programme all school premises are given mirrors and combs. Beore coming to class, students have to check and groom themselves. To promote hygiene, towels and soaps have also been provided. Under the programme, nail cutters are supplied to all schools and students have to keep their nails clean and trimmed. Handwashing before lunch has been made compulsory. Student leaders monitor the programme and all students get an opportunity to become a monitor on rotation basis.
Mr. Prabhakar Reddy said: “Neatness and personal hygiene habits, clean environment in schools will make students responsible in all aspects. The programme is designed to develop leadership qualities among students. The Chief Minister’s recognition has enhanced our responsibility and motivated us to launch new schemes in the future.”

title: Mysore varsity seminar stresses nutritional research among faculty
summary: Mysore varsity's seminar focuses on enhancing nutritional research methodologies among faculty to tackle contemporary nutrition challenges.
content:
The Department of Studies in Food Science and Nutrition, University of Mysore, in collaboration with the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centre, University of Mysore, organised a two-day faculty improvement seminar on “Reimagining Nutritional Research: ABCDE and Ethnography as Complementary Approaches” here on Thursday.
The programme was conducted under the aegis of RUSA 2.0 with the objective of strengthening methodological competencies in contemporary nutritional research among faculty members, research scholars, and postgraduate students.
Komala M., chairperson, Department of Studies in Food Science and Nutrition, outlined the theme of the programme and emphasised the need for integrating quantitative nutritional assessment frameworks with qualitative research approaches to address emerging nutrition challenges holistically.
K. Mantelingu, director, College Development Council, University of Mysore, inaugurated the seminar.
In his inaugural address, Prof. Mantelingu underscored the relevance of faculty development initiatives in enhancing research quality and academic excellence. He highlighted the relationship between organic chemistry and food science and nutrition and their application in translational research to improve the overall health status of the population and reduce disease burden, such as obesity, diabetes, and cancer. Prof. Jamuna Prakash emphasised the continued relevance of the ABCDE framework— Anthropometric, Biochemical, Clinical, Dietary, and Ecological assessments—in evaluating nutritional status.
Prof. Jamuna Prakash, former faculty, Department of Food Science and Nutrition, University of Mysore, and Tara M.S., former regional director, NIPCCD and Development Practitioner, Bengaluru, were present.

title: Prayas: Nearly 12,000 kids in Chamarajanagar identified with speech, hearing issues
summary: Prayas identifies nearly 12,000 children with speech and hearing issues in Chamarajanagar, promoting early intervention and support.
content:
ThePrayasprogramme, specially designed and implemented in Chamarajanagar district to identify and treat speech and hearing problems among children, has earned appreciation and is being hailed as a model initiative in the State.
As part of the programme, early screening for speech and hearing issues has been conducted for all children below six years of age across the district. Through the anganwadi network, 34,935 children aged between six months and six years were identified and screened. Of these, 11,824 children were found during the primary screening to have possible speech and hearing issues.
The second phase of screening has already been completed in Gundlupet taluk and is currently underway in Chamarajanagar taluk.
Launching the second phase of screening at Santhemarahalli, Deputy Commissioner Shilpa Nag said the programme would be extended to the remaining taluks as well. “ThePrayasprogramme has the potential to serve as a model for other districts and has already received State-level recognition. Plans are also in place to extend the programme beyond children to include senior citizens. The objective is to comprehensively address speech and hearing problems and make Chamarajanagar a district free from such impairments,” she said.
The Deputy Commissioner said that children’s academic performance is adversely affected if speech and hearing problems are not identified and treated at an early stage. Delayed intervention, she added, could lead to multiple challenges later in life.
In view of this, thePrayasprogramme has been implemented to ensure early screening, timely medical intervention, and the provision of necessary hearing aids, entirely through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding.
The programme is supported by the All India Institute of Speech and Hearing (AIISH), Mysuru, the Department of Women and Child Development, and the Department of Health and Family Welfare. The Rotary Club of Mysuru West has extended financial assistance for treatment, while various organisations and industries, including Automotive Axles Ltd. have provided CSR support.
Ms. Nag expressed her gratitude to all supporting institutions.
Manjula, the in-charge director of AIISH, Mysuru, said that a programme likePrayaswas perhaps being implemented for the first time in the country, owing to the special interest and concern shown by the Deputy Commissioner.
On the occasion, doctors from AIISH and representatives of CSR organisations supporting the Prayas programme were felicitated and presented certificates.

title: Bengaluru urban district has most number of ex-servicemen in the State; Yadgir lowest
summary: Bengaluru Urban district leads Karnataka with 31,999 ex-servicemen, while Yadgir has the lowest at just 66.
content:
There are around 94,376 registered ex-servicemen in Karnataka of which a majority of them are living in Bengaluru Urban district.
As per information given by the Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth in a reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha during the ongoing winter session of Parliament, there are 31,999 registered ex-servicemen from the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force residing in Bengaluru Urban district as of June 30, 2025. Yadgir with 66 people is the district with the least number of registered ex-servicemen.
As per data, of the 31,999 ex-servicemen around 21,742 are former Army personnel, 1,691 are former Navy personnel and 8,566 are former Air Force personnel.
The district with the second highest number of ex-servicemen is Belagavi, with 22,869 followed by Kodagu with 4,578 ex-servicemen, Dharwad with 3,440 ex-servicemen, Mysuru with 3,413 ex-servicemen, and Bagalkot with 3,262 ex-servicemen.
Of the 94,376 registered ex-servicemen residing in the State, 78,633 are from the Army, 3,133 from the Navy, and 12,610 from the Air Force.
In Chickballapur district there are no ex-Navy personnel while in Yadgir district there is only one ex-Air Force personnel.
The Minister to a question on whether any region-specific skilling and entrepreneurship support has been provided under the Directorate General Resettlement (DGR) said that the DGR runs resettlement schemes and skill development training for ex-servicemen, disabled soldiers, widows and their dependents to provide job opportunities based on the region-specific skilling/entrepreneurships facilities as well as the demand.
Further, courses have been conducted for the ex-servicemen in Bengaluru by the National Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD) and Indian Institute of Management in 2024-25 and 2025-26, training 240 ex-servicemen.
Eight courses were conducted in the NIESBUD during this period, training 160 personnel in the Entrepreneurship Development Programme. The IIM also conducted two courses during this period, training 80 personnel in certificate courses in Business Management.

title: A.P. farmer develops cost-effective tool to remove weeds
summary: A farmer invents a ₹1,000 cycle weeder, revolutionising weed removal and saving costs for local agricultural communities.
content:
P. Lakshmi Narayana, a farmer from Reddypalem village in Kothapatnam mandal of Prakasam district, has developed a simple weeder that costs just ₹1,000.
Speaking toThe Hindu, he said the idea to make his ‘Cycle Weeder’ came from a random discussion on getting rid of weeds on fields without spending large sums. He said the tool, which he made by removing the front wheel of his old bicycle and welding a blade to it, allows him to easily weed an acre of field alone, a task which otherwise took 10 workers to complete.
Mr. Lakshmi Narayana currently cultivates chilli, groundnut and vegetables on his own one-and-half acre in the village. He pays a farmhand ₹1,500 a day to weeds his field using the ‘cycle weeder’. He said he used to spend over ₹5,000 a day for the task earlier.
“Taking their cue from the ‘cycle weeder’, many local farmers have made similar tools by spending ₹1,000 at the wielding shop,” he claimed.

title: Workers escape unhurt as fire guts sheds near construction site in Chandanagar
summary: Workers escape unharmed as a massive fire destroys sheds near a Chandanagar construction site, triggered by a gas cylinder leak.
content:
Several workers had a narrow escape after a massive fire broke out at the workers’ sheds near a construction site in Chandanagar on Thursday (December 18, 2025). No casualties or injuries were reported.
According to an official from the Fire Control, a distress call was receivedat 11.48 a.m., following which three fire tenders from Madhapur, Vattinagulapally and Patancheru were rushed to the spot. The blaze was brought under control soon after. Officials said the labourers escaped unharmed as they had already left for work at the construction site when the fire broke out.
Preliminary investigation suggests that the fire was triggered by a gas cylinder leak in one of the sheds. Four sheds were completely gutted in the incident.
A case has been booked and further investigation is underway.

title: India, Netherlands reaffirm defence ties
summary: India and the Netherlands strengthen defence ties, focusing on cooperation in emerging technologies and military engagement through a new Letter of Intent.
content:
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met the Foreign Minister of the Netherlands, David van Weel in New Delhi on Thursday (December 18, 2025), reaffirming the strong and steadily expanding defence partnership between the two nations.
During the meeting, both Ministers held wide-ranging discussions on bilateral security and defence cooperation, including priority areas for the co-development and co-production of defence equipment, the Ministry of Defence stated.
Also read:EAM Jaishankar meets Netherlands FM Caspar Veldkamp
The two countries reiterated their commitment to strengthening military-to-military engagement, and developing defence cooperation as a key pillar of the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership.
The talks also underscored the shared commitment of India and the Netherlands to a free, open, inclusive, and rule-based Indo-Pacific region. Emphasising the need for a closer defence partnership, the Ministers highlighted the importance of connecting the defence industries of both countries, particularly in niche and emerging technologies.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh with Netherlands Foreign Minister David Van Weel during a meeting, in New Delhi on December 18, 2025. Photo: X/@SpokespersonMoD via PTI.
A Letter of Intent on Defence Cooperation was exchanged between Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and the Ambassador of the Netherlands to India, Marisa Gerards, in the presence of the two Ministers. The document aims to provide an institutional framework for advancing defence collaboration.
Both sides agreed to explore new avenues of cooperation through the development of a defence industrial roadmap focusing on technology collaboration, co-production, and co-development of defence platforms and equipment for mutual benefit.
Strong people-to-people ties form the foundation of the bilateral relationship, with the large Indian diaspora in the Netherlands acting as a living bridge that continues to strengthen bonds of friendship between the two countries.

title: Unmet demands for money, new school uniform cited as causes for student’s suicide
summary: A nine-year-old boy's suicide in Hyderabad highlights distress over unmet financial demands for money and a new school uniform.
content:
A day after a nine-year-old boy allegedly ended his life at his residence in Chandanagar, the police on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) said preliminary inquiries suggest that the child may have been distressed over unmet demands for money and new school uniform.
The deceased was a Class IV student of Krishnaveni Talent School in Chandanagar. He was found unresponsive in the washroom of his residence near Rajinder Reddy Colony on Tuesday, December 16, at around 5.30 p.m., after which the incident was reported to the police.
During inquiries with family members and relatives, the police learnt that the child had been asking his parents for ₹100 over the past two days, which the parents did not give him.   The boy’ sparents had also recently bought him a new pair of shoes, following which he asked for a new school uniform as well. “His parents had told him that they would buy the uniform later,” said an official from the Chandanagar police.
The official added that the child was academically bright and a topper in his class, and there was no indication of academic pressure or reprimand from school or family members.
A case has been registered, and further investigation is underway.
(Roshini suicide prevention helpline number are: 8142020033/44 and 040 66202000/2001.)

title: IMA flags threats to nation’s affordable, accessible health system
summary: IMA warns that chronic under-investment threatens India's affordable healthcare system, urging increased government funding and regulation of foreign investments.
content:
India’s healthcare system, which is unique because of its high accessibility and affordability, driven largely by neighbourhood clinics and small to medium hospitals, is under serious threat because of chronic under-investment in public health by the government, insurance-driven price controls and unregulated foreign investment in health sector, according to the Indian Medical Association (IMA).
In the document, “IMA’s blueprint for a healthier India”, which was recently released as a policy document, IMA points out that the minimum government allocation for health sector alone should be 2.5% of the GDP and that separate provision should be made for the provision of drinking water, sanitation and such social determinants of health
The document is a summation of the concerns IMA has regarding the nation’s health sector, as well as policies that the organisation thinks that the nation should embrace for an equitable and accessible healthcare system, says V.R. Asokan, former national president of IMA. The document is being circulated by IMA amongst the Members of Parliament.
India’s overall health spending (public and private) is currently estimated to be 3.8% of its GDP, much lower than the average health spending by low-and-middle income nations, which is 5.2% .
Sustained underfunding of public sector facilities and the rapid growth of the private sector has contributed to rising out of pocket (OOP) costs on health care for households. Of this, a significant share, almost two-thirds of OOP expenses, are for purchasing Outpatient care, especially medicines.
Because households bear the burden of the high OOP health expenses in India, more than 55 million people are impoverished each year on account of expenses for ill health, says IMA.
In 2024, the government (Union and States) expenditure on health was ₹4.95 lakh crore, while the private health expenditure was ₹9.3 lakh crore, of which OOP expenditure was ₹8 lakh crore, while health insurance provided for Rs. 1.32 lakh crore.
In order to achieve the goals of Viksit Bharat 2047, allocation to the health sector should go up to at least 5% of the GDP by 2030, the document says.
IMA points out that FDI has brought capital and technology into Indian healthcare, but unregulated inflows could undermine medical autonomy and  alter the character of the Indian health system. It says that unregulated FDI and cross holdings  across hospitals, diagnostics, insurance, pharma sector and medical equipment could lead to a situation where business interests could begin to influence clinical decisions, commercial exploitation of patients happen, pushing up healthcare costs.
Apart from tighter government controls over FDI and strengthening domestic capital mobilisation, IMA urges the Union government to set up a National Healthcare Fund, akin to other government funds for specific purposes,  so that it could support healthcare entrepreneurs and enable hospital expansion. This would ensure that Indians retain strategic ownership and governance of the healthcare ecosystem and that clinical decision making will always remain with doctors, independent of commercial influence.
IMA also seeks to distinguish between Universal Health Care, which is all about equitable access to quality health care for all and Universal Health Coverage, which ensures that everyone has financial protection against healthcare costs.
It holds that the Government should be primarily responsible for guaranteeing universal health care.  IMA advocates a tax-based system of health financing. The public sector should be the primary provider, supplemented by strategic purchase from private  hospitals. Intermediaries such as insurance companies and TPAs should not control healthcare delivery, it says.
IMA warns that insurance-led models risk pushing India toward the US healthcare model of high cost, inequity, and exclusion.
It assesses AB-PMJAY to be a scheme which was well-intentioned, but which has serious flaws. Inadequate funding and unscientific package rates have made the scheme totally unviable for small and medium private hospitals, which are being forced to deliver services at sub-par costs.
IMA suggests that government hospitals should be funded directly by the Government and PMJAY should be exclusively used for strategic purchase from private sector with pricing of services based on a scientific system, It points out that the current allocation for PMJAY – ₹9,406 crore – is grossly inadequate

title: An open letter to the Indian government in support of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
summary: MGNREGA has captured the world’s attention with its demonstrated achievements and innovative design. To dismantle it now would be a historic error, say Thomas Piketty and other scholars, policymakers, lawyers, and civic actors
content:
We, the undersigned scholars, policymakers, lawyers, and civic actors (all friends of India), write to express profound concern regarding the imminent repeal of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). We urge a recommitment to this landmark legislation, which stands as the world’s most significant policy operationalizing a demand-driven, legal right to employment.
Originally passed with unanimous parliamentary support, MGNREGA transcends political lines. Its foundational principle — that the national government must guarantee an employment safety net — affirms economic dignity as a fundamental right. Empirical evidence underscores its impact.
MGNREGA routinely generates over 2 billion person-days of work annually for some 50 million households, with transformative equity: more than half of all workers are women, and about 40% are from Scheduled Castes or Tribes. The early years of the Act coincided with unprecedented rural wage growth, and studies confirmed the program’s positive effects on economic output and efficiency, dispelling myths of unproductivity.
However, chronic underfunding and payment delays have long hampered implementation. The current shift to devolve the scheme to states and without commensurate fiscal support, now threatens its existence. States lack the central government’s financial capacity. The new funding pattern creates a catastrophic Catch-22: states bear legal liability for providing employment, while central financing is withdrawn. Previously contributing only 25% of material costs, states now face burdens of 40% to 100% of total costs, ensuring poorer states will curb project approvals, directly stifling work demand.
This structural sabotage is compounded by discretionary “switch-off” powers, which allow the scheme to be suspended arbitrarily and render the guarantee meaningless. The unexplained defunding of West Bengal in the last three years exemplifies this political misuse. The new framework institutionalizes this risk, imposing unfunded mandates on states without consultation.
Editorial |The move to alter MGNREGS beyond recognition must be dropped
MGNREGA’s demand-driven design not only provides wages but also builds vital rural assets such as wells, roads, ponds, stimulating local economies. By making projects financially untenable for states, these multiplier effects are extinguished.
MGNREGA has captured the world’s attention with its demonstrated achievements and innovative design. To dismantle it now would be a historic error. It would abandon a proven instrument for poverty alleviation, social justice, and care for the environment. We call for its restoration through assured central funding, timely wages, and an unequivocal return to its foundational guarantee of the right to work.
Pavlina Tcherneva
Thomas Piketty
Isabelle Ferreras
Darrick Hamilton
Randall Wray
James Galbraith

title: Halaga village to switch off screens to help students study
summary: Halaga village in Belagavi enforces daily screen blackout to boost student study time, using sirens to signal the initiative.
content:
Members of the gram panchayat in Halaga village of Belagavi district have passed a resolution to urge all residents to switch off all kinds of screens, TV and mobile phones, to enable students to study.
The village will use sirens to signal the blackout between 7 p.m. and 9 p.m. every day.
The exercise was inspired by a similar experiment in Agran Dhul village near Sangli in Maharashtra.
Gram panchayat members and teachers will visit individual houses to urge parents to adhere to the timeline, said a release.

title: Parliament passes SHANTI Bill to open nuclear sector for private participation
summary: Parliament passes SHANTI Bill, allowing private participation in nuclear energy, highlighting its reliability over other renewable sources.
content:
Parliament on Thursday (December 18, 2025) passed the nuclear energy bill, with the Rajya Sabha giving its nod to the legislation that seeks to open the tightly-controlled civil nuclear sector for private participation.
Parliament Winter Session:Follow LIVE updates on December 18, 2025
The Upper House passed the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Bill by a voice vote. It waspassed in the Lok Sabhaon Wednesday (December 17, 2025).
Minister of State, Department of Atomic Energy, Jitendra Singh said nuclear is a reliable 24x7 power supply source, which is not so in the case of other renewable energy options.
He asserted that no compromise will be made with the safeguard mechanism in place.
EDITORIAL | ​Stepping stone: On nuclear policy, the SHANTI Bill
Replying to a discussion on the Bill, Mr. Singh allayed fears of radiation, saying so far there has been no report of any radiation-related hazards to the public.

title: Three foreigners arrested in EAGLE operation for alleged drug peddling
summary: Three foreign women arrested in Telangana for alleged drug peddling during EAGLE operation near Andhra Pradesh border.
content:
Three foreign women were arrested by the Telangana Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE) in a cross-State operation after they were found to be involved in drug peddling and related unlawful activities, officials said.
The arrests were made near the Telangana–Andhra Pradesh border following sustained electronic and physical surveillance by officials from Warangal. Although the suspects managed to discard a small quantity of drugs while attempting to evade the police during the chase, officers recovered fake passports and visas from their possession.
According to the EAGLE Force, the three women had left Delhi by flight to Visakhapatnam a day before a planned operation in the national capital. With most teams deployed to Delhi, a special team was constituted from Warangal to track the suspects, who had rented a service apartment in Visakhapatnam. Surveillance revealed that they visited the Andhra University campus and allegedly contacted two individuals, identified as Suresh and Harshavardhan, for the sale of drugs.
The police further said the women had been engaged by a man identified as Sandeep from Parvathipuram through a foreign female escort website and that he spent the night with them. By the time the police team reached the service apartment, the women had checked out and were travelling towards Hyderabad, where they were allegedly on their way to meet another contact, Pruthvichandra, at Quthbullapur.
Officials said all three were staying in India illegally and allegedly funding a luxurious lifestyle through drug peddling and flesh trade. A request has been made to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office in Hyderabad for a Movement Restriction Order against the accused.
The EAGLE Force has appealed to the public to remain vigilant and report suspicious activities, including illegal stay of foreign nationals and drug trafficking, assuring confidentiality and rewards for credible information.

title: Hijab row: Javed Akhtar demands unconditional apology from Bihar CM Nitish Kumar
summary: Javed Akhtar demands Bihar CM Nitish Kumar's apology for pulling down a Muslim doctor's hijab at a public event.
content:
Lyricist and poet Javed Akhtar on Thursday (December 18, 2025) demanded an unconditional apology from Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar forpulling down the hijab of a Muslim womanduring a function in Patna.
Also Read |Backlash not new for me, but pained to see it in Kolkata: Javed Akhtar
Last Monday (December 15), while distributing the appointment letter to newly appointed AYUSH doctors, Mr. Kumar pulled down the hijab of one of the doctors who came to receive the appointment letter.
Mr. Akhtar has demanded the apology by writing a post on social media platform ‘X’.
Every one who knows me even in the most cursory manner knows how much I am against the traditional concept of Parda but it doesn't mean that by any stretch of imagination I can accept what Mr Nitish Kumar has done to a Muslim lady doctor . I condemn it in very strong words . Mr…
“Everyone who knows me even in the most cursory manner knows how much I am against the traditional concept ofPardabut it doesn’t mean that by any stretch of imagination I can accept what Mr. Nitish Kumar has done to a Muslim lady doctor. I condemn it in very strong words. Mr. Nitish Kumar owes an unconditional apology to the lady,” Mr. Akhtar said in the post.
Ever since the video of his act went viral on social media, different sections of people have been criticising Mr. Kumar. Earlier, Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal posted the video on its social media platform X calling him “Sanghi”.
On December 16, Peoples Democratic Party chief Mehbooba Mufti posted the message on ‘X’ criticising Mr. Kumar and asked him to step down.
By posting the video, she wrote, “Having personally known & admired Nitish ji, I was shocked to see him pull down a young Muslim woman’s naqaab. Does one attribute it to old age or the normalisation of humiliating Muslims publicly. The fact that people around him watched this horrific incident unfold as some form of an entertainment is even more unsettling. Nitish Sahab perhaps it’s time you step down?”
Having personally known & admired Nitish ji I was shocked to see him pull down a young Muslim woman's naqaab. Does one attribute it to old age or the normalisation of humiliating Muslims publicly. The fact that people around him watched this horrific incident unfold as some form…pic.twitter.com/1nXl1Xzg1l
However, senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader and Union Minister Giriraj Singh supported the act of Mr. Kumar saying he had not done anything wrong.
“This is not an Islamic country, anyone he or she going to receive the appointment should show the face. Nitish Kumar ji did it as a guardian. Don’t you show your face when you go to passport office and airport. This is India not Pakistan, what Nitish ji did was right,”Mr. Singh told reporters in New Delhi.
Also, Uttar Pradesh Minister Sanjay Nishad has already triggered controversy by his statement in support of Mr. Kumar saying what would have happened if he had “touched” somewhere else.
While speaking to a local news channel Mr. Nishad on Wednesday said, “Arey, woh bhi toh aadmi hain na, peeche nahi padna chahiye. Naqab chhoo diya toh itna ho gaya...kahin aur chhoo dete toh kya ho jaata(He’s also a human being after all. One should not hound him like this. Just by touching the ‘hijab’ caused such an uproar, what would have happened if he had touched something else)”.
The Cabinet Minister in the Yogi Adityanath government was laughing while making the statement, following which Samajwadi Party leader Sumaiya Rana has filed a complaint seeking legal action against him.
In view of the hijab row, Bihar Janata Dal (United) State president Umesh Singh Kushwaha praised Mr. Kumar for doing several welfare schemes in the social, economic, and educational upliftment of the minority community.
Mr. Kushwaha said the community, which felt neglected before 2005, had now fully joined the mainstream of development due to the sincere and visionary efforts of Mr. Kumar. He asserted that in the past 20 years, the Nitish Kumar government had taken several concrete and historic steps in the interest of the minority community.
Meanwhile, Mr. Kumar on Thursday donated his one-month salary to the Janata Dal (United) fund. He handed over a cheque of his one-month salary to Lalan Kumar Saraf, Deputy Leader of the ruling party in the Legislative Council and Treasurer of the party.
Mr. Kumar appealed to party ministers, MPs, legislative party members, leaders holding important positions, and all wealthy and influential individuals who believe in the party’s ideology to contribute as much as possible to strengthen the party.

title: ACB traps two officials in separate bribery cases
summary: ACB arrests two officials in bribery cases, recovering ₹19,000 in Nirmal and Khammam districts for demanding illegal payments.
content:
The Anti Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Thursday (December 18, 2025) arrested two government officials in separate cases in Nirmal and Khammam districts for demanding and accepting bribes for official favours.
In the first case, G. Bheemanna, Senior Assistant at the Primary Health Centre Basara and in charge of PHC in Thanur mandal of Bhainsa, Nirmal district, was trapped by the ACB Adilabad range. Officials said he demanded and accepted ₹9,000 through PhonePe from a complainant at his residence in NB Nagar, Bhainsa, for preparing General Provident Fund (GPF), surrender leave and Fixed Travelling Allowance (FTA) bills and for processing medical reimbursement bills.
In a separate incident earlier in the day, Vusa Subha Kameshwari, Revenue Inspector at the office of the Tahsildar, Karepalli mandal in Khammam district, was trapped by the ACB Khammam range. She demanded and accepted ₹10,000 from a complainant at her residence in Karepalli for verification, attestation and forwarding of a family member certificate required for mutation of land records. The tainted amount was recovered from her possession.
Both the officials were arrested and produced before the special courts for SPE and ACB cases at Karimnagar and Warangal respectively. Further investigations are underway, and the identities of the complainants have been withheld for security reasons.
The ACB reiterated that members of the public can report demands for bribes by public servants through the toll free number 1064. Complaints can also be made via WhatsApp at 9440446106 or through the bureau’s official social media platforms.

title: Two die after being hit by tractor near Athani
summary: Two women died in Belagavi after being struck by a reversing tractor while working on a farm.
content:
Two women, sixtyfive-year-old Laxmibai Rudragoudar and sixty-year-old Baravva Kobadi, who were working in a farm, died when a sugarcane tractor hit them in Satti village near Athani of Belagavi district on Wednesday.
The tractor driver was backing up the vehicle. He had no idea that the two women were working behind the vehicle. The trolley hit the two women and they bled to death.
A case has been registered.

title: Five arrested in twin STF raids, 2.34 kg ganja and hash oil seized
summary: Five arrested in Hyderabad raids, with 2.34 kg of ganja and hash oil seized by the Telangana State Task Force.
content:
Five persons were arrested in two separate raids conducted by the State Task Force of the Telangana Prohibition and Excise Department in Hyderabad. The officials seized 2.34 kgs of ganja, 4.2 grams of hash oil, two mobile phones, and an autorickshaw used in committing the offence.
In the first operation, STF- A team, along with staff from the Dhoolpet excise station conducted a raid at a residence in Dilawar Gunj in Mangalhat area in Dhoolpet. Three persons, identified as Jaya Bai, Dilip Singh and Sunita Bai, were arrested and 1.220 kgs ganja was seized from them.
A case has been registered against Shivani Singh, Durgeshwari and two others in connection with the offence. The arrested accused and the seized contraband were handed over to the Dhoolpet excise station for further investigation.
Meanwhile, the STF- B team arrested two individuals, identified as K. Suryaprakash and K. Robert Antony Raj, during checks conducted in Madhapur. Officials seized 1.120 kgs ganja and 4.2 grams of hash oil. Two mobile phones and an auto-rickshaw used for offence were also confiscated.
The accused and the seized contraband was handed over to the Alwal excise station. Further investigation is underway in both cases.

title: Did land related issues play a key role in LDF’s setback in Idukki
summary: Land-related grievances and a surge in wild animal attacks have been cited as the primary reasons for the Left Democratic Front’s (LDF)  defeat in the local body elections in Idukki. The LDF suffered major setbacks across the district’s municipalities, district panchayat, block panchayats, and grama panchayats.
content:
Land-related grievances and a surge in wild animal attacks have been cited as the primary reasons for the Left Democratic Front’s (LDF)  defeat in the local body elections in Idukki. The LDF suffered major setbacks across the district’s municipalities, district panchayat, block panchayats, and grama panchayats.
The Idukki diocese of the Syro-Malabar Church, a major influential factor in the constituency, saw a shift in support as the LDF faced a debacle in areas under the diocese’s influence, where the Congress party gained the upper hand.
Fr. Jins Karakkatt, director of the Idukki Diocese Media Commission, stated that the government’s failure to address farmers’ issues was a key factor in the loss. “The people of the district realized that the government has failed to solve land-related issues over the past decade, and this was reflected in the local body election results,” Fr. Karakkatt said.
“Our demand is for the government to find solutions before the Assembly elections. If the LDF government fails to address these concerns, it will likely see a similar impact then,” said the priest.
Rasak Chooravelil, Chairman of the Idukki Land Freedom Movement (ILFM), noted that the election results reveal a broader trend among farming communities across the State’s hilly regions. “Farmers’ anger was reflected across Idukki, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, Kannur, Kozhikode, and Wayanad,” Mr Chooravelil said.
“ However, the LDF maintained its hold in the plantation belts of Devikulam, Udumbanchola, and Vandiperiyar, where these specific land issues were less prevalent “, he said.
Kerala Congress (Joseph) District president M.J. Jacob attributed the LDF’s poor performance specifically to the “anti-farmer” policies of the current government. “The Kerala Congress (M) and Minister Roshy Augustine supported land laws that hurt residents, resulting in their failure at the polls,” Mr. Jacob said.”
“ The construction ban, issues with the new Land Assignment (Amendment) Act, title deed delays, and wild animal attacks are unresolved crises.” Said Mr Jacob.
Following the election, the United Democratic Front (UDF) has taken control of the majority of the district’s local bodies, including both municipalities, the district panchayat, multiple block panchayats, and 36 out of the 52 grama panchayats.

title: KLE Society launches Ayurveda spa in Belagavi
summary: KLE Society inaugurates Ayushmati Ayurveda Spa in Belagavi, emphasizing Ayurveda's role in modern healthcare and holistic wellness.
content:
Minister for Medical Education Sharan Prakash Patil inaugurated KLE Society Ayushmati Ayurveda Spa in Belagavi on Wednesday.
He said that Ayurveda’s relevance is growing in preventive and promotive healthcare. He appreciated KLE Society’s role in preserving traditional medical wisdom while aligning it with modern science.
The centre set up at KAHER B. M. Kankanwadi Ayurveda College is a state-of-the-art wellness facility dedicated to authentic Ayurvedic therapies and holistic healing, KLE Society Chairman Prabhakar Kore said.
Director, Kerala Ayurvedic Clinic, Mumbai, Devika Deshmukh, MLAs Abhay Patil and Mahantesh Koujalgi, the former MLC Mahantesh Kavatagimath, director of BMKAC Suhas Shetty and others were present, said a release.

title: Work honestly and take decisions with courage, Bhatti advises AIS officers
summary: Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka urges AIS officers to serve with honesty, courage, and a humanitarian approach in leadership.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka has advised the All India Services officers to serve with honesty, take decisions with courage and adopt a humanitarian approach while moving forward in leadership roles.
Civil servants will do justice to their duties when people remember them as public servants, not just officers. The Deputy Chief Minister was speaking at a ceremony organised at the Marri Channa Reddy Human Resource Development Institute (MCRHRD) marking the successful completion of a 10-week training programme of AIS  officers on Thursday.
A total of 203 officers completed the course and the Deputy Chief Minister said they arrived here as engineers, doctors, economists, lawyers and technical experts and were leaving with the highest level of recognition and respect. Numerous opportunities lay ahead of them, befitting their talent and qualifications. He said the completion of this rigorous training programme marked not just an end, but the beginning of a new journey filled with responsibility, wisdom, discretion and public trust. Officers would face responsibilities, transfers, complex problems and files related to people’s lives besides situations which demand timely responses. A single negligent decision in public service could affect lives for years, he said advising the officers to discharge their duties with utmost commitment.
Stating that governance involved pressure, difficult situations, humane decision-making and constant efforts for public welfare, he said there would be praise as well as criticism, but officers should move forward with the conviction that everything they did was for the public. People at present were more informed, more questioning and often less patient. Officers should therefore continuously learn, unlearn when necessary, and transform themselves in tune with changing times.
Officers should maintain constant engagement with ordinary people, meet them with respect and listen patiently. Time spent with citizens was not time away from work, is was the very purpose of the work. Sitting in air-conditioned offices and clearing files was necessary, he said, but it could never replace human connection.

title: Stress on collective responsibility to prevent trafficking in women and children
summary: Workshop in Ballari emphasizes collective responsibility and awareness to combat trafficking in women and children through effective law implementation.
content:
Deputy Director of the Department of Women and Child Development M. Ramakrishna Naik on Thursday said that preventing trafficking in women and children is a collective responsibility and called for effective implementation of existing laws to protect vulnerable sections of society.
He was speaking after inaugurating a one-day district-level workshop on the Prevention of Trafficking in Women and Children and the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 at the old Nazirsaab Hall of the Zilla Panchayat in Ballari.
The workshop was jointly organised by the district administration, the Zilla Panchayat, the District Legal Services Authority and the Department of Women and Child Development.
Mr. Naik stressed the need to create awareness across all urban local bodies in the district about the adverse consequences of trafficking in human beings. He said that coordinated efforts among various government departments are crucial to effectively prevent trafficking in women and children.
Deputy Director of Public Instruction B. Umadevi highlighted the importance of sensitising schoolchildren about trafficking in human beings.
She said that schools must be treated as safe spaces for children and stressed that parents should be contacted if students remained absent for more than seven days to ensure their return to school.
She underlined the need for close monitoring of adolescent girls, especially at the high school level, and called for the active involvement of officials from partner departments.
Ms. Umadevi also said that no child should be subjected to bonded labour and that the protection of all children between the ages of six and 18 is a shared responsibility.
She added that the district administration is taking necessary steps to strengthen child protection mechanisms.
District Child Protection Officer Subhadra Devi said that the United Nations adopted a Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989 to which India became a signatory in 1992.
Since then, several laws, including the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, have been enacted to safeguard children’s rights.
She pointed out that children, women and senior citizens are particularly vulnerable to trafficking and are often exploited for bonded labour, organ trafficking, illegal overseas placement and begging.
Committees comprising officials at the gram panchayat, taluk and district levels have been formed to curb such practices and effective coordination among them is essential, she added.
Member of the State-level Core Committee on Human Trafficking William Christopher, who participated as a resource person, said that incidents of trafficking in human beings have increased in the recent years and are affecting children, women, youth and the working class.
He stressed the need for heightened vigilance, as women and children are more susceptible to deception and exploitation.
Officials later conducted an awareness session on the provisions of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956.

title: 12 cases booked against ‘Pakistan Zindabad’ slogan shouting in 30 months
summary: In the last two-and-a-half years, 12 cases, including six suo motu, were filed against those who had raised “Pakistan zindabad” slogans in Karnataka, Home Minister G. Parameshwara informed the Legislative Council on Thursday.
content:
In the last two-and-a-half years, 12 cases, including sixsuo motu, were filed against those who had raised “Pakistan zindabad” slogans in Karnataka, Home Minister G. Parameshwara informed the Legislative Council on Thursday.
Replying to C.T. Ravi’s question, he said that a total of 61,299suo motucases had been filed in the State by the police in the last two-and-a-half years pertaining to various incidents and of them chargesheets had been filed in 57,646 cases.
The Home Minister said that 12 persons were arrested in the ‘Pakistan zindabad’ sloganeering cases and of these chargesheets had been filed in five cases, B report in two cases, C report in one case, and three cases were under investigation. In one case FSL report was awaited, he added.

title: Expert seeks inclusion of Indian Knowledge System in school curriculum
summary: Expert advocates for integrating Indian Knowledge System into school curriculum to enhance education on heritage, culture, and traditional practices.
content:
Former Vice Chancellor of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University and director of Valmiki Research Center of Ramanarayanam temple Dr. Hanumanthu Lajapathirai said that school curriculum needs to be updated and include aspects of the Indian Knowledge System. Lessons related to indigenous wisdom, heritage, culture, governance, philosophy, environmental practices, traditional medicine and others need to be included in the school education.
He was speaking at the two day awareness programme on '’Relevance of Valmiki Ramayanam for the present society-Indian Knowledge System-National Education Policy-2020' organised at the Government Degree College in Vizianagaram on Thursday.
Principal of the College K. Rekha, Lecturer of Telugu M. Rama Geeta Devi thanked the representatives of the Ramanarayam temple for conducting essay competitions for degree students to raise awareness about the Ramayana and dharma followed by Lord Rama till January 2, 2026.

title: SNIST students excel at Smart India Hackathon
summary: SNIST students excel at Smart India Hackathon
content:
Sreenidhi Institute of Science and Technology (SNIST) students excelled at the Smart India Hackathon 2025 Grand Finale, and its ‘Team Vertex’ emerged as a joint winner in the Hardware Edition.
The SIH 2025 grand finale was conducted this month, and four teams from SNIST qualified for the finale. In the Hardware Edition, Team Vertex (PS ID 25221) developed a VR and eye-tracking solution for EV product design, winning the top position and securing a cash prize of ₹75,000.
Other teams of SNIST like Team Trata, designed a hardware system to detect and prevent unauthorised use of electric fences, Team Margadarsh presented a civic issue reporting app for Jharkhand citizens, while Team Civic Pulse showcased a remote classroom solution for rural colleges in Rajasthan.
Dr. T. Ch. Siva Reddy, principal, Dr. Shruti Bhargava Choubey, dean – Innovation, and K. Abhijit Rao, CEO, Sreenidhi Educational Group, congratulated the winners. The Smart India Hackathon (SIH) is India’s flagship national innovation initiative, bringing together the brightest student minds to solve real-world challenges posed by government ministries, public sector units, and industry.

title: Hoax bomb threat to Nampally Criminal Court triggers security checks
summary: Hoax bomb threat at Nampally Criminal Court prompts extensive security checks, later declared false; police investigate sender.
content:
A bomb threat email sent to the Nampally Criminal Court complex on Thursday (December 18, 2025) triggered a full-scale security drill, prompting extensive anti-sabotage checks before it was declared a hoax.
According to Nampally Inspector K. Narayana Reddy, the email was received at around 10.30 a.m., following which local police, along with the Hyderabad police’s bomb detection and disposal squad, immediately swung into action. Security teams conducted a thorough search of the court premises, which continued until about 2 p.m., after which the threat was ruled out. The inspector said the email was non-specific, merely claiming that an explosive had been planted inside the court complex and warning that it could detonate at any time.
A case has been registered in connection with the hoax threat, and police said efforts are underway to trace the sender.

title: Income soars to ₹210 crore at Sabarimala
summary: Sabarimala temple income reaches ₹210 crore as pilgrim numbers soar, prompting plans for special passes and enhanced crowd management.
content:
Riding on the back of a sharp rise in pilgrim inflow, income at the Sabarimala Ayyappa temple has reached ₹210 crore. Of this, ₹106 crore was earned from the sale of ‘aravana’. Compared to previous years, there has been a significant increase in revenue, said K. Jayakumar, president, Travancore Devaswom Board.
As the Sabarimala pilgrimage season, which began on November 16, completed one month, the total number of devotees who have had darshan of Lord Ayyappa reached 28 lakh. The number of pilgrims arriving through forest trekking routes has also increased this season, with a total of 46,690 devotees reaching Sannidhanam via the Azhuthakkadavu-Pampa route, while 74,473 pilgrims arriving through the Sathram route. Discussions are ongoing with the police and the Forest department to regulate this flow, including the introduction of special passes for those arriving via the Erumely-Azhutha forest path. Overall, 25,60,297 devotees reached Sabarimala from Pampa.
Meanwhile, a joint inspection by the police and the Forest department was carried out along the Pullumedu forest trail on Thursday to ensure the safety of Ayyappa pilgrims. The inspection followed an incident on the night of December 17, when elephants damaged the roof and fencing of the Forest department’s check-post at Pandithavalam
Following this, officials thoroughly examined the forest trail in the morning, confirming that it was free from any wildlife hazards. Once safety was ensured, devotees were allowed to proceed along the route.
Meanwhile, the restriction of 20 tins of aravana per person will continue. Following the mandala puja, the temple will close on December 27, and reopen after three days. Additional aravana will be produced to build buffer stock, said K. Jayakumar, president, TDB.
The pilgrimage season began this year with a stock of 45 lakh aravana tins. While daily sales were initially expected to be around 3.5 lakh tins, actual sales averaged 4.5 lakh tins a day, rapidly depleting stocks. Currently, more than 10 lakh tins are available as reserve. At present, about 3 lakh tins are produced daily, with an additional 1 lakh drawn from reserve stock.
Efforts are also under way to resolve logistical issues related to serving Kerala-style meals as part of ‘annadanam.’ Adequate stocks of provisions have already been procured.
Meanwhile, Mr. Jayakumar said there was no rigidity regarding spot booking. The court has allowed flexibility based on circumstances, and decisions will be taken depending on pilgrim inflow. For now, the daily limit of 5,000 spot bookings will continue.
The TDB also aims to adopt greater use of technology in managing the pilgrimage. A technology master plan is being prepared, in line with the court directives. AI and GPS-based systems could be used to estimate travel time from Nilackal to Pampa and waiting time on queues, enabling smoother crowd management, the TDB president added.

title: R. Ramakumar chosen as Calicut varsity senate nominee for V-C search panel
summary: R. Ramakumar elected as Calicut varsity's senate nominee for the Vice-Chancellor search panel amid a competitive election.
content:
R. Ramakumar, member, Kerala State Planning Board, and Professor, Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai, has been chosen as the senate nominee for the search-cum-selection committee that will pick a new Vice-Chancellor (V-C) for the University of Calicut (CU).
Mr. Ramakumar got elected at a special senate meeting held on the university campus at Tenhipalam in Malappuram on Thursday (December 18). According to sources, 58 members participated in the election process presided over by senior member M. Rajan. Mr. Ramakumar was proposed for the post by the pro-Left members.
Those belonging to the United Democratic Front (UDF) proposed the name of Achuthsankar S. Nair, former Director, Centre for Development of Imaging Technology, and the pro-BJP members proposed the name of K. Muralidharan, principal scientist, Central Plantation Crops Research Institute. Mr. Ramakumar bagged 33 votes, Mr. Nair got 20 votes, and Mr. Muralidharan got four votes.
This is the third time the senate is choosing its nominee for the panel. Dharmaraj Adat and A. Sabu, who were earlier picked for the post, on August 23 and October 30, respectively, had declined to take up the job. Thursday’s meeting was held following the direction of the Kerala High Court, where the State government had challenged the Chancellor’s constitution of the search-cum-selection committee on October 31. The court had also asked the university to ensure the consent of the senate nominee.
Meanwhile, when pro-UDF members asked if Mr. Ramakumar had given his consent to be in the panel, pro-Left members reportedly replied that the Registrar would inform him of the senate’s decision.

title: Hyderabad CP calls for zero-delay response at tri-commissionerate meet
summary: Hyderabad CP V.C. Sajjanar emphasizes zero-delay crime response across jurisdictions to enhance policing effectiveness at tri-commissionerate meeting.
content:
Boundaries must never come in the way of effective policing, said Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) and directed officers to strictly implement a ‘Zero Delay’ policy to ensure immediate response to crimes and swift relief to victims.
The directive was issued during a coordination meeting of the Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Rachakonda police commissionerates held at the Telangana Integrated Command and Control Centre in Banjara Hills. The meeting was chaired by Mr. Sajjanar and attended by Cyberabad Police Commissioner Avinash Mohanty and Rachakonda Police Commissioner G. Sudheer Babu, along with senior officers from the three commissionerates.
Addressing the gathering, the official said criminals increasingly exploit jurisdictional gaps by committing offences in one area and taking shelter in another. He warned that any delay caused by confusion over territorial limits could allow offenders to escape. “There should be no communication gap between field-level personnel. Regardless of where a crime occurs, the nearest police unit must respond immediately without debating jurisdiction,” he stated.
“When criminals do not respect borders, the police should not either,” Mr. Sajjanar said, adding that the ultimate objective was a safer Hyderabad through technology-driven policing and unified action. He warned that there would be no leniency for those disturbing law and order, regardless of where they attempt to hide.
Commissioner Mohanty said the rapid expansion of the IT Corridor and Financial District made seamless coordination and integration of CCTV networks essential for tracking criminal movements in real time. Rachakonda Police Commissioner Babu proposed the formation of joint teams to tackle organised crime and illegal activities such as ganja smuggling, emphasising that intelligence sharing remained the backbone of effective urban policing.
The meeting was attended by Additional Commissioner of Police (Crimes) M. Srinivasulu, Joint Commissioners Tafseer Iqubal, D. Joel Davis and Gajarao Bhupal, and Deputy Commissioners of Police from all three commissionerates.

title: KKCCI seeks restoration of flights, industrial revival in meetings with Kharge, Kumaraswamy
summary: KKCCI urges restoration of Kalaburagi flights and industrial revival in meetings with leaders Kharge and Kumaraswamy.
content:
A delegation from the Kalyana Karnataka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KKCCI) met senior national leaders in New Delhi during the ongoing Winter Session of Parliament to press for key development demands in the Kalyana Karnataka region, including the early restoration of flight services to and from Kalaburagi and the revival of sick industries in the district.
The delegation, led by KKCCI president Sharanabasappa M. Pappa and honorary secretary Shivraj V. Inginshetty, met Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge at his residence on Wednesday.
During the meeting, the delegation highlighted the adverse impact of the suspension of flight services to and from Kalaburagi on trade, industry, healthcare access and regional connectivity and sought immediate steps to restore air connectivity to the region.
Mr. Kharge assured the delegation of his support and informed it that he has already spoken to the Union Minister for Civil Aviation on the issue, the KKCCI said in a statement issued on Thursday.
On the same day, the delegation also met Union Minister for Heavy Industries H.D. Kumaraswamy to discuss the revival of sick industrial units in Shahabad and the need for developing an industrial corridor in the Kalaburagi region to promote industrial growth and employment generation.
According to the KKCCI, both Mr. Kharge and Mr. Kumaraswamy extended their support to facilitating an appointment with the Union Minister for Civil Aviation to take forward the demand for early restoration of flight services to and from Kalaburagi.
Members of the delegation included Santosh Nandyal, Lingaraj Bhavikatti and Ravishankar Jhamadarkhani.
The chamber thanked the leaders for their time and positive response and said that it will continue to engage with the Union government to pursue inclusive development of the Kalyana Karnataka region.

title: New crest gates for Tungabhadra Dam by June 2026: Deputy CM
summary: After the water level recedes to 1,613 ft in the Tungabhadra reservoir by December-end, the installation of new crest gates would be taken up and would be completed by June 2026, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar informed the Karnataka Legislative Council on Thursday.
content:
After the water level recedes to 1,613 ft in the Tungabhadra reservoir by December-end, the installation of new crest gates would be taken up and would be completed by June 2026, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar informed the Karnataka Legislative Council on Thursday.
Replying to a question by Basanagouda Badarli, he said that design and drawings of the crest gates had been verified by the Chief Engineer of Central Design Organisation, Vijayawada, and certified by Director, Gates Design (NW&S) of Directorate of CWC, New Delhi.
Subsequently the installation work of gate no. 19  worth ₹1.66 cr and work worth of ₹ 34.48 crore pertaining to changing of 32 gates had been entrusted to M/s Hardware Tolls and Machinery Project Ltd. Ahmedabad, Mr. Shivakumar said.
“At present out of gate no. 19 and remaining 32 crest gates, the fabrication of 14 crest gates has been completed, the dismantling process has begun from December 12. It has been planned to begin installation of the crest gates after the water level in the reservoir recedes to 1,613 ft by December-end and complete the work by June 2026,” he said.
The Deputy Chief Minister said that while Karnataka had released ₹10 crore for the work, Andhra Pradesh had released ₹20 crore and steps would be taken to release the remaining amount for the work.

title: Concerns mount over suspected bird flu outbreak in Kuttanad
summary: Concerns rise over a suspected bird flu outbreak in Kuttanad as unexplained poultry deaths prompt urgent investigations.
content:
The poultry farmers in Kuttanad are once again facing a festive-season nightmare as unexplained deaths of chickens and ducks raise fears of a looming bird flu outbreak in the region.
Widespread deaths of broiler chickens and ducks in farms across western Kottayam have cast a shadow over the festive cheer. Official reports indicate around 5,000 chicken deaths within the limits of the Kottayam municipality so far. However, farmers claim the actual toll is likely double that figure, with significant losses reported in Vaikom, Manjoor, and Thiruvarppu.
Amid rising concerns about a potential avian influenza outbreak, the Animal Husbandry department has launched an investigation. Samples have been collected and sent to the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal for analysis to determine the cause of the deaths.
Official data reveals that one farmer reported a loss of approximately 5,000 chickens, while another reported 350 deaths in wards 37 and 38 of the Kottayam municipality. While additional deaths have been noted in Vaikom, Ullala, Chengalam, and Thiruvarppu, officials clarified that no formal reports have yet been received from these areas. Meanwhile, quail deaths have been confirmed in Manjoor.
Many of the affected deaths occurred in integrated chicken farms operating under contract arrangements, where companies from Tamil Nadu supply chicks, feed, and other resources, and reclaim the birds once they reach maturity. Animal Husbandry officials noted that farmers involved in these arrangements typically rely solely on the companies for support, often bypassing departmental assistance.
Although bird flu has not been confirmed, the officials highlighted the significant presence of migratory birds in affected areas. “Historically, outbreaks tend to coincide with the arrival of migratory birds. November through March is their peak migration season, making this region particularly vulnerable,” an official explained.
Authorities have already alerted poultry farmers in the region and advised them to implement precautionary measures. For farmers raising birds for Christmas and New Year celebrations, any outbreak could mean severe economic losses. Last year, a strict ban on poultry products from September to December was imposed to contain the disease.

title: Live-in relationships are not illegal, State must protect such couples, says Allahabad High Court
summary: Allahabad High Court rules live-in relationships are legal, ordering police protection for 12 couples threatened by families.
content:
Stating that the concept of a live-in relationship may not be acceptable to all, but such relationships are not illegal, the Allahabad High Court on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) ordered the Uttar Pradesh police to provide protection to 12 live-in couples allegedly threatened by their families.
The Bench of Justice Vivek Kumar Singh, who was hearing the petitions filed by 12 women from different parts of the State, stated that it cannot be said that living together without the sanctity of marriage constitutes an offence.
The court cited the example of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, which says that a woman who is in a domestic relationship has been provided protection, maintenance, etc. But the act has not used the word “wife”.
“Once an individual, who is a major, has chosen his/her partner, it is not for any other person, be it a family member, to object and cause a hindrance to their peaceful existence. It is the bounden duty of the State, as per the Constitutional obligations casted upon it, to protect the life and liberty of every citizen,” the court said.
It added that the right to human life is to be treated on a much higher pedestal, regardless of a citizen being minor or major, married or unmarried, and due to the mere fact that the petitioners have not solemnised marriage, would not deprive them of their fundamental rights as envisaged in the Constitution of India.
The court also cited Section 114 of the Indian Evidence Act/Section 119(1) of Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which States that if couples live together for a significant amount of time as husbands and wives, they will be presumed to be married.
“The courts shall apply this presumption to protect the rights of the parties in a live-in relationship, i.e. women and the children born as a result thereof,” it added.

title: Yashoda Hospital completes over 1,000 major robotic surgeries in a year
summary: Yashoda Hospital in Hyderabad achieves a milestone of over 1,000 major robotic surgeries in a year, showcasing advanced medical excellence.
content:
Yashoda Hospitals Hitech City has completed over 1,000 complex major robotic surgeries within a single year. The achievement was announced at an event in Hyderabad on Thursday.
Yashoda Hospitals managing director Dr. G. S. Rao said the milestone includes 434 gynaecology and gynaec-oncology surgeries, 310 general, gastrointestinal and hepatopancreatobiliary procedures, 177 urology surgeries, 79 thoracic surgeries, as well as highly complex robotic procedures in head and neck surgery.  “The hospital had consistently invested in new technologies and integrated them with patient-centred care,” he added.
Addressing the gathering, Madhapur DCP Riti Raj, who was the chief guest for the event, said the milestone is a matter of pride for Hyderabad, Telangana and the wider Telugu States. She noted that the completion of over 1,000 complex robotic surgeries in a year reflects the hospital’s commitment to advanced medical technology, patient safety and clinical excellence.

title: GBA aims to transform storm-water drains from sewage-carrying channels into public and ecological spaces
summary: GBA plans to convert Bengaluru's storm-water drains into ecological spaces, addressing flooding and groundwater issues through nature-based solutions.
content:
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) aims to transform storm-water drains from sewage-carrying channels into public and ecological spaces, Chief Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao, said on Thursday, underscoring the need for nature-based solutions to address Bengaluru’s recurring flooding and rapidly declining groundwater levels.
Mr. Rao was speaking at a multi-stakeholder dialogue titled ‘Nature-based Solutions for Bengaluru: Reflections on Drainage’, convened by the Jana Urban Space Foundation (JUSF) in the city.
The convention brought together senior government officials, urban practitioners, researchers, civil society organisations, and industry stakeholders to deliberate on reimagining the city’s drainage systems through ecological approaches, according to a release.
Outlining the GBA’s priorities, Mr. Rao said, “Efforts were under way to prevent sewage from entering storm-water drains, strengthen underground drainage networks, create additional storm-water capacity, and make better use of Bengaluru’s lake system by enhancing storage.”
He further stressed that restoring the ecological function of drains and lakes was critical to improving the city’s flood resilience.
Mr. Rao also released a draft working paper titled “Rebuilding Urban Drainage Systems: Learnings from Nallurahalli Nallah Rejuvenation in Bengaluru”. The paper gains insights from a nature-based solutions-led pilot project and outlines pathways to integrate such approaches across storm-water drains, nallahs, lakes, and groundwater recharge systems at scale. The draft has been shared to invite informed critique and inputs before finalisation, a release stated.
The dialogue featured five thematic discussions examining urban drainage and nallahs, lake rejuvenation and community stewardship, rainwater harvesting, institutional and financing frameworks, and best practices from other Indian cities.
Participants noted that Bengaluru’s water challenges marked by flooding during monsoons and groundwater depletion despite significant rainfall stem from systemic gaps in planning, governance, and coordination rather than isolated infrastructure failures.
According to the release, speakers emphasised the need to break departmental silos and move away from fragmented, project-based engineering responses towards integrated, catchment-based approaches that combine ecological design with resilient grey infrastructure. There was broad consensus that accelerating run-off by widening drains often shifts flood risks downstream while worsening groundwater depletion.

title: Forum flags delays in ACB prosecutions, says conviction rate stuck at 50%
summary: Forum highlights delays in ACB prosecutions and low conviction rates, urging swift action to combat corruption in Telangana.
content:
The Forum for Good Governance has written to Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy flagging ‘abnormal delays’ in prosecuting Anti-Corruption Bureau cases, warning that prolonged proceedings and low conviction rates were undermining deterrence against corruption in Telangana’s administration.
In a representation dated December 18, the forum said the ACB had registered 621 cases over the past five years, averaging about 120 cases annually. However, it alleged that once the Director General of ACB completes inquiries and submits reports seeking permission to prosecute the accused officials, decisions in the Secretariat are often delayed, sometimes by more than a year. The forum claimed that sanction to prosecute was accorded in barely a quarter of cases, with the remainder being sent for departmental inquiries or to the Tribunal for Disciplinary Proceedings, where cases can take decades to conclude.
The forum further pointed out that even after charge-sheets are filed, cases frequently remain pending in courts for more than a decade, with only about 20 to 25 cases being disposed of each year. Citing ACB data, it said that in 2023–24, only 19 old cases were disposed of, resulting in nine convictions and 10 acquittals, while in 2024–25, a total of 22 cases were disposed of, with 12 convictions and 10 acquittals. Overall, the conviction rate stands at around 50%, it said.
The forum referred to a disproportionate assets case registered against a motor vehicle inspector, B. Bhadru Naik, in December 2008. Although the officer was suspended and an inquiry report submitted seeking prosecution sanction, it took 16 months for the government to accord permission, during which time the officer was reinstated. A charge-sheet was filed in 2011, but the case remains pending even after 15 years, the forum said. It added that the officer was subsequently promoted and later caught again while allegedly accepting a bribe, leading to a second case that is still under inquiry. This, the forum argued, reflected a lack of fear of punishment and pointed to rampant corruption.
The forum’s president M. Padmanabha Reddy urged the Chief Minister to issue directions to ensure prosecution sanctions are granted within a month of being sought, accused officers are not given postings until cases are disposed of, trials are completed within two years, and the conviction rate is raised from 50% to 90%. The forum said such measures were essential to restore public confidence and effectively curb corruption in administration.

title: Karnataka govt. to recruit more bilingual teachers
summary: The State government would appoint over 11,000 schoolteachers to reduce long pending vacancies in the Department of Education, Madhu Bangarappa, Minister for School Education and Literacy, said on Thursday.
content:
The State government would appoint over 11,000 schoolteachers to reduce long pending vacancies in the Department of Education, Madhu Bangarappa, Minister for School Education and Literacy, said on Thursday.
Responding to queries by members Harish Poonja and Sharanu Salagar in the Assembly, he said that the process of recruitment would begin soon.
He said the government was not opposed the idea of having English teachers in government schools.
“We have already begun hiring bilingual teachers, who can teach English and other subjects. We will continue doing this and see that all schools, including Kannada medium and other medium schools, have teachers who teach English as a subject,” he said.
To a question on teachers being assigned non-academic duties like census and election-related work, the Minister said he was not personally inclined to it, but there was no alternative.
“We are bound by several directives of the Union government that ask us to depute teachers for such duties. It is also due to the general realisation that such a large number of employees that are so skilled and credible are found only in the Education Department,’’ he said.

title: Baby found in Ammathottil in Thiruvananthapuram
summary: A healthy 10-day-old girl named Ithal was found in Ammathottil, Thiruvananthapuram; adoption inquiries welcomed.
content:
A 10-day-old infant was received in the Ammathottil cradle of the Kerala State Council for Child Welfare at Thycaud here early Wednesday.
The infant, weighing approximately 3.3 kg, was given a preliminary examination and then taken to Women and Children Hospital, Thycaud, for a detailed medical check-up where she was found healthy.
The girl child was named Ithal, council general secretary G.L. Arun Gopi said in a statement.
Nine children (six girls, three boys) have been received by the council here from October till now.
Anyone claiming the child should contact the council at the earliest as her adoption procedures have to be initiated, Mr. Arun Gopi said.

title: Notification shortly for recruitment of 3,600 policemen, says Parameshwara
summary: Home Minister G. Parameshwara announces upcoming recruitment of 3,600 policemen after Finance Department approval.
content:
Home Minister G. Parameshwara told the Legislative Council on Thursday that recruitment notification for filling 3,600 vacant posts in the Police Department will be issued shortly, as the Finance Department has given the requisite approval.
