In the future, we will take measures to create new posts based on the patient load,” he said.

title: Wanaparthy agriculture officer caught taking ₹10,000 bribe
summary: Wanaparthy agriculture officer arrested for accepting ₹10,000 bribe in exchange for fertilizer supply favors, reveals ACB investigation.
content:
The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) sleuths arrested the District Agriculture Officer of Wanaparthy district on Friday (December 19)  while taking bribe from a complainant in return for extending an official favour related to the supply of fertiliser.
The accused officer, identified as Puppala Anjaneyulu Goud, was trapped by the Mahabubnagar Range unit of the ACB while accepting a part of the bribe amount. Investigation revealed that the officer had demanded a bribe of ₹20,000 on October 23, 2025, to ensure regular supply of fertiliser (urea) to the complainant without any interruption.
Investigators said that the officer had already accepted ₹3,000 on October 28, 2025, as part of the demanded amount, and was caught while receiving another ₹10,000 on Friday. The bribe amount was recovered from his possession.
Following his arrest, he was produced before the special court for SPE and ACB cases at Nampally in Hyderabad. The case is currently under investigation.
In a public advisory, the ACB reiterated that citizens facing demands for bribes from public servants can contact its toll-free number 1064 to report such incidents. The bureau assured that the identity of complainants would be kept confidential.

title: Collector, SP launch ‘Drugs Vaddhu Bro’ rally in Kadiri
summary: The 'Drugs Vaddhu Bro' rally in Kadiri promotes drug awareness and encourages community action for a drug-free district.
content:
The Sri Sathya Sai district administration on Saturday launched the ‘Drugs Vaddhu Bro’ awareness campaign at Kadiri town, with senior officials of various government departments and public representatives calling for collective action to make the district drug-free.
District Collector A. Shyam Prasad and Superintendent of Police S. Satish Kumar flagged off the programme at the R&B Guest House. Addressing students, DWCRA groups and members of NGOs, the Collector cautioned that drug consumption posed a serious threat to human survival and social well-being. He urged the public to act responsibly and report instances of ganja and drug use to toll-free numbers or local police stations. He appealed to the public to take a pledge against drug consumption.
Superintendent of Police Satish Kumar said drug abuse was a growing challenge that directly impacted youth and law and order. He warned that possession, consumption and sale of ganja and drugs were punishable offences, carrying imprisonment ranging from 10 to 20 years depending on the quantity involved. He disclosed that 40 to 42 persons had been arrested in ganja-related cases in Kadiri alone. The SP said that preventive detention and externment measures were being initiated against repeat offenders.
Later, a public rally was taken out from the R&B Guest House to the RTC Circle, with participants displaying placards and raising slogans against drugs. A human chain was formed at the RTC Circle, and a pledge to stay away from narcotics was administered.

title: NCVET recognises A.P. Board of Intermediate Education as awarding body
summary: A.P. Board of Intermediate Education gains NCVET recognition, enabling nationally certified vocational skills starting with Sericulture Technician qualification.
content:
The  (BIE) has become the first school education board in India to be recognised by the National Council of Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) as an awarding body (dual category).
“This milestone enables nationally recognised certification of vocational skills, beginning with the approved Sericulture Technician qualification, and opens up future-ready employment pathways for our youth,” HRD Minister Nara Lokesh posted on social media platform ‘X’ on Saturday.
The NCVET is an autonomous, non-statutory and regulatory body under Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship for monitoring the institutions engaged in providing short-term and long-term educational training in vocational education and designing the basic standards required for operations of such institutions.
The NCVET and the State Board of Intermediate Education signed an agreement on Friday for the NCVET’s recognition as awarding body (AB-Dual) to BIEAP.
Through this recognition, the BIEAP will be eligible to award, assess and certify learners where training is directly being imparted by the Awarding Body in campuses or training centers owned or fully managed by it for its approved or adopted qualifications.
As part of the initial rollout, the Sericulture Technician Qualification submitted by BIEAP has already been approved by NCVET.

title: Himachal orders drug recall after 47 samples fail quality tests
summary: Himachal Pradesh orders recall of 47 substandard drug samples, affecting medications for fever, heart attacks, and diabetes.
content:
Notices have been issued to companies whose medicine samples failed quality tests, and they have been instructed to recall their stock from the market, according to Himachal Pradesh State Drug Controller Manish Kapoor.
“Out of 200 medicine samples tested nationwide, 47 were manufactured in the State. These include medications for fever, heart attacks, and diabetes. The failed samples originated from various districts: 28 from Solan, 18 from Sirmaur, and one from Una. Notices have been issued to the respective companies,” officials said on Saturday (December 20, 2025).
In November 2025, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) collected 65 samples, while the State Drug Controller collected 135 samples. Of these, 47 samples were identified as substandard. "Notices have been issued to the companies whose medicine samples failed the quality tests. They have also been asked to recall the stock from the market," Mr. Kapoor said.
“Explanations have been sought, and actions will be taken against the companies in accordance with regulations,” Mr. Kapoor informed media personnel in Solan.
The samples of medicines which failed the quality tests include Paracetamol for fever, Clopidogrel and Aspirin for heart attacks, Metformin for lowering blood sugar, Ramipril for heart conditions, Sodium Valproate for epilepsy, and Mebeverine Hydrochloride for reducing muscle spasms, along with several other medicines deemed substandard.
There has been a consistent trend of medicine samples manufactured in the State failing quality tests. Health Minister Dhani Ram Shandil had earlier announced that companies with recurring failures would be blacklisted, and that the government has been taking action in that regard.
Additionally, a monthly alert issued by the central drug regulator in March 2025 noted that 38 drug samples produced by various pharmaceutical companies in the State did not meet quality parameters.

title: Watch: K. Kavitha on contesting polls and the welfare vs development debate | Talking Politics
summary: In this episode of Talking Politics, K. Kavitha discusses her plans to contest the upcoming elections and reflects on the thin line between welfare politics and development. She outlines her political thinking, priorities, and how she views the balance between social welfare schemes and long-term development in today’s political landscape.

title: Chandrababu Naidu launches ‘Mustabu’, counsels schoolstudents to maintain personal hygiene
summary: Chandrababu Naidu launches 'Mustabu' to promote hygiene among students, emphasizing personal care and goal-setting for success.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu launched ‘Mustabu’, a programme aimed at promoting self-hygiene among school-going students, at the Social Welfare Girls Residential School at Tallapalem of Kasimkota mandal in Anakapalli district on December 20, 2025 (Saturday).
After launching the programme, Mr. Naidu had a friendly interaction with the students and spoke to them about the importance of maintaining personal hygiene. He advised the students to follow basic habits such as washing face regularly, keeping nails clean, wearing neat uniform and shoes, combing hair properly, and dressing in a proper manner.
“These habits will help improve your hygiene and attentiveness, and concentrate better on your studies. These habits also help develop discipline, build confidence, encourage creativity, and support overall self-development,” the Chief Minister said.
Mr. Naidu said that ‘Mustabu’ was first conceptualised and implemented by the Collector of Parvathipuram-Manyam district. “Impressed by the concept, I decided to implement the programme across the State,” he added.
Mr. Naidu also encouraged the students to set clear goals in life, dream big, work hard, and strive to reach greater heights. He said children were a valuable asset of the State, and noted that many students come from families where parents work as daily wagers and make great sacrifices to educate their children.
He urged the students to recognise their parents’ efforts, study well, secure good jobs, and help their families come out of poverty. He further said that students should become part of the knowledge economy and excel in their lives.
The Chief Minister also informed the students that the government was providing financial assistance under the Thalliki Vandanam scheme and supplying textbooks, uniforms, and meals free of cost to help them achieve better academic results.
Mr. Naidu also announced that health check-ups would soon be conducted for nearly 75 lakh students across the State. He appreciated IT and Education Minister N. Lokesh and other Ministers for their efforts in shaping the future of the students and working towards their overall development.
R. Gunasreevalli, a second-year MPC student from B.R. Ambedkar Gurukulam, Tallapalem, interacted with the Chief Minister during the programme. Mr. Naidu personally spoke with class monitors and enquired about how they were checking the neatness of other students as part of the ‘Mustabu’ initiative.

title: Telangana to introduce spoken English training for MBBS students
summary: Telangana to implement spoken English training for MBBS students to reduce language barriers and prevent dropouts.
content:
The Telangana government is set to introduce spoken English and communication skills’ training for MBBS students in the State, after concerns were raised that language barriers were contributing to stress, isolation and dropout in students hailing from rural and economically weaker backgrounds.
The decision was taken at a recent review meeting chaired by Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha.
Many students are struggling to cope with English-medium curriculum, particularly medical terminology, leading to severe academic stress and in some cases, discontinuation of studies.
Telangana currently has 35 government and 26 private medical colleges, together offering around 9,000 MBBS seats.
A senior Health official, present at the meeting, said that the Minister observed that talented students should not be pushed out of medical education due to language-related disadvantages.
He directed the Health department to roll out structured Spoken English and communication skills programmes for first and second-year MBBS students. “The training is to be on the lines of language courses already being implemented in government nursing colleges, where students receive instruction in English as well as foreign languages,” the official added.
The review also flagged concerns over the financial burden faced by students admitted to private medical colleges under the Convener Quota. While tuition fees for meritorious poor students are reimbursed by the State Government, private college managements have been collecting large sums under additional heads such as hostel charges, mess fees, library fees and other amenities. These so-called hidden costs are running into lakhs of rupees annually.
Taking a view of the issue, the Minister directed Health Secretary Christina Z. Chongthu and Vice-Chancellor of KNRUHS Ramesh Reddy, to constitute a special committee to study the extent of these additional expenses and examine how the government could extend further financial support to students from poor and middle-class families, the sources said.
Mental health and suicide prevention measures were also discussed during the meetings. Referring to isolated incidents of suicides among medical students reported from different parts of the country, the Minister instructed officials to strengthen counselling mechanisms in medical colleges. “Directions were issued to ensure the availability of psychologists and psychiatrists and to develop systems to identify students showing early signs of distress or withdrawal,” the official said.

title: Emergency healthcare unit at district and sessions court complex in Yadgir soon
summary: Emergency healthcare unit to be established at Yadgir's district court complex for advocates, litigants, and court staff.
content:
The present district and sessions court complex will soon get an emergency healthcare centre to attend to health emergencies of advocates, litigants and also court staff.
The new court complex, which was built at a cost of ₹32 crore in a 10-acre area, having eight court halls, including the court halls of the principal district and session judges and the additional judges, the bar association building, vehicle parking, a canteen, and washrooms for men and women, was inaugurated on September 19 by Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court Vibhu Bakhru.
All courts housed in the complex are functioning. Despite having basic facilities, the premises doesn’t have a health centre to attend to any health issues of the elderly litigants, advocates and others.
“It has been planned to set up a health centre to extend emergency healthcare to the people, including litigants, advocates and court staff,” Principal District and Sessions Judge Marulasiddaradhya toldThe Hindurecently.
He said discussions would be held with the department concerned on setting up a healthcare centre shortly.
The old district and session court building, which is located in the heart of the city and is under the judiciary department, will be used for the Consumer’s Dispute Redressal Forum and other offices.
“The building is in good condition except for a few minor repairs and painting. There is a proposal to establish a consumer court on the premises. There is also another proposal to establish a Lok Ayukta office in another portion of the building. Therefore, a decision on establishing the required forum and government offices will soon be taken,” Mr. Marulasiddaradhya said.
The Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (KKRTC) is operating local buses from the central bus stand to the new district and session court, via Subhash Chandra Circle (near the old bus stand) and the Deputy Commissioner’s Office, to lead to the Yadgir Institute of Medical Sciences (YIMS) for the convenience of the public.

title: 60 FIRs for child pornography registered in 2025 based on 1,197 leads from Delhi Police special unit
summary: 60 FIRs for child pornography registered in 2025 based on 1,197 leads from Delhi Police special unit
content:
The Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC) has forwarded 1,197 leads on online sexual abuse of minors and child pornography to district units for action during 2025, leading to the registration of 60 FIRs, official data shows.
According to Delhi Police data, from January 1 to December 19 this year, 1,197 Delhi-specific inputs from the U.S.-based National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) led to the registration of 60 FIRs related to child pornography.
Also read:Viewing, storing child sexual exploitative and abuse material an offence under POCSO, IT Act, says Supreme Court
This marks a nearly 56% decline compared to 2024, when 136 FIRs were registered based on 1,809 leads forwarded to district units, the data suggests.
In 2025, SPUWAC received 10,151 inputs related to child pornography, through referrals from the NCMEC. Of these, 106 were referred back to NCMEC after it was found that they did not pertain to India, officials said.
Another 6,022 leads were transferred to other states after verification revealed these incidents were outside Delhi Police jurisdiction, the data says.
Police officials said 2,826 leads were closed following verification as non-actionable, while the remaining Delhi-specific inputs were processed by the SPUWAC and district units.
In 2024, the SPUWAC received 16,321 inputs related to child pornography, according to official figures.
Of these, 7,865 were transferred to other states while another 6,554 leads were closed after verification as non-actionable.
Meanwhile, 1,809 Delhi-specific inputs on online sexual abuse of children were forwarded to district units, leading to the registration of 136 FIRs in 2024, the data shows.
Cumulatively, 3,006 such leads were sent to district units of Delhi Police in 2024 and 2025, leading to the registration of 196 FIRs.
Apart from child abuse-related matters, counselling remained a major function of the SPUWAC, officials said.
Counselling was undertaken in complaints related to dowry harassment, marital disputes, domestic discord and mental harassment, they added.
According to the data, SPUWAC received 3,578 such complaints since 2015 till December 19 this year.
During this period, police registered 976 FIRs when counselling did not suffice and criminal action was warranted, while 42 cases were registered under provisions of the Domestic Violence Act, officials said.
Between January 1 and December 15, 2025, SPUWAC took up 186 counselling-related matters.
Of these, 34 were resolved through reconciliation after counselling, while 6 cases were settled through mutual agreement, officials said.
In 27 cases, no action was taken as complainants or family members did not wish to proceed, while 2 cases were transferred to other districts, they added.
The data shows that 36 pending complaints from 2024 were carried forward into 2025, taking the total number of cases handled by SPUWAC during the year to 222.
According to the figures, all pending complaints from 2024 were disposed of, while 127 of the complaints registered in 2025 were also resolved, bring the total number of cases disposed of during the year to 163, with 59 cases pending.
“The SPUWAC remains committed to the protection and promotion of rights of women and children, and to shielding them from all forms of abuse through diligent investigation and prosecution of offenders,” Deputy Commissioner of Police, SPUWAC, Anjitha Chepyala toldPTI.
A designated nodal agency, SPUWAC will continue to collaborate with relevant stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of justice, she added.
Additionally, since 2002 till December 15 this year, 16,922 self-defence training programmes were organised across Delhi, including workshops conducted under SPUWAC, according to the data.
These programmes trained 30,09,298 women and girls over the years as part of community outreach and prevention efforts, police said.
In 2025, 4,13,004 women and girls were trained under such self-defence programmes, the highest annual figure recorded so far, they added.

title: Assam allots 25 acres for TTD’s first Lord Venkateswara temple in Northeast
summary: Assam allots 25 acres for TTD’s first Lord Venkateswara temple in Northeast
content:
In a significant boost to the spiritual outreach of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams(TTD), the Assam government has agreed in principle to allot 25 acres of land in Guwahati for the construction of a Lord Venkateswara temple, marking a major step towards establishing the first such shrine in Northeast India. The decision followed a series of consultations between Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.
The extent of land was enhanced from the initially proposed 10.8 acres after concerns were raised about an overlap with an existing temple and cultural complex in Kamrup Metropolitan district. In a letter dated December 18, Mr. Naidu urged the Assam government to allot land within Guwahati, citing the city’s strategic importance as the gateway to the Northeast. He also recalled that Andhra Pradesh had earlier allotted 25 acres of land in Amaravati for a similar temple.
Responding positively, the Assam government also agreed to extend financial support for the project. Thanking both the Chief Ministers, TTD Board Chairman B. R. Naidu said the required formalities would be completed soon and that construction of the Lord Venkateswara temple would begin at the earliest.

title: Create awareness on hazards of using plastic: Minister
summary: Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy calls for awareness on plastic hazards to protect nature and promote recycling in Banganapalle.
content:
Roads and Buildings (R&B) Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy stressed the need for students and teachers to create awareness on the hazards of using plastic in the society.
Participating in the Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra programme on Saturday at the MPDO office in Banganapalle, the Minister said the aim of the programme was to protect nature, and to create awareness on the ill-effects of plastic usage. Mr. Janardhan Reddy said it was the responsibility of every individual to keep their environments clean.
Mr. Janardhan Reddy also stressed on the importance of waste recycling. He said they had been striving for a plastic-free Banganapalle for nearly a year, but plastic was still being used by several people in the town. “Plastic can be completely avoided from our lives only if people get to know about its hazards,” he said. Mr. Janardhan Reddy said a healthy society can be built only if the people keep their environtments clean.
Later, the Minister inspected the quality of food items at a food stall set up at the venue. He found that the saplings that were planted earlier had dried and asked the staff to take proper care of them.

title: Customs officials foil hydro ganja smuggling attempts, arrest two
summary: Customs officials at Bengaluru airport arrest two passengers and seize 7.19 kg of hydro ganja from Bangkok.
content:
In separate incidents, Customs officials at the Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) seized 7.19 kg of hydro ganja from two passengers arriving from Bangkok, Thailand, over two days.
On Saturday, the officials intercepted a passenger and seized 7.18 kg of hydro ganja, valued at ₹2.51 crore, concealed in a check-in baggage. The accused was arrested under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985.
On Friday, the officials intercepted another passenger arriving from Bangkok and seized 0.86 kg of hydro ganja, valued at ₹30.10 lakh, also concealed in a check-in baggage.
The officials said that further investigations are under way to determine the travel details of the accused and the source of the contraband.

title: Election campaign materials litter Kochi despite government circular, High Court directive
summary: Election campaign materials clutter Kochi despite directives from the government and High Court for immediate removal and compliance.
content:
A government circular directing that election campaign materials be removed by candidates and political parties immediately after voting and handed over to the Haritha Karma Sena with the prescribed user fee stands violated in several places across Ernakulam district, including the Kochi Corporation limits.
The circular, issued by the Local Self-Government department (LSGD) on October 31, stated that if candidates and parties failed to comply, secretaries of local bodies should remove the campaign materials and hand them over to agencies such as the Clean Kerala Company for recycling within five days of polling, the cost for the same shall be collected from the candidates concerned and legal action initiated.
The Kerala High Court had also directed that publicity materials—including posters, flags, festoons and banners—that deface public spaces should be removed forthwith. The court further ordered that cases be registered against the parties concerned in addition to imposing fines. It also instructed the police, the Kerala State Electricity Board and the telecom authorities to assist the LSGD in removing materials disfiguring public spaces. This followed a request from the association of local body secretaries. The police have already begun registering First Information Reports in this regard.
“We have issued directions to candidates and political parties to comply with the circular and the High Court order without fail. Moreover, enforcement squads at the local body level have been instructed to remove election campaign materials that come to their notice and issue notices to the candidates concerned complete with the fee to be paid. We conduct review meetings at least once every fortnight to monitor the implementation of the court order. The next meeting will be held after the swearing-in ceremony of elected representatives of local bodies next week,” said a senior LSGD official.
The official clarified that campaign materials displayed on private properties, such as the compound walls of individual households, would not be removed by enforcement squads unless the affected property owners explicitly lodge complaints stating that their premises were used without permission. The LSGD has already received a few such complaints.

title: Newly-married couple die after falling from moving train in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district
summary: A newly married couple tragically died after falling from a moving train in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district.
content:
A newly married couple died after falling from a moving train on the Vangapalli–Aler railway line in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district late on Thursday (December 18, 2025).
The deceased were identified as Korada Simhachalam, 25, and his wife Bhavani, 19, natives of Ravupalli village in Garugubilli mandal of Parvathipuram Manyam district in Andhra Pradesh. The couple got married about two months ago.
According to the railway police, the couple had boarded the Machilipatnam Express at Secunderabad on Thursday night and were travelling to Vijayawada to visit relatives. After the train crossed Vangapalli railway station in Yadagirigutta mandal, the two were standing near the door of the coach when they slipped and fell from the moving train.
The incident came to light on Friday morning when railway trackmen found the bodies along the tracks and alerted the railway police. The bodies were later shifted to a hospital for postmortem examination.
Police said Simhachalam was employed with a chemical company in Hyderabad and was residing in the Gandhinagar area of Jagadgirigutta along with his wife.
A case has been registered by the railway police, and further investigation is underway.

title: E-Khata melas planned in large apartment complexes across north corporation
summary: North City Corporation to host e-khata melas in large apartments, requiring 100 applications for khata issuance.
content:
The North City Corporation will organise e-khata melas in large residential apartment complexes in its jurisdiction, provided at least 100 complete applications with required documents are submitted, Commissioner Pommala Sunil Kumar said on Saturday.
Addressing a meeting with representatives of such complexes in Yelahanka, the Commissioner discussed issues related to e-Khata issuance. He said that based on requests raised by apartment representatives, office-bearers of apartment associations in all sub-divisions of the city corporation limits should coordinate with owners to prepare a minimum of 100 applications along with the necessary documents.
Once the applications are ready, a date would be finalised in consultation with corporation officials, following which e-khata melas would be conducted and khatas would be issued, Mr. Kumar said.
The documents required for e-khata issuance include the sale deed, up-to-date property tax paid receipts, Bescom electricity meter bill, previous khata document indicating ownership of the property, a GPS photograph of the house, and the Aadhaar card.

title: The Hindu Journalist wins award
summary: Sarat Babu George of The Hindu wins Best Reporting award at Kerala School Kalolsavam 2024-25, receiving ₹20,000 prize.
content:
Sarat Babu George, journalist with the Thiruvananthapuram Bureau ofThe Hindu, won the award for Best Reporting (English Media) of the 63th edition of the Kerala School Kalolsavam held in Thiruvananthapuram in 2024-25.
The award carries a cash prize of ₹20,000, citation and certificate.

title: Munnar records -1°C, tourism sector eyes big push
summary: Munnar experiences record low temperatures, boosting tourism as visitors flock to enjoy the early winter chill and frost.
content:
The Munnar hill station in Idukki recorded the lowest temperature of the season on Saturday, with the mercury dropping to -1° C at Sevenmallay. As temperatures dropped to sub-zero levels, grasslands and valleys were seen carpeted in white frost in the morning.
According to data from the United Planters Association of South India (UPASI) tea research foundation, temperatures touched 0° C in Chenduvarai, Silent Valley, Letchmi, Devikulam and at the UPASI headquarters in Nallathanni. Devikulam recorded 1°C. The R&D centre at Mattupetty recorded 2°C. This follows a previous seasonal low of 2°C recorded on Friday.
Climatologist Gopakumar Cholayil said that sub-zero temperatures were likely to persist. “The current weather pattern is favourable for continued sub-zero temperatures,” Mr. Cholayil said.
Climate experts noted that these freezing temperatures had arrived earlier than usual this year. Normally, Munnar does not see sub-zero temperatures until the last week of December.
The local tourism sector is expecting a heavy surge in visitors eager to experience the chilly weather and frost-covered landscapes.
G. Sojan, coordinator of My Munnar Movement, an initiative to promote local tourism, said that news of the cold snap had already led to an influx of travellers. “Tourism stakeholders are receiving huge bookings and inquiries for the coming days,” said Mr. Sojan.
The winter season typically begins in December and peaks with extreme cold in the last week of the month. Experts noted that in recent years the winter season in Munnar extended up to February.
Kerala Travel Mart (KTM) managing committee member Vinod Vattekkatt said that while IndiGo flight cancellations initially impacted the tourism in the hill station in the first week of December, the early onset of winter helped the industry recover. “The early start of winter in Munnar has helped us overcome the initial crisis. Most resorts and hotels are now receiving high volumes of bookings and inquiries, a trend we expect to continue until January 30,” said Mr. Vattekkatt.
“Both tourists and tour operators have been closely monitoring Munnar’s weather patterns. When they see favourable conditions, bookings rise. For the past several years, Munnar’s winter pattern has shifted, with sub-zero temperatures typically occurring in late December, January, and the first week of February. However, this year the frost began in the second week of December itself, providing the much-needed boost to the tourism sector,” said Mr. Vattekkatt.

title: ‘Take action to shift high-tension power lines, transformers from school zones’
summary: Karnataka's child rights chief urges swift relocation of high-tension power lines near schools to ensure student safety.
content:
Chairman of the Karnataka State Commission for Protection of Child Rights Shashidhar Kosambe has given the officers of departments concerned a month’s time to shift high-tension electricity cables and transformers from the vicinity of schools.
Chairing a district-level review meeting here on Saturday, he reviewed the implementation of the programmes under the Compulsory Education Act - 2009, the POCSO Act - 2012 and the Child Protection Policy - 2016.
Mr. Kosambe said that high-tension cables were passing near 72 school premises and electricity transformers were installed near 42 schools in the district. “Officials should take immediate action to shift high-tension  cables and transformers within a month. Asuo motucase will be registered if it is not done,”  he warned, adding that it is a prime duty to ensure a fearless education atmosphere for students.
The chairman directed the Education Department and other officers to supply quality grains for mid-day meals in government-run schools. The Aadhaar card verification and seeding of 2.66 lakh children should be completed in a week, he said while giving January 5, 2026 as the deadline to correct mismatching and duplication of birth certificates.
Referring to the considerable number of dropouts, Mr. Kosambe said that an efficient effort is needed to reduce the percentage of school dropouts.
He said that the Education Department must correct mistakes in improving the pass percentage in SSLC results. Follow the guidelines, particularly police verifications, while appointing guest teachers/lecturers for schools, and submit a compliance report, he said.
The officers should ensure that each school mentions the child helpline number (1098) on the boards mandatorily and strictly implements the guidelines issued under Child Protection Policy 2016 for the protection of every child with proper basic needs, including good condition schoolrooms and toilets.

title: Excise Department tightens grip while scaling up supply as liquor demand surges ahead of year-end festivities
summary: Excise Department tightens grip while scaling up supply as liquor demand surges ahead of year-end festivities
content:
As the festive season reaches its peak, the Telangana Excise and Prohibition Department has adopted a twin approach of tightened enforcement and robust supply management to deal with rising demand for liquor, while ensuring that illegal trade does not gain ground.
Officials said that the year-end period sees a surge in alcohol consumption and private gatherings, along with increased attempts to smuggle illicit liquor and drugs into the State.
Speaking toThe Hindu, Shahnawaz Qasim, Director (Enforcement), said that the department’s primary focus would be on curbing the inflow of non-duty paid liquor (NDPL), particularly from Delhi, Haryana and Goa, which poses a serious threat to State revenue, as well as synthetic drugs whose demand typically rises at this time of the year.
As part of the enforcement drive, around 20 inter-State border checkposts will be activated from the weekend until December 31. These will operate in addition to regular transport checkposts, with excise teams carrying out random and surprise inspections of vehicles suspected of transporting NDPL or drugs.
Four mobile border patrol units have also been deployed in vulnerable corridors to monitor routes known for illicit movement. While Medak, Mahabubnagar, Rangareddy and the areas surrounding Hyderabad are considered key routes for NDPL inflow, Khammam, Kothagudem, Mulugu and Adilabad are in focus for ganja trafficking from Odisha.
With contraband now increasingly being moved by train, the department has strengthened coordination with the Government Railway Police. All trains arriving from Delhi, Haryana and Goa are particularly being monitored. Checks have also been intensified on highways, Outer Ring Road and airport exit points, which are commonly used routes for NDPL movement.
State Task Force (STF) units have been tasked with maintaining heightened vigilance in Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Rangareddy, including farmhouses and pubs, where large-scale parties, many without the necessary permissions, are expected and drug use is a concern.
Alongside enforcement, the department has also stepped up arrangements to meet the seasonal rise in liquor demand. Telangana has 19 liquor depots that supply stock to retailers based on orders placed by licensed shops. On an average day, liquor worth ₹100–120 crore is supplied from depots to shops, officials said.
However, during the last 7-10 days of December, daily sales typically rise from the usual ₹100-120 crore to nearly ₹150 crore, translating into an additional ₹200–300 crore in sales during the final stretch of the month. To prevent shortages, officials said stock levels are being closely monitored and maintained.
The State has 2,620 liquor shops, including around 600 in Hyderabad, and 1,171 bars, offering as many as 1,035 varieties of liquor. Sources in the department said that liquor sales had already risen by about 20% by December 20, fuelled in part by recent Gram Panchayat elections. Warangal, Nalgonda, Nizamabad and Mahabubnagar emerged as the top districts in terms of sales during this period.
While Telangana typically records around ₹3,000 crore in liquor sales each month, sources said this threshold had already been crossed well before the end of December. With Christmas and New Year celebrations still ahead, the department expects total liquor sales this month to touch ₹5,000 crore.

title: Mixed bag for BJP in Arunachal civic body polls
summary: BJP achieves mixed results in Arunachal civic polls, winning four uncontested seats but facing setbacks in Pasighat.
content:
The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday (December 20, 2025) won the civic body election in Itanagar, the capital ofArunachal Pradesh, but suffered a setback in Pasighat, the State’s oldest urban centre.
Elections to 16 of the 20 wards of the Itanagar Municipal Corporation (IMC) and eight wards of the Pasighat Municipal Corporation were held on December 15, along with most of the State’s 245 zilla parishads. The BJP won four of the IMC wards uncontested.
According to State election officials, the BJP candidates won 10 of the 16 IMC wards, where elections were held. The Nationalist Congress Party, the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), and an Independent followed with three, two, and one wards, respectively.
In East Siang district’s Pasighat, the regional People’s Party of Arunachal won five of the eight wards. The BJP won two wards, while an Independent candidate secured Ward 8.
“The counting of votes for the simultaneous panchayat election is continuing. We expect the results to come in from 27 districts by Sunday afternoon,” an election official said.
The BJP won 58 of the State’s 245 zilla parishad seats uncontested.

title: Tigress Thayamma in critical condition
summary: Thayamma, a tigress at Mysuru zoo, is in critical condition due to a severe infection and lack of appetite.
content:
The health condition of Thayamma, a tigress at Mysuru zoo, is critical.
Aged about four years and 10 months, she was rescued from Bandipur on March 28, 2021, and has since been under the care of the zoo.
Recently, the wild cat stopped consuming food and was found to be suffering from the haemoprotozoan infection. Veterinarians at the zoo have been providing treatment continuously. However, Thayamma’s condition remains serious, and there has been no significant improvement in her health condition so far, stated a press release from the zoo.

title: Public urged to make cleanliness a part of lifestyle
summary: Collector Nishanth Kumar urges communities to embrace cleanliness as a lifestyle for a healthier society and environment.
content:
Annamayya District Collector Nishanth Kumar urged people to make cleanliness a way of life and support efforts to eliminate plastic by promoting the use of reusable materials. The Collector was addressing a gathering at the Swachh Andhra-Swarna Andhra programme in Kalakada, on Saturday.
Addressing a gathering of officials, students, and villagers, the Collector said cleanliness was not a one-time activity, but a continuous process that must become a part of daily life. Maintaining hygiene in villages, towns, schools, and public spaces was essential in building a healthy society, he said. The Collector cautioned that poor sanitation could lead to serious health and environmental problems.
Highlighting the State government’s focus on environment-friendly initiatives, Mr. Nishant Kumar said monthly themes were being introduced to raise awareness among the public. Under the Green Andhra programme, plantation drives were being taken up to enhance green cover and improve environmental conditions.
“Top priority should be given to reducing single-use plastics and encouraging reusable alternatives. Banning plastic water bottles in government secretariats and introducing glass bottles resulted in a significant reduction in plastic waste. Similar measures should be adopted at district, mandal, and village levels,” he added.
Earlier, the Collector inspected a waste-to-wealth centre, reviewed vermicomposting practices, and visited local livelihood units. He later flagged off a rally from the Government Junior College to the RTC bus stand, where a human chain was formed, and a pledge was administered.

title: Flower fest, light show to begin in Thiruvananthapuram on December 24
summary: Join the Vasantholsavam flower fest and light show in Thiruvananthapuram, December 24 to January 4, 2026.
content:
Ranging from competitions in floral decorations and installations to a Chrysanthemum festival, the much-anticipated festival of flowers and lights, ‘Vasantholsavam,’ is all set to offer a visual treat for people from December 24 to January 4, 2026 in Thiruvananthapuram.
This edition of Vasantholsavam, organised by the department of Tourism and the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC) on Kanakakkunnu grounds in the city, is curated by Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanical Garden and Research Institute, Palode. The flower fete along with the light festival illuminating the city’s streets and heritage structures during the Christmas and New Year season  will be a double delight for visitors.
The Tourism department has earmarked a budget of ₹1.18 crore for the light show. The flower festival will have competitions in around 70 categories including those relating to exhibition of flower plants, ornamental plants, orchids, anthurium, cactus, and adenium. Government and private institutions, nurseries and individuals can take part in the competitions. There will be separate first, second and third prize winners, besides overall champions in each category.
More than 25,000 plants will be on display at the fete, apart from around 15,000 plants in the competitions category. An expo of flower decorations and a competition in this category will also be held for adults and students. Visitors can buy flowers and plants from the stalls put up by nurseries as well.  Ticket for adults is priced at ₹50 while for children it is ₹30.

title: Indigenously built stroke device approved on domestic trial data, launch set for February 2026
summary: India's Supernova stent retriever, approved for severe stroke treatment, launches in February 2026, promising affordable healthcare solutions.
content:
The indigenously developed Supernova stent retriever—approved in India using only domestic clinical trial data— is expected to be manufactured in the country and launched in February 2026. The device is used to treat severe strokes by removing clots and restoring blood flow to the brain within 24 hours.
Developed by Gravity Medical Technology, its clinical trial was led by the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has approved the device’s manufacturing and marketing in India after the trial demonstrated good safety and efficacy outcomes. It is the first time a stroke device has been approved in India based solely on domestic clinical trial data.
AIIMS Delhi was the national coordinating centre and the lead enrolling site of the GRASSROOT trial for the Supernova Stent.
“This trial is a turning point for stroke treatment in India. Supernova stent showed strong performance in real-world clinical settings involving severe stroke cases,” said Shailesh B. Gaikwad, professor and head, Department of Neuroimaging & Interventional Neuroradiology, AIIMS Delhi, and National Principal Investigator of the GRASSROOT Trial.
“The Supernova stent has shown excellent safety and efficacy outcomes in the treatment of severe strokes,” according to findings published recently in the Journal of Neurointerventional Surgery (JNIS).
In the first prospective multicentre thrombectomy (procedure to physically remove a blood clot from a blocked artery) trial, the Supernova stent retriever achieved high successful restoration of blood flow with brain bleed (3.1 per cent), mortality (9.4 per cent), and 50 per cent functional independence at 90 days.
The India trial was conducted across eight centres. The device has already been used to treat more than 300 patients in Southeast Asia and will now be manufactured and made available in India at affordable prices, offering new hope to the 1.7 million Indians who suffer strokes each year, added Dileep Yavagal, professor of Neurology and Neurosurgery, University of Miami, who was part of the global trial.
Shashvat M Desai, chief technology officer at Gravity Medical Technology, said the approval reflects India’s ability to conduct globally competitive trials. “The Supernova stent is tailored to India’s unique stroke profile, where strokes tend to occur at a younger age compared to Western populations. The device has already been used to treat patients in Southeast Asia, reinforcing its safety and versatility,’’ he said.

title: Policeman suspended over suspected ties to civil case accused
summary: Bengaluru sub-inspector Nagaraj suspended for alleged ties to accused in civil disputes, raising concerns about police conduct.
content:
Sub-inspector Nagaraj of the Yelahanka New Town, has been suspended for having alleged links with an accused involved in multiple land disputes and civil cases.
Ramesh Banoth, Joint Commissioner (East Division), issued the suspension order on Friday. Nagaraj was allegedly part of the close circle of the accused Dasa.
Despite being aware of his background, Nagaraj was reportedly seen in public with Dasa. Multiple videos and photographs of the policeman celebrating a birthday with Dasa and being seen in public while on duty went viral on social media.
As the images circulated on social media and drew criticism, Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh ordered an inquiry headed by Mr. Banoth. The inquiry report by the Joint Commissioner reportedly established that the sub-inspector was in close association with Dasa.
Sources said while Dasa did not have cases in the city limits, he was involved in several cases, including mediating civil disputes, in the Bengaluru Rural jurisdiction.
Nagaraj’s ‘friendship’ with Dasa came to light amid repeated statements by Home Minister G. Parameshwara that the government would not tolerate the involvement of police officers in civil cases.
Director-General of Police M.A. Saleem has also warned officers against engaging in such matters.
With this suspension, the total number of officers suspended from duty this year has risen to 131.

title: Workshop to impart life skills to youth begins at University of Mysore
summary: University of Mysore hosts a seven-day workshop to equip youth with essential life skills for resilience and healthy living.
content:
The Department of Studies in Food Science and Nutrition, University of Mysore (UoM), has organised a seven-day faculty improvement workshop with the theme ‘Building Resilient and Responsible Youth: Life Skills for a Healthy Mind and Body’from December 20 to 27. The workshop is sponsored by the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) 2.0 and the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centre, UoM.
Prof. N.K. Lokanath, Vice-Chancellor, UoM, inaugurated the workshop.
The workshop aims to address the challenges faced by today’s youth, including academic pressure, digital exposure, emotional stress, social comparison, and uncertainty about future prospects. The programme seeks to equip participants with essential life skills to enhance emotional regulation, stress management, ethical decision-making and healthy interpersonal relationships.
A total of 24 technical sessions have been planned; these focus on life skills education, emotional intelligence, resilience building, conflict management, self-awareness, media literacy, cyber stress, effective communication, empathy and problem-solving. Sessions will also cover topics such as mental resilience, gender respect, creativity, ethics, civic engagement, and responsible citizenship, a press release stated.
The workshop will follow experiential and participatory learning methods, including group discussions, role plays, case studies, reflective exercises, and action planning. Resource persons include academicians, mental health professionals and subject experts from universities and institutions across Karnataka.

title: T.N. to survey hornbill population for long-term conservation
summary: Tamil Nadu initiates a hornbill population survey to enhance conservation efforts during the birds' breeding season.
content:
Forest officials in Tamil Nadu plan to launch an extensive field exercise to understand the status of hornbill populations across forest landscapes.
Timed to coincide with the birds’ breeding season, the effort is part of the State’s initiative for hornbill conservation announced earlier this year, a senior official said.
Beginning in late December, teams will survey hornbill habitats until the end of March or early April 2026. The first phase will cover the Anamalai, Srivilliputhur–Megamalai and Kalakkad–Mundathurai tiger reserves, along with the Karamadai and Mettupalayam ranges under the Coimbatore forest division. These locations were prioritised based on earlier records and sightings of hornbills, the official said.
The survey is expected to be carried out using the line transect method, wherein forest personnel, biologists and researchers will walk several kilometres each day through identified habitats to record sightings and estimate population density.
Four species are expected to be documented during the survey — the Great Hornbill, Malabar Grey Hornbill, Indian Grey Hornbill and Malabar Pied Hornbill. Beyond population counts, the initiative also aims to protect habitat, particularly the conservation of large, mature trees with natural hollows that hornbills depend on for nesting, the official added.
In July 2025, the State government announced the establishment of the country’s first Centre of Excellence for Hornbill Conservation at the Anamalai Tiger Reserve (ATR) in Coimbatore district.
Once the current phase is completed, the survey is expected to provide accurate population estimates that will help guide long-term conservation strategies.

title: Three-car pile-up on PVNR Expressway disrupts traffic in Rajendranagar
summary: Three-car pile-up on PVNR Expressway causes significant traffic disruptions in Rajendranagar; injuries reported amid ongoing overspeeding concerns.
content:
A collision involving three cars near pillar number 253 on the P. V. Narasimha Rao (PVNR) Expressway caused traffic disruptions in the Rajendranagar area on Saturday (December 20, 2025) with congestion stretching from Upparpally to Aramgarh.
According to Rajendranagar traffic police, a car travelling at a high speed from Warangal towards Mehdipatnam first rammed into the road divider. Moments later, a car following it crashed into the damaged vehicle, while another car coming from the opposite direction collided head-on, resulting in a pile-up on the two-lane stretch of the elevated corridor.
Drivers, who sustained injuries, were shifted to a nearby hospital for treatment and their condition was said to be stable.
A traffic police official said overspeeding continues to be a major concern on the PVNR Expressway, particularly because of its limited carriageway width. “As the expressway has just two lanes and due to frequent over speeding by drivers, accidents are being reported regularly on this stretch,” the official said.
The latest incident comes amid a spate of accidents on the expressway this week. On Wednesday, a car rammed into a road divider near pillar number 123.
Earlier, on Monday night, mild tension prevailed on the expressway after a three-car collision near pillar number 112 was reported after a hatchback car broke down in a no-parking zone. When the owner attempted to move the vehicle, three cars approaching from behind crashed into one another. Two men sustained minor injuries and were given first aid at the scene.

title: Elderly man killed after being hit by SUV near HAL
summary: Elderly man Jayapal, 60, killed by SUV in Bengaluru; driver charged with negligent act as police investigate incident.
content:
An elderly man was killed after being hit by an SUV on HAL Airport Road on Friday night.
The deceased has been identified as Jayapal, 60, a resident of HAL who worked as a housekeeping staff at HAL. The incident occurred on Friday around 11 p.m. when Jayapal was crossing the road, a short distance from the UR Rao Satellite Centre in east Bengaluru.
An SUV  heading towards the Marathahalli bridge from the Domlur side hit Jayapal. He was flung some distance due to the impact and fell down leading to severe head injuries. He succumbed later.
Police said the driver did not stop the vehicle immediately. She drove some distance, halted briefly, and then proceeded directly to a nearby traffic police station.
The Jeevan Bima Nagar police have registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) section pertaining to causing death by a rash or negligent act.
The police were reviewing CCTV footage from the vicinity to establish the sequence of events.

title: Economist flags widening inequality in India; calls for wealth and inheritance taxes
summary: Economist Prabhat Patnaik highlights India's growing inequality and advocates for wealth and inheritance taxes to support fundamental economic rights.
content:
Noted economist Prabhat Patnaik has flagged India’s sharply rising income and wealth inequality and advocated the introduction of a wealth tax and an inheritance tax to finance a set of constitutionally guaranteed fundamental economic rights for citizens.
Delivering a special lecture titled ‘A Set of Constitutionally Guaranteed Fundamental Economic Rights’ after the release of a book in honour of late economist V.K. Nataraj at the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Research and Extension Centre, Manasagangothri, on December 20, Prof. Patnaik said income inequality in India had reached its highest level in the last 100 years.
Citing estimates for 2022–23, he said the top 1% of Indians accounted for 23% of the total income. While income inequality had declined steadily from the pre-Independence period until the 1980s, it had risen sharply in recent decades, he observed.
Wealth inequality, he added, was even more stark. The top 1% holds nearly 40% of the country’s wealth, making India “probably one of the most unequal economies in the world”. “Such levels of inequality are inimical to democracy and to any civilised society,” said Prof. Patnaik, who is also a former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi.
More “worrying” than income inequality, which had been accompanied by the country’s high GDP growth, was the rise in the relative magnitude of absolute poverty, Prof. Patnaik argued. He rejected claims in the media that poverty was disappearing in India, recalling that when official poverty studies began in 1973–74, the Planning Commission defined poverty in terms of access to a minimum of 2,100 calories per person per day, with estimates actually calculated at 2,200 calories.
Based on these nutritional norms, he said that in 1993–94, when the neo-liberal economic regime began, urban poverty stood at about 57% and rural poverty at around 58%. By 2011–12, urban poverty had risen to 65% and rural poverty to 68%.
Prof. Patnaik further claimed that data from the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) showing rural poverty levels exceeding 80% in 2017–18 were “suppressed” by the Union government. Subsequently, he said, the methodology for data collection was altered. Poverty, he maintained, had continued to increase when measured against nutritional benchmarks.
Arguing for the recognition of fundamental economic rights on par with civil and political rights, Prof. Patnaik listed five such entitlements: the right to food, the right to employment, the right to free, universal, publicly provided healthcare through a national health service, the right to free, publicly provided quality education, and the right to a non-contributory old-age pension and disability benefits.
He estimated that implementing these rights would cost an additional 10% of GDP. The required resources, he said, could be mobilised through just two taxes imposed on the top 1% of the population — a wealth tax and an inheritance tax.
“It is utterly shocking that India has no wealth tax,” he said, noting that despite the top 1% owning 40% of the country’s wealth, no such levy exists.
Referring to inheritance tax, Prof. Patnaik pointed out that all advanced capitalist countries impose death duties. “In Japan, the rate is 55%. In Britain and the United States, it is around 40%,” he said.
“Taken together, these two taxes are more than sufficient to finance a rights-based welfare state in India,” he added.

title: Rajdhani Express mows down seven elephants in Assam
summary: Train derailment in Assam kills seven elephants; no passenger injuries reported, disrupting train movement and causing multiple cancellations.
content:
Seven elephants were killed and a calf injured when the Mizoram-New Delhi Rajdhani Express hit a herd of wild elephants in central Assam’s Hojai district early on Saturday (December 20, 2025).
The collision led to the derailment of the locomotive and five coaches of the Train no. 20507 Sairang Rajdhani Express in the Jamunamukh-Kampur section under the Lumding Division of the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR). Railway officials said no passenger was injured.
Also Read|Three elephants run over by train in West Bengal’s Jhargram
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said he had directed a probe into the incident. “I have directed the Forest Department to conduct a detailed enquiry on this deeply disturbing accident and take steps to further secure our wildlife corridors, particularly during low visibility seasons,” he said.
The injured calf, a few days old, was rushed to the Centre for Wildlife Rehabilitation and Conservation near the Kaziranga National Park for treatment. “The condition of the elephant is critical,” Bhaskar Choudhury, the centre’s veterinarian, said.
The NFR claimed the location, 126 km east of Guwahati, was not a designated elephant corridor. There are nearly 80 designated elephant or animal corridors within the zone, which covers eight northeastern States and parts of Bihar and West Bengal.
“The loco pilot, on observing the herd of elephants, applied emergency brakes. However, the elephants collided with the train,” a spokesperson of the country’s easternmost railway zone said.
He further said that the passengers of the affected coaches were temporarily accommodated in the vacant berths available in the other coaches. The train left for Guwahati after the affected coaches were detached, he said.
In a statement, the NFR said several trains were cancelled, short-terminated, or short-originated/regulated on the route following the mishap, which damaged the track. Restoration work was under way, officials said.
Assam’s Forest and Environment Minister Chandra Mohan Patowary said the deaths were a matter of grave concern. “Two senior officials of our department have been directed to take up the matter with the seniormost officials of Indian Railways to prevent the recurrence of such incidents in the future,” he said.
Bibhab Talukdar of Aaranyak, an Assam-based biodiversity conservation organisation, called for better coordination between the railways and the Forest Department to track the movements of elephants and prevent such accidents, particularly during winter.
Dulu Borah of Hati Bondhu (Friends of Elephants), a non-profit organisation focused on resolving human-elephant conflicts, said a thermal camera-based early warning system could have saved the lives of the elephants. “It is not necessary that such incidents cannot happen beyond notified elephant corridors,” he said.
Assam has a history of elephants being mowed down by speeding trains. The last time so many elephants were killed was when lightning struck 18 of them in central Assam’s Nagaon district in June 2021.

title: Amara Raja Group celebrates 40th foundation day
summary: Amara Raja Group celebrates its 40th Foundation Day, honoring achievements and supporting rural entrepreneurs with the Better Way Awards.
content:
Amara Raja Group, a $2 billion global conglomerate with presence in varied industries, celebrated its 40th foundation day in Tirupati, on Saturday. The group, which came into existence in 1985 as Amara Raja Power Systems has now transformed itself with six companies, 17 businesses and more than 21,000 employees.
As part of the foundation day celebrations, the group announced the winners of the Amara Raja Better Way Awards to take forward its legacy of providing better access to better opportunities. At the event, three rural entrepreneurs were selected and given ₹3 lakh cash prize along with one-year-long support.
“This year’s theme, ‘Forever Through Time’, is a true reflection of our resilient and agile story. It is not only about celebrating the milestones, but also looking ahead even as the world is changing faster than ever before. In the last 40 years, we have redefined the industries that we operate in and are marching ahead with greater success,” said Jayadev Galla, chairperson of Amara Raja Group.
Amara Raja’s founder-chairperson Ramachandra Naidu Galla, co-founders Galla Aruna Kumari, Ramadevi Gourineni, Amara Raja excutive directors Harshavardhan Gourineni, Vikramadithya Gourineni, and the top leadership from the group including chief operating officer Narasimhulu Naidu participated in the celebrations.

title: Youth told to opt for courses offered in Advanced Technology Centres
summary: Youth told to opt for courses offered in Advanced Technology Centres
content:
Labour & Employment Minister, G Vivek Venkatswamy said that learning more than one skill enhances the chances of employment and opportunities for youth, and the government is committed to provide skill development ambience through various measures.
Skill competitions are a great opportunity for young people and these help enhance and refine the existing skills, he said while speaking at the closing ceremony of India Skills 2025 competitions on Saturday.
The Minister said that State government is aiming for $3 trillion economy in next few years.  If the economy grows, new industries come up and thus the requirement of skilled youth enhances automatically. Skilled youth get more and more opportunities in this competitive world, he said.
He recalled how the State government is establishing 115 Advanced Technology Centres (ATC) in order to provide futuristic training for the youth. Such centres do not exist anywhere else in the country, he said, and urged the youth to opt for courses offered in ATCs.
Principal Secretary, Labour and Employment, Dana Kishore, said zonal competitions were conducted for the India Skill 2025 competitions, and 240 candidates were selected across 40 categories.

title: University of Hyderabad records 6.3°C, cold wave alert in 11 Telangana districts on December 21
summary: Hyderabad temperature, IMD
content:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a cold wave alert in 11 Telangana districts for Sunday.
According to IMD’s latest bulletin, cold wave conditions are very likely to prevail at isolated pockets in Adilabad, Kumram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Nirmal, Warangal, Hanamkonda, Jangaon, Siddipet, Sangareddy, Medak and Kamareddy districts.
Hyderabad and its surrounding areas for the next 24 hours will see mainly clear sky. “Fog and misty conditions are very likely to prevail during morning hours. Mist or hazy conditions are very likely to prevail during morning or night hours. Minimum temperatures are likely to be below 3°C to 4°C during the next two days. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 29°C and 11°C respectively,” the bulletin said.
Meanwhile, according to the Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS), between December 19 and 20, 29 districts recorded minimum temperatures of 10°C or below. The lowest minimum temperature was 4.5°C in Kohir (Sangareddy) while University of Hyderabad recorded 6.3°C (lowest minimum temperature), under GHMC limits. This was followed by 7.5°C in Uppal and 10°C in Marredpally.
Sirpur in Kumram Bheem Asifabad recorded 4.8°C followed by 5.1°C in Moinabad (Rangareddy), 5.8°C in Mominpet (Vikarabad), 5.9°C in Bheempur (Adilabad), 7.2°C in Yeldurthy (Medak), 7.4°C in Gandhari (Kamareddy), 7.5°C in Markook (Siddipet), 8°C in Midjil (Mahabubnagar) and Kuntala (Nirmal), 8.2°C in Bodhan (Nizamabad), 8.3°C in Kothapalle (Narayanpet), 8.4°C in Tekumatla Jayashankar Bhupalpally), 8.5°C in Govindaraopet (Mulugu) and Kalwakurthy (Nagarkurnool), 8.6°C in Ramagiri (Peddapalli) and Kotapally (Mancherial), 8.8°C in Rudrangi (Rajanna Sircilla) and 8.9°C in Dharmapuri (Jagtial).
The remaining districts recorded temperatures ranging between 9°C and 12°C.

title: CUET-PG application process for 2026-27 has begun, says Central University V-C
summary: CUET-PG 2026-27 applications are open until January 14; exams scheduled for March 2026, says Central University V-C.
content:
The application process for the Common University Entrance Test for postgraduate courses (CUET-PG) for the academic year 2026-27 has commenced from December 14, Vice-Chancellor of the Central University of Karnataka (CUK) Battu Satyanarayana has said.
Addressing a press conference here, Prof. Satyanarayana said the examination will be conducted in Computer-Based Test mode by the National Testing Agency (NTA). Online applications will be accepted till January 14, 2026 (up to 11.50 p.m.). Candidates can apply through the NTA websites - https://exams.nta.nic.in/cuet-pg/ or www.nta.ac.in ; and details are also available on the university website www.cuk.ac.in
The last date for payment of examination fees is January 14. Candidates will be allowed to make corrections in their application forms on the website from January 18 to January 20. Examination centres will be announced later, after which admission cards can be downloaded from the NTA website. The examinations will be held in March 2026.
Prof. Satyanarayana said CUET-PG will be conducted for Central Universities and other participating universities across the country. In addition to the existing 30 postgraduate programmes, CUK has introduced five new courses this academic year — M.A. in Library and Information Science; M.Sc. in Botany, Zoology, and Statistics and Data Analytics; and M.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.
The intake capacity for most programmes is 30 seats, while MBA has 60 seats and M.Ed. and B.Ed. have 50 seats each. For M.Tech programmes, 50% of the seats will be filled through CUET-PG and the remaining 50% through GATE.
Prof. Satyanarayana said that the students currently pursuing the sixth semester of undergraduate courses and those appearing for fifth semester examinations are also eligible to apply. Replying to a query, he said of the total seats in each postgraduate programme, three seats are reserved for students from the Kalyana Karnataka region and three for candidates belonging to the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).
CUET-PG examinations will be conducted at 292 centres, including 16 outside the country. In Karnataka, exams will be held in 15 cities, including Kalaburagi and Ballari in the Kalyana Karnataka region, he added.
Registrar R.R. Biradar, Controller of Examinations Dr. Kota Sai Krishna, and Public Relations Officer Dr. Ganapati Sinnoor were present.

title: Colloquium on ‘Puppet and Child’ at Indian Institute of Educational Theatre on December 21
summary: Join the IIET's colloquium on 'Puppet and Child' in Mysuru on December 21 to explore innovative educational techniques.
content:
The Indian Institute of Educational Theatre (IIET), Mysuru, has invited all educationists, academicians, theatre practitioners, and parents to a colloquium on ‘Puppet and Child’ organised by the Indian Theatre Foundation on IIET premises in Hardwicke School on December 21 at 11 a.m.
The event will highlight the use of puppets as an effective tool in educational theatre, making a lasting impact on children and strengthening generations, even as we progress with technology.
Puppet designer Shashidhar Adapa, agriculturist Ramakrishna Bhat, teacher and puppeteer Gagan Kumar, and special educator Subbalakshmi Jenardanan will attend as expert contributors.
IIET said the event is an opportunity to explore innovative approaches in child education through puppets. For further details, contact +91 9845605012.

title: Ganja, cocaine and MDMA seized from six drug peddlers in multiple raids in Telangana
summary: Six drug peddlers arrested in Telangana; police seized ganja, cocaine, and MDMA in coordinated raids across multiple locations.
content:
Six drug peddlers were arrested in various raids conducted across Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Warangal by the Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE) Force in coordination with the police department. The police seized a total of 330 grams of ganja, 43 grams of cocaine and 11.5 grams of MDMA, along with one car, one motorcycle and five mobile phones from the accused.
In the first case, Warangal Narcotics Police of the EAGLE, along with Warangal police, apprehended two persons identified as Reddaboina Karthik, 25, a welder, and Reddaboina Rajesh, 18, a farmer, both residents of Rangapur in Huzurabad. Police seized 50 grams of ganja, two mobile phones and one motorcycle from them. During interrogation, Karthik disclosed that he was sourcing ganja from one Md. Fardeen of Hanamkonda. Acting on this information, the police conducted a search at Reddy Colony in Hanamkonda and apprehended Md. Fardeen, 21, a car kit marketing executive, seizing 30 grams of ganja and one mobile phone. Karthik and Rajesh were handed over to Huzurabad police, while Md. Fardeen was handed over to Hanamkonda police for further legal proceedings.
In the second case, the Cyberabad Narcotics Police Station of the EAGLE, in coordination with Miyapur police, arrested Dudukuri Akhil at Sai Anurag Colony in Miyapur and seized 250 grams of ganja from him. During questioning, the accused stated that he procured the drug from Ganesh, a resident of Sileru in Andhra Pradesh. Police said efforts were underway to apprehend Ganesh, who is suspected to be a part of an inter-State ganja smuggling network operating in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Akhil was handed over to the Miyapur Station House Officer (SHO) along with the seized contraband.
In the third case, on Friday (December 19), the State Task Force of the EAGLE, along with Masab Tank police, apprehended Nitin Singhaniya, 35, a real estate broker from Saleem Nagar Colony in Malakpet, and Shranik Singhvi, 36, a businessman from Akberbagh in Malakpet, behind Chacha Nehru Park at Masab Tank in Hyderabad. Police seized 43 grams of cocaine, 11.5 grams of MDMA, one car and two mobile phones from them. Both the accused are natives of Nagaur district in Rajasthan.
According to the police, the accused had established contacts with an African national during a visit to Mumbai in April 2024 and subsequently procured cocaine and MDMA through African couriers. The drugs were delivered at secluded locations in Hyderabad against cash payments, with part of the contraband allegedly used for self-consumption and the remainder supplied to a limited circle of associates.

title: Leadership issue: High command will call us at an appropriate time: Shivakumar
summary: Hinting that the party high command had sent a message that a decision on change in leadership would be taken soon, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday said it had been conveyed to both the Chief Minister and him that they would be “called [to Delhi] at an appropriate time”.
content:
Hinting that the party high command had sent a message that a decision on change in leadership would be taken soon, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday said it had been conveyed to both the Chief Minister and him that they would be “called [to Delhi] at an appropriate time”.
Mr. Shivakumar’s statement comes a day after Chief Minister Siddaramaiah asserted in the Legislative Assembly that he would continue in office and that, in his view, the Congress high command was in his favour.
“They have said that they will call both of us at an appropriate time. When that happens, both of us will go to Delhi together,” Mr. Shivakumar said, responding to questions on whether he had been invited by party leaders in Delhi.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, when questioned about this by reporters in Belagavi, refused to comment.
In Bengaluru, referring to the National Herald case, Mr. Shivakumar said the chargesheet filed by the Enforcement Directorate had been rejected by the court and that only one FIR now remained.
He said the Congress was staging protests to highlight what it viewed as pressure being exerted through investigation agencies.
Delinking his proposed visit to Delhi from the political developments, Mr. Shivakumar said he would on Tuesday appear before the Delhi Police.
He said the Union Jal Shakti Minister had also convened a meeting on river interlinking on the same day, during which he would raise key Karnataka projects, including Mahadayi, Upper Krishna, Mekedatu, and Upper Bhadra.
The Deputy Chief Minister said he had also sought appointments with the Union Ministers for Environment and Forests and for Housing and Urban Affairs to discuss issues related to the State. He added that meetings with Karnataka MPs were also being considered and that he would meet the Prime Minister if possible.
Earlier in the day, addressing the Satyameva Jayate protest organised by the Congress at Freedom Park, Mr. Shivakumar said the party would resist attempts to undermine Mahatma Gandhi’s legacy. “Congress workers will not allow Gandhi’s India to be turned into Godse’s India,” he said.
Recalling that Mahatma Gandhi had presided over the Congress session in Belagavi a century ago, Mr. Shivakumar accused the BJP-led Centre of attempting to remove Gandhi’s name from the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).
He said the scheme, introduced under Manmohan Singh’s leadership with Sonia Gandhi’s initiative, had provided livelihood support in rural areas.
He said BJP leaders had lost the moral right to protest in front of Gandhi statues if they continued to remove Gandhi’s name from public schemes.

title: Supplyco Christmas-New Year fairs begin on Monday
summary: Minister for Food and Civil Supplies G.R. Anil will perform the State-level inauguration of Christmas-New Year fairs organised by Kerala State Civil Supplies Corporation Ltd. (Supplyco) at Nayanar Park, Putharikandam grounds, here on Monday.
content:
Minister for Food and Civil Supplies G.R. Anil will perform the State-level inauguration of Christmas-New Year fairs organised by Kerala State Civil Supplies Corporation Ltd. (Supplyco) at Nayanar Park, Putharikandam grounds, here on Monday.
The fairs will be on till December 31. In six districts, the fairs will be held at special locations – Putharikandam grounds in Thiruvananthapuram, Ashramam grounds in Kollam, Rose Mount auditorium in Pathanamthitta, Thirunakkara grounds in Kottayam, Marine Drive in Ernakulam, and Thekkinkadu grounds in Thrissur.
One prime Supplyco outlet in each taluk in the State will host a Christmas fair.
The fair will provide special offers on more than 280 products from major brands and discount of 5% to 50% on branded everyday use items. The 20 of kg rice currently provided by Supplyco will be available for ₹25 at the fairs.
Those purchasing non-subsidised items above ₹500 will be given 1 kg Sabari salt for ₹1.
Special kits comprising 12 items will be available under the name Santa offer in connection with Christmas in Supplyco outlets from December 22. Cake, sugar, tea leaves, payasam mix, Sabari appam powder, and masalas are included in the ₹667-kit that will now be available at ₹500.
Supplyco will offer special coupons to customers in connection with Christmas. These will be given to two-wheeler and autorickshaw drivers who fill fuel to the tune of ₹250 from Supplyco petrol pumps and other vehicles that fill fuel worth over ₹1,000. These coupons can be produced when purchasing subsidised products to the tune of ₹1,000 to get a discount of ₹50.
Signature mart, a modern shopping mall from Supplyco, will begin operations next month. A Signature Mart will be inaugurated at Thalassery on January 10 and another at Kottayam in the third week of January.
The last date for submitting applications online for converting ration cards into priority category has been extended to December 31, a statement from the Minister’s office said on Saturday.

title: A.P. a role model in implementing energy efficiency programmes: Chief Secretary
summary: Andhra Pradesh sets an example in energy efficiency and conservation, achieving significant savings and recognition at the National Energy Conservation Awards.
content:
Chief Secretary and Special CS (Energy) K. Vijayanand on Saturday (December 20) said Andhra Pradesh (A.P.) has emerged as a role model for other States in energy efficiency and energy conservation, driven by its forward-looking policies, effective implementation and sustained commitment across industries, buildings, institutions and urban local bodies (ULBs).
Participating as chief guest in the valedictory function of the National Energy Conservation Week–2025 celebrations organised by the State Energy Conservation Mission (SECM) here, Mr. Vijayanand said the State adopted a structured approach to energy conservation from 2015, beginning with the conversion of streetlights in Visakhapatnam to LED lights after the Hudhud cyclone. The move resulted in up to 45% energy savings.
With the support of Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL) and Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), over two crore households were covered under LED lighting. Energy savings stood at 30%. Energy-efficient agricultural motors and industrial interventions under the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme led to the completion of three PAT cycles and savings of about 1.35 million tonnes of oil equivalent.
Alongside technology adoption, the State took policy measures, including mandatory energy-efficient and green building norms, leading to approvals for 2,000–3,000 green buildings, he said, highlighting the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, which was aimed at achieving net zero carbon emissions with a target of 160 GW of green energy, of which nearly 100 GW has already been approved.
AP-Genco MD and SECM CEO S.
