title: Activists demand land distribution for Scheduled Castes ahead of protest
summary: Activists demand land distribution for Scheduled Castes, planning a protest to urge government action on December 29.
content:
Ambedkar Porata Samithi State president Soru Sambayya on Sunday urged the government to distribute house sites and agriculture lands to Scheduled Caste communities to help them attain financial stability and live a respectable life in society.
Addressing the media in Bobbili on Sunday, Mr. Sambayya said that the association, along with other organisations would stage a protest at the Vizianagaram Collector’s office on December 29 to urge the government to distribute lands to eligible Dalit families as recommended by the Koneru Rangarao Committee in 2007.
He said that the committee had directed the then United AP government to survey lands and assign them to SC families so that the they would earn a regular income through agriculture. “The present government instead of expanding and distributing lands is trying to confiscate the assigned lands. It is a cause of concern to Dalit sections of society. Against  this backdrop, we will stage a protest on December 29 to draw the attention of the government,” said Mr. Sambayya.

title: Newly elected members of three-tier bodies assume charge in Kottayam, Pathanamthitta
summary: Newly elected members of the Kottayam District panchayat were sworn in at a ceremony held at the District Panchayat Auditorium here on Sunday. District Collector and Returning Officer Chetan Kumar Meena administered the oath first to the senior-most member, Thomas Kunnappally, who then administered the oath to the remaining members.
content:
Newly elected members of the Kottayam District panchayat were sworn in at a ceremony held at the District Panchayat Auditorium here on Sunday. District Collector and Returning Officer Chetan Kumar Meena administered the oath first to the senior-most member, Thomas Kunnappally, who then administered the oath to the remaining members.
Simultaneously, elected representatives to the district’s municipalities, block panchayats and grama panchayats also took the oath of office. In each local body, the senior-most elected member was sworn in first before the Returning Officer, following which the oath was administered to the other members. The first meeting of the newly constituted bodies was held after the swearing-in ceremonies.
The senior-most members who took the oath first at the six municipalities in the district were Joyi Mannamala (Ettumanoor), Abdul Salam Rawther (Vaikom), Sally Mathew (Kottayam), Prasannakumari Teacher (Changanassery), Shaju Thuruthan (Pala) and Subair Vellappallil (Erumely).
In Pathanamthitta, the oath-taking ceremony for the 17 newly elected District Panchayat members was held at the District Planning Secretariat Conference Hall. District Collector and District Election Officer S. Prem Krishnan administered the oath first to senior-most member Sam Eappen, who later administered it to the other elected members.
Following the ceremony, the first meeting of the District Panchayat was held at the District Panchayat Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Sam Eappen. The election to the posts of District Panchayat president and vice-president will be held on December 27 at the same venue.

title: Local leaders creating confusion over leadership issue: Kharge
summary: With a section of the Congress leaders hoping that the high command will bring an end to the confusion caused by the tussle over leadership, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday — without naming anyone — blamed the local leaders for having created the confusion.
content:
With a section of the Congress leaders hoping that the high command will bring an end to the confusion caused by the tussle over leadership, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday — without naming anyone — blamed the local leaders for having created the confusion.
“Congress high command has not created any confusion. It is some leaders in the State [Congress] who are doing it,” Mr. Kharge told presspersons in Kalaburagi on Sunday.
He was responding to queries over a letter sent to him by some leaders seeking intervention to resolve the infighting in the State unit of the party. “I have not received any such letter so far. I will try to understand the intention of it once it reaches me.”
For over two months, the tussle over leadership between Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has intensified with public statements being issued by their followers in favour of their leaders.
The government crossing the midway mark of its tenure on November 20 has rekindled speculation over a “power-sharing agreement” between the two leaders, who are now looking at the party’s high command for a resolution.
Cautioning against projecting the Congress as being dependent on one person, Mr. Kharge said, “No one should claim that they alone brought the party to power or built the Congress. The party has been built by its workers. Every leader and worker had a role in strengthening the party.”
Amid the show of one-upmanship by both camps, Mr. Shivakumar met his fierce opponent and sacked former Minister K.N. Rajanna, who has been publicly supporting Mr. Siddaramaiah to complete the full five- year term, on Saturday night.
While both leaders did not reveal the purpose of the meeting, it is learnt that Mr. Shivakumar wanted to offer truce in his bid to take every leader into confidence as he mounts pressure on the Chief Minister. The Deputy Chief Minister had also met Public Works Minister Satish Jarkiholi, another confidant of the Chief Minister recently.
Sources said that the meeting was to also seek Mr. Rajanna’s support to Congress MLC S. Ravi, a relative of Mr. Shivakumar, in the election to the post of Apex Bank president.
‘Rajanna is close to me too’
“Is Chief Minister close to him (Mr. Rajanna)? He (Mr. Rajanna) is close to me too. Who is not close to him (Mr. Rajanna)? I made Mr. Rajanna the president of Apex Bank during S.M. Krishna’s term as Chief Minister. All Congress leaders are working together. We are all friends and colleagues,” Mr. Shivakumar told presspersons when asked if he had met Mr. Rajanna to garner support.
On the leadership tussle, he said, “Are not Chief Minister and I working like brothers? I do not have any differences with any Congress leaders. Have I had any difference with the Chief Minister since he came to the party 16 years ago? I have not spoken against any one.”
The Deputy Chief Minister also claimed that there was no confusion in the party, and said that it was a creation of the BJP and the media. “The BJP is trying to cover up its own internal mess,” he said.
The Deputy Chief Minister, who will be in Delhi this week to meet Union Ministers, is also like to meet the party’s central leaders to push for his case, sources close to him said. Incidentally, the Chief Minister will also be in Delhi likely next week to attend the Congress Working Committee meeting.
Meanwhile, Mr. Rajanna said that the discussion revolved around strengthening the party. When asked about his opposition to Mr. Shivakumar in the past, he clarified, “There is no change in my stand. Whatever I had said then, I stand by it. Ultimately, high command matters on the leadership issue. The Chief Minister has also reiterated that the high command matters.”

title: Kakarla Suresh dismisses ‘NRI jibe’, says he is here to stay
summary: Kakarla Suresh rejects NRI jibes, asserting his commitment to constituency development and political presence for the next 25 years.
content:
Udayagiri MLA Kakarla Suresh on Sunday (December 21, 2025) firmly asserted that “he is here to stay,” dismissing his opponents claims that “the NRI who would soon disappear from the constituency,” and cautioned them to stay out of his affairs or risk facing his anger.
Addressing the media at Nellore for the first time in eighteen months after the NDA Alliance came to power, the MLA dismissed allegations of corruption against him.
He also released statistics on funds allocated to his constituency’s development, department-wise, mandal-wise. The far-flung constituency lacks major water resources and the mandals are scattered, he said. Of the eight mandals viz., Udayagiri, Jaladanki, Kondapuram, Vinjamur, Varikuntapadu, Kaligiri, Duttalur and Sitaramapuram, irrigation water from Somasila reservoir is available only to two, making the rest dependent on rain-fed irrigation, he added.
“The government is spending ₹67 crore for widening of the Somasila north canal. Of the 149 tanks in our constituency, elections were conducted to the respective associations and ₹7 crore spent for strengthening the tanks. Today, every farmer gets water twice a year,” Mr. Suresh said.
Similarly, the State had allocated ₹150 crore towards development of roads, and another ₹46 crore for two years from the MGNREGA funds to strengthen the rural roads. “For three decades, we were listening to the tall talk of establishing a dialysis centre at Vinjamur Community Health Centres (CHC), which we have realised today”.
Mr. Suresh also announced an ambitious plan to run compressed biogas plants across the dry belt. He recalled an NRI investor evincing interest to grow Napier grass in 200 acres to run a five-tonne capacity plant, followed by similar offers from the Reliance group.
On the tourism front, ₹52 crore had been released to develop the Udayagiri fort, Vengamamba Thalli, and Siddheswaram temples. “We will have enough footfall once the three are linked to form a tourism hub,” he said, seeking support of the Endowments and Tourism Departments.
With so many development projects in his kitty, the MLA said that he would never leave the constituency ‘as dreamt by some’ and would stay active in politics for the next 25 years.

title: Minister urges Maharashtra MP to stop raking up border issue
summary: Minister H.K. Patil urges Maharashtra MP to cease border disputes, emphasizing harmony between Kannada and Marathi speakers in Karnataka.
content:
Minister H.K. Patil has urged Maharashtra MP Dhairyasheel S. Mane to stop raking up the border issue with Karnataka.
“I would like to address my brother leaders from Maharashtra and ask them why are they trying to create confusion over this issue. There is no confusion anywhere in the State, including Nippani and Belagavi,” he said.
“We live with a lot of solidarity. Kannada and Marathi speakers are living in harmony in Belagavi and other places in Karnataka. They are living with more affection than brothers. In such a situation, why raise the issue and create unnecessary confusion?” Mr. Patil said in Chikkodi on Sunday.
He was responding to Mr. Mane’s letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla seeking action against Belagavi Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Roshan for stopping him from entering the district on November 1.
He said that the State government is considering dividing Belagavi district to create a new Chikkodi district.
“I think the process will begin soon,” he said.
Earlier, during the inauguration of the new court complex there, Mr. Patil said that it is a historical court. It is a 200-year-old institution. It was the only major court in this region during the British period.
“Among its achievements are that B.R. Ambedkar argued here as an advocate. It is this court that gave us veteran leader B. Shankaranand,” Mr. Patil said.

title: Two killed in separate road accidents in Bengaluru
summary: Two men tragically die in separate road accidents in Bengaluru over the weekend, highlighting traffic safety concerns.
content:
Two men died in separate road accidents in the city since Saturday night.
In the first incident, a 31-year-old software engineer was killed after losing control of his speeding motorcycle and skidding on Hulimavu Lake Road in the early hours of Sunday. The accident occurred near the Kodandarama Swami Temple.
The deceased has been identified as Muniswami, a resident of Kammanahalli and a native of Dharmapuri district in Tamil Nadu.
According to the police, around 1.30 a.m., Muniswami was returning home after meeting a friend when he lost control of his bike, fell off, and suffered severe injuries. Passers-by rushed him to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead. The Hulimavu Traffic Police have registered a case.
In another incident, a 32-year-old man died after a two-wheeler he was riding hit a road hump and he was thrown off the vehicle. The accident took place near the Sulikunte bus stop on Sarjapura Main Road on Saturday night.
The deceased has been identified as Gopi Mohan, an audiologist from Vellore district in Tamil Nadu. Police said Mohan had come to Bengaluru for work and had been staying at Thayyakannahalli for the past two days. He had rented a two-wheeler for commuting.
Around 9.30 p.m., while returning after finishing work, Mohan was reportedly riding at a high speed and failed to notice a road hump near the Sulikunte bus stop, causing him to lose balance and fall. He was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he later succumbed to his injuries. The Whitefield Traffic Police have registered a case.

title: Two-day PESA Mahotsav in Visakhapatnam on December 23-24
summary: Join the two-day PESA Mahotsav in Visakhapatnam on December 23-24, celebrating tribal culture and marking PESA Day.
content:
A two-day ‘PESA Mahotsav: Utsav Lok Sanskriti Ka’ will be held in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday and Wednesday (December 23 and 24, 2025) to mark the enactment of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA). PESA Day is observed on December 24  to mark the anniversary of the Act.
The event being organised by the Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj will be inaugurated by Deputy Chief Minister and Minister for Panchayati Raj & Rural Development, K Pawan Kalyan. The Union Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Vivek Bharadwaj, along with other senior officials of the Centre and the State, will also attend the event. The celebration is expected to witness the participation of nearly 2,000 representatives from all 10 PESA States, including panchayat representatives, sportspersons, cultural artists and others. The PESA Mahotsav is envisaged as a national platform to celebrate the cultural and traditional heritage of tribal communities from PESA areas.
According to an official statement, several important national initiatives on PESA will be launched on December 24, including the PESA Portal for dissemination of information and monitoring of PESA implementation, PESA Indicators to assess the status of implementation across States, Training Modules on PESA in Tribal Languages to strengthen awareness and grassroots capacity-building and an E-book on Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh, documenting the region’s traditional knowledge, culture and heritage.
As part of the celebration, special Gram Sabhas will be held in PESA Gram Panchayats of Andhra Pradesh with the participation of elected representatives from the participating States on 10 identified PESA themes. In addition, special Gram Sabhas will also be organised across all 10 PESA States on December 24, focusing on strengthening community participation, protection of natural resources and preservation of customary practices, livelihoods and social justice.
The programme will witness a range of sports and cultural activities, showcasing the diversity and vibrancy of India’s tribal heritage. The main venue for the Mahotsav will be Visakhapatnam Port Authority Campus, with activities spread across Ramakrishna Beach, Indoor Stadium, Cricket Stadium and the Kalavani Auditorium, all in Visakhapatnam city.
In terms of Article 243M(4)(b) of the Constitution of India, Parliament enacted “The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996” (called as PESA Act), to extend the provisions of Part-IX of the Constitution, with certain exceptions and modification, to the Scheduled Areas.
Scheduled Areas are those areas which are declared by the President of India. Article 244(1) and the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution deal with provisions relating to the Scheduled Areas. Since those Scheduled Areas are mentioned under Fifth Schedule of the Constitution, therefore, they are called as Fifth Schedule Areas. Currently, Fifth Schedule Areas have been declared in 10 States—Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan and Telangana.

title: Kerala State Electricity Boards invites EoI for establishing public EV charging stations under PM E-DRIVE scheme
summary: KSEB invites expressions of interest for public EV charging stations under PM E-DRIVE, enhancing electric vehicle infrastructure in Kerala.
content:
The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has invited expressions of interest (EoI) from charge point operators (CPO) for establishing electric vehicle (EV) public charging stations under the Centre’s PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) scheme.
The KSEB on Friday invited the EoI for operators under category C of the scheme for establishing charging stations on land parcels with ‘unrestricted public access.’ Category C covers charging infrastructure for locations such as city streets, shopping malls, market complexes and highways.
The charge point operator must be an established organisation or company engaged in the development and management of EV charging infrastructure, according to the KSEB.
PM E-DRIVE has a national outlay of ₹10,900 Crore. The Union Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has earmarked ₹2,000 crore for public charging infrastructure under four categories of the PM E-DRIVE. The key objective is to accelerate EV adoption by establishing a robust network of public charging network across the country.
Through an October 16 order, the Kerala government has designated KSEB as the State nodal agency for the scheme to aggregate the demand for charging stations and submit proposals to the MHI. Under category C, the CPOs are eligible for 80% subsidy on upstream infrastructure costs.
The KSEB had already submitted Phase-I and Phase-II proposals under the scheme covering KSEB-owned and government-allotted land parcels. These proposals cover 342 locations with 1,030 chargers across categories A and B, with an estimated project cost of ₹274 crore.  Category A covers State and Union government premises and category B, locations in cities and along highways owned or controlled by the State and Union governments.
“While the KSEB is directly coordinating with government departments for category A and B (public land), it has developed a dedicated online portal to facilitate the applications from the CPOs for category C,” the EoI document said. The MHI has full authority for the final evaluation and approval of proposals and is responsible for sanctioning and releasing subsidies under the scheme.
Kerala has over 3 lakh electric vehicles, mostly passenger vehicles, on its roads at present. The State is now in the process of establishing high-capacity charging infrastructure and related facilities for e-trucks along freight corridors under the PM E-DRIVE.

title: Thrissur Corporation councillors, district panchayat members take oath
summary: Thrissur Corporation and district panchayat councillors take oath in a ceremonial event, marking the start of their official duties.
content:
All 56 members elected to the Thrissur Corporation and 30 members elected to the district panchayat were sworn in at a ceremony on Sunday held at the corporation hall and the District Planning Bhavan respectively.
District Collector Arjun Pandian administered the oath to the senior-most elected councillor M.L. Rosy at the function in the corporation hall. Elected from the Kalathode division, Ms. Rosy later administered the oath to the remaining councillors.
Revenue Minister K. Rajan, MLA P. Balachandran, former Mayors and councillors, and other public representatives attended the ceremony. Following the oath-taking, the first meeting of the newly elected Corporation council was convened at the corporation hall, chaired by Ms. Rosy.
During the swearing-in ceremony of the district panchayat members, Mr. Pandian administered the oath to the senior-most elected member Mary Thomas.
Elected from the Vazhany division, Ms. Thomas subsequently administered the oath to the remaining members. Of the newly sworn-in members, nine took the oath in the name of God, while the remaining 21 members opted for a solemn affirmation.
The oath-taking ceremony was attended by Mr. Balachandran, former district panchayat president V.S. Prince, former vice-president Latha Chandran, and other members.
Following the ceremony, the first meeting of the district panchayat was convened at the District Panchayat Hall to initiate steps for commencing administrative functions.

title: Global repute to Kalamalla inscription soon: Deepa Venkat
summary: Deepa Venkat announces global recognition efforts for the historic 575 CE Kalamalla inscription at Kadapa's CP Brown Library.
content:
Swarna Bharat Trust’s managing trustee Deepa Venkat on Sunday (December 21, 2025) said that all steps will be taken to make the 575 CE’s Kalamalla inscription, considered the first inscription to be entirely in a Telugu script, famous across the globe.
Ms. Deepa Venkat, daughter of former Vice-President M. Venkaiah Naidu, formally unveiled the replica of the inscription stone at CP Brown Library and Research Centre in Kadapa, at an event organised by Janumaddi Sahithi Peetham on Sunday.
The event marks the centenary year of litterateur Janumaddi Hanumath Sastry (1925 - 2025), who was fondly called as ‘Brown Sastry’ in view of his contribution to the development of the CP Brown Library.
It may be recalled that the replica was specially made by the Swarna Bharat Trust and installed at the library premises, while the original inscription stone is left at its original place in Kalamalla village in Yerraguntla mandal.
“It is upon everyone to popularise Telugu language across the globe and also pass on its literary grandeur to posterity,” she said, while crediting her father Venkaiah Naidu for the idea of making a replica for the inscription and entrusting the task to her.
Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao Official Language Commission’s president P. Trivikrama Rao paid rich tributes to the Britisher Charles Phillip Brown for initiating steps towards revival of Telugu language and wanted every Telugu to exhibit such a spirit towards one’s mother tongue.
Brown Library advisory committee member Janumaddi Vijayabhaskar recalled the Swarna Bharat Trust’s role in making the replica and called it yet another effort by the trust towards safeguarding the ancient traditions and culture.
Yogi Vemana University Vice-Chancellor B. Rajasekhar accompanied Ms. Deepa Venkat to the exhibition on rare inscriptions and research publications at the library.

title: Forest dept. blocks Kumily panchayat attempt to install temporary toilets
summary: Forest Department officials on Sunday blocked the Kumily panchayat’s attempt to set up temporary toilets for Sabarimala pilgrims near the Holiday Home in Kumily in Idukki.
content:
Forest Department officials on Sunday blocked the Kumily panchayat’s attempt to set up temporary toilets for Sabarimala pilgrims near the Holiday Home in Kumily in Idukki.
The town serves as a major transit point for Sabarimala pilgrims travelling from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Puducherry.
According to Kumily panchayat secretary R. Ashok Kumar, hundreds of pilgrims stay overnight at the Sree Dharma Shasta Temple near the town during the pilgrimage season. “During an all-party meeting held before the season began, there was a public demand for temporarily toilets. Consequently, temple authorities petitioned the District Collector Dineshan Cheruvatt, who then ordered the panchayat to install the facilities,” said Mr. Kumar.
The Secretary added that a copy of the Collector’s order was sent to the Periyar Tiger Reserve (PTR) East Deputy Director. Following these instructions, the panchayat invited quotations and alerted the Forest Department. “However, the Forest Department did not respond to the letter,” said the official.
On Sunday, when the panchayat authorities and a contractor arrived to begin the installation of temporary toilets, a Forest Department team led by the Thekkady Range Officer intervened. “The officer reportedly cited a Supreme Court directive that restricts construction activities within forest land. But he failed to produce any order,” said the official.
“The panchayat began this work based on the Collector’s direction, and we have already submitted a report to the Collector regarding the Forest Department’s intervention,” said Mr Kumar.
“ The nearest public toilet is a km away, leading many pilgrims to resort to open defecation near the temple and forest borders. The toilets were planned to remain there till  till January 15. Further action will depend on the Collector’s instructions.” said Mr Kumar.
Meanwhile, the PTR Deputy Director refused to comment, and the Thekkady Range Officer remained unavailable for comment.

title: Christian organisations thank CM for welfare assurance, law against hate speech
summary: Christian organisations thank CM for welfare assurance, law against hate speech
content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s address at the government’s Christmas celebrations held at LB Stadium on Saturday, was “proactive and compassionate”, and marks a significant step towards religious harmony in Telangana, Christian leaders and organisations observed on Sunday.
According to Telangana United Christians & Pastors’ Association (TUCPA), a delegation had met with Minister for Minorities Affairs Mohammed Azharuddin recently and a range of issues concerning welfare of Christians in the State were discussed. It had also met Mr. Reddy and issues of atrocities and hate, both offline and online, and pressing need such as burial grounds, among others, were presented.
Mr. Reddy not only assured that the State government will soon bring out a legislation against hate speech but also expressed his administration’s commitment to safeguard minorities and their welfare, including allocation of land for graveyards for minorities.

title: Kharge slams Centre over hurried changes in VB-G RAM G Act, opposes SHANTI Bill
summary: Mallikarjun Kharge criticizes the Centre for hastily replacing MGNREGA with VB-G RAM G Act, threatening rural employment rights.
content:
All India Congress Committee (AICC) president Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday criticised the Union government for rushing through changes to the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) and, in its stead, bringing in the VB-G RAM G Act, saying that the amendments will have serious consequences for the rural poor
Addressing presspersons at his residence in Kalaburagi, Mr. Kharge said that the proposed changes should have been subjected to detailed discussion and scrutiny.
Instead, the Centre has hurriedly replaced MGNREGA with a differently named scheme, he said.
Questioning the rationale behind renaming the MGNREGA scheme as VB-G RAM G Bill 2025 (the Bill has since received the Presidential assent to become an Act), Mr. Kharge asked what the Modi-led government hopes to achieve by merely changing the scheme’s name while weakening the guarantees provided in MGNREGA.
“Earlier, workers were guaranteed employment and timely wages. Today, their basic right has been taken away by the Union government,” he said.
Referring to the VB-G RAM G Act, he said that the government has effectively diluted the Right to Work.
“The Central government itself admits that there will be at least 60 days with no work. What are the poor supposed to do during that period? This is nothing but an attack on their livelihoods,” he said.
Mr. Kharge pointed out that MGNREGA acted as a lifeline for millions during the COVID-19 pandemic and had earned global recognition.
He questioned the removal of Mahatma Gandhi’s name from the scheme. “What was wrong with MGNREGA that helped the poor survive an unprecedented crisis?” he asked.
The veteran leader accused the BJP-led Central government of first opposing welfare schemes launched during the UPA government era and later reintroducing them by merely changing their names.
Stating that the Centre lacks long-term vision and is acting against Constitutional principles, Mr. Kharge said that the Central government is systematically dismantling social security measures and pushing privatization across sectors.
Mr. Kharge also condemned the Union government for replacing the Atomic Energy Act with the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Bill 2025.
He said that the Bill will weaken public oversight and promote privatisation. The Congress will oppose the SHANTI Bill both inside and outside Parliament by intensifying agitation across the nation.

title: CREDAI thanks government for amending building rules in Andhra Pradesh
summary: CREDAI praises Andhra Pradesh government for amending building rules, enhancing regulatory clarity and promoting sustainable infrastructure for developers.
content:
Members of the Andhra Pradesh chapter of the Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI) have expressed gratitude to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MA&UD) Minister P. Narayana for introducing significant amendments to the Andhra Pradesh Building Rules-2017 through G.O. Ms. No. 273.
Speaking after meeting the Minister, CREDAI office-bearers Buddiga Srinivas and Bayana Srinivasa Rao said that CREDAI-AP had been in constant dialogue with the State government through representations and consultations with senior officials from the department, the Directorate of Town and Country Planning (DTCP), the Fire Services Department, and other relevant authorities.
They said these changes ensure alignment with prominent national jurisdictions and provide clear regulatory certainty for both developers and the approving authorities.
A practical mechanism had also been introduced, allowing for initial approvals for buildings up to 24 meters, with subsequent approvals contingent upon the submission of a Fire No Objection Certificate (NOC). At the same time, the newly amended regulations ensure that structural design and safety certifications cover the entire proposed height from the beginning, balancing safety requirements with procedural efficiency, they said.
The members said to promote sustainable infrastructure, impact fee reductions of 10%, 15% and 20% had been extended to IGBC-rated Silver, Gold, and Platinum skyscraper projects respectively.
The G.O. also includes provisions to withdraw incentives and impose penalties if developers failed to honour their commitments, they said.

title: Jagan’s birthday celebrated in Kadapa district
summary: Jagan's birthday celebrated in Kadapa with a Rachabanda event, featuring community outreach and charitable activities.
content:
A ‘Rachabanda’ was organised to celebrate former Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s birthday in his native district Kadapa on Sunday (December 21, 2025).
The party’s State official spokesperson and former Proddatur MLA Rachamallu Sivaprasad Reddy attended and presided over the meetings of the party’s village and mandal-level affiliated units.
Mr. Reddy called for a comprehensive look to reach out to the voters at the grassroots. He stressed on the need for  concrete steps to wrest power back from the NDA in the 2029 general elections.
Later, Mr. Sivaprasad Reddy offered special prayers at the Bollavaram Anjaneya Swamy temple and conducted ‘Annadanam’ and distributed bread and fruits to patients at the Government Hospital.

title: Stop floating fantasies, fulfil guarantees first: Kishan Reddy to Congress leaders
summary: Stop floating fantasies, fulfil guarantees first: Kishan Reddy to Congress leaders
content:
Union Minister for Coal and Mines and Secunderabad MP G. Kishan Reddy has urged the Congress leadership to clarify its stance on fulfilling the commitments made during the Assembly elections. “The TG Government is misleading people by introducing a new narrative through its Vision Document while earlier guarantees remain unaddressed,” he said.
In an open letter to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, a copy of which was released to the media, the BJP leader accused the party of being content with “self-congratulation” rather than demanding “accountability”. “Is the ruling Congress now abandoning the guarantees made during the elections? Has the 420 promises’ manifesto been thrown into the Musi River or quietly buried within the walls of Gandhi Bhavan? The people of Telangana deserve a clear and honest answer,” he demanded.
Pointing out that the Congress Government has completed two full years in office, Mr. Kishan Reddy questioned whether Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, or Priyanka Gandhi Vadra had reviewed the status of manifesto implementation. “Did you even raise this issue when Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy met you recently?”he asked.
He also took exception to the ‘congratulations’ conveyed to Mr. Revanth Reddy on completing two years in power, saying it gave the impression that Mrs. Gandhi is unaware of the ground reality regarding the implementation of the six guarantees, or that no serious attempt has been made to assess whether the promises made to the people have been fulfilled.
Referring to the ‘Telangana Rising 2047 ‘ vision document and the party leadership’s appreciation of the Congress Government and the Chief Minister, the Minister urged the Congress Party leadership to clarify its position on guarantees promised to farmers, women, unemployed youth, students, Dalits, tribals, and Backward Classes.
“Before floating new visions, fantasies, and promises, the Congress government must first demonstrate its integrity by fulfilling the commitments already made to the people of Telangana as they are watching and waiting. This betrayal of public trust will not go unanswered. If the Congress Government continues to fail in delivering on its promises, people will deliver a fitting lesson,” he warned.

title: Karnataka notifies auction of 569 liquor vends in January to raise resources
summary: The State government, which is hoping to bridge revenue deficit and raise resources, has announced the timeline to auction 569 discontinued/unallotted liquor licences across Karnataka.
content:
The State government, which is hoping to bridge revenue deficit and raise resources, has announced the timeline to auction 569 discontinued/unallotted liquor licences across Karnataka.
The live e-auction to bring transparency in allocation will be held between January 13 and January 20, 2026, and is expected to bring between ₹600 crore and ₹1,000 crores to the cash-starved exchequer.
While the base price in some interior rural areas has been fixed at ₹70 lakh, the highest base price of ₹1.5 crore has been fixed for 101 licences in Bengaluru city.
For certain licences in Mangaluru and Mysuru, the base price is ₹1.1 crore and in Tumakru base price is ₹1 crore.
Apart from monetisation of land and increasing excise duty on liquor, e-auction of liquor licences was among the means to raise resources to bridge the revenue deficit.
GST rate rationalisation in October, increase in cess collection by the Centre that is not devolved to the States and unable to garner the anticipated ₹3,000 crore through taxes on mines had hit the State’s anticipated revenue resource mobilisation.
The State is staring at a reduction in revenue between ₹15,000 crore and ₹18,000 crores this fiscal even as it is under pressure to fund its five guarantee schemes totalling about ₹60,000 crore annually.
The notification for e-auction through the MSTC portal was issued on Friday, and the auctioned licence will be granted for a period of five excise years for the period ending June 30, 2030.
The e-auction of licences had been announced by Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, who holds the Finance portfolio, in the Budget for 2025-2026.
A note from the government said that the discontinued/unallotted CL (2) given for retail shops and CL (11-C) given to government-owned Mysore Sales International Ltd. are classified as CL (2-A).
The discontinued CL (9) licences are classified as CL (9-A). The licences to be auctioned include 477 CL 2 for retail shops and 92 CL 9 for bars and restaurants licences across the State.
Of the total licences being e-auctioned, 24% will be reserved for Scheduled Castes (17%) and Scheduled Tribes (7%).
Within the 17% reservation for Scheduled Castes, the newly implemented internal reservation matrix of 6% each to Category A (Dalit Left-Madigas) and Category B (Dalit Right-Holeyas), and 5% to Category C (Lambani, Bhovi, Korama and Koracha along with 59 Alemari-nomadic communities) will be provided.
The e-auction of licences has generated interest in the liquor industry since the last allocation of liquor licences in the State was in 1992-1993.
In the absence of any fresh licences, the current licences are being leased out by licences holders at premium rates, especially in the urban centres.
A note from the government said that amendments had been made to the Excise Rules. The process to register bidders will commence on Monday, and training to the prospective bidders and district-level e-auction nodal officers will be held between December 23, 2025 and January 7, 2026.

title: ‘Nagara Natya Sankeertana’ lights up Beach Road in Vizag
summary: "Nagara Natya Sankeertana" celebrates Indian classical arts on Beach Road, Vizag, as a prelude to ITDC-2026.
content:
A unique cultural and spiritual initiative ‘Nagara Natya Sankeertana’—  a celebration of Indian classical dance and music was held on Beach Road in Visakhapatnam city on Sunday morning.
The event, organised by the Nataraj Music and Dance Academy, in association with ‘The Dance India Magazine’, brought together over 200 classical dancers, musicians, and devotees in a devotional procession.  The rally commenced at the Ramakrishna Beach Kalimatha Temple and proceeded along the beachfront to the Annamacharya Statue. Participants rendered soulful `sankeertana’ and performed traditional dances all along the route.
Classical dancers trained in Kuchipudi, Bharatanatyam, and Andhra Natyam, along with senior dance teachers, paid tribute to great saint-poets and the rich heritage of Indian classical arts. The procession drew widespread appreciation from the public and ‘rasikas’ lining the route.
This event served as a prelude to the upcoming International Traditional Dance Congress (ITDC-2026), scheduled to be held from January 2 to 4, 2026 at Kalabharathi AC Auditorium, Visakhapatnam.
The ITDC-2026 centred on preserving and propagating India’s classical dance and music traditions, with a special focus on the devotional compositions of saint-poets, will feature performances, seminars, and workshops.
Vikram Kumar B.R., founder-chairman of ITDC, said ‘Nagara Natya Sankeertana’ was conceived as a spiritual and artistic expression for ITDC-2026.
At the conclusion of the rally, certificates signed by Padma Shri awardees were presented to all the participating children in recognition of their artistic commitment and to encourage them to pursue classical dance and music with dedication and devotion.
The organisers expressed their heartfelt gratitude to cultural institutions, dance schools, parents, and art lovers in Visakhapatnam for their overwhelming support, and invited them to join hands to make ITDC-2026 a memorable, spiritually uplifting, and culturally enriching event for the city.

title: Justice delayed: consumers caught in a web of systemic inconsistencies
summary: Consumers face prolonged litigation and systemic delays in Indian consumer courts, undermining the promise of swift justice.
content:
For many wronged consumers across India, the promise of “speedy justice” enshrined in law remains distant. Consumer courts, conceived asaccessible and inexpensive forums for ordinary citizens, have increasingly become arenas of prolonged litigation.
That reality unfolds in the life of 60-year-old Ashok (name changed), whose consumer dispute has been pending for nearly a decade. At 4 a.m., the small paint factory owner locks his home in Panchkula, Chandigarh, and takes the long road to Delhi. By the time he reaches the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) in the heart of the national capital around 11 a.m., he has already spent seven exhausting hours in transit.
Mr. Ashok’s case relates to an insurance claim arising out of a fire incident that gutted his small paint factory in 2015. When the bench rises for the day, his matter remains unheard. The court master announces the next date — six months later.
“This has been happening for the past three years. For one reason or another, my case never comes up. I don’t know what to do anymore,” Mr. Ashok says.
Mr. Ashok is not alone in experiencing this ordeal.
Twenty-eight-year-old Raju (name changed) from a small district in Chhattisgarh had dreamt of setting up a paper cup manufacturing unit five years ago. He paid the full amount online for a paper cup-making machine and took loan from a local bank to fund the purchase. The machine never arrived.
Mr. Raju has since been embroiled in a protracted litigation — first before the district consumer court, and later at the State forum. His case has now reached  the National Consumer Court after the opposite party decided to challenge the order passed in his favour in the lower forums.
Each hearing requires him to undertake a 24-hour train journey to the national capital — with no assurance that his case will actually be heard.
“The last date was November 24. My case did not come up because the court’s time got exhausted with cases at the top of the list,” he recalls.
“This has happened three or four times already. Every time, I am given another date six months later. I have now turned into a loan defaulter,” Mr. Raju says. “I have been wronged, so I will keep fighting — even if it takes another 10 years.”
The challenges of being your own ‘lawyer’ at the consumer court
Stories such as Mr. Ashok’s and Mr. Raju’s mirror a systemic crisis playing out across consumer courts nationwide.
A response by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution in Parliament shows that as of January 30, 2024, a total of 5.43 lakh consumer complaints were pending before district, State and national consumer commissions.
In 2024, the commissions received 1.73 lakh fresh cases but disposed of only 1.58 lakh, leading to a net increase of nearly 14,900 cases. The trend continued in 2025. Up to July this year, 78,031 new complaints were filed, while 65,537 cases were disposed of.
This backlog persists despite clear statutory timelines under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Section 38(7) of the Act mandates that complaints be decided within three months where no testing or analysis is required, and within five months where such examination is necessary.
The law also explicitly discourages delays, stating that adjournments should not ordinarily be granted unless sufficient cause is shown and reasons are recorded in writing.
Advocate Anand Prakash attributes the delays to deep-rooted structural issues.
“Many consumer commissions are burdened with thousands of pending matters and lack sufficient staff, modern facilities, or effective digital case management systems,” he says. “Vacancies in judicial and non-judicial posts, limited courtrooms and logistical constraints continue to impede timely hearings.”
The staffing crisis has intensified over time. As of August 19, 2025, 18 posts of President and 62 posts of Member were vacant in State Consumer Dispute Redressal Commissions. At the district level, 218 posts of President and 518 posts of Member remained vacant.
This marks a significant rise from February 2, 2024, when 13 posts of President and 47 posts of Member at the State level, and 131 posts of President and 340 posts of Member at the district level were vacant.
Another challenge, Mr. Prakash says, lies in the nature of disputes themselves. “Many commission Members are legally trained but lack subject-matter expertise in specialised areas such as medical negligence, marine insurance, foreign trade or complex financial products.”
This often necessitates expert opinions, laboratory reports or technical clarifications, leading to repeated adjournments. “Without continuous training or specialised benches, complex cases inevitably move much slower than the Act contemplates,” he says.
Delays are also caused by procedural hurdles — non-service of notices, late filing of affidavits, and requests for time to submit additional evidence. “At times, opposite parties deliberately seek adjournments to harass complainants and wear them down,” Mr. Prakash alleges.

title: CPI (M) urges State govt. to reject Labour Codes
summary: Urging the State government to not implement the four Labour Codes notified by the Centre, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) has sought a labour conference, including representatives of political parties and trade unions, on the lines of Kerala model to discuss the adverse effects of these codes.
content:
Urging the State government to not implement the four Labour Codes notified by the Centre, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) has sought a labour conference, including representatives of political parties and trade unions, on the lines of Kerala model to discuss the adverse effects of these codes.
It has also asked the State government to reject Viksit Bharat G Ram G Act brought by the Centre and extend guaranteed employment in urban areas too.
The party has condemned the rising attack on federalism by the ruling BJP at the Centre in terms of financial, legislative, and administrative powers of the State.
Criticising the “anti-democratic” rules, it asked the government to withdraw restrictions imposed on protests and processions across the State, including in Bengaluru.
“Contract and outsourced employment that does not provide security should be regularised. Social Security Act for workers should be implemented. The minimum wages for non-permanent employees in private sector and gram panchayat workers should be increased to ₹36,000 per month and provide a minimum pension of ₹9,000 for the retired,” stated a petition submitted to the State government here.
The petition containing 20 demands was handed over to Agriculture Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy during the CPI (M)’s ‘Janadani’ rally, culmination of a 45-day door to door campaign to collect people’s feedback.
Seeking reservation for locals in employment in the private sector, it urged the State and Union governments to fill vacancies and ensure implementation of Kannada in administration in private sector and Central government offices.
Urging to strengthen government schools and ensure BPL cards to all the eligible people, it demanded that the government provide housing for the houseless. Corruption should be curbed and atrocities on women and Dalits should be controlled, the petition said, expressing fears of minorities due to rise in communalism.
The party has sought diversion of Krishna river waters to address the water shortage in Bayaluseeme districts of Kolar, Tumakuru, Chickballapur, and Bengaluru Rural.

title: Post deadline extension, Waqf Board deals with  new challenges
summary: With the UMEED portal deadline extended by three months, the Telangana State Waqf Board is racing to complete data uploads, while grappling with the tougher task of identifying and verifying numerous unregistered waqf institutions that lack basic documentation.
content:
With the Waqf Tribunal extending the deadline for uploading details on the UMEED portal by three months, the Telangana State Waqf Board (TGWB) is once again racing to complete the exercise. While the Muslim endowments body has identified its immediate areas of focus, it now faces a tougher task: dealing with the many unregistered waqf institutions that lack basic documentation — such as the waqfnama and object of waqf — and may require physical verification.
Sources at the board, who did not wish to be identified, said it was difficult to estimate the exact number of such properties, but acknowledged that they were substantial. As a matter of procedure, whenever properties without a formal declaration of their waqf status are identified, they are registered aswaqf by user,a provision that allows institutions to be treated as Muslim endowments based on their longstanding use for religious purposes.
“There are many properties that have not been registered with the waqf board. In such cases, when they come for registration on the UMEED portal, there will be  a need for awaqfnama(waqf deed). If that is unavailable, then building permission, or an electricity bill. Meaning, any document that establishes the existence of the institution. The verification at the checker level, and the clearance at the approver level, will be based on the document,” the source said.
“There may be cases when a physical verification of these properties is required in case documents are deficient. An inspector-auditor will inspect the property and submit a report. This activity will require a lot of legwork.”
Meanwhile, officials said the UMEED portal was made accessible recently. Work has resumed, and will be further streamlined.
Speaking toThe Hindu, TGWB chief executive officer Mohammed Asadullah said the immediate focus is to register, upload documents, check and approve institutions that are enumerated in thekitabul awqaaf(Book of Waqf), and then those that have been listed under the second waqf survey.
“There are approximately 3,000 properties that are a part of the kitabul awqaaf. These will be taken up first, as documents connected to them are available. Secondly, we will also take up the properties that were a part of the second survey, there are approximately 13,000 such properties. Work has already begun, and we will go full steam in the next few days,” Mr.Asadullah said.

title: Post-SIR, size of electorate in Chennai and nearby districts remains larger than votes polled in 2021 and 2026 polls
summary: Chennai's electorate size surpasses 2021 and 2024 votes, revealing significant voter deletions and concerns among political parties.
content:
Following the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Tamil Nadu, the size of the electorate in most Assembly constituencies in Chennai and its three neighbouring districts is larger than the votes polled during the 2021 Assembly and 2024 Parliamentary elections.
Only in four constituencies, all in the city, did the number of votes polled in 2021 exceed the revised strength of the electorate. The four seats were Villivakkam, R.K. Nagar, Perambur, and Anna Nagar, where the margin of difference varies from 206 in Perambur to 1,386 in Villivakkam to 2,961 in Anna Nagar to 8,671 in R.K. Nagar.
A comparison of the data of votes polled and the existing strength in 37 Assembly constituencies falling under the districts of Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, and Chengalpattu, apart from Chennai throws up interesting details. These four districts have seen a very high degree of deletion of names from the electoral rolls. While examining the data, the fact that during 2020 and 21, the State witnessed two waves of the COVID-19 pandemic, causing a large number of deaths, should also be considered.
On an average, nearly 2 lakh persons had voted in every constituency in 2021 and 1.85 lakh in 2024. The revised draft electoral rolls, published on Friday (December 19) puts the voter size at about 2.3 lakh.
Concern has been expressed by political parties in general, particularly the ruling DMK’s allies in particular, about the level of  deletions, whereas the AIADMK has contended that most of the deleted entries belong to bogus voters. But, the overall picture of the voters’ strength does not indicate any discrepancy with regard to the electorate in the 37 Assembly constituencies, even though what has been released is only the draft electoral roll.
