Some students, however, pointed out that they had earlier faced technical issues while entering registration details. Later, problems reportedly cropped up while remitting fees. At present, a section of teachers were reportedly finding it difficult to upload the students’ internal marks.
According to sources, the internal marks were supposed to be uploaded between December 10 and December 18. When the problems were highlighted, the date was reportedly extended up to December 23.
However, the university authorities refuted the allegations saying none of them are true. The software might go slow if a large number of people use it at the same time, they added. Meanwhile, academics attached to the United Democratic Front have reiterated their claim that K-REAP was launched without adhering to norms.

title: Pregnant woman hospitalised after alleged assault at Jagan’s birthday event
summary: Pregnant woman hospitalized after alleged assault by party activist during Y.S. Jagan's birthday celebrations in Puttaparthi.
content:
The birthday celebrations of former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy took an ugly turn when a pregnant woman was allegedly assaulted by a party activist at Muthyalavaripalle village in Tanakallu mandal of Sri Sathya Sai district late on Sunday.
According to locals, a party activist identified as Ajay organised fireworks involving high-decibel crackers during the celebrations. The loud noise reportedly caused discomfort to a pregnant woman, Sandhyarani. When her family members urged the organisers to stop bursting such crackers, it led to an argument.
The family members alleged that Ajay lost his cool and physically assaulted Sandhyarani, despite knowing that she was pregnant. She was immediately rushed to the government hospital in Kadiri town for medical care. Hospital authorities said that her condition was stable.
The incident led to outrage in the village, with the neighbourhood demanding criminal action against the accused. On Monday, Kadiri TDP MLA Kandikunta Venkata Prasad visited the hospital and spoke to the victim and her family members, assuring them that prompt legal action would be initiated against those responsible for the incident.
A police official said that the incident was under investigation and the medical records would also be verified.

title: R.P. Sivaji to be LDF Mayor candidate for Thiruvananthapuram Corporation
summary: The Left Democratic Front (LDF)’s decision to contest in the Mayor election in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation has added to the drama and uncertainty of the Mayoral contest this time. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has decided to field R.P. Sivaji, Vilappil Area Secretary of the party, for the Mayor post, but has been tight-lipped about the front’s strategy for the election to be held in the council hall on December 26.
content:
The Left Democratic Front (LDF)’s decision to contest in the Mayor election in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation has added to the drama and uncertainty of the Mayoral contest this time. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has decided to field R.P. Sivaji, councillor and Vilappil Area Secretary of the party, for the Mayor post, but has been tight-lipped about the front’s strategy for the election to be held in the council hall on December 26. 

“The CPI(M) district committee has taken the decision on the candidature. There has been no other political discussions in this regard,” says Mr.Sivaji, who has in the past also served as a councillor in the Corporation. 

Despite the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) scoring a historic victory at the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation in the local body elections, it has still fallen one short of the required majority number of 51 in the 101-member council. The two Independent candidates who won in the Kannammoola and Poundkadavu wards have kept their options open. It remains to be seen whether they would bargain for key positions including the Mayorship or the chairperson post of one of the standing committees in exchange for their support.

The LDF’s tally of seats had fallen from 51 seats in 2020 to 29 seats this year. However, the BJP’s inability to get a majority appears to have led the front to contest the Mayor election. Though the election in the Vizhinjam ward is pending, the LDF and the United Democratic Front (UDF) have an upper hand over the BJP in the region. 

The BJP itself is caught in a bind regarding its Mayor candidate with former district president V.V.Rajesh, three-time councillor Karamana Ajith and R. Sreelekha, former Director General of Police, in contention. The party is expected to announce the Mayor candidate a day ahead of the elections.

title: PDS rice, vehicle seized, two booked
summary: Officials seized 2,280 kg of PDS rice and a vehicle in Kalaburagi, booking two for illegal transport and sale.
content:
Based on specific information that rice meant for the public distribution system (PDS) was being illegally transported for sale in the black market, officials intercepted a vehicle near the Vishwaradhya temple on Aland Road on the outskirts of Kalaburagi on Monday and seized 2,280 kg of rice.
Officials of the Sub-Urban Police Station along with the Food Inspector intercepted the vehicle near a petrol bunk connecting Aland Road and seized it along with the rice packets being transported to Osmanabad district in Maharashtra for illegal sale.
Officials seized the rice, valued at ₹82,000, and the vehicle worth about ₹5 lakh.
A case has been registered at the Sub-Urban Police Station against Siddu Poojari and driver Rahul Kalakutagi. Investigation is under way.

title: British-era missionary letters, photos reveal early plantation life in Munnar
summary: Discover early plantation life in Munnar through translated letters and photos from British-era missionary Father Alfonse Maria De Los Angeles.
content:
Early missionary accounts from Munnar have shed new light on the history of plantation sector in the hill station during the British period. The historical records came to light when letters and photos were uncovered during a research pertaining to a book on Mount Carmel Basilica, the first Catholic Church established in the high ranges of Munnar.
According to Church authorities, Spanish missionary Father Alfonse Maria De Los Angeles arrived in Munnar around 1894. His letters and those of other missionaries, originally written in Spanish and French, were published in “Carmelite” journals from 1900 to 1980. A collection of 46 letters and photos has been preserved in Spain and recently translated into English, Tamil, and Malayalam to document Munnar’s history.
A tree house at Pallivasal near Munnar in 1929. A photo taken by the missionaries. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
“The missionaries’ letters and photographs highlighted the old Munnar town, tree houses, the ropeway system, and the transformation of the wilderness into a sprawling plantation station. The book also details an ambitious but unsuccessful attempt by missionaries to erect a cross atop Anamudi, the highest peak in South India,” said a church representative.
The Church has published a book titledMunnar Basilicain Malayalam, English, and Tamil. The book was written by Fr. Antony Pattapparampil, Sojan G. Munnar, and Fr. Anosh Abraham. Fr. Abraham, a researcher in Spain, collected the letters and photographs from the church archives.
Munnar Basalica, a multilingual book on Mount Carmel Basilica. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
Sojan G., one of the book’s contributors, explained that the recovery of these letters was essential to the project. “These letters and photographs are an eye-opener. During the 1924 flood, the water level reached St. Anthony’s chapel at Mount Carmel Church. The church provided shelter to hundreds of people. After the flood, the new Munnar town was developed close to the church,” said Mr. Sojan.
Fr. Pattapparampil said, “These historical documents provide a rare, first-hand look at the British era in Munnar. Unlike other historical texts, these letters were written and photographs captured in real-time, describing the daily reality of life in the hills.”
Munnar in early period. A photo taken by missionaries. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
Fr. Angeles arrived in Munnar in 1894 after travelling over 128 km on foot from Varapuzha. After four years of effort, and with the support of tea plantation management, he erected a prayer shed in 1898. In May 2024, Mount Carmel Church was officially elevated to the status of a Minor Basilica.

title: Policing is a service-oriented responsibility, Chittoor SP tells trainee constables
summary: Chittoor SP emphasizes policing as a service-oriented duty during training for new constables at the District Police Training Centre.
content:
A nine-month intensive residential training programme for the 2025 batch of Stipendary Cadet Trainee Police Constables commenced on Monday (December 22, 2025) at the District Police Training Centre (DPTC) here. The batch consisted of 139 trainees, including 61 from Srikakulam and 78 from Vizianagaram district.
Interacting with the trainees, Superintendent of Police Tushar Dudi stressed that policing is a service-oriented responsibility rather than just a job. He said that the training period would remain crucial for shaping their careers and expressed his desire for the batch to emerge as the best in the State.
Speaking to the media, the SP said that the office of the Director General of Police (DGP) had issued the updated training curriculum, focusing on physical fitness, drill, weapon handling, legal studies, ethics, discipline, and community policing to address evolving crime patterns and modern challenges. Medical examinations of the trainees were conducted on the first day to ensure physical and mental fitness, Mr. Dudi said.
The SP highlighted the importance of discipline, punctuality, and commitment, urging trainees to remain field-ready to respond to law and order issues, emergencies, and disasters. Senior officers, including Additional SP (Operations and In-charge Administration) S.R. Rajashekar Raju, Deputy SP T. Sainath, and other police officials, were present.

title: Three Sabarimala pilgrims injured in accident
summary: Three Sabarimala pilgrims injured in Pathanamthitta bus accident; residents demand stricter traffic enforcement amid safety concerns.
content:
Three people sustained serious injuries after the driver of a bus carrying Sabarimala pilgrims lost control of the vehicle, which then hit other vehicles at Thulappally, near Ranni in Pathanamthitta, on Monday.
The accident occurred around 7.45 a.m. at the Thulappally-Alappattu junction. The bus carrying pilgrims from Tamil Nadu was on the Thulappally slope when the driver lost control of it. The bus first hit two cars before colliding with a tourist bus. The three injured were travelling in one of the cars. All the vehicles involved in the accident were carrying Sabarimala pilgrims.
The seriously injured were shifted to a hospital at Erumely. Those who sustained minor injuries were taken to hospitals at Nilackal.
Meanwhile, local residents alleged that the accident occurred as pilgrim vehicles were being allowed to ply along the Thulappally-Sabarimala old road in violation of restrictions. They pointed out that there was a court order directing that pilgrim vehicles should be diverted through the new road and not through the old route. The residents demanded stricter enforcement of traffic regulations to prevent further accidents during the pilgrimage season.

title: Left parties stage protest, criticise changes in rural job scheme
summary: Left parties protest in Kalaburagi against the BJP's changes to rural job schemes, criticizing the new VB-G RAM G Act 2025.
content:
Opposing the BJP-led Union government’s move to alter the erstwhile Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), members of Left parties, including the CPI, CPI(M) and SUCI(C), staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s office in Kalaburagi on Monday.
Addressing the protestors, CPI(M) district secretary K. Neela said that the erstwhile MGNREGA was implemented during the UPA regime following sustained pressure from Left parties. It was conceived as a universal, demand-driven law guaranteeing a limited but legally enforceable right to work.
She said that the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act 2025, which has replaced MGNREGA, will fundamentally dilute this right and deny rural workers their entitlements.
Ms. Neela said that the new law will free the Centre from its obligation to provide funds based on demand for work. She dismissed the Central government’s claim that it will increase guaranteed employment from 100 to 125 days as a hollow promise.
She said that the rationalisation of job cards will push large sections of rural households out of the scheme.
She further said that suspending employment for up to 60 days during peak agricultural season will deprive rural workers of work when it is most needed, forcing them to depend on landlords.
Changes in the funding pattern will shift the financial burden onto State governments while denying them any role in decision-making, including making them bear the cost of unemployment allowance and compensation for delay in payments.
“These changes are aimed at shrinking the scope of the scheme and weakening the accountability of the Union government,” she claimed.
Renaming MGNREGA as G RAM G amounts to an insult to Mahatma Gandhi and reflects the BJP-RSS’ hostility towards his legacy, she said.
The Left parties demanded the immediate withdrawal of the VB-G RAM G Act and urged the Central government to strengthen the MGNREGA ensuring adequate budgetary allocation to guarantee at least 200 days of employment.
CPI State Council member Moula Mulla, district secretary Mahesh Rathod, executive council member Bheemashankar Madiyal, SUCI(C) secretary Veerabhadra and activists Meenakshi Bali, Prabhudev Yelasanghi, S.M. Sharma, Mahesh S. Sudhama Dhanni, Lavitra Vastrad and others participated in the protest.

title: ₹146.84 crore subsidy credited to mango farmers in Chittoor, says Collector
summary: Andhra Pradesh credits ₹146.84 crore subsidy to 31,929 mango farmers in Chittoor, ensuring financial relief and support.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has credited ₹146.84 crore as subsidy to the bank accounts of as many as 31,929 mango farmers in Chittoor district, said Collector Sumit Kumar on Monday (December 22, 2025).
During an interaction with farmers at the Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS) programme here, the Collector said that more than 20,000 farmers received subsidies exceeding ₹1 lakh each, a relief from market volatility. The government remained committed to safeguarding the interests of mango farmers. Data of farmers had been collected, and a supporting price of ₹4 per kg was deposited directly into their bank accounts, the Collector added.
The Collector said that the State was pursuing the proposal for setting up mango boards in the district.

title: BWSSB conducts 4,000 inspections in a month, cracks down on illegal water connections
summary: BWSSB conducts over 4,000 inspections to eliminate illegal water connections, enforcing penalties and legal actions against violators.
content:
The Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) has carried out over 4,000 inspections across the city in the past month, as part of an intensified drive to curb illegal water and sewerage connections, officials said on Monday.
The special task force, known as the ‘Blue Force’, detected and acted against hundreds of unauthorised connections during the month-long operation, which, the BWSSB said, were contributing to revenue losses and reduced water pressure in several areas.
The teams inspected 237 buildings across four zones and disconnected 70 illegal water connections in a single day, on December 20.
The south zone recorded the highest number of violations, with 33 illegal connections disconnected from 61 buildings. This was followed by the east zone, where 18 connections were severed, and the west zone, which saw 15 disconnections. In the north zone, the authorities disconnected four illegal connections, out of 44 buildings.
BWSSB Chairman V. Ram Prasath Manohar said the task force was formed to identify connections that bypass official meters or operate without approval.
Highlighting that the drive would continue until every drop was accounted for, Mr. Manohar said the board was increasingly using data-based inputs to identify areas with a high likelihood of violations. He warned that properties found with illegal water or sewerage connections would face not only disconnection but also penalties and legal action, particularly in cases involving bypass lines or unauthorised sanitary connections.

title: Suspense over Pala deepens as Congress State leadership set to intervene
summary: Three independent members seek both the chairperson and vice-chairperson posts for the first three years
content:
Amid the euphoria of a strong comeback in Kottayam, the United Democratic Front’s march towards power in the Pala municipality has hit an unexpected roadblock.
What should have been a smooth post-poll consolidation has instead turned into a tense political standoff,  prompting an inervention by the State leadership of the Congress. The 26-member Pala municipal council has 12 councillors with the Left Democratic Front (LDF), 10 with the UDF, one Congress rebel elected as an independent, and three members belonging to an independent collective.
On paper, the UDF is within striking distance of power while in practice, the negotiations have become a minefield. According to sources, lying at the heart of the impasse is an opening demand by the independent collective seeking both the chairperson and vice-chairperson posts for the first three years. The proposal would see Diya Binu as chairperson and her father, Binu, who leads the collective, simultaneously occupying the vice-chairperson’s post.
While sections of the district Congress leadership appear inclined to accept the demand in the interest of securing numbers, the move has triggered a backlash within the party. All six Congress councillors have reportedly drawn a firm line, warning that conceding both posts to the Pulikkakandam family would set a damaging precedent and weaken the party’s authority within the council. “Handing over both top posts is politically indefensible and could haunt the Congress,” a senior party leader remarked, suggesting that a staggered arrangement would be more equitable.
The complexity deepens within the UDF itself with competing ambitions at play with the Kerala Congress and the lone Congress rebel too staking claims for the chairpersonship, at least for one-year terms. If the independents insist on a three-year tenure, the remaining two years would barely suffice to accommodate all claimants, threatening to unravel the alliance before it takes shape.
Meanwhile, the independent collective has maintained that it has not entered into formal talks with any political front. Instead, soon after taking oath on Sunday, it convened a ‘Janasabha’ (people’s council) in Pala to gauge public opinion on its political stance. Organisers claim the overwhelming mood at the meeting favoured the UDF.

title: Over 900 students in Vizianagaram take talent test ahead of finals
summary: Over 926 students in Vizianagaram participate in talent tests to prepare for upcoming final exams in physics, chemistry, and math.
content:
Vizianagaram District Skill Development Officer G. Prasanth Kumar on Monday said that competitive examinations for schoolchildren enable them them to assess their knowledge and take steps towards improving and preparing to face future academic challenges and interviews.
Avanthi’s St. Theressa Institute of Engineering and Technology, Garividi in Vizianagaram district conducted talent tests over the last three days for class 10 students in physics, chemistry and mathematics ahead of their final exams which will be held from March 16 to April 1, 2025.
Mr. Prasanth Kumar distributed cash prizes to meritorious students K. Avanthika, Ch. Niharika, J. Harini and others. Avanthi College principal J. Bala Bhaskara Rao said that 926 students participated in the talent test which is held every year for students from Garividi, Cheepurupalli, Merakamudidam, Gurla and other nearby areas. He announced that more tests would be conducted soon as the response was overwhelming this year.

title: State also empowered to issue directions to power generators during emergency scenarios: Karnataka High Court
summary: Karnataka High Court affirms state's authority to direct power generators during emergencies, ensuring adequate supply to the state grid.
content:
The State government also has the power, like the Central government, to invoke emergency clause under the Section 11 of the Electricity Act, 2003 to mandate all the power generating companies within the State to supply power exclusively to the State grid in ‘extraordinary circumstances’ like acute electricity shortage, said the High Court of Karnataka.
A Division Bench comprising Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice Rajesh Rai.K delivered the verdict while allowing the appeals, filed by the State Load Dispatch Centre and the State government, against the March 11, 2024 verdict of a single Judge.
The single Judge had quashed the State government’s October 16, 2024 order asking all the power generators in Karnataka to operate and maintain the concerned generating stations to maximum exportable capacity and supply all the electricity generated to the State grid subject to certain conditions.
Single judge’s view
While allowing the petitions filed by NLS Sugars Ltd., Chamundeshwari Sugars Ltd., and Altilium Energie Private limited, the single Judge had said that only the Central government is the “appropriate government” under Section 11 of the Act for issuing direction under ‘extraordinary circumstances” to even those energy generating companies engaged in inter-state electricity transmission.
The State government, invoking Section 11 of the Act, had issued on October 16, 2023 a notification when Karnataka was reeling from a severe power crisis triggered by a failed monsoon and depleted hydel reservoirs, resulting in a deficient power supply of approximately 3,000 to 3,500 MW. The State had directed all power generators, including captive and co-generation plants, to operate at maximum capacity and supply their entire power to the State grid at a provisional tariff of ₹4.86 per unit.
Reserved
While reversing single Judge’s verdict, the Bench said: “In our view, the internal coherence of Section 11 of the Act is a bulwark interpretation in circumstances when the embedded generators operate within a State, although trades/sells power inter-state, the State Government is the appropriate government capable of both issuing directions and ensuring compensation through the State Electricity Regulatory Commission.”
Also, the Bench said that “ideally extraordinary circumstances, in context of Section 11 of the Act are archetypically regional and confer jurisdiction on the State government over generators physically located within the State during state specific crises.”
On the nature of power generation by the petitioner-sugar industries, the Bench said that though the regulatory framework permits captive generators and co-generation plants, like the ones operated by the petitioners, to sell surplus power through myriad mechanisms, however, this flexibility does not alter their fundamental character as embedded State generators primarily serve captive load.
Mere grant of No Objection Certificates (NOC) from the SLDC for scheduling power through open access and registered on power exchanges to sell surplus power does not transform captive generators like the petitioners into inter-State generating company under a composite scheme, the Bench said.

title: Eight-member online cricket betting gang busted in Guntur
summary: Police in Guntur arrest eight in online cricket betting raid, seizing ₹13.60 lakh in cash and electronic devices.
content:
Police busted an online cricket betting gang and arrested eight persons, including two organisers, in Guntur on Monday. They seized cash and electronic gadgets worth several lakhs from the accused. Acting on specific information, the Pattabhipuram police and Task Force raided a house at Vikas Nagar around 11.30 a.m. and found betting in progress during an overseas Big Bash League (BBL) match.
Police seized ₹13.60 lakh in cash, froze ₹5.05 lakh in online transactions, and recovered eight mobile phones, a laptop and cards used for transactions, said Superintendent of Police (SP) Vakul Jindal at a press conference. He stated that the operation was part of intensified surveillance to curb betting and other unlawful activities.
Investigation revealed that Tatineni Srinivasa Rao, with associate Yerrabothula Vijaya Bhaskar Reddy, had been running online cricket betting for nearly a decade using mobile applications and WhatsApp groups. Bets ranging from ₹100 to ₹10,000 were accepted ball by ball, with payments routed through digital platforms and settlements made within 24 hours.
The accused were caught while preparing to conduct betting on the Sydney Thunder-Brisbane Heat match in the BBL. All the eight arrested are residents of Guntur and will be produced before the court soon.

title: Attack, protest against Christmas carols unfortunate: Archbishop
summary: Thrissur Archbishop condemns attacks on Christmas carols, emphasizing their message of joy and the need for peaceful responses.
content: Terming the attacks on and opposition to Christmas carols as unfortunate, Thrissur Archbishop Mar Andrews Thazhath said such incidents were deeply condemnable and went against the spirit of Christmas. “Christmas carols are the music of angels. They convey messages of joy and peace to all humanity. Attacks on such expressions of goodwill are highly deplorable. However, there should be no hostile or retaliatory response to such provocations, because Christmas is a celebration of peace and happiness,” the Archbishop said.

title: Police to launch State-wide special drive against drunk-driving from December 24
summary: Bengaluru police will launch a special anti-drunk driving campaign from December 24 to curb festive road accidents.
content:
In an effort to reduce the number of road accidents caused due to rash, negligent, and drunk-driving, the State police will launch a State-wide special drive against erring motorists from December 24 to December 31, ahead of the New Year celebrations.
In a circular issued by the office of the Additional Director General of police (Traffic and Road Safety) on Saturday, to the heads of the city commissionorates and district police chiefs, the officials have been directed to take stringent action against motorists driving under the influence of alcohol.
The directive follows a meeting chaired by Justice Abhay Manohar Sapre, former Supreme Court judge and chairman of the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety, held on Friday  to review road safety measures in the State. The committee reportedly observed that incidents of road accidents caused by drunk-driving tend to rise significantly during festive and New Year celebrations, leading to an increase in fatalities and injuries.
In view of this, the police have been instructed to intensify enforcement across all police units in the State. According to the order, all unit heads have been directed to ensure that station house officers conduct a special enforcement drive in their jurisdictions. Apart from drunk and drive cases, the police have been instructed to book cases against motorists for violations including riding without helmets, driving without seat belts, overspeeding, wheeling, triple-riding, and using mobile phones while driving.
The special drive will be implemented across all police commissionerates and district police units, including Bengaluru city and KGF, under the supervision of senior officers.

title: Private hospitals flag concerns over KPME (Amendment) Bill, 2025
summary: Private hospitals in Karnataka express concerns over the KPME (Amendment) Bill, 2025, warning it may harm healthcare and enable quackery.
content:
Private medical establishments in Karnataka have raised strong objections to several provisions of the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments (Amendment) Bill, 2025, terming them impractical, ambiguous and potentially counter-productive. The Bill was passed in the recent Winter session of the State Legislature in Belagavi.
In a representation to the State government, the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and the Federation of Hospital Associations of Karnataka (FHAK) said the amendments, while ostensibly aimed at improving regulatory efficiency and patient safety, could adversely affect bona fide private hospitals and inadvertently enable quackery and regulatory misuse.
Pavan Kumar Patil, chairman of the Hospital Board of IMA in Karnataka and joint secretary of FHAK, said the concerns stem from “serious gaps between the intent of the law and ground realities of hospital administration”.
“The amendment Bill, in its present form, risks criminalising procedural lapses, disrupting healthcare delivery and weakening regulation by creating loopholes. We urge the government to hold detailed stakeholder consultations before implementing it. We will soon meet Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao in this regard,” Dr. Patil toldThe Hinduon Monday.
One of the key objections relates to the removal of representation from private medical establishments in the Registration and Grievance Redressal Authority. While the principal Act of 2007 provided for a representative of private hospitals in the authority, the amendment removes this provision, retaining only one IMA member and a woman member. The associations argued that excluding hospital administrators from the decision-making process would lead to regulatory decisions being taken without practical understanding of issues such as staffing norms, emergency care obligations, infrastructure requirements and compliance timelines.
Another major concern is the replacement of the earlier provision for “deemed approval” with a six-month provisional registration system. Under the original Act, applications not disposed of within three months were automatically deemed approved. The associations said the new provision creates prolonged regulatory uncertainty for hospitals that have already made significant financial investments and complied with requirements.
The representation also flagged ambiguity in the term “existing establishments”, which the amendment states will be deemed provisionally registered at the commencement of the Act. “As the term is not defined, it could be misused by illegal or unregistered operators, thereby providing a temporary legal shield for quacks,” Dr. Patil said.
Issues surrounding renewal of registration were also highlighted. At present, hospitals that miss renewal deadlines are forced to apply afresh, pay double fees and are issued new KPME registration numbers. This disrupts continuity of empanelment with government health schemes, insurance companies and third-party administrators, affecting both payments and patient services, he said.
The provision granting registration without inspection to establishments with accreditations such as NABH or NQAS was described as conceptually flawed. Accreditation bodies require hospitals to be registered and functional before granting accreditation, making this clause impractical for new hospitals, the doctor explained.
Concerns were also raised about powers granted for seizure of documents during inspections. “Hospital records are often completed after procedures or emergencies, and immediate seizure of incomplete records could unfairly incriminate doctors, especially in emergency situations. There should be a safeguard clause mandating written requisition and a minimum of 72 hours to furnish records, except in cases of proven tampering,” he said.

title: Strive to protect India’s glorious educational heritage, says Joshi
summary: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi emphasizes the need to protect India's educational heritage and overcome colonial inferiority complexes.
content:
“India has a glorious cultural and educational heritage. We are emerging as a developed and powerful nation today due to the strength of this heritage. All of us need to realise this and strive to protect it,” Union Minister Pralhad Joshi said in Belagavi on Sunday.
He was speaking at the centenary ceremony of B.K. Model High School.
“The British wanted to enslave us. That is why, they sowed the seeds of inferiority in our minds. India was given the image of a poor and ignorant nation. We need to get out of the inferiority complex given to us by them. We need to realise that under the rule of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has reached unprecedented levels of development. There is significant progress in removing such inferiority. We should never forget that our country has the legacy of wisemen like Aryabhata, Brahmagupta, Varahamihira, Charaka and Sushruta,” he said.
“Our country is endowed with the unique knowledge of sages and saints. Some people try to term the new education policy as saffronization. It is rather a move that reflects India’s sacred knowledge heritage. Today, India has become the fourth largest economic power in the world because of our knowledge heritage,” he said.
KLE Society chairman Prabhakar Kore recalled the contribution of the founders of the school. “The influence of missionary schools was high during the time when Belagavi was the regional headquarters of the British rulers. In such difficult times, some courageous teachers and donors came together to start this school. It is a matter of pride that B.K. Model School has completed a successful journey of a hundred years through quality education,” he said.
The school committee has organised several programmes, including an alumni meet.
School committee office-bearers Avinash Potdar and A.K. Hungund, Mayor Mangesh Pawar, Deputy Mayor Vani Joshi, writer Basavaraj Jagajampi, the former MLA Sanjay Patil, school alumnus Jayant Deshpande and others were present.

title: Suvendu Adhikari leads protests outside Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata against attack on Hindus
summary: Protests led by Suvendu Adhikari and Congress in Kolkata demand justice for Hindus attacked in Bangladesh amid rising tensions.
content:
Leader of the Opposition Suvendu Adhikari and Congress leaders held protests outside the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata on Monday (December 22, 2025) against the attack on Hindus in the neighbouring country.
These protests came in response to the Hindu community memberDipu Chandra Das’s lynchingin Bangladesh amid the growing unrest in their nation after the death of their popular youth leaderSharif Osman Hadi, who was shot deadin public.
Mr. Adhikari and other Bharatiya Janata Party supporters tried to march to the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in the Beck Bagan area. Their protest march was joined by many Hindu monks, which was stopped by the Kolkata Police due to safety concerns. The protesters scuffled with the police as they were barred from entering the commission. Effigies of Muhammad Yunus, Chief Adviser to Bangladesh interim government, were burnt on the road.
When they were barred from moving ahead, Mr. Adhikari and other protesters conducted a sit-in demonstration on the road.
They also announced that a protest would be conducted across the border areas in West Bengal on December 24 if there was no action against Das’s lynching in Bangladesh. Mr. Adhikari said they would head back to the Deputy High Commission on December 26 to protest.
“We will not let this matter go. Dipu Das was burnt alive. We will not allow them to sit here [at the Bangladesh High Commission],” Mr. Adhikari said, while heading back from the protest.
The protesters carried posters of “We want revenge for Dipu Das’s murder”.
Congress workers also held a similar protest outside the Deputy High Commission a few hours before the BJP. They were also stopped by the Kolkata Police before they could enter the commission office to file their deputation.
“We have come to share this message and urge the Bangladesh Deputy Commissioner so that every community in Bangladesh can live together peacefully,” one of the Congress leaders said. They raised slogans of “Vande Mataram” and asked for an end to violence against minority Hindus in Bangladesh in the name of politics and religion.

title: ‘Gen Z Grooves’ launched to train young percussionists
summary: ‘Gen Z Grooves’ empowers young percussionists through workshops led by renowned artistes, fostering musical talent across Kerala.
content:
Noted tabla artiste Umesh Moghe launched ‘Gen Z Grooves’, a State-level workshop series for training young percussionists, at Pookkad Kalalayam near Koyilandy in Kozhikode district on Monday (December 22, 2025). Nearly 30 learners from different parts of the State turned up for the workshop.
Opening the sessions, Mr. Moghe said artistes should be considered and treated like soldiers for their selfless role in safeguarding the tradition of music and culture. “We should honour the tradition first even while valuing the services of artistes,” he observed.
Emerging percussionist Arjun Kaliprasad, who conceived the ‘Gen Z Grooves’ project, introduced its features and objectives to the audience. He said the project was designed with a mission to pick talented young percussionists from all the 14 districts and offer them district-level training under the leadership of eminent artistes.
He said the workshop series, formally launched in Kozhikode, would continue in other districts and conclude in Thiruvananthapuram in December 2026. The trained students would be given all assistance in the future to connect with celebrated artistes and to know more about various scholarship programmes.
After the inaugural session, Mr. Moghe was also honoured with a ‘ponnada’ in the presence of veteran tabla artiste Sivadas Chemanchery. Pookkad Kalalayam president K.T. Sreenivasan, former president V.K. Raghavan, tabla artiste Sumith Naik, and senior tabla trainers were present.

title: Son-in-law, his brother rob mother-in-law of ₹60 lakh in Shidlaghatta; three arrested
summary: Three arrested, including a son-in-law, for robbing mother-in-law of ₹60 lakh in a shocking Shidlaghatta robbery case.
content:
The Shidlaghatta police of Chickballapur district have cracked a sensational robbery case in which a woman was attacked and robbed of valuables worth ₹60 lakh when she was alone at home.
Three persons, including the victim’s son-in-law and his brother and father, have been arrested in connection with the crime that took place on December 10.
The accused have been identified as Sharukh Pasha, 25, the victim’s son-in-law, his brother Sahil Pasha, 24, and their father Inayath Pasha, 54. The victim is also elder sister of Inayath Pasha, the police said.
According to the police, the accused were in urgent need of money and conspired to rob a close relative, knowing that the family was well-off. They waited for an opportunity and struck when the victim, Mubarak, was alone at home after her husband and children had left for Ajmer on a religious trip.
Soon after Mubarak returned home on December 10, Sharukh and Sahil allegedly entered the house disguised in burqas. They gagged her mouth with adhesive tape, tied her hands and legs, assaulted her when she resisted, and ransacked the house. The duo fled with gold and silver ornaments worth around ₹60 lakh.
Despite her injuries, Mubarak managed to untie herself and alerted her relatives, who rushed to the house and shifted her to a hospital.
Based on her complaint, the Shidlaghatta police registered a case of robbery and formed a special investigation team to track down the accused.
During the investigation, it emerged that the brothers had handed over a portion of the stolen gold to their father, Inayath Pasha, to dispose of it. Acting on a tip-off, the police traced Inayath to Devanahalli, where he was attempting to pawn the stolen gold. He was caught red-handed.
During interrogation, Inayath Pasha confessed to his role in the crime, leading to the arrest of his two sons and the recovery of a major portion of the stolen valuables.
Superintendent of Police, Chickballapur, Kushal Chowksey, appreciated the Shidlaghatta police team for their swift and effective investigation in cracking the case.

title: 200 students take part in National Agritech Hackathon in Guntur
summary: 200 students from 17 states participated in the National Agritech Hackathon-2025 in Guntur, showcasing innovative agricultural solutions.
content:
The National Agritech Hackathon-2025 was inaugurated at R.V.R. and J.C. College of Engineering (Autonomous) in Chowdavaram, on Monday, highlighting cutting-edge technological solutions for the agriculture sector. Organised by the STP Foundation, with support from central agricultural institutions, the two-day national-level event saw participation from 200 students in 66 teams representing 17 States.
ICAR-NAARM aIDEA Additional CEO A.N.A. Vijay called upon students to pursue agri-innovations and startups to support farmers. As part of the event, an MoU was exchanged between ICAR-NAARM aIDEA and the college to jointly nurture agritech innovations, incubation support and technology commercialisation.

title: Minister Vivek pays tributes to Venkatswamy on 11th death anniversary
summary: Minister Vivek honors his father Venkatswamy on the 11th death anniversary, reflecting on his impactful legacy in labor and governance.
content:
Labour, Employment, Mines and Geology Minister G. Vivek Venkatswamy said that the footprints of late Gaddam Venkatswamy’s work can be seen in every sector, especially those concerning labour. He paid floral tributes, accompanied by his wife Mrs. G. Saroja, to the statue of his father Venkatswamy (Kaka) at Tank Bund on Monday observing the 11th death anniversary.
Speaking on the occasion, Minister Vivek Venkatswamy stated that fulfilling the ideals of former Union Minister Venkatswamy and continuously striving to deliver people-centric and transparent governance is his foremost objective. He added that the thoughts and vision of Kaka will continue to guide present-day political leaders as well as future generations. Mr. Vivek Venkatswamy further said that Kaka Venkatswamy always stood by the poor, fought for their cause, and worked towards providing long-lasting solutions to their problems.

title: Cong. got 29.17%, CPI(M) 27.16%, and BJP 14.76% votes in local  body polls
summary: In Kerala's 2025 local body polls, Congress leads with 29.17% votes, followed by CPI(M) at 27.16% and BJP at 14.76%.
content:
The Congress got 29.17% of the votes polled in the 2025 Kerala local body elections while the Communist Party of India (Marxist) stood second with 27.16%, and the Bharatiya Janata Party 14.76% votes, show the data on party-wise vote share released by the State Election Commission (SEC) on Monday.
The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) took home 9.77% of the votes, while the Communist Party of India (CPI) trailed behind the Independents (5.77%) with 5.58% of the votes. The Congress received 1,60,24,802 votes, the CPI(M) 1,49,22,193 votes, the BJP 81,08,137, the IUML 53,69,745, and the CPI 30,66,476 votes.
Independents, who also include party-backed candidates although the SEC has not specified as such, polled 31,67,381 votes.
The Congress-led UDF clearly had the upper hand across panchayats, municipalities and corporations in the two-phased 2025 elections, while the CPI(M)-led LDF trailed in second position overall. The BJP-led NDA scripted an upset in the crucial 101-ward Thiruvananthapuram Corporation by emerging as the single largest party with 50 seats.
Among the other parties in the UDF fold, the Kerala Congress won 1.33% of the votes (7,30,110), the Kerala Congress (Jacob) 0.16% (85,457), and the Revolutionary Socialist Party 0.48% votes (2,63,202).
Among the other parties in the LDF, the Kerala Congress (M) won 1.62% (8,91,977) votes and the Kerala Congress (B) 0.16% (60,712) votes. The Congress (Secular) won 40,316 votes (0.07%). The Rashtriya Janata Dal won 3,93,182 (0.72%), the NCP- 3,290 (0.01%), the NCP (Saratchandra Pawar) - 2,01,956 (0.37%), and the Janata Dal (Secular) 2,15,125 (0.39%) votes.
In the BJP-led NDA, the Bharat Dharma Jana Sena won 0.26% votes (1,45,402), while the Shiv Sena got 877 votes.
Among the other parties, the Socialist Democratic Party of India got 4,05,246 votes, which accounts for 0.74% of the total votes, and the Welfare Party of India, 0.12% (68,507).
The People’s Democratic Party won 22,994 (0.04%) votes, and the Aam Aadmi Party won 69,450 (0.13%).
The Revolutionary Marxist Party of India claimed 0.11% of the votes (60,829) and Twenty20 Party - 2,11,355 (0.38%) votes.
Among the Kerala units of major parties elsewhere in India, the Bahujan Samaj Party won 31,525 (0.06%) votes, the Samajwadi Party 675 votes, and the AIADMK, 2,348 votes.

title: BRS asks Congress govt. to withdraw letter given for use of 45 tmc ft for PRLIS, pursue for 90 tmc ft
summary: BRS urges Congress to withdraw its water allocation request for PRLIS, demanding full rights for Telangana's irrigation needs.
content:
The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) demanded that the State government withdraw its letter addressed to the Ministry of Jal Shakti seeking environmental clearance to the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme (PRLIS) with 45 tmc ft water instead of the proposed 90 tmc ft and protect the water rights of Telangana by pursuing for the originally intended quantity.
The Congress government led by A. Revanth Reddy had been working against the interests of Telangana from day one and it had almost handed over the irrigation projects to the two river boards, senior leader of the party and former Minister T. Harish Rao said here on Monday. But the government had stepped back after BRS founder and former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao raised the voice against the move, he said addressing a press conference.
Hitting back strongly at Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy for making what he (Harish Rao) called ‘senseless remarks’ against Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao and BRS on the front of irrigation in Telangana during 2014-23, Mr. Harish Rao said. He sought to know the rationale in Mr. Reddy’s claim that the Centre had returned the detailed project report (DPR) of PRLIS in 2023 itself, when seven clearances, including from the Central Electricity Authority, Central Soil and Material Research Station, Ministry of Tribal Affairs and Central Groundwater Board, were secured in that year.
He explained that the DPR was returned to the State in April 2023 but the BRS government had reverted to the MoJS within three days and Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao spoke to the ministry officials to give instructions to the Central Water Commission and different directorates and to continue the process of PRLIS appraisal. But the Congress government had kept silent when the DPR was returned again in December 2024 and had not pursued even one clearance in two years.
As if that was not enough, Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and Chief Minister Revanth Reddy wrote to the Centre seeking EC for PRLIS with just 45 tmc ft water, the BRS leader said adding that he (Harish Rao) had already explained on the floor of the Assembly how the temporary shares of 299:512 tmc ft water were allocated to Telangana and Andhra Pradesh at the time of State formation how the BRS government had been opposing it since 2014, including getting the matter referred to KWDT-II for reapportionment of water.
He explained that Telangana had become number one paddy producer in the country in 2020-21 itself with a production of 141 lakh tonnes in Kharif with the help of Kaleshwaram project. A total of 17.24 lakh acres of new ayacut was irrigated and stabilisation of another 31.5 lakh acres was done during 2014-23, whereas the Congress government did not even give water for 11,000 acres out of 11.61 lakh acres promised in the first two years.

title: CPI urges Naidu to press Centre for changes in VB–G RAM G Act
summary: CPI leaders urge CM Naidu to address funding issues and employment concerns in the VB–G RAM G Act implementation.
content:
A delegation of the Communist Party of India led by its national secretariat member K. Ramakrishna on Monday sought Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s intervention in the implementation of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, earlier known as the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.
The CPI leaders expressed concern that the reduction of the Central government’s funding share from 90% to 60% would place a heavy financial burden on the States, which would now have to bear 40% of the expenditure as against 10% earlier. They also alleged that, contrary to the Centre’s claim of increasing the guaranteed work days from 100 to 125, not even an average of 50 days of employment had been provided so far, making access to wage employment in rural areas more difficult under the new law.
The delegation requested Mr. Naidu to take up the issue with the Central government and seek suitable amendments to the Act in the interests of rural wage seekers. They also opposed the removal of Mahatma Gandhi’s name from the nomenclature of the legislation. CPI leaders G. Eswaraiah and Muppalla Nageswara Rao were present.

title: Truck carrying decorative items catches fire at Vyttila
summary: A truck carrying decorative items caught fire in Vyttila, but no injuries were reported thanks to a quick alert.
content:
A truck transporting decorative items belonging to a Kumbalam-based event management company caught fire along the service road of the national highway at Vyttila on Monday (December 22) around 3.30 p.m.
While most of the cargo was gutted, no injuries were reported, including to the truck driver, who was initially unaware of the fire. A tragedy was averted after an autorickshaw driver passing by noticed smoke billowing from the cargo area and alerted the truck driver. By then, passers-by had gathered, and the Fire and Rescue Services had been informed.
“The lorry contained decorative items, including lights, clothes, and carbon dioxide cylinders. Since the vehicle was on the service road, traffic was not significantly disrupted. The vehicle was isolated and the fire was extinguished within a short time,” Fire and Rescue Services sources said. Fire contingents from the Gandhinagar and Thripunithura stations responded.
The decorative items were being transported back after an event in Mangaluru. The truck, which was contracted for the job, sustained only minor damage.

title: ‘Operation Gajamukthi’ at Aralam Farm to enter next phase from Dec. 23
summary: Operation Gajamukthi at Aralam Farm begins December 23, 2025, to safely guide stray elephants back to their habitat.
content:
The Forest department will launch the next phase of ‘Operation Gajamukthi’ on Tuesday (December 23, 2025) to safely drive wild elephants that have strayed into Aralam farm and nearby rehabilitation areas back into their natural habitat within the wildlife sanctuary.
The two-day intensive driving operation, scheduled to continue till December 24, 2025, will be carried out under the leadership of the Forest department with coordinated support from various government departments. Officials said the mission has been planned with full preparedness, extensive arrangements, and complete inter-departmental cooperation, and would be implemented strictly as per the Forest department’s standard operating procedure. Similar operations have been carried out earlier at regular intervals based on necessity.
As part of the operation, advanced drones and camera traps will be used to accurately track both elephant herds and lone elephants within the farm area. The Kottiyoor Range Officer and the Aralam Assistant Wildlife Warden will function as incident commanders, while two special driving teams have been deployed for the task.
Based on real-time monitoring through drones and camera traps, the driving operation will begin after 10 a.m. Traffic restrictions will be enforced at Palappuzha, Odanthode bridge, Odanthode school Junction, Block 6 check post, Thalippara Junction, and Block 13 Junction during the operation.
The comprehensive action plan is being implemented with the coordinated support of the local self-government institutions, Health department, Revenue department, and the Aralam Farm Corporation. Special teams have been deployed to ensure the safety of residents in the rehabilitation areas and to conduct awareness programmes. Night patrol will be intensified in vulnerable areas, including Pookund, where elephants may attempt to return after the operation.
The mission is being overseen by an organising committee chaired by the Sub-Collector, with the Divisional Forest Officer serving as the general convener.

title: Swift action by Hoysala: Abandoned new born rescued
summary: Hoysala police swiftly rescue an abandoned newborn in Bengaluru, ensuring the child's safety and care after urgent community alert.
content:
A newborn baby abandoned near a petrol bunk at Lingarajapuram was rescued following swift action by the K.G. Halli police on Sunday.
According to the police, local residents noticed the abandoned baby around 11.38 a.m. and immediately alerted the emergency helpline, Namma 112. The Command Centre relayed the information to the K.G. Halli police station, following which the Hoysala-46 staff, assistant sub-inspector N. Nagaraj and head constable Gopi, were dispatched to the spot.
The officers reached the location within seven minutes and conducted inquiries in the surrounding area. The newborn was immediately rescued and shifted to a nearby hospital for medical examination. However, they were unable to trace the baby’s parents or guardians.
After ensuring the child’s health and safety, the infant was handed over to the authorities concerned in the Banaswadi police station jurisdiction for further care and protection, the police said.
In a similar incident, the Chandra Layout police traced and rescued a 50-year-old woman who was found sitting in a distressed condition near the police station on Saturday night. The police said local residents noticed the woman around 10.25 p.m. and alerted the Namma 112, suspecting that she was missing or in need of assistance.
Based on the information, the Command Centre informed the Chandra Layout police station, and Hoysala-60 staff, assistant sub-inspector Shanthakumar and head constable Umesh M.S., rushed to the spot, reaching the spot within 12 minutes. Though the officers attempted to question the woman, she was unresponsive. Following standard operating procedures, the police ensured her safety and later handed her over to the Asare Foundation for further care and rehabilitation.

title: New scheme dismantles legal job guarantee for rural poor: Sachin Pilot
summary: Sachin Pilot criticises the new VB-G Ram G scheme for undermining the job guarantee for rural workers established by MGNREGA.
content:
:
Senior Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Monday opposed the name change of the MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Act), and said the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G Ram G) dismantled the job scheme’s core promise of a legal job guarantee that gave rural workers, women, and the unemployed dignity and protection.
The MGNREGA, which was enacted during the UPA regime in 2005, was renamed as VB-G Ram G, and President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent to the Bill on December 21, 2025.
The new Act brings structural changes to the rural job scheme while increasing the number of guaranteed days of work from 100 to 125 days.
Speaking at a press conference at the party office here, Mr. Pilot said the new Act would disempower the gram panchayats and curtail the constitutionally guaranteed right to a job of the rural people. During the COVID-19 crisis, it acted as a critical livelihood lifeline, preventing millions from slipping into hunger and debt.
Mr. Pilot pointed out that the UPA government’s rural jobs programme was named after Mahatma Gandhi, and it mandated 100 days of employment to the poor constitutionally, and sought to know why it was renamed by the BJP-led dispensation.
“What was the need to change it (scheme name)?. People will not like this,” the former Rajasthan Deputy Chief Minister said. Under the new Act, the Centre decides which areas are rural areas and provides jobs to rural people based on the availability of funds. “Now it’s a mere scheme and not a constitutionally right-based scheme,” the Congress leader said.
Noting that all civil society groups had condemned the new Act, he said instead of strengthening it, the Union government weakened it by reducing funding to the State under the scheme.
The NDA government led by the BJP does not want people to remember the good work done by Congress governments in the past, the Congress MLA from Rajasthan alleged.

title: Arrangements to fly body of mob attack victim to Raipur
summary: Arrangements made to fly mob attack victim's body and family from Kochi to Raipur, with ambulance support to native village.
content:
Thrissur Collector Arjun Pandian has said that arrangements have been made to fly the body of Ram Narayan Baghel, who was killed in a mob attack at Walayar in Palakkad, to his native place in Chhattisgarh. His family members will also be flown home.
The body will be taken from Kochi to Raipur on Tuesday morning. A seven-member team, including Ram Narayan Baghel’s family members who had come to Kerala, will travel by air from Kochi to Raipur. Ambulance facilities have been arranged to transport the body and family members from Raipur to their native village in Chhattisgarh.
The Collector spent time with the bereaved family, offering words of comfort to Ram Narayan's wife, children and brother, as well as those accompanying them. He assured them that the administration stood firmly with the family and that all necessary assistance would be extended.
The Collector presented pens to the children and encouraged them to continue their studies, conveying the administration’s concern and support. He also said that the Palakkad district administration was taking steps to ensure that the family received all eligible financial assistance at the earliest.

title: Crime comes down by 5.5% in A.P. in 2025
summary: Crime in Andhra Pradesh decreased by 5.5% in 2025, with notable declines in violence against women and cyber crimes.
content:
The overall crime in the State has declined by 5.5% with 16 districts reporting a fall in the number of cases and 10 showing a rise in the count.
A report on the crime data up to November 25, 2025 has been submitted to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu by DGP Harish Kumar Gupta at a crime review meeting recently.
As per the data, 1,04,095 cases have been registered this year, as against 1,10,111 cases in 2024. There has been a rise in the number of economic offences, road accidents and property offences.
A rise in crime was noticed in Annamayya district (9.5%), Konaseema (8.5%), Nellore (7.8%), Guntur and Tirupati (6.5%), Sri Satya Sai (4.8%), Parvathipuram Manyam (2.7%), Kakinada (2%), East Godavari (1.5%) and Kurnool (0.7%).
Cases related to attempt to murder, housebreaking by day and theft cases increased. Detection of property offences stood at 56% and recovery 55%, according to police officials.
In all, 8,035 economic offences, including cheating and criminal breach of trust cases, were registered (6.6% rise). The economic offence cases registered in 2024 were 7,539.
Cyber crime cases dropped to 1,771 as against 2,853 in 2024. The victims lost about ₹751 crore in cyber frauds, while the police froze about ₹89 crore in banks and returned nearly ₹2.21 crore, this year.
As many as 16,288 cases, including rape and murder, gang rape, cyber crime and assault on women were registered this year, which is lower than the figure for 2024 that stood at 16,913.
The cases of crime against women, however, increased in Sri Satya Sai, Nellore, Vizianagaram, Kadapa, Guntur, Annamayya, Palnadu, Parvathipuram Manyam and Tirupati districts.
On the other hand, at a law and order review held a few days ago, police officers told the Chief Minister that under ‘Operation Trace’, a special drive, 1,177 missing girls and 2,483 women were traced in the last four months.
As many as 6,139 accused were arrested under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. Police seized 721 vehicles, and attached properties worth about ₹9 crore belonging to the offenders. They booked 68 accused under the Prevention of Illicit Trafficking in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PIT-NDPS) Act, police officials said.
The police detected 6,993 cases by using 347 drones and vigil has been stepped up on ganja peddling and consumption, gambling, eve-teasing and other crimes through drones.
Of the total 26,518 rowdy sheeters in A.P., 11,728 were bound over, 15 were externed and PD Act was enforced against 153 criminals.
The Andhra Pradesh police achieved significant results in combating Left Wing Extremism (LWE), with the assistance of their counterparts in Chhattisgarh and Odisha. About 58 Maoists were arrested and about 16 top cadre Naxalites were neutralized in 2025, the police said.

title: Police shoot knife-wielding suspect after attack on inspector
summary: Police shot a knife-wielding suspect after he attacked an inspector during an attempted murder arrest in Anantapur.
content:
Police on Monday (December 22, 2025) opened fire on an accused after he attacked a circle inspector who had gone to arrest him in connection with an attempted murder case on the outskirts of the town. The accused injured three persons with a knife and tried to attack others, prompting the police to fire two rounds in order to apprehend the fleeing suspect.
According to Superintendent of Police P. Jagadeesh, four friends from Naik Nagar — Chakali Raja, Ajay, Sohail, and Akram — consumed alcohol at Arvind Nagar around 7 p.m. on Sunday. After some time, Raja demanded that his friends purchase more liquor, which led to an argument. In a fit of rage, Ajay stabbed Raja in the stomach with a knife. Raja was shifted to Government General Hospital, where he is currently on a ventilator. A case was registered, and police launched a search to nab Ajay, who fled from the spot.
On Monday morning around 8.30 a.m., Anantapur II Town police inspector Srikanth received information that Ajay was hiding near the TV Tower area where ‘shikharis’ (hunter community people) reside. “Our sub-inspector Rupendra Babu, constables Raghu Naik, Panava, Sudhakar, and others went to the area in mufti in an auto to nab him. We surrounded Ajay from all sides and were approaching him when he noticed the police team coming towards him and attacked the auto driver with the knife. He later fled into the nearby bushes. The local shikaris too tried to nab him but Ajay tried to attack them also. Ajay also tried to stab a woman but she luckily escaped,” Mr. Srikanth said. Ajay even tried to attack constable Raghu but the latter was lucky.
The injured auto driver, Baba, was shifted to a private hospital for treatment.
Mr. Srikanth said that Ajay jumped into the lake beside the bushes and fled to the other side. “We searched the lake but could not find him. Then we rushed to the other side on two-wheelers and in police vehicles and launched a search,” he said.
Ajay hid in the sugarcane fields, and we immediately surrounded them from all sides. “The sugarcane fields were dense and very tall. I cautioned Ajay to surrender, but he suddenly attacked me with a knife, striking my left shoulder. I immediately pulled out my 9 mm service weapon and fired one round into the air as a warning, again asking him to surrender. Ajay did not comply and once more pounced on me, at which point I shot him in the knees,” Mr. Srikanth said.
“Even after being hit by the bullet, Ajay was shouting at us, saying he wouldn’t hesitate to kill us if we moved towards him,” Srikanth said. Both Srikanth and Ajay were shifted to GGH for treatment. Ajay has a past criminal record and is known to be very aggressive, Mr. Srikanth added.
SP Jagadeesh, who visited the injured CI at the hospital, said stringent action will be taken against Ajay as per law.

title: Every MP and MLA takes commission, says Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi
summary: Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi claims all MPs and MLAs take commissions, stirring controversy within the National Democratic Alliance.
content:
Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi has once again put the National Democratic Alliance in an awkward situation with his remarks that all MPs and MLAs take commissions from their constituency development funds.
The Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) leader further claimed he had given his commission money to the party several times and advised party leaders to use the money to buy a car.
Mr. Manjhi made the comment at a party event on Sunday (December 21).
He told legislators that if they were not able to get a 10% commission, they should at least take 5%. He further said “every MP and MLA takes commissions” and “even 10 paise taken from a rupee” was a significant amount.
“I have personally given my commission money to the party fund several times. An MP gets ₹5 crore, and if he gets a 10% commission, it would be ₹40 lakh,” said Mr. Manjhi, who represents Gaya ji Lok Sabha constituency.
He also asked his son and party president Santosh Kumar Suman, who is a Cabinet Minister in the State, to take commissions as this “was no secret and everyone did it”. Looking at his son, Mr. Manjhi said, “If these people [the party leaders] are unable to do this, it is the fault of the party president.”
He declared that in the next Assembly election, the HAM(S) should contest 100 seats and if the demands were not met, then the party will go it alone. Mr. Manjhi asked his son to prepare an action plan to achieve the target, adding people of his caste will support it, though the HAM(S) will need the support of a few more castes.
He also said NDA allyBharatiya Janata Party (BJP)had made a mistake by underestimating him.
“We are not a ordinary party in Purnia, Magadh, and Munger divisions. We also have supporters in West Champaran. Our party is strong everywhere, but the BJP has underestimated us in every election. Whatever has happened so far is fine. If we are not given importance in the next election, we will go our own way,” Mr. Manjhi said.
A few days ago, a purported video of Mr. Manjhi’s speech had gone viral on social media, in which he was heard saying that in the 2020 Assembly election, he helped his Tikari candidate, who was trailing by 2,700 votes, win with the support of then District Magistrate of Gaya ji.
His remarks that he would walk out of the alliance if his demand for a Rajya Sabha seat was not met had also caused a stir.
“I saw in the news that Janata Dal (United) was being given two Rajya Sabha seats, the BJP two, and the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) one. Where does our party stand? In the 2024 election, a promise was made to us on two Lok Sabha seats and one Rajya Sabha seat. At that time, we were given one Lok Sabha seat, which I won, and I thank the Prime Minister for making me a Minister, but we are still waiting for the Rajya Sabha seat,” Mr. Manjhi said.
Minister and BJP leader Dilip Kumar Jaiswal termed Mr. Manjhi’s remarks on Sunday his “personal opinion”. Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) spokesperson Shakti Singh Yadav said all was not well in the NDA even after winning 202 seats in the Assembly election.

title: Indian Navy receives third indigenous ASW Shallow Water Craft ‘Anjadip’ from GRSE
summary: Indian Navy receives third indigenous ASW Shallow Water Craft 'Anjadip', enhancing anti-submarine capabilities and showcasing self-reliance in defense.
content:
The Indian Navy on Monday (December 22, 2025) received Anjadip, the third of eight Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW SWC), indigenously designed and built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata.
The delivery took place in Chennai, marking another significant step in India’s drive towards self-reliance in defence shipbuilding.
The Navy informed that the ASW SWC project is being executed under a Public-Private Partnership between GRSE and L&T Shipyard, Kattupalli. The vessels have been designed and constructed in accordance with the classification rules of the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS), demonstrating the success of collaborative defence manufacturing in the country.
At approximately 77 metres in length, the ASW SWCs are the largest Indian naval warships to be propelled by waterjets. They are equipped with state-of-the-art lightweight torpedoes, indigenously developed anti-submarine rockets and shallow-water sonar, enabling effective detection and engagement of underwater threats. These platforms will significantly enhance the Navy’s anti-submarine warfare capability, coastal surveillance and mine-laying operations, the Navy added.
Anjadip is named after Anjadip Island off the coast of Karwar in Karnataka and is a reincarnation of the erstwhile INS Anjadip, a Petya-class corvette that was decommissioned in 2003. The naming underscores India’s commitment to safeguarding its extensive maritime domain.
With this delivery, GRSE has achieved the rare feat of delivering five warships to the Indian Navy in a single year. Anjadip is the 115th warship built by the shipyard and the 77th delivered to the Navy. The vessel was accepted by Rear Admiral Gautam Marwaha, VSM, Chief Staff Officer (Technical), Eastern Naval Command.
Earlier in 2025, GRSE delivered the Advanced Guided Missile Frigate Himgiri, the first two ASW SWCs Arnala and Androth, and the Survey Vessel (Large) Ikshak, all of which have since been commissioned.
Fitted with an indigenous 30 mm Naval Surface Gun and boasting over 80% indigenous content, Anjadip exemplifies the government’s ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ vision and the growing strength of India’s domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem, the Navy said.

title: State hopeful of submitting DPR of metro rail project in February
summary: With hardly a few months left for the incumbent government in office, the Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) have sped up the process to prepare the detailed project report for the metro rail project in Thiruvananthapuram. It is expected that the DPR could be submitted by the end of January or the first week of February.
content:
With hardly a few months left for the incumbent government in office, the Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) have sped up the process to prepare the detailed project report for the metro rail project in Thiruvananthapuram. It is expected that the DPR could be submitted by the end of January or the first week of February.
Speaking toThe Hindu,senior government sources said the DPR of the project is in the finalisation stage, with changes being made to the earlier DPR prepared by the DMRC.
As per the new alignment approved by the State government, the first phase of the project has a length of 31 km with 27 stations, with the metro rail project starting from Pappanamcode and terminating at Eenchakkal. The major revision of the DPR comes in areas like the newly added Technopark stretch in the first phase of the project, which is included considering the persistent demands raised by various stakeholders, along with the new stretch from Pattom to Ulloor via Medical College instead of the Pattom-Ulloor stretch via Kesavadasapuram.
The traffic projections along with the technical feasibility of the newly added stretches will be figured in detail in the revised DPR. Once the DPR is submitted and vetted by the State government, it will be sent for Cabinet approval. Thereafter, it will be submitted to the Union Ministry for Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) for final approval. The DPR is being revised by the DMRC as per the instruction of the KMRL, and the State government sources are hopeful that the revised DPR could be submitted to the Centre before the term of the current government.
Based on the progress in getting final approval from the Centre government, the KMRL can float tenders to engage consultants for executing the project and start land acquisition measures. In between, the KMRL could complete the road widening works along the approved stretch while it will be waiting for the final approval. The flyover at Pattom should also be redesigned, as the alignment favours taking the metro rail project from Pattom to Ulloor via Medical College instead of the previously agreed Pattom to Ulloor stretch via Kesavadasapuram.
The work on the Sreekaryam flyover is in full swing, where no major redesigning is required. At the same time, there would be minor changes in the Ulloor junction with the new proposed line going straight towards the Medical College route, said government sources. The project is expected to cost around ₹8,000 crore for completion, with per kilometre cost coming to ₹250 crore. The funding options, including the agencies from which the loans are to be borrowed, will be fixed after approval from the Centre, said sources. The project was in limbo for quite some time, and now it is redesigned in line with the Metro Rail Policy, 2017, and guidelines of the Central Government, which insisted that North Railway Station and the airport have to be brought into the new alignment.

title: Youngster found drowned in swimming pool of former MP’s house in Guntur
summary: Young man drowns in former MP's swimming pool in Guntur; suspicious death investigation launched after incident.
content:
A young man was reportedly found drowned in a swimming pool at the residence of a former MP at Reddypalem village in Guntur Rural mandal. A suspicious death case was registered at Nallapadu police station following the incident. According to police, the deceased was identified as Polepogu Harsha Vardhan, who worked as a swimming pool cleaner.
The incident occurred when Harsha Vardhan went to clean the swimming pool at the residence of former MP Modugula Venugopala Reddy. For reasons yet to be fully ascertained, he accidentally fell into the pool and drowned. He was immediately shifted to the Government General Hospital (GGH), Guntur, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.
Based on a complaint lodged by his mother, Polepogu Madhavi of Swarnabharathi Nagar, police registered a case under suspicious death provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNSS) and took up investigation.
Guntur Superintendent of Police (SP) Vakul Jindal said CCTV footage from the premises was examined and it showed Harsha Vardhan falling into the pool and drowning as he was unable to swim. When the incident occurred, he was only the person seen in the visuals. Further clarity on the cause of death will emerge after the medical report, he added.

title: Wife, two others held for murder of logistics manager in Boduppal
summary: Three arrested, including wife, for the murder of a logistics manager in Boduppal, uncovering a chilling conspiracy.
content:
The Medipally police uncovered murder plot behind the death of a logistics manager and arrested three persons, including the wife of the deceased, for allegedly strangulating him at their residence in East Brundavan Colony, Boduppal.
The accused were identified as J. Purnima, 36, wife of the deceased V.J. Ashok, Paleti Mahesh, 22, a construction worker, and Bhukya Sai Kumar alias Sai, 22, a student. Police said Ashok, 45, was working as a logistics manager at Srinidhi University.
According to the police, Purnima lodged a complaint on December 12, stating that her husband was found unconscious in the washroom of their house and was later declared dead at the Government Hospital in Malkajgiri.  A case was registered and investigation was taken up.
During the investigation, officers noticed injuries on the cheek and neck of the deceased, which raised suspicion over the cause of death. Examination of CCTV footage and analysis of technical evidence subsequently led to the arrest of the three accused.
Police said the investigation revealed that Purnima had developed an illicit relationship with Mahesh, who had earlier been residing in the same colony. Ashok allegedly suspected the relationship and frequently questioned her. Following this, Purnima and Mahesh allegedly conspired to eliminate him and roped in Sai for assistance.
On December 11, at about 6.15 p.m., after Ashok returned home from work, Mahesh and Sai allegedly caught hold of him and assaulted him, while Purnima held his legs. Mahesh is said to have strangulated Ashok using three chunnis, causing his death. The accused later changed the clothes of the deceased and disposed of incriminating articles in an attempt to destroy evidence. Purnima allegedly informed relatives that Ashok had died due to a heart attack.
Police seized a phone allegedly used by Mahesh, three blood-stained chunnis, more blood-stained clothes, broken teeth of the deceased, a pen drive containing incriminating photos and videos, and a two-wheeler used by Sai.
The case has been altered to include charges of murder and criminal conspiracy. All three accused were arrested and remanded to judicial custody. Police said further investigation was underway and efforts were being made to strengthen the case with scientific and forensic evidence.

title: Assam tribal council chief’s house torched as anger over ‘encroachers’ explodes
summary: Protestors set fire to Assam tribal council chief's home amid escalating tensions over alleged encroachment by 'outsiders.'
content:
Protestors torched the ancestral residence of anAssamtribal council chief on Monday (December 22, 2025) for his alleged failure to evict “outsiders” from two categories of government-designated grazing reserves.
At least three protestors were among four people injured in clashes with security personnel at Donkamokam in central Assam’s West Karbi Anglong district, where the Karbi tribe is in the majority. The place is 155 km southeast of Guwahati.
West Karbi Anglong and Karbi Anglong, located further east, are Sixth Schedule areas governed by the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC), where the Bharatiya Janata Party is in power. The protestors marched 26km from West Karbi Anglong’s Kheroni, where they had been on hunger strike for a fortnight, demanding the eviction of “non-locals” allegedly occupying large swathes of village grazing reserves (VGRs) and professional grazing reserves (PGRs).
Tension gripped the Kheroni area after the police picked up nine protestors on Sunday (December 21, 2025) night. This enraged the protestors, who blocked the roads and vandalised shops before proceeding to Donkamokam.
